texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Let me summarize it as follows: First of all, measures adopted by the electricity sector in order to eliminate the  tariff deficit have had an impact on Red Eléctrica. They have postponed the payment of remuneration arising from  entry into service in one year and bringing down revenues by €45 million, as a result of remunerating assets,  which are in service, but not amortized as the net value basis. Then, tax wise, there's been elimination of  amortization freedom and therefore the payment – the deferral payment of the corporate tax for investments  made after April 1. You know that we are a high investment company and therefore this is very important to us.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Red Eléctrica has made investment in transmission amounting to €672 million with very many parts of it  becoming operational after paralyzing the new investments as set forth in Royal Decree 13/2012. The Ministry has  approved a new essential investment package in order to guarantee certainty of supply and cutting costs in the  electrical power system and this work is urgent.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: 2012 results is a new milestone in integrating renewable energy in Spain, in which wind power is especially  significant, new historical records have been achieved in coverage 64% and instantaneous wind production as well  as daily and energy, and energy by the hours. In addition, we've again surpassed levels in 2013 and electrical  interconnection between the mainland and Balearic is fully operational since mid-2012, and now contribute 30%  to the power system in Balearic, and we're meeting the objectives of quality, certainty of supply and overall  savings.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Finally, the average lifecycle of our debt is up 5.7 years, but if we do away with the €800 million, that – which  have their maturity in this 2013, due this year, the average lifespan will be increased up to 6.6 years. These are  most significant elements I wanted to point out regarding this year. And concerning the elements that have made,  of course, 2012 a tough year macroeconomically difficult year and we of course cannot – have also been affected  by this, but we've had to work on energy measures such as reducing tariff deficit.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: And now, I'd like to talk about strategic plan up to 2017, 2013-2017, there are five essential pillars in this strategy.  First, operational excellence, in order to achieve efficiencies that place Red Eléctrica as an international  benchmark; second, market integration and sustainability of the electric system that justify a sufficient, significant  level of investment and finally strengthening of the company's balance sheet debt, focusing on prudent financial  policies. So these are the three most significant elements.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: As a system operator, we guarantee the balance between supply and demand immediately, because a generation  makes it difficult to foresee what the needs are going to be with greater weight renewable energies, we have been  pioneers in creating a Center for Renewable Energy Control, CRCRE, which have made it possible to integrate  renewables at the European level despite the lowest international interconnection. Therefore, this is extremely  important, the importance of renewable energy, but they don't have any international interconnections.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Renewable energies have very many good things. But, they have some weakness that we need to offset and it's that  they're not manageable, there is either wind or not, but the market demand does – isn't dependent on there being  wind or not, so we need to offset that. Germany and other countries have very many international  interconnections, so it's automatically offset on the grid, but Spain has had to develop its own model.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: This center, I talked to you about the control of renewable energy sources, offering quality and guarantee of supply  despite a very low international interconnection. We also manage the only completely operational interconnection  with Europe – between Europe and North Africa. I'd also like to underscore that all our corporate policy is aimed  at proactive maintenance of our grade in order to guarantee the quality of the services we offer. Thus,  guaranteeing this at the very same time certainty of supply and we need to properly qualify and train experts so  that they can have optimum maintenance in operation of facilities, maintenance, conservation, repairs of all our  lines.  We have to carry a special specific renewal program in order for it to have all it – meet the necessary standards.  One of the most important elements in Red Eléctrica is integrating, improving, and renewing acquired assets. Red  Eléctrica is the owner of facilities in Balearic and Canaria since 2010 and it's – since then significantly improved  energy ratios and average interruption times in 2011 and 2012, in which we started working on renewal and  improvement.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, I'd like to talk about the second pillar of our future programs and this is electrification in optimum level. So  the TSO plays a key role in energy policy. So the main criteria for articulating energy, the energy policy is to  increase electrification in Spain, as a means of promoting internal energy sources and reducing the dependence on  external sources by decreasing the use of oil and gas in transport. This is extremely important for us and for many  reasons including environmental ones, and two, also our deficit, Spain's deficit which has been highly conditioned  by our low energy – our high energy deficit.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: So we're talking about high percentages compared to other countries in our environment and this has led to  important macroeconomic issues. So if we're talking about, of course, environmental issues as well, so that's why  it is so important for us to increase electrification throughout the country. As you can see on the next slide, we see  here that in Spain, we have a ratio which is lower than other countries in terms of these issues.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, number two, we need to increase our energy saving and efficiency without increasing cost for the system. In  other words, through such measures expanding electrical appliances, which have low energy efficiency. Now, our  supply security, here on the Mainland and on the Island is also important to have interconnection levels with the  rest of Europe of at least 10% of installed capacity, compared to 3% today. In 2002, in our Barcelona agreement,  we agreed that throughout Europe, we would have interconnection levels of at least 10% of installed capacity if we  have a 100,000 megawatts installed, then – and then thanks to that agreement. We should have 10,000  megawatts rather than the level that we are talking about today.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, Red Eléctrica should also support the inclusion of power storage throughout the whole electricity supply  train to be able to optimize our network design, maximize the integration of new renewable energies and minimize  the final cost of electricity supplies to promote the development of a smart grid and smart meters. Well, that  would make it possible for us to drive the future growth of electric cars and faster – more rational use of energy  thereby moving demand curve throughout the day. All of these are elements which are very important to  guarantee our energy supply over the next few years, as I will show you now.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: As I've already pointed out today, Spain's electricity system is – doesn't represent the goals for our European  amount of import capacity to run stability to the system, therefore strengthening our interconnections with our  neighbor systems, it's going to represent the biggest investments that Spain is going to have to make.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: As you all know, we're working on the construction of interconnection measures between Spain and France  through the East Pyrenees and this interconnection will double the electricity interconnection capacity between  the two countries to reach 2,800 megawatts to enhance the security of the Mainland electricity system and  interconnection and we hope that this program will be commissioned in 2014.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: So apart from improvements in quality of service and the reduction of unsupplied – non-supplied electricity, we  also need to produce savings and to also reduce our environmental impact. Let me just say that our underwater  connections between Mallorca and Ibiza can save €30 million in cost. If we can use more efficient stations and  reduce contamination in the next few years, we will be investing between €125 million to €150 million in the  Island for these purposes.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, let me tell you about the main investments that we will be making on the Mainland to reinforce  interconnection between Spain's different regions by strengthening the grid and support of transmission in areas  like Cataluña, Levante and Cantabria and we want to boost the efficiency by supporting the transmission of power  from regions like Galicia, Asturias, Navarra and Aragón with more competitive generation.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: The planning of electricity transmission must incorporate economic efficiency criteria and taking into account  changes in the – our macroeconomic context and we must always adapt to trends and demand. Therefore, the  Ministry has begun to drop a new investment plan for 2014-2020, which will take in to account the new scenarios  and transform Spain's energy system to meet the needs established in our 20/2020 energy efficiency, renewable  energy and environmental targets.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: So here, let me say that in terms of what Red Eléctrica is doing, we feel that we're very much in line with our plan  as it has been set out in terms of providing infrastructures. And because of this, there are two elements which we  must be taken to account and of course I am talking about the 20/2020 plan. Here we have the publication of that  group of investments with these – critical investments that the Ministry has published, which is going to make it  possible, thanks to investments already made to have the right – and to make the right investment over the next  few years. And so until the new energy plan has been established and plan for 2020 and that will come to effect at  the end of 2014, then – so we believe that everything will be in place by then.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, let me talk about the third pillar then to strengthen – in terms of our future plans which is to strengthen our  balance sheet. So we need to take a series of regulatory measures which have affected the company through 2012.  So we have gone from the investments where our CPI has been adapted to the new index. And so any energy plans  that we are going through the process of defining methodology as we see in Royal Decree 13/2012, so that we can  adapt in terms of all of the assets that we will be requiring and to adjust these as I say to our asset.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: As for our dividend policy, we will continue to have growth in dividends. Yesterday, the Board of Directors agreed  this – to submit a dividend per share of €2.3651, which is a payout of 65%, in line with the last years. Red  Eléctrica will continue to focus its efforts on creating value for shareholders, while preserving its solid capital  structure and working to guarantee high quality and efficient power supply. In other words, we want to create  value. We want to have a structure, solid capital structure and guarantee the quality of our power supply. So thank  you very much for your attention.

texts.speaker: A
texts.profession: Thank you very much. Perhaps we have some questions through our webpage [indiscernible] (00:47:11) has asked
texts.text: us a few questions. And the first one is when do we think the new infrastructure plan will be approved? The  second question is, is the CapEx through – due to 2013 and 2014 has been confirmed, are we pending or are you  pending approval by the government can it be changed?

texts.speaker: A
texts.profession: Thank you very much. Perhaps we have some questions through our webpage [indiscernible] (00:47:11) has asked
texts.text: [ph] Javier (0:48:02) would also like to know the following. The government has said that electricity prices are  very high today, what could Red Eléctrica do to contribute to reducing electricity prices?

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: The initial forecast would be – for it to be approved during the second half of 2014, it's a 2014-2020 plan, as we  now have an investment margin for 2013-2017 based on administrative permits plus a critical infrastructure  investment, this would be linked to the 20, 2022. It's always a very extensive process in time. Since the first  studied analyses, engineering and all that is done and until it becomes operational, it's commissioned until – and  the government starts paying a year behind six, seven years of investment can go by and after they've concluded,  we get paid. So what timeline horizon are we looking at then?

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Storage now, storage is an essential element to certainty of supply and soundness of the system. So its government  – we cannot say more, it will be the government that decides. But storage is absolutely essential to the operation of  the energy system in Spain. Everything done in storage will be very important for the sustainability of our system  and we're thinking about the Islands too. And there you are, Juan, you could talk about the other questions?

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Corporate Director of Economics and Finance (CFO), Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: And there is one question left, how can Red Eléctrica contribute to reducing energy prices. Well, in our math of  energy cost per year, Red Eléctrica amounts to 4.6% overall, of overall energy costs for citizens. How can Red  Eléctrica contribute? Well, the same as everyone else by being efficient without making things worse, without  risking supply certainty and Red Eléctrica ratios do – when compared to efficiency ratios of other companies, we  come out very well. So that's the work we have to do. And Spain's TSO model is good for achieving this. Thank  you.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: The most noteworthy of these investments commissioned during the year are the following. First of all, the  Almaraz-Guillena line, which guarantees the quality of supply to Extremadura and Andalusia, which is basically  the center – south axis; the Guillena-Puebla de Guzmán line, which alongside the Almaraz-Guillena line  strengthens the connection with Portugal; and then in the North, the [ph] Grago -Sallas (3:50) line, which forms  part of a wider project to fully connect the Cantabrian coast line and allow wind energy to be evacuated from  Galicia and Asturias to areas with high demand and supply shortfalls, such as the Basque Country and Cantabria.  We also continue working on several major projects, which will be completed in the next few months.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Of these, I'd like to highlight the new interconnection through Catalonia to France, which will make it possible to  double the exchange capacity with our neighboring country and will make the entire Spanish electricity system  more flexible.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: The final method for calculating the remuneration of the electricity transmission business was approved. This  method reinforces and clarifies the principles for remunerating electricity transmission activities in line with our  European peers. Later on, we will examine these regulatory developments in greater detail.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Our notable performances in socially responsible practices was also recognized by the market with the Company  being listed on the prestigious Dow Jones and FTSE for good sustainability indexes. Additionally, Red Eléctrica  has renewed the European Seal of Excellence 500+ in accordance with our EFQM 2013 model achieving 67 8  points, which is, I think, the highest score in Spain.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Firstly, revenues were boosted mainly because of the revenues generated by new facilities brought online. The  Company's net revenue climbed to €1,822.6 million, which is almost 95% of it coming from electricity  transmission.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: The most noteworthy were the measures contained in Royal Decree-Law 9/2013, which reduced income from  electricity transmission by €7 2 million or €50.6 million after-tax, as you can see in the graph.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: I would like to continue by stressing the importance of all of the measures that have been taken over recent  months to guarantee the financial stability of the Spanish electricity sector and to ensure that energy in our  country is not a limiting factor for economic development. As an electricity sector playe r, Red Eléctrica has been  involved in the solution to the tariff deficit.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: The transmission business remuneration scheme has been created within the context of a new benchwork  framework for the entire electricity sector, that is the law 24/2013. The basic aim of that law is to establish  regulation for the sector that guarantees electricity supply with the required quality levels and at the lowest cost  possible; thereby ensuring the economic and financial stability of the system to safeguard the system's financial  sustainability.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: A hypothetical scenario has been defined for this calculation involving net investment of €600 million including  the incentive for availability and assuming that the first year of the first regulatory period will be 2015. The  projections include the remuneration for Gas Natural Fenosa's transmission assets.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Moreover, additional measures designed to unlock value must also be considered, redefining the Company's  financial policy and process management approach. And lastly, pursuant to the transitional method set out in  Royal Decree-Law 9/2013, the 2014 tariff allocated to Red Eléctrica in the ministry rule published in the official  state gazette on the 1 of February sets out revenues for the transmission business at €1,622 million in 2014.

texts.speaker: Javier Suarez
texts.profession: Analyst, Mediobanca
texts.text: And the last question is about the reform of the wholesale electricity market. I know that the government is trying  to reform the market. Could you tell me what Red Eléctrica's position is in this discussion, does Red Eléctrica feel?

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Corporate Director of Economics and Finance (CFO), Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: So well, rather that's the reduction; that's not the cost, of course, that's 1.5%. And that reduction has only been  seen over three-and-a-half months. So of course that will be seen over eight-and-a-half months, like-for-like next  year on 2014. So we expect the cost of debt, the average cost will be closer to 3.5% and I think -- or 3.5%, I think  that's good news when you're talking about a CapEx-intensive company like ours.

texts.speaker: Javier Suarez
texts.profession: Analyst, Mediobanca
texts.text: And then, the third question I had was about the reform of the wholesale electricity market. It seems that the  Spanish Government would like to reform that market. I want to know what your position is as a Company, Red  Eléctrica, as you manage the grid; you are the transmission system operator. Do y ou think that this reform of  wholesale market will be advantageous for the electricity industry and what could Red Eléctrica do to help bring  down the cost of electricity in Spain? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Corporate Director of Economics and Finance (CFO), Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: So the idea is that we want to have more stability for that price, so that at any one time, the wholesale market  knows what the values are and when they go up, as happened in December, because of what happened with the  change with respect to the nuclear feed [ph] and such lengths (45:00), this won't change the whole system.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: In March 2002 at the European Barcelona Summit, it was said that by 2005, all European Union countries should  have an interconnection of at least 10% of the installed capacity. We have an installed capacity of more than  100,000 megawatts. So right now, well not right now, but back since 2005, 10 years ago, we should have the 10%  of that figure, 10,000 megawatts.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: So as you can see, we still continue to be almost an electricity island and that has meant that we have not been  able to get the benefit of a broader trading market with those interconnectors that we could use for the surplus  capacity renewable power that is being generated to take advantage of the more competitive pricing in Europe.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: So we are very much limited and this has to be done. This has to be done because  it was the European Union that  set out that these were the things that had to be done to establish that single internal market for energy. So  INELFE is working really well.

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Corporate Director of Economics and Finance (CFO), Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: I'm just talking strictly speaking about the tariffs there because you could also talk about the delay in actually  implementing N plus one and N plus two because that is the real impact on the tariff, if you add that in.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Focusing now on investments and commissioned assets. It should be noted that in 2014, Red Eléctrica made  significant progress in international interconnections. We completed the interconnection with France through the  Eastern Pyrenees, which will allow Spain's electricity exchange capacity with France to be doubled to 2,800  megawatts, as well as a new interconnection with Portugal through the 400 kilovolt Almaraz-Guillena line. These  are emblematic interconnections and certainly the country needed these interconnections. They're absolutely key  and Red Eléctrica has played an important role there.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: As far as system operation is concerned, there was also significant progress made. We'll only make a brief mention  to this at this point, but due to its relevance, we'll go back to it in deeper detail later in the presentation. At March,  2014, Red Eléctrica started posting on its website information on the hourly prices of the unit electricity costs to  be applied to the electricity bill of consumers, with a contracted capacity of less than 10 kilowatts and under the  small consumer voluntary price schemes.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Additionally, Red Eléctrica has started to organize and manage the new auction system to assign the  interruptibility service in a competitive and efficient manner. And finally, it's important to also mention that a  crucial step was taken towards a single European electricity market, with the rollout of simultaneous and  synchronized operations, which seek to couple the daily electricity markets of Southwest and Northwest Europe.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Finally, the company invested €956 million, including the investment relating to the ADIF transfer contract, in  specific, the €493 million in the development of electricity transmission grid in Spain. All of these figures  underscore the company's constant growth path and the appeal of our investment proposal for shareholders by  combining increased earnings with an attractive dividend payout for shareholders.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Additionally, a series of transitory imbalances were recorded in 2014, relating to the electricity tariff, totaling  €390 million and VAT linked to the purchase of the usage rights for the fiber optic network amounted to €90  million. Both of those items are expected to be collected during the early months of 2015.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We will now discuss the main lines of this strategic plan for the upcoming years. The reality of Red Eléctrica and  the plan we are presenting today for the upcoming years is framed within a European context, with many  challenges both present and future. The new package of climate and energy for 2030 was presented into 2014,  which covers these challenges and seeks to guarantee the competitiveness, reliability and sustainability of the  economy, and the energy sector of the European Union.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The goals ratified by the European Council are 40% cut in greenhouse gas emissions, with respect to 1990 levels; a  binding target at EU level of at least 27 % of renewable energies; renewed ambition in energy efficiency policies;  with a cut of 27 % on consumption forecast; a new governance system; and a new series of indicators to guarantee  a competitive and safe energy system.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: These objectives pose new challenges for the electricity system, which is in a state of transition towards a new  model characterized by the preponderance of renewable energies, which require different management approach  than conventional energies reduction, independence on fossil fuels, and the emergence of consumer gr oups that  traditionally played a passive role.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Now, in this sense, compensating a lower manageability of renewable energies promoting energy efficiency  measures and managing the new role of consumers, which is much more participatory, represent just some of the  challenges that will need to be tackled over the coming years to ensure the efficient management of the system as  a whole. Network integration and energy storage will be the key tools that will help developing a low -emission  electricity system, giving shape to a fully functioning and totally connected domestic energy market.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The goals established for 2030 at European level determine the challenges and issues that Red Eléctrica will have  to overcome over the coming years. We are in a stage of transition towards a more dynamic electricity system,  characterized by the increasing active role that consumers will play and the more and more important role of new  factors such as flexible generation, energy storage, the development of supranational grids and the mass adoption  of electrical vehicles.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The grid of the 21st century must be flexible, capable of conforming to the changing needs of the system,  bidirectional, intensive and safe in the use of infrastructures, a grid that can be operated and protected safely and  easily. This grid must be fed with relevant, real-time information, satisfy energy demands, while optimizing the  needs for new investments and safely integrate renewable energies. It must facilitate the creation of new business  opportunities, be environmentally friendly and, very importantly, the tool that drives the development of  electricity markets.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Thanks to our vast know-how in the management of networks, both within the Spanish mainland and in non- mainland activities, our proven track record in the management of fiber optic networks and international  electricity transmission businesses, REE is ready to take on these challenges.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The strategic plan that we are presenting today for the 2014-2019 period rests on the core of our business, which  is the management of power transmission grids. Our line of action will be an efficient management of the TSO and  the fiber optic networks, ensuring solid growth in consolidated activities.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Our mission is focused on the achievement of sustainable development. This will entail promotion of a more  efficient electricity system, focusing on ensuring the economic sustainability of the company in the mid and long- term and on the promotion of socially responsible relationships with the value chain, paying special attention to  shareholders, customers and suppliers.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Red Eléctrica cannot disregard the environment in which it operates, and must build quality ties with the different  stakeholders that integrate it, developing our relationship with society that aims to generate shared value, with a  high commitment to the protection and preservation of the natural environment, ensuring the preservation of  biodiversity and fighting against climate change.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Another key line of growth for the company will be enabled by new activities such as the investments in storage  activities in the islands, and the international investment in electricity transmission activities. All this will require  an investment of about €1 billion.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: For the development of this function, it is essential to have a transparent, stable and predictable regulatory  framework. In this regard, Royal Decree 1047/2013 was approved in December, 2013, establishing a new  methodology for the calculation of the remuneration for the electricity transmission activity. This is a transparent,  stable and predictable, and helps regulatory stability to our business, establishing mechanisms to ensure the  sustainability of the system and providing incentives to improve efficiency.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Keep in mind that a hypothetical scenario was defined for this calculation entailing an investment of €600  million, including the incentive for availability and assuming that the first year of the first regulatory period will  be 2015. Also, the projections include the remuneration for Gas Natural and Fenosa's transmission assets. The  accuracy of the projections will depend on the actual investment that is carried out and  on the company's  operational performance which results in the availability incentive.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Therefore, in 2015, we see that the tariff finally defined for the year 2015, approved by order IET/2444/2014 of  the 26th of December determining the electrical power and energy access tools has established €1.675 billion as  the remuneration for Red Eléctrica; €1.654 billion of which correspond to the remuneration for the use of  transmission infrastructures and €21 million to the availability incentive. This figure is co nsistent with the €1.685  billion figure defined in the projections, reflecting the effects of Gas Natural and Unión Fenosa and, therefore, we  can affirm that this tariff is reasonably in line with estimate calculations.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Once the regulatory framework is almost closed, we are now awaiting the approval of the new infrastructure plan  2015-2020, which is being developed. A draft of which is available on the Ministry of Industry's website. This new  plan will envisage investments' commission for an amount of €4.4 billion linked mainly to key requirements such  as network grid reinforcement; reinforcement of international connections with France and Portugal; new  interconnections between mainland Spain and non-mainland subsystems and between the mainland and Ceuta;  network reinforcement in the islands, mainly the Canaries; and destined to evacuate wind generation; as well as  the need to connect power storage installations.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We would like to point out that the ENTSO-E methodology applied in the definition of the plan based on the  cost/profit analysis in the development of the transmission work allows achieving one of our key objectives to  ensure that investments help reduce system costs and secure the consumer's supply guarantee. All this with  sustainable integration of the facilities in territory.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So here key actions – achievement of this goal include the reinforcement of the interconnections in the northeast  axis, the Basque Country-Navarra link, and the phase-shifting transformer in Arkale. European Council has  stressed that the importance of developing a fully functional and totally connected internal energy  structure  highlighting this is essential to mobilize all means required to achieve the minimum 10% goal of the installed  generation capacity through international interconnections as a matter of urgency, raising the goal to 15% by  2030.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Another objective linked to energy efficiency is flashing system costs in order to ensure that the most efficient  generation can be evacuated and, finally, increasing the flexibility of electricity supply process to efficiently  integrate user behavior.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Also, among the actions or nine mainland systems is worth mentioning: the interconnection between islands,  which improves the reliability of electricity systems due to the possibilities for mutual support should they be  enabled in the event of a lack of capability in one of them.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The plan envisages interconnections between Fuerteventura-Lanzarote, Tenerife-La Gomera, Mallorca-Ibiza,  which will be the world's longest and deepest alternating current undersea link, which will also yield  environmental advantages and cost reduction benefits for the electrical system of Mallorca-Majorca and Ibiza- Formentera. This plan also aims to improve the network grid into archipelagos, fostering competition on the  islands' generation market to seek integration of renewable energies and the progressive replacement of fuel with  renewable sources and reduction in system costs mainly.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We will now analyze another one of the fundamental pillars on which our strategy is built: the new tools at  disposal of Red Eléctrica as the system operator, island storage. Now, the electricity system in the Canary Islands  is characterized by certain particularities that need to be overcome. It's actually integrated by six electrically  isolated subsystems and they're small if you compare them to the mainland network because it's also [ph] then  (32:14) level of difficulty to make some interconnections between the islands.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Now, that factor makes it harder to take full advantage of the synergies that electricity interconnections enable,  epitomized by a greater stability of the system. It also results in increase in generation related costs due to the  complexity when performing joint optimization of the system to guarantee service quality.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Also, a strategy has been devised for the integration of renewable energies, which are highly intermittent and hard  to predict in these systems and there are no known references, posing additional challenges in the management of  the required balance between generation and consumption. For all of those reasons, promoting the increase in the  power storage infrastructure for tool of the service of the systems operation, mainly in pumping, although keeping  in mind other future technologies, will allow to guarantee a greater level of integration of renewable energies.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: And at the same time, it will make electricity system more secure. The deployment of storage installations will  represent a huge leap forward in the carbon emission cutting process in the Canary Islands. Currently, only 8% of  demand is covered with zero emission technologies, compared to 64.8% in the Spanish mainland.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Since 2007, a series of initiatives have been promoted to consider pumping installations as a system operation  tool that will help to integrate renewable energy sources in isolated systems. Now in this context, the planning in  electricity and gas sectors 2008 to 2016 paper that was published in May 2008 already include an estimate of  benchmark power values that storage systems should yield in the reversible plants that need to be built in the  Canary Islands.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Subsequently, in October 2009, the Council of Ministers approved the comprehensive strategy for the Canary  Islands region. That detailed the measures to be adopted to reduce their energy dependence and foster the  penetration of renewable energies in the islands.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: In March 2013, the law on the assurance of supply and increase of competition in island and non-mainland  electricity systems was passed. Now, that established that the ultimate purpose of pumping stations will be the  adequate management of these systems and assigns exclusive property rights over them to the systems operator in  Red Eléctrica de España.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Furthermore, this proposal indicates that Red Eléctrica will have to purchase existing installations in April 2,  2014. Through ministerial order, Red Eléctrica was commissioned to execute the 200-megawatt Chira-Soria  reversible hydroelectric plant in the greater Canary Island. Finally, Endesa and Red Eléctrica reached an  agreement on the transfer of the concession over the hydroelectric plant detailing the terms of the transfer of  operating management duties. Now, that agreement entailed a payment of €11.2 million as a transfer fee, covering  all the expenses incurred by Endesa between 2011 and to -date.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The Chira-Soria project includes a 25-year concession with a possible extension to 50 years over the waters on the  Chira and Soria reservoirs. The project also envisages the construction of a reversible pumping station and the  connection with the Santa Águeda substation through a 220 -kilowatt power line. The project's total investment  could amount to around €300 million.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: It's absolutely essential on this point to indicate to you that Island storage infrastructure is a tool of the system  operator, which acts exclusively as the owner of these pumping stations in order to go into the supply and  integration of renewable sources received in regulated remuneration exchange. Therefore, Red Eléctrica does not  act as a conventional electricity generator in this case. I want to make that absolutely clear. It is at the heart of Red  Eléctrica's functions.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Besides storage, there are other activities that allow the system operator to manage the system in efficient and  secure manner. As mentioned at the beginning of this presentation, in 2014, Red Eléctrica started to arrange and  manage the new auction system to assign the interruptibility service in a competitive and efficient manner. As you  already know, interruptibility is a demand management tool. It provides flexibility and a quick response for  the  operation of the system in situations of imbalance between generation demand. This service is activated in  response to a power reduction command instructed by the company as the system operator, to consumers that are  supplied with the service.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Also, since last March 2014, Red Eléctrica has started posting on its website information on the hourly prices of  the unit electricity costs to be applied to the electricity bill of consumers with a contracted capacity of less than 10  kilowatts, and who fall under the small consumer voluntary price scheme. The acronym for that scheme is SCVP.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: As you know, this scheme replaces the previous Last Resort Tariff from its independent and usual position when  electric informs consumers about the process and does so in absolutely transparent manner by offering a tool  through which each system will be able to manage his or her electricity consumption in a more efficient manner.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Finally, it's important to mention that in 2014, too, a decisive step was taken towards a single European electricity  market with the rollout to simultaneous and synchronized operations, which seek to couple the daily electricity  market for Southwest and Northwest Europe. These services are known as cross-border energy mix services or  balancing services. And last June, and Red Eléctrica, REN and RTE successfully launched the cross-border energy  mix services in the interconnection between Spain and France and the interconnection between them and  Portugal.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: This new cross-border energy service between TSOs will contribute to optimizing the use of the exchange  capability that may have been rendered idle after the adjustments in the trade exchange programs in the intraday  market, to greater coordination of interconnected electricity systems and to a greater level of competition in the  balancing markets. And this will also entail a more efficient use of the balancing resources and will send out the  most competitive and efficient economic signals both in the balancing markets and in price deviations. It will  also  enable integration of renewable energies in the electricity system. And the goal for the future is establish these  cross-border services with the United Kingdom.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Just recently one of the new interconnection has just been inaugurated and it will mean that there will be no  longer in the future that high percentage of saturation in the existing interconnection. So that will lead us to more  competition, more competitiveness in this integrated market. Also, new activities linked to developing smart grid  will be promoted. All of these activities require a remuneration framework that is adequate for system operation.  And therefore, after the progress made in 2013 and 2014, we will continue to work to finally achieve this.

texts.speaker: José Folgado Blanco
texts.profession: Executive Chairman & Chief Executive Officer

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Our main priority areas are efficiency in engineering and construction processes for the facilities by optimizing  their design, managing supplies, meeting new demands in terms of quality, and looking for efficiencies throughout  the entire process. texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: To conclude my presentation, I would like to briefly reflect on the company's challenges vis-à-vis the 2030  horizon. The Paris Agreement confirmed this approach. In  late 2016, a new package of measures was presented, the winter package, with proposals concerning internal  market rules on the annuity side of the electricity market, the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators, the  governance of the current energy union renewables, and energy efficiency.

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: A shifting of the set of commitments assumed in an international and European label requires Spain to establish,  for the first time, a regulatory framework with a force of law that reflects the medium and long-term targets for  reducing greenhouse gases. This framework will provide a solid legal backing for energy planning that facilitates  the achievement of these goals. In 2017, a committee of experts was set up to prepare a report on the different  scenarios of energy transition, ensuring the competitiveness of the economy, economic growth, job creation, and  environmental sustainability. The electricity system will play a key role in energy transition. Cutting our  dependence on fossil fuels will prompt the electrification of demand, which must be accompanied by the  developing of emission-free power generation storage and the active management of demand. Electricity  networks will play a key role in this new context.

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Red Eléctrica will play a central role in the energy transition in Spain. The increase of our international  interconnection level will play a critical role. Doubled submarine and underground link will  be direct current and will have a transmission capacity of 2 times 1,000 megawatts. This project is currently in the  consultation phase. Operation is expected to begin between 2014 and 2025. In addition, to reach an  interconnection level of approximately 8,000 megawatts to further new projects will be required crossing the  Pyrenees.

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: In terms of interconnections both in the Canaries and Balearic Islands, new links will be necessary to reduce  variable costs of generation and ensure supply in isolated systems interconnections in combination with a storage  demand management digitalization and automation will facilitate this energy transition. Progress will only be  possible with the support of a solid network that is sufficiently meshed, properly interconnected, and equipped  with the appropriate management mechanisms. This will require investments in the transmission rate until 2030,  greater than the historical average of the past 15 years.

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: This stability as the suitable remuneration of the electricity networks are essential for the correct undertaking of  heavily capital-intensive activities. To accelerate the transition to clean energy  and maintain competitiveness in Spain, electricity rates should be a clear indication of price efficiency  compatibility between the changing energy model.

texts.speaker: Juan Lasala Bernad

texts.text: No serious company nowadays, I think, and I'd imagine most of you would agree with me, can even think of  coming up with a strategy plan that doesn't include technology and sustainability. It mainstreams everything we do in this company, from our  commitments up until 2030, which are in part reflected in the strategy plan to get 100% green finances, then  specific commitments to bringing more women and more diversity into our management teams and our board,  and wanting to be 100% circular company by 2030.

texts.speaker: María Teresa Quirós Álvarez
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Although there are some things that aren't completely financial, we got a new record in wind generation last year  with 43.2% of the mainland electricity generation mix being generated by wind power and 40% of all the electricity  generation came from renewables compared against 34% the previous year. We've already said when we  presented the results in June, but I think I might as well repeat that in the first six months of 2018, Red Eléctrica,  along with other operators and TSOs from various European countries, have worked on the implementation of the  Continuous Intraday Market, which works across all of Europe.

texts.speaker: María Teresa Quirós Álvarez
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: 2018 has been a year of important progress in the area of sustainability as well. In November, the board, at the  proposal of its chairman, established a Sustainability Committee in response to the strategic nature of  sustainability for the group. We've also signed up to the commitment to sustainable mobility in 2018, as I said.  And Red Eléctrica once again has been distinguished by the prestigious Dow Jones Sustainability Index.

texts.speaker: María Teresa Quirós Álvarez
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: And there's another couple of things I wanted to mention before finishing. First of all, Red Eléctrica has reduced  the cost of our syndicated loan, and that's because of the improvement we have in our ESG metrics, which  brought down the cost of the syndicated loan. And we are the very first company to come up with a multi-currency  syndicated loan using blockchain technology, €150 million, and that's backed by three banks, which I'd like to  thank for moving into this kind of innovation with us.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: As I was saying, although 2019 has not yet come to a close, we are already achieving our targets up to 2018, and  very close to being able to confirm to you that we will very probably reach all of the targets we committed to the  market for the period 2014-2019. We have made investments totaling €3.45 billion on the transmission grid,  telecoms, energy storage, as well as investments internationally. We've also committed investments for €1.46  billion under the agreement with Bow Power, which was mentioned to you just a little earlier. That line in Northern  Peru was another international investment, as well as the implementation and the execution of the Hispasat  transaction announced recently. I'll give you further details on that transaction in a moment.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Let me now comment on the key elements for the development of the 2018-2022 strategic plan, as you already  heard briefly from our Chairman. To achieve our long-term targets and our commitment to sustainable  development, we will have to take a series of steps that I can summarize in the following strategic plans, the four  of them. The first one, perhaps the most important one, to promote energy transition; secondly, to become the  operator of preference in relation to telecommunications infrastructures; thirdly, to unlock the value of our core  skills through international investments; at the same time, this is the fourth one, while preserving operating  efficiency and financial discipline.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Maximizing the integration of renewable energies within the Spanish electricity system is quite obviously one of  the company's key tasks. This will require investment on the transmission grid an average of €575 million per  year. That's almost 40% higher than the investment recorded in the previous strategic plan 2014-2017.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: In addition, Red Eléctrica will also allocate a significant portion of that investment to achieving an increased  interconnection capacity both international and the very subsystems of the Spanish electricity system. You also  heard that from the Chairman. This increased interconnect capacity will enable us to confront the greater  variability renewable generation. We minimize waste in the context of increased green generation capacity and  reduce the need for any back-up generation facility [indiscernible] (36:10) energy market in Europe which is and  will be a key tool for the operations of the electricity system.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Another key element in the stabilization optimization of the grid in a system of higher renewables present  penetration will be storage and that is why part of the investment to be made by Red Eléctrica will be allocated to  the hydraulic pumping stations in the Canary Islands. These storage projects will serve as operating tools to  ensure supply, to improve the security of the system, and also to optimize the integration of renewables on the  islands.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: We are committed to ensuring the security and the quality of the existing supply by maximizing integrated  renewables. And to do so, we will probably invest more than €3.2 billion that can be broken down mainly into €2.9  billion [indiscernible] (36:54) to the transmission grid, €200 million for storage in the Canary Islands, and €50  million for systems operation, another €50 million in miscellaneous areas, probably the technology that was  explained by the Chairman.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Just before regulation now. Regulation must be a facilitating element, taking us towards the energy transition  offering high visibility and aiming for stability. The next regulatory period, as Teresa said just earlier, begins on the  1st of January 2020 and run for six years until 2025, as you're aware. The financial remuneration rate proposed  by that draft bill submitted to the Council of Ministers in Spain is a nominal 5.58% before tax. Now, this proposed  rate is in line with the proposal made by the CNMC in its report of 30th of October last year.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Now, of course, instead of 6.5%, it will be – this year, it will be 6% in 2020. And, of course, by the time we get to  2021-2022, it will be down to 5.58% percent. That's what we've estimated. In addition, let me remind you that the  current regulatory framework offers incentive based on the efficiency and the availability of the transmission grid.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Still, on regulatory matters, I should also mention that one critical aspect for energy transition will be the  development of networks while maintaining an added cost for the consumer. Measures to minimize the cost of the  system could include allowing the extension of the useful life of the installations, providing essential services in  this regard, and we're talking about the whole electricity sector.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: We consider that [ph] probably (00:41:55) what the figures an adequate return on investment will be that, which  exceeds the cost of capital by at least 100 basis points. Red Eléctrica's intention is to remain for the long term in  countries with low risk and stable regulatory frameworks. And thus, over the coming years, the company will  consolidate its position in the countries in which it's already operating, Chile and Peru, whilst analyzing investment  possibilities in countries elsewhere such as the United States and Brazil, both through greenfield and brownfield  projects.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: Digitalization has become a core driver for process optimization and is an indispensable foundation for improving  the efficiency of the company's regular business. Thus, consolidating digital technology in the group's business  areas will expand our company's transformative vision, the digitization to our operating processes, thereby  maximizing benefits. Additionally, to underpin the company's strategy, we intend to maintain strict financial  discipline during the period with a target average net debt-to-EBITDA ratio for the period of around 4 times,  keeping our funds from operations or FFO-to-debt levels at above 17%. Sound financial management, optimizing  the cost of borrowing and incorporating ESG criteria into the way we finance our activities will be key to success  in rolling out our strategy plan.

texts.speaker: Juan Francisco Lasala Bernad
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Red Eléctrica Corp. SA
texts.text: So, finally, I wanted to show you our commitments in the Red Eléctrica Group for 2018 to 2022. I'd like to point out  that our commitment to energy transition is a commitment sustained over time, aiming to create value for all of our  stakeholders. Thus, the company's actions will be underpinned by five elements. Total investment in 2018 to 2022  period, including acquisitions we've already mentioned will reach approximately €6 billion. Around 50% of this  figure will be allocated to investment for the transmission grid and storage in Spain, promoting the energy  transition. The average EBITDA margin will be more than 76%, maintaining a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of around  4 times. Net profit will show a compound annual growth rate of over 1% in the 2018 to 2022 period. And we will  maintain a shareholder remuneration of €1.05 per share in 2019 with the dividends paid out in that year and at  least €1 per share in the 2020 to 2022 period.

Repsol sold a total 11.6% stake in YPF in the market, 3.8% through direct sales and  7.7% through an IPO, including the greenshoe, making great progress towards achieving Repsol’s  objective of diversifying its portfolio. Due to current accounting rules, we are booking, after the  previously described operations, €355 million as reserves. Taking into account that the Petersen  Group announced last week that it will exercise its 10% coal option, Repsol’s stake in YPF will be  58.2%. We are now ready to initiate the last stage of the plan, the placement of a stake of YPF  among retail Argentinean investors.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Now going into further detail on the operational highlights of the quarter, and starting with the  upstream business. In the upstream business, and as part of our exploratory drilling campaign, we  are currently drilling five exploratory wells, two in the Brazilian Santos 44 block, Itaboraí and  Tingua, one in Campos 33 block, Gavea, one in Bolivia, Sararenda, and one in the U.S. onshore,  Garden Island Bay 1.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Regarding new exploratory acreage, we want to highlight the farm-in into 164 blocks at Alaska  prolific North Slope that we announced in March. [audio disturbance] (9:03) very low-risk portfolio  and extensions of fields within the Colville High and a group of high-potential exploration prospects  in a basin that together sum up a potential of almost a billion barrels on a risk basis. The project  represents an excellent opportunity for accessing the onshore exploration blocks adjacent to  Alaska, [ph] again (9:35) North Slope fields. These blocks, governed by the laws of the state of  Alaska, are close to open infrastructures with surplus capacity.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: In LNG, the improvement of marketing conditions, mainly in our North America operations, is  particularly worth mentioning. Marketing activities in North America benefited from low winter  temperatures, thereby increasing the volume sold. Sales growth was not merely due to harsh  weather, but also due to increasing our capacity for supplying the plant, thanks to the agreement  with Qatargas. Seven Q-Max from Qatar were delivered during the quarter. This agreement made it  possible to meet supply in the area.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Meanwhile, the marketing activities of Peru LNG benefited from the agreement executed with  KOGAS supplying eight vessels to Korea during the quarter.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Lastly, on 12th March, ENARSA announced the outcome of the tender process for supplying LNG  to the Argentinean Bahía Blanca terminal between May and October 2011. Repsol has been  awarded nine out of the 25 shipments put out to tender, with Gas Natural Fenosa to deliver another  seven shipments.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Moving into downstream, our business obtained this quarter an integrated margin of $5 per barrel,  still ranking solid among the peer group and confirming once again the resilience of the business. In  refining, better diesel and heavy-light oil spreads increased margin, although this impact was offset  by higher oil prices, placing margins at the same level as in the first quarter 2010.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Prices at the pump station increased on a year-on-year basis, 11% in dollar terms both for gasoline  and diesel. The government of Argentina, however, enacted resolution 46/2011 that allowed new  price increases, which were already implemented at the beginning of April.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Let me elaborate on the progress achieved in relation to non-conventional resources. In tight gas,  following the agreement with the mining company Vale in 2011, plans are under way for repair work  and drilling operation at the [ph] Lahas (12:57) formation to ensure that the 1.6 million cubic meters  per day production will be available as of 2015.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Regarding shale oil and gas, I would like to remind you that exploration work conducted in 2010  confirmed the great potential of the Vaca Muerta basin, very similar to the Bakken and Eagle Ford  formations. As part of these exploration activities, YPF announced last Tuesday a new shale oil  discovery in the Vaca Muerta formation. The preliminary results of the first six vertical wells  indicated initial flows of 200 up to 560 barrels of oil equivalent per day that, along with geological  and seismic studies done, allows estimated 150 million of technically recoverable oil equivalent in  this area.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: In light of these results, YPF will begin a pilot development in an area of 25 square kilometers and  the appraisal of another 200 square kilometers. 17 new wells will be drilled over the remaining part  of the year, and 14 existing wells will be fractured, thereby launching the first massive development  of oil from a non-conventional reservoir in the world outside North America. Lastly, negotiations with  the province of Mendoza made it possible to extend the concessions of YPF’s 16 blocks in this  region. We’re also pursuing negotiations with other provinces to extend the terms of the permanent  concessions.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: The variation in these quarters is mainly the result of the following factors: The 13% increase in oil  realization prices and 15% in gas, net of royalties on a year-on-year basis, had a positive impact of  €153 million. The decrease in production volumes of 7%, mainly in oil, had a negative impact of  €171 million. Lower exploration expenses in the quarter versus the same quarter last year when the  depreciation offset was accrued, had a positive impact of €25 million. Lastly, lower depreciation  charges, as a result of lower production volumes, had a positive impact of €16 million. Other minor  items explain the remaining differences.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Moving to LNG, adjusted operating income in first quarter 2011 was €115 million versus €34 million  posted in the same quarter last year. The increase between the periods is due to higher volumes,  mainly because of the start-up of the Peru LNG in June 2010, higher LNG marketing margins, and  the improved performance of the Canaport project. In the downstream business, adjusted CCS  operating income was €216 million, 16% up year on year. Year-on-year earnings growth is mainly  due to the recovery of the chemical business.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: By business segment, in the refining business, the slight increase in distillate volumes in Spain, as  well as greater production optimization, had a positive impact of €11 million on this division’s  operating income. The ongoing positive performance of the marketing business was achieved  thanks to strong margins that were able to offset lower sales volumes. Chemical activities with  higher volumes and margins had a positive impact of €38 million. Lastly, the variations in oil  activities such as LPG trading and transport, as well as other minor items, explain the remaining  difference.       corrected transcript

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Moving on to YPF, adjusted operating income was €392 million in the first quarter of 2011, 7%  lower than the €420 million recorded in first quarter 2010. Higher dollar-denominated fuel prices in  the domestic market had a positive impact of €151 million. The increase in the revenues from  exports from products sold domestically but linked to international prices had a positive impact of  €104 million. The drop in the oil production and in refinery process led to an increase in oil and oil  product purchases to meet growing demand. On top of this, the mandatory use of biofuels as of  March 2010 made it necessary to increase the purchases of these products. The net impact of all  the above-mentioned was €95 million decrease in operating income.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: In gas, better prices in the industrial sector, as well as the slight increase in shares to domestic  markets, had a positive impact of €15 million. Higher operating costs had a negative impact of €122  million. Other factors, mainly not having been entitled to the Petróleo Plus incentive, explain the  other variations. The production in this quarter was 4.7% lower than in the same quarter last year,  mainly because of the impact of December’s strikes and the natural field decline. Gas production  fell 5.9% compared to the 3.7% drop in oil output. In Gas Natural Fenosa, a €249 million adjusted  operating income in first quarter 2011 was 2.7% lower than the €266 million reported in the same  quarter a year ago.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: Let us move now into the results. Please remember that all the numbers are ex-YPF and ex- Repsol YPF gas, the  LPG division which was expropriated as well. This quarter we released CCS adjusted net income of €474 million,  4% higher year-on-year and a CCS adjusted operating income of €1.1 billion, 8% higher than in the same quarter  last year. These results have improved also in relation to the previous quarter.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: The good results have been driven by the performance of our upstream and LNG divisions. In upstream, the  adjusted operating income was €659 million, 35% higher than the same period last year. The normalization of the  activity in Libya, a better production output in the Gulf of Mexico and the higher realization prices have been the  main reasons behind this improvement.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: Now with the operations back into normal conditions and the new projects starting as scheduled this year, we  expect this quarter's good results to start a steady increasing contribution of our upstream division to the  performance of the company. In the LNG division, better margins resulted in an adjusted operating income of  €158 million, 37% better than during the same period last year. The market opportunities have been optimized  again this quarter, and we will keep on doing so with the non-contracted volumes. In the downstream business,  the CSS adjusted operating income was €82 million, 61% lower than the first quarter of 2011. The results were  mainly affected by the negative effect of the deterioration of the chemicals environment and the marketing  volumes.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: All the volumes are dedicated to supply the Bolivian government export agreements with Brazil and Argentina.  Prices for the second quarter on both contracts will be US$926 per million Btu and US$11.08 per million Btu,  respectively. The main contracts for the construction of the second phase which will add up to 6 million cubic  meters per day to the production of the field have already been signed. The second phase will take around 19  months to be commissioned and once it's fully operational the total processing capacity of the plant will be up 15  million cubic meters per day.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: In Peru, our Kinteroni project carries on as planned as we expected to reach first gas early during the last quarter  of 2012, with a gross production 5 million cubic meters plus associated liquids.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: We have already signed the lease of the second FPSO, Cidade de Ilhabela, through the company SBM Offshore.  Such FPSO will be dedicated to produce the Northern part of the field, and its production is expected to start in  2015.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: Now, let us review the status of the principal exploratory activity. As announced in our previous results  presentation, we will mainly focus on the Pão de Açucar discovery in the Campos 33 basin after Sapinhoá and  Carioca. We expect to start the appraisal work later in 2012. In Alaska, we have finished the drilling campaign  with a total of two wells drilled, both wells Kachemach and Qugruk 4 found oil-bearing sands, but initial delays  and the early end of the winter season have not allowed any further tests.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: The second well, Mercury-2, found a thick good quality reservoir section in the Cretaceous, but water bearing. Our  wells in Cuba and Guyana are progressing in depth, and we are expecting to have results by the end of this month  and the beginning of the first quarter respectively – of the third quarter, respectively.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: Our seismic campaigns in Portugal, Indonesia and Alaska are already completed. The remaining appreciation  activity for the year will be concentrated in the U.S. and Algeria. We continue to be very active with our acreage  acquisition with six new concessions awarded in Norway, four in the Norway Sea and two of them in the Baron  Sea with Repsol as operator in one of them.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: We also have three new licenses in the West Siberia area through Eurotek, our 100% owned subsidiary, all of them  in the Ural-Volga basin. On LNG Peru LNG delivered its first cargo to the Mantinea plant in Mexico with the first  ship arriving in March. Deliveries are expected to ramp up over the few years while in 2012, they will take at the  most 25% of the Peru LNG annual volumes.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: In relation with the profile for next year, 335,000 barrels per day, our – we keep with our expectation. I think that  along the year, we'll have a small ramp up in Libya, but also we'll have Margarita and Kinteroni helping the  production to go upwards a little. And in relation with CapEx ex YPF, it's going to be €4 billion if you include Gas  Natural. Without Gas Natural, it would be €3.5 billion. Okay, Theepan?

texts.profession: Analyst, Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
