And just related to that as well, do  you have any idea on timing of the tribunal in Argentina to decide the value of YPF and just in terms of your  balance sheet, could you just give an update of how much cash you have access to, from the Repsol Sinopec  subsidiary in Brazil? And then just a final question, going back to refining rhythm and just struggling a bit with  the numbers over here. Your Spanish refining margin was up $0.90 year-over-year, you said on top of that you've  got $1.70 of improvement from the refinery upgrade. So when you look at that on 50 million barrels of production  in the quarter, it would imply an EBIT increase of around €100 million, whereas on a CCS basis, your refining  Miguel Martínez San Martín  Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA  A Okay. Well in relation with the first one, spinning the situation with YPF, we have thought of it, but we haven't  taken any decision. Basically if at a given moment, we will decide, we'll let you know. The second one refers, sorry,  can you repeat the second one?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: No idea about the timing. In relation with the cash of Brazil, we have an agreement with the partner. So each one  takes his percentage of the free cash of Repsol Sinopec Brazil. So we have rights to the 60% of the liquidity of the  company. And in relation with the refining, you have to take into account that all we talk about is gross figure,  then you have to include the extra depreciation and some extra fixed costs. And on top of that, also last year, we  have an income from the transaction with CO2. So the combination of all these three factors are the ones that  probably distort your figure, Anish, okay?

file: REP - Q1 2013 Earnings Call 9May2013 700 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 09-May-13.pdf

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Thanks, Ángel, and thank you all for attending this conference on our first quarter results. This quarter, we  released a CCS adjusted net income of €676 million, 40% (sic) [47%] (01:31) higher year-on-year, and a CCS  adjusted operating income of €1.3 billion, 22% higher than the same quarter last year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Before we focus on our earnings performance, I would like to highlight the main events of the quarter. First, the  sale of our LNG division we announced earlier this year. We signed an agreement with Shell to sell all of the assets  and operations related to our LNG business outside U.S. and Canada for an enterprise value of US$6.7 billion.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The sale includes a minority stake in Atlantic LNG, Peru LNG and Bahia de Bizkaia Electricidad, as well as the  LNG sale contracts and time charters with their associated loans and debt. The deal strengthens the company  balance sheet and financial position.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Third, in the Upstream business and regarding our exploratory drilling campaign, seven out of the nine wells  drilled during the first quarter 2013 have found hydrocarbons. In Alaska, in the North Slope, we recently  announced three new good-quality hydrocarbon discoveries. The Qugruk-1 and Qugruk-6 wells produced two oil  shows with encouraging results during production tests.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Qugruk-3 well, hydrocarbons were identified at multiple levels. Exploration and assessment and eventually,  start-up development will continue next winter. In Russia, in West Siberia, wells Gabi-1 and Gabi-3 have found  hydrocarbons gas with an oil ring at two different levels. Gabi-3 is testing productivity right now.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Brazil, in Block BM-S-50, Petrobras has already reported the presence of oil in Sagitario. And finally in Algeria,  in Block Sud-Est Illizi, a significant gas discovery assures the commercial development of this block where we  previously announced a further discovery back in November 2012. Further test will be performed to determine the  commercial possibilities of these discoveries.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Production output was 360,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, 11% higher than in the first quarter 2012, since 5  out of 10 key growth projects of the strategic plan 2012-2016 have come on stream, together with better volumes  from Trinidad & Tobago. We are confident that we will achieve the 10% average growth targeted for 2013.  Incremental production will come from the ramp-up of Mid-Continent in the U.S. and Sapinhoa in Brazil and the  start-up of Phase 2 of Margarita in Bolivia.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: On the other hand, Kinteroni is already technically prepared to come onstream, but the delay is mainly due to the  negotiation with the final contractual arrangements that we completed with the Camisea partnership, and  Trinidad will undergo planned maintenance. The increased production volumes had a positive impact of €72  million. Repsol crude realization prices remained flat despite the weaker performance of Brent prices in  comparison with first quarter 2012, while gas realization prices increased by 26%, having a positive effect of €43  million.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving to LNG, adjusted operating income in first quarter 2013 was €311 million versus €158 million posted in  the same quarter last year. We achieved a very positive operating profit of €129 million from the North American  assets that will remain in our portfolio due to exceptionally extreme cold temperature in Northeast Coast of North  America. The 97% increase between the periods is due also to higher volumes and better marketing margins in the  rest of the businesses.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Regarding our Downstream, we have remained profitable even though the market environment was tough during  the quarter, showing the resiliency and efficiency of our integrated operations. Adjusted CCS operating income  was €183 million, 123% up year-on-year. Better margins in the refining business, improvement of the chemical  division, and better LPG results explain the year-on-year earnings growth, while the marketing division continues  to suffer from the weakness in the Spanish environment.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The group's net financial debt at the end of first quarter 2013, excluding Gas Natural Fenosa, amounted to €3.9  billion, approximately €560 million lower than at year-end 2012. When the LNG sale is concluded, net financial  debt will decrease by around €2.2 billion. The net debt plus preference shares over capital employed ratio,  excluding Gas Nat, was 19.1%.

texts.speaker: Thomas Y. Adolff
texts.profession: Analyst, Credit Suisse Securities (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: And then just on Upstream, production was decent, 360 kboed. Let's say Kinteroni doesn't contribute this year,  are you still confident on the 10% year-on-year target? Or in other words, can you talk about contingencies? And  finally, just staying also in Upstream, when you look at these seven discoveries with at least encouraging signs, do  you feel you would have met your annual target for net contingent resource addition? Or is it still too early to say?  Thank you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In CapEx, we keep attached to the €3.3 billion, €3.5 billion ex-Gas Nat. It stood at the first quarter was light. I  think it was €717 million or €720 million. But normally, it always happens that the last quarter is the one that gets  more loaded. And it's always the first one, the one that is lighter. So I keep attached to the €3.3 billion, €3.5 billion  ex-Gas Nat. Okay, Haythem?

texts.speaker: Alejandro A. Demichelis
texts.profession: Analyst, Exane BNP Paribas
texts.text: Yes. Good afternoon, gentlemen. A couple of questions from my side. Coming back to Kinteroni, should we think  that the Kinteroni royalties are completely separate from, let's say, the disposal of the Peruvian Downstream  assets and any kind of approval that you need to get for the LNG plant? That's the first question. And the second  question turns to the LNG numbers that we have seen this quarter particularly out of Canaport. Maybe you can  tell us how much do you think is sustainable from that.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Well, the first one, I mean, Kinteroni as mentioned is linked to the back half in one hand of the Peruvian LNG and  also to the guys that has to go to the local markets. And think that in the coming [ph] separate (31:04), we have  approximately eight or nine partners.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: So, it's not that easy to end up closing a deal that satisfies everyone. And this is the only thing that is taking us  more time. And for sure, it's not linked to the Downstream movement. It's only linked as mentioned to the –  which would be the gas that we have to place for the LNG and which would be the one that will go into the local  market.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And in relation with the LNG Canaport, I would say that it is not sustainable. I mean, basically, the good results  there, which has been the whole increase in the LNG division, has been due to the real cold weather they had  during January and February in the East Coast. Four cargos went to Canaport through the quarter and at that  given moment, even prices were above $20 per millimeter use. So, I would say one-off in one sense and we'll have  to see.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: What we have done is a project to reduce the limit of what the Canaport plant needs to operate, down to 10 million  cubic feet per day. And we know that this plant will be working two, three, four months at the maximum for the  year, but I don't see any possibility to repeat this. Last year, to give you an example, operating results in the assets  we kept in the U.S. were minus €8 million in the first quarter. And this year would have been €116 million. So  basically, it has been a good quarter and that's it. Okay?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean to predict is difficult especially the future. But I'll say that I think that approximately almost 50% of our  diet it's on heavy stuff. So the spread between heavy and light really affect us. Also, we have seen, especially in the  last month, that the diesel spread with Brent has reduced enormously, which implies that those refineries with no  real complexity are producing with more heavy stuff, which also implies a reduction in the spreads.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Our estimate for the whole year, I would say, we will keep attached to $5.5 per barrel more or less. Though I can  tell you that right now, there's no margin in Europe in refining. And this is due to the, more or less, spread we  have today between the fuel oil and the crude oil. But we will see. I mean as mentioned, the future is quite difficult  to predict.

texts.speaker: Bruno Silva
texts.profession: Analyst, BPI
texts.text: Yeah, okay. Just another follow-up, I forgot to mention the first time. Can you make an update or confirm whether  or not you are taking actions to sell the remaining interest in LNG, namely Canaport?

texts.speaker: Bruno Silva
texts.profession: Analyst, BPI
texts.text: I was asking if you are taking any actions or if there is any process ongoing for the divestment from the remaining  assets in the LNG unit?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: But several things are clear. I think that we were, last year, at the worst scenario for the plants with an average of  $2.4 per million Btu. It was sure that no LNG was possibly coming to North America. This situation will change  one way or the other. I mean, first, if the U.S. allowed exports of all the gas they are producing, for sure prices will  go up. If they don't, I'm sure that all the fleets will start shifting into gas, their trucks. So this also will imply a  higher price.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And also, as looking to the issue from the other side, from the LNG producers, more and more LNG will come to  the sea in the following months and years. So at the given moment, I think that Canaport will be in a better  situation than the one we have today. Right now, what we are doing is having contingent plans to analyze which  are our options and how operationally we can reduce that short term, okay?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: So I mean, in a market that is being reduced 10% after 10%, right now, we are simply, somehow, trying to put the  margins where they were last year. I think that by the beginning of the year, there was an extra taxation for the  biofuels. And we are absorbing this tax increase, though we expect to, little by little, to capture it back. But there's  no other thing to do. I mean, we are not losing market quota. So, it's the whole market the one that is falling.

texts.speaker: Anish Kapadia
texts.profession: Analyst, Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
texts.text: Hi. Good afternoon. I have three questions. Firstly, on the Mississippi Lime, we've seen SandRidge just recently  cut back the number of rigs being run to 25 from over 30, given its focus on liquidity. So I think they're running –  they're intending to drill less than 500 wells this year. Just wondering what this means for your medium-term  Mississippi Lime production targets as I think your original plan was to drill something like 1,000 wells next year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean, we'll have to look at it. For this year, there's particularly no valuation on our figures. And what I think is  important is that I think that SandRidge is a very good operational company. In fact, some of the initial estimates  we did in our investment plan like the cost per well, which will include $3.6 million there drilling at almost $3  million per well. And I think that part of the reason why we entered with them was the carbonates.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Okay. Sorry. I understood it was for the whole project. In Carabobo, the ramp-up will start May-June. And I mean,  we expect really small figures. I mean, we are talking that we will end up on average at 2,200 barrels per day. So  it's, I would say, quite a small one. And in Perla, there would be no production within the year. We expect to start  production in 2014, okay?

texts.speaker: Anish Kapadia
texts.profession: Analyst, Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
texts.text: One other just quick follow-up on Mississippi Lime. So where would you see – under the kind of the new plan of  drilling with 25 rigs over the next few years, where would you see production in 2016 versus your previous target  of 40,000 barrels a day?

texts.speaker: Biraj Borkhataria
texts.profession: Analyst, RBC Europe Ltd. (Broker)
texts.text: Hi, guys. Biraj Borkhataria from RBC. I had a couple of questions. First one just on the LNG disposal to Shell,  when do you expect that to close? And secondly, are you in discussions with the rating agencies regarding  potential implications if the Shell payment wasn't received by the end of 2013? Thanks.

texts.speaker: Rahim N. Karim
texts.profession: Analyst, Barclays Capital Securities Ltd.
texts.text: Hi. Good afternoon, gentlemen. Two questions, if I may. To ask the second half of Irene's question around  realizations, gas realizations are very strong in the quarter. And I understand it's probably due to Bolivia. But is  there anything else in there that we should be aware of? Or should we expect current levels of realizations to be  sustainable?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The first one, as mentioned before, I mean in realization prices, we think it's sustainable what we have achieved  this year. I think that in liquids, I comment to Irene that the disposal of Ecuador plus more U.S. and Brazil is  helping out the price in liquids. And in relation with gas, the one that moves the dial, it's Bolivia which, as a firm  rule, we are obtaining 10% of the Brent price for our gas there. So yes, I think it's sustainable.

texts.speaker: Jason S. Kenney
texts.profession: Analyst, Banco Santander SA (London Branch)
texts.text: Hi there. Thanks for taking the questions. Just a couple of data points, if I may. Can you give me the EBIT for the  North American LNG business that you're going to retain for the full year 2012? I know you mentioned the first  quarter EBIT number earlier.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And in relation with the consensus, I think that the only difference that the consensus have with us in this quarter  was our North American LNG assets. I mean, the rest of them were really accurate. And probably nobody was  expecting that we will be selling gas in the Eastern Coast $20 per million Btu. But I mean, it's up to the consensus  to approach [indiscernible] (58:32). I mean, the rest of the areas, I think that it was really accurate.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And the second one refers to also the start-up of, for example, in Sapinhoa. I mean, we have the whole cost of the  FPSO that can produce up to 120,000 barrels while we are only producing 20,000 barrels. So, extra costs come for  these reasons. It would be sustainable, but progressively coming down in a cost per barrel, I would say. And in  relation with the conversion, the answer is yes, I think we can keep the percentages of utilization we are having.

file: REP - Q1 2014 Earnings Call 8May2014 700 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 08-May-14.pdf

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: I'll now describe our operational activity during the quarter, together with the main events since our full year  results conference call. In the upstream business, as a summary, we can underline that we continue delivering our  commitments and accomplishing the targets included in our strategic plan with the startup of Kinteroni and the  connection of the second well in Sapinhoá. In April, we connected the third one. With Kinteroni onstream, seven  out of the 10 key growth projects included in our strategic plan are already onstream and we are expecting to have  [indiscernible] (03:22) gas from our Cardón project by year-end.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Exploration continues in Brazil, U.S., Libya, Kurdistan, Mauritania and Namibia. Production during the quarter  was 342,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, which means 5% less than in the first quarter of last year. On the  one hand, we increased our production year-on-year in Brazil, United States, Russia, Bolivia and Peru.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: On the other hand, there were disruptions in Libya, which costs a reduction of 24,000 barrels of oil equivalent of  average production per day, and stoppages in Trinidad and Tobago due to drilling work in the Savonette field  during January.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: As we mentioned before, Kinteroni start producing at the end of the quarter initially with an average of 20,000  barrels of oil equivalent per day in gross terms of which almost 25% are liquids. We will almost double our  production from 2016 onwards.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Other operational highlights of the quarter were the following. In Sapinhoá, we have already connected the second  and third wells and both are producing above the expectations with a gross total production of the field above  100,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day confirming its excellent productivity. We expect to connect the fourth  well by June reaching full capacity of our first FPSO.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The second is already in Brazil and we'll be producing and ramping up before year's end. The average net  contribution of Sapinhoá to Repsol's production during 2014 will be around 15,000 high-margin barrels of oil per  day.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the U.S., we continue with the development of the fields and associated production ramp-up in the  Mississippian Lime. In Venezuela, Cardón continues its development on schedule and we're expecting to be on  stream by the end of this year. We expect that this project will add 22,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day to our  production from April 2015.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving to the downstream division, first, we would like to explain that from this quarter on we include the gas &  power business within this division. Starting with refining, although margins in Europe continue to decline, our  margin indicator was $3.9 per barrel, the same as in the first quarter 2013. The utilization rate was 74% as we still  have some maintenance in January. The conversion capacity reached 97% of utilization. In chemicals, we'll reach  the breakeven point once we'll restart our Tarragona plant, which had stopped for maintenance during the fourth  quarter 2013.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving to gas and power, due to low temperatures in North America and taking advantage of the flexibility of our  Canaport facility, we managed to obtain very good results reaffirming our expectation of reaching at least  breakeven in the year. Moreover, we are increasing our trading activity in the region and capturing additional  value.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: I'll now explain our third quarter earnings performance. This quarter we have decided to modify our reporting  criteria, providing more information for each business segment. The main aspects are following. We will report  operating and net operating income per business segment. As a result, we will report corporate taxes and results  from associate companies and minority interest in every business segment. Our gas and powers business will be  reported included in the downstream business segment. Gas Natural Fenosa will be reported as an equity  investment. The financial result will be reported within corporation.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Lower crude and gas prices had a negative impact of €19 million. Increased depreciation charges had a negative  impact of €22 million, mainly because of the additional investment in the Shenzi water injection project.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving to gas and power, the increase in results of the quarter were €90 million due to different aspects. The  winter has been very cold in the Northeast Coast of North America, the same as last year. Therefore, the  Algonquin benchmark reached extraordinary high price levels during short periods of time during the quarter.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Gas Natural Fenosa, the €123 million adjusted net income in the first quarter of 2014 was 2% lower than the  €125 million reported in the same period last year, mainly because of the lower income from power generation  and distribution activities in Spain and in Latin America partially offset by better electricity commercialization  results underpinned by lower pool prices.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In corporate and other businesses segment, we had a net expense of €136 million, which is lower than the €177  million posted in the same quarter a year ago. This reduction derives mainly from the lower cost of debt, the  variations in the exchange rate, and the higher valuation of the CO2 rights.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Turning now to our financial situation, we continue maintaining the robust financial position we had at the end of  2013 enhanced by the collection of the last proceeds from the LNG disposal in January.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Our P&L performance improved compared to the same quarter of last year and we were able to offset the impact  of Libya with the results of our gas and power assets and the increasing contribution from our growth projects.

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Hi, Ángel. Thank you very much. Good afternoon, gentlemen. Thank you for the presentation and congratulations  on the agreement with Argentina. Just first question on that actually, if you could just talk a little bit about how we  should think about your prioritization in the portfolio management process now going forward, is your plan still to  use proceeds from the sales to invest in upstream assets? And also, is your sort of investment dependent on how  much you eventually sell from the bonds that you receive or do you have a sort of size in mind of any upstream  sort of acquisition, which would then be funded by either sales of the bonds or potentially sale of the gas now at  stake? A little bit about that would be helpful.

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: And then final question again on the downstream within the gas and power segment, you mentioned, Miguel, that  guidance has sort of reaffirmed the breakeven overall for the business for the next year. Should we therefore  expect – I mean, the losses in the business later on in the year obviously given the strength and the results in this  quarter or has the strength you've seen recently sort of changed your view on profitability from that business?  Thank you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In both cases with higher margins, in the wholesaling and in the network. Okay? Going to the first one. I'll have to  say that we keep [ph] attached (19:33) to what we have mentioned several times. I mean it's true that after the  expropriation of YPF and the sale of the LNG division, we need somehow to rebuild the P&L of the company and  this will imply acquisitions or – one or several acquisitions and we are looking for companies or assets.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And in relation with the third one, I mean normally we expect some losses in the second and third quarter, fourth  quarter would depend on how the weather – [ph] helped up the weather becoming (21:50) in the East Coast, and  how tense is the market in the U.S. But normally, I mean for us the initial goal was zero as a result for the gas and  power division. This quarter has been good. So perhaps we can make some profit. But originally and our objective  was zero result.

texts.speaker: Alejandro A. Demichelis
texts.profession: Analyst, Exane Ltd.
texts.text: Yes. Good afternoon. Ángel and Miguel, thank you for taking my question. Just following up to the answer about  the use of profits from the bonds and the divestment of the YPF stake. Given that there seems to – that Pemex  may be looking to dispose some of their stake, could the profit that you have taken so far be potentially used to  buy back some of those shares at some point? And maybe you can update us on how do you see the Gas Natural  stake at this moment.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with Gas Nat that I didn't comment in Haythem question, Gas Nat for us it's, first, a very good assets. It  give us optionality and this is it. I mean if at the end, the proceeds from – I mean or the – we need the Gas Natural  stake to make an acquisition that really generates value. In the upstream division, we'll go for it but right now the  situation is quite stable. We are happy with the asset. I think that the Gas Nat truly is a company that is very well- managed and it's in the right direction. So we are happy with the asset and only if we see something that really  deserves a try in our side in the upstream level, we will go for it. Okay, Alejandro?

texts.speaker: Jon Rigby
texts.profession: Analyst, UBS Ltd. (Broker)
texts.text: Hi. Thanks, Ángel. Hi, Miguel. Two questions please. Can you just go in a little bit more detail about the  mechanics of your gas and power business now with the kind of port operation obviously and you've alluded to  some increased trading opportunities. So I guess now we can just focus on that business so that you can just talk a  little bit more about what it is that will drive earnings in a bit more detail.

texts.speaker: Jon Rigby
texts.profession: Analyst, UBS Ltd. (Broker)
texts.text: And also, just referring back to the very good result that you've got this quarter, how much of that is a legacy of  some sort of preferred LNG pricing that you had from your old position that you can't repeat going forward?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Starting with the first one, I think that the basic difference with what we had before is that before the selling, we  had our own gas. Right now, we do not. So basically, what we have done in Canaport is really to obtain the  maximum flexibility there to use it in order to trade with gas and electricity in the U.S. basically. So I would say it's  exactly the main situation we had before, but only with the minimum [ph] send out (27:14) we are able to use it as  a trading facility, if you want. Okay.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: As far as I know, there's no any legacy impact on P&L from the prior existing assets. The only thing is that we  signed a – within the agreement with Shell, we had a contract for some gas with them and it's the only thing I can  remember right now that is impacting the first quarter result. So basically, no impact and only the 10 year contract  with Shell is the one that could be in line with what you have mentioned, okay.

texts.speaker: Jon Rigby
texts.profession: Analyst, UBS Ltd. (Broker)
texts.text: So there's no sort of cost of sale benefit from it because you've taken it on the previously sort of cheaper LNG  contract, which you'd have to replace with a market contract or market supply going forward.

texts.speaker: Irene Himona
texts.profession: Analyst, Société Générale SA (Broker)
texts.text: Thank you. Thank you.  Miguel Martínez San Martín  Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA  A  In relation with Venezuela, I would say that first the price we are going to obtain from the gas is $3.69 per million  Btu. And then there's some inflation regarding some industrial American index or something like that. So  basically it's [ph] $3.69 per million Btu (31:29). And if we talk about the return of the project, we are in the mid- teens...

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Other than that, it's true that we are tight and we knew that that in 2014 and 2015 the cash generation is going to  be tight, but that was clear since we sell the LNG division, though the liquidity position of the company allowed us  in the case that we do not have any inorganic transaction will help us to cross these two years. Other than that, by  2016, really the cash generation in the upstream division will fly. So...

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA

So the whole thing would be flying clearly at least in our  projection by 2016. But your comment is totally right. I mean, 2014 and 2015 without the LNG division, we are  going to be tight...

texts.speaker: Thomas Y. Adolff
texts.profession: Analyst, Credit Suisse Securities (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: And then the other question is just some numbers if possible on Libya. Where do we stand right now in terms of  production and on your comments on Sapinhoá where you said 15 kbd on average in 2014, is that just oil or oil  and gas? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA

Okay, Thomas?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with the Orca, Orca would be spudded in the second part of the year. I mean I look more for the money; they look for the geological concept. And this is the reason why I  didn't mention it. But it will be spudded in the second part of the year.

texts.speaker: Peter W. Hutton
texts.profession: Analyst, RBC Europe Ltd. (Broker)
texts.text: And Libya, not stripped but out of the formal guidance or just leave us to do that with the 40,000 barrels a day  guidance?

texts.speaker: Filipe Rosa
texts.profession: Analyst, Banco Espirito Santo de Investimento SA (Broker)
texts.text: And my third question relates to this new gas and power division with the North American assets, should we  assume that even your increased trading capabilities, even in normalized weather conditions, you should be able  to get some returns out of these assets or should we model these as a [ph] EBIT (59:23) operation over the long  term? Thank you very much.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And finally, remember that in relation with the gas and power, we accrued last year almost $1.8 billion, $900  million refers to the asset space and $900 million to the contracts in the pipelines. Other than that, if we are able to really trade better  as we did in the first quarter, we probably will make some gains but it will not be material in relation with the rest  of the results of the company.

file: REP - Q1 2015 Earnings Call 7May2015 700 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 07-May-15.pdf

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Thanks, Ángel, and thank you all for attending this conference on first quarter 2015 results. CCS adjusted net  income of the quarter was €928 million, 74% higher compared with the same period of last year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Let me now give you an update on the market environment and the operational activity of the quarter. Starting  with the macroeconomic environment, during the first quarter of the year, the weakness in oil price continue,  counterweighted by a strong U.S. dollar. Brent crude prices after a month of January in which a minimum of $45  per barrel was recorded, show a small upward rally ending the period of the same level with which 2014 closed  around $54 per barrel.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: After the end of the quarter, we continued observing a certain upward trend in oil prices, which supports our  medium-term view of higher prices necessary to achieve the right balance between demand and supply. This  scenario has occurred within a context of higher volatility which we believe will still be the case in the short term.  However, thanks to the reverse correlation between oil prices and the U.S. dollar, our earnings are somehow  hedged, given that we generate our earnings in U.S. dollars, while a significant part of our expenses are euro  denominated.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Nevertheless, what is more important is that our integrated model allow us to remain resilient even in a low crude  oil price scenario. Sustained higher refining margins are protecting us in the short term from this situation.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Additionally, the significant portion of our gas production not linked to oil price provides further stability. And on  top of that, we have the likelihood of the dividend flow on results of our affiliate Gas Natural Fenosa, a stake that  provides further optionality to protect the company against any possible scenario.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Let me highlight the find in Algeria, we're continuing with the successful exploratory campaign, a new gas  discovery was made, the TESO-2 well. It's the third one in the Illizi block, a high potential area in Southeast  Algeria. Repsol is the operator of the block with a 52.5% stake.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Let me highlight also our activity in the prolific Caipipendi area in Bolivia, where new discoveries in wells  Margarita 7 and 8, with a 5 million cubic meters per day production capacity will have reserves and bolster Repsol  gas production in the country.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: At the end of 2015, big production is expected to be reached in this second FPSO, which has a growth capacity of  150,000 barrels per day. Together with the first FPSO, the field will reach a plateau of 270,000 barrels per day.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Venezuela, first gas from Cardón is planned for mid-2015. This first phase of the development will produce 150  million standard cubic feet per day, and we maintain the original dates for the other phases.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Turning to production, the average production for the quarter stood at 355,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.  The production was 4% higher year-on-year and 10% if Libya is stripped out from both years. The main factors  behind the increase are the ramp-up of Sapinhoá and Mid-Continent and the startup in March 2014 of Kinteroni,  all partially offset by the suspension of activity in Libya.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In relation with costs, Repsol has always especially in the current situation has applied strict cost efficiency  culture. Several cost reduction initiatives are already in place and are starting to deliver with regards to high- impact drilling and logistic costs. Others are also being identified to be implemented in the near term. This  quarter, we already had a 5.7% year-on-year decrease of Upstream operating cost on a homogeneous basis.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Moving now to the operational highlights of the Downstream division. And with regards to the refining  environment, we have average record margins during the quarter, thanks to the strengthening of the spreads of  products linked and not linked to oil prices, together with lower energy costs.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: We were able to better capture the benefits of this advantageous situation due to the complexity of our refining  system reached after the strategic investments carried out in our refining system between 2007 and 2011 and the  self-consumption efficiency program addressed under the CO2 emission reduction program.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In 2014, this energy savings rendered an extra premium of $1 per barrel compared to 2011 when this program was  put in place. Our refining margin indicator in the quarter was $8.7 per barrel, higher than the $3.9 per barrel  reached during the first quarter of 2014.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In gas and power, while sales increased, the price environment in North America was tougher. Price fell around  40% year-on-year. And the gas price reference Algonquin lost almost $9 per million Btu. Despite these factors, our  result was above breakeven.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Let me now move to the first quarter 2015 earnings performance. First quarter 2015 CCS adjusted net income was  €928 million, 74% higher compared with the same period of last year. The good results in the Downstream  business and the one-off gains coming from the exchange rate positions due to the net asset dollar position held  for the acquisition of Talisman more than compensated the lower results coming from the Upstream business.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: It's worth noting that even in this challenging scenario, the company has been free cash flow positive during the  quarter. Starting with the Upstream business, adjusted net income for the first quarter was minus €190 million.  The result has been affected by the lower oil prices, the suspension of our Libyan operations that had an impact of  €148 million on the operating income and €51 million at the net income level, the exploration costs, the unusual  tax affects related to the depreciation of the real against the dollar in Brazil in an amount of €69 million, and the  one-off adjustments in Venezuela carried from 2014 coming from the operator in an amount of €50 million.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: The year-on-year performance excluding Libya is explained as follow. Lower crude and gas realization prices had a  negative impact at the operating level of €349 million. Higher production, thanks to the ramp-up of Sapinhoá and  Mid-Continent and the startup production in Kinteroni in March 2014, resulted in a positive impact of €76  million.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Turning to our Downstream division, CCS adjusted net income in the quarter was €534 million, which compares  with the €290 million of first quarter 2014. Drilling down into the quarterly results, in refining, we saw a year-on- year increase in margins per barrel due to a generalized strengthening of the bulk spread and to lower energy costs  derived from the efforts in efficiency undertaking in the past years.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: During this quarter, we have taken the steps in order to achieve this transformation and we have been able to  demonstrate that our integrated model is resilient even in this low price oil scenario. We are now focusing on a  smooth integration of Talisman which is already a reality and thereafter on establishing the strategy of Repsol.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In relation with the guidance for Downstream EBITDA, it's true that results are much, much better that we  initially estimate. And I have to say that, in the other side, actually was a little lower. So, in global terms, and it  shows the resiliency, we are more or less where we should be. But I agree with you, I mean, it looks like it's going  to be higher, let's say between €2.8 billion and €3 billion at CCS. I think that the EBITDA would be there.

texts.speaker: Brendan Warn
texts.profession: BMO Capital Markets Ltd.
texts.text: And could you just expand upon, if I correctly – if I quote it correctly, that you've achieved 5.7% operating cost  reductions year-on-year in the Upstream, just what you believe will be achievable and what will remain sticky in  terms of cost saving?

texts.speaker: Brendan Warn
texts.profession: BMO Capital Markets Ltd.
texts.text: And could you just further expand that in terms of the net CapEx expenditure in the Upstream, if you could just  split out or talk about what was expansion or development CapEx versus maintenance? And again, just what sort  of structural maintenance CapEx cost savings do you believe you've been able to achieve and will see throughout  this year? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Second question that I had was just relating to the Mississippi Lime, you talked about that being a sort of  contributor to growth year-on-year. Thank you.

texts.profession: Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP

texts.profession: Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP

file: REP - Q1 2016 Earnings Call 5May2016 700 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 05-May-16.pdf

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Let's continue now with the Repsol first quarter conference call. CCS adjusted net income was €572 million and   net income was €434 million.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: With respect to our efficiency program, the first quarter results show how Repsol's focus on becoming a leaner and  more efficient upstream operator, together with further improvements in our refining and chemical businesses, is  already delivering results. It's worth mentioning that the initiative focus on identifying and delivering real cost  savings are performing better than expected.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Going into detail in our Upstream business, we are well above our 2016 OpEx reduction target and in line with our  CapEx target. The sum of measures implemented across all countries and business areas had a cash impact of  more than €100 million in the quarter. In 2016, we will reduce our Upstream OpEx per barrel by more than 13%.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Our quarterly results reflect our efforts to deliver on CapEx reduction together with OpEx efficiency targets and  capture synergies resulting from the integration of Talisman into the wider Repsol Group. As a consequence of  these actions, we have achieved a significant reduction in our cash neutrality breakeven and maintained net debt  levels even with Brent averaging at around $34 per barrel.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: We have announced three significant disposals in the first quarter, with the major ity of cash proceeds projected to  be delivered later in the year. Firstly, we completed in January the sale of another portion of our piped LPG  businesses for a total of €136 million. This transaction, together with the sale completed in September 2015 of  piped gas assets, will generate around €800 million of proceeds, out of which €38 million were received in the  first quarter. Cash-in is expected to be finalized before the end of the year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Secondly, we reached an agreement to sell our offshore wind power business in the UK to SDIC, State  Development & Investment Corporation of China for €238 million. The cash from this sale is expected to be  received during the second quarter of 2016.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Let me now address the current market environment and the principal operational activities for the quarter.  During this quarter, we saw a further weakening of oil price, together with a continuous strength of the U.S. dollar  versus the euro. Brent crude averaged around $34, which compares to $44 per barrel in the previous quarter. In  recent weeks, we have seen a partial reversal of the trend, with Brent trading well above $40. Gas prices continue  at weak levels, with Henry Hub averaging just $2.1 million per million BTU.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Moving now to operating activity starting with Upstream division, production averaged 714,000 barrels of oil  equivalent per day. This is 2% higher than in the previous quarter and 100% higher year on year, mainly thanks to  the contributions of the start-up of Cardón in Venezuela, the ramp-up of Sapinhoá in Brazil, together with the  consolidation of Talisman assets.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Colombia, the early production scheme for Akacias was temporarily suspended in March due to low oil prices.  Project sanction has been rescheduled, and the FID is now expected to happen in 2017, awaiting a better oil price  outlook.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In the UK, we are continuing the progress to the redevelopment of MonArb and Flyndre Cawdor, with a focus on  cost efficiency and CapEx optimization, expecting first oil early in 2017. Delivery of this project will significantly  improve the economics of our JV.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In April, we receive encouraging news from the Gávea appraisal well in the Brazilian pre -salt. The well  encountered a hydrocarbon column of 175 meters in a good quality reservoir and was successfully tested  producing around 16 million standard cubic feet of gas and 4,000 barrels of oil. With this well, we finalized the  appraisal activities in the block Campos 33, which comprises the Seat, Gávea and Pão de Açúcar discoveries.  Additionally, contingent resources have been discovering our appraisal campaign in Sud-Est Illizi in Algeria.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: The mild winter weakened the performance of our Gas and Power business, but it remained at breakeven level.  The commercial businesses were in line with the first quarter of last year. Spanish motor fuel demand continued  to recover and the market grew at rates of 3.4% up to March.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Turning to our Downstream division, CCS adjusted net income in the quarter was €556 million, 4% higher than in  the first quarter of last year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: With regard to Gas Natural Fenosa, adjusted net income in the quarter of 2016 amounted €99 million, 19% lower  than that of the same quarter of 2015, mainly due to lower results in the gas commercialization business as a  result of lower margin, and in gas and electricity distribution business in Latin America affected by the  depreciation of local currencies.

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Firstly, I wondered if you could just give us an update on Venezuela. We get a lot of headlines in the press about  the difficulties the government and PDVSA are facing with the lower oil price and managing sort of budg ets and  power, et cetera. But I just wanted to understand how you're finding it from an operational perspective. What is  the impact that you are seeing? And also arguably more importantly, from a sort of cash flow perspective, are you  finding that you're still getting paid and how are the sort of payments working with yourselves with regards to the  country?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Starting with the LPGs, the pipeline LPGs all in would be around €800 million and would be cashed in within this  year. The sales are already signed so the SPAs are already signed, and we are pending on administrative approvals.  So that would be cash and would be cash within the year. The wind power in the UK will also be cash and cash  within the year. That's the [ph] €240 million (27 :14) more or less. The LPG in Ecuador and Peru will be also cash  and will be cashed in within the year.

texts.speaker: Brendan Warn
texts.profession: BMO Capital Markets Ltd.
texts.text: Y eah. Thanks, Paul, and thanks, Miguel, for the opportunity to ask questions. It's Brendan Warn from BMO  Capital Markets. Just two questions, first question I guess is on your results, and I appreciate you've now had an  additional quarter with the Talisman assets under your belt, Miguel. Just out of the three regions that you sort of  broadly talk about, and I'm referring sort of back to your strategic presentation where you break down to North  America, Latin America and Southeast Asia, where we've just seen probably some or I hope some of the worst oil  and gas prices. Can you just talk about three regions broken down by which are the better regions in terms of  contribution? Did you see any of them "break even" in terms of cash contribution? And what just cou ld we expect  for 2016 if we were to sort of average out at a sort of $45 oil price environment?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Also, the $40 scenario have not been reached in the first quarter. So if we have to go into our $4 environment, the  three areas will clearly improve. But more than that it's quite difficult to assess more and to see what the next  three quarters will provide us.

texts.speaker: Biraj Borkhataria
texts.profession: RBC Europe Ltd. (Broker)
texts.text: And then finally, just a quick one, the breakeven or the free cash flow neutrality target at $40 in 2016 and 2017,  can you just remind me what refining margin assumption is baked into that plan? Many thanks.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: I think that a second factor relates to the resiliency of the company. I mean, Repsol delivers better than our peers  in the lower part of the cycle, thanks to the Downstream division, which is larger to our size than our peers. Gas  Nat and also the dollar euro, normally when the barrel is low, the dollar [ph] strengthens, (39:53) and we have  many costs nominated in euros.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In relation with the working capital, the €572 million that we have suffered in this first quarter has a component  of – I mean, if we go to pure accounting, instead of €570 million, the figure would have been €360 million, to be  precise, €357 million. And this is due to the fact that we are working and all of that I will refer to CCS, and I will  try to elaborate a little.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: I mean, if CCS is higher than MIFO, that implies that the cost of sales that we are including in the CCS calculation  is lower. Put it in these words, we are taking cheapest barrels from our inventory. So in order to be fair, we have to  increase somehow the working capital for the difference between CCS and MIFO in order to be consistent. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving now on the financial results, I will briefly summarize the principal outcomes of the quarter. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Upstream, adjusted net income in the quarter was €224 million, €207 million higher than the same period in  2016, principally due to higher realized prices, the resumption in Libya and lower costs. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: We expect our Upstream investment intensity to pick up in the remainder of the year and CapEx guidance for  2017 for the whole company remains unchanged at around €3.6 million, of which €2.7 million refers to the  Upstream division. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Looking forward, current assets ramping up are due to start up in the near future, along with FIDs this year, will  allow us to maintain our referenced production level of 700,000 barrels a day past 2020, whilst continuing to focus  the portfolio on delivering higher margin barrels. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Downstream, our integrated business continues to deliver strong results quarter-on-quarter. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Chemicals, we expect our business to continue to benefit from the cost and energy efficiency projects already  initiated, supported by solid demand, favorable margins from higher value products and our enhanced feedstock  flexibility.
