texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In CPO-9 block in Colombia, the phase one of Akacias reached 20,000 barrels per day of gas production of which  45% correspond to Repsol. Exploration had a very good quarter with four positive wells out of the seven that were  concluded in the period. As of the end of March, two wells remained under evaluation while the remaining well  was deemed unsuccessful.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Indonesia, the Repsol-operated Kali Berau Dalam well in the Sakakemang block is the largest discovery in the  country in 18 years and the seventh largest discovery worldwide between 2018 and 2019. Initial estimates are of  at least a 2 TCFs of recovery, more reserves with relevant resource upside. This project will allow for a fast track  development in an area of good margins due to high gas realization prices.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving now to the Downstream, starting with Refining, the margin indicator averaged $5.30 in the first quarter  impacted by weak gasoline spreads. However, CCS unit margin rose around $1.15 higher than indicator as the  flexibility and attributes of our system, together, of course, with an efficient management of the crude slate allow  for a higher yield of middle distillates.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: The chemical business delivered a good quarter as well supported by the advantage of feedstock flexibility, higher  sales and healthy international merchants. Our chemicals production system benefits from our ability to use up to  40% of gas feedstock. Compared to the same period of 2018, sales and results were also helped by an improved  operational performance. In the commercial businesses compared to first quarter of 2018, the positive  contribution from Mexico was partially offset by a lower result in LPG due to a milder winter.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the mobility business, implementation of new growth levers is allowing us to maintain profitability despite an  increasingly competitive market. We also reached an important milestone with the opening of the first ultrafast  charging point for electric vehicles in Spain and the Iberian Peninsula. [indiscernible] (00:13:00) will reach more  than 830,000 retails client at the end of the quarter. Let me underline that today, they are 850,000 clients. And we  continue with our growth plans supported by our customer-centric energy supplier strategy.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Turning now to the financial results, I will summarize the main figures for the first quarter of the year and how they  compare with the same period in 2018. First quarter 2019, CCS adjusted net income was €818 million, a 6%  increase from the first quarter of 2018. Upstream adjusted net income the first quarter was €323 million, €36  million higher than in the same period of 2018. And the stoppage in Libya, lower gas sales in Venezuela, and  lower realization prices were more than compensated by lower exploration costs, a stronger dollar, a lower tax  due to the lower contribution from Libya.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Before moving to the conclusions, let me review the outlook to the end of 2019. Before we know our results in the  first quarter, we maintained probably unchanged our targets for the year despite a lower contribution from Libya  during the first two months of 2019 after an average production is expected to reach 720,000 of oil equivalent per  day budgeted at the beginning of the year.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Development activity in [indiscernible] (00:16:27) will continue towards achieving first oil objective in the third  quarter. In Akacias in Colombia, the FID for the full development of the field is expected to be taken towards the  end of the year with that targeted maximum production of 50,000 barrels per day in the medium term.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Refining, our updated margin indicator assumption for 2019 is lower compared to budget, but we expect to  offset this impact partially with a higher premium in the actual CCS margin as we managed to achieve in the first  quarter. This together with a somewhat higher oil price expectation make us maintain our target of €8 billion of  EBITDA at CCS with an organic CapEx of €3.8 billion.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Structural change in the bunkering business will make Repsol a clear winner, considering scrubbers' limited  penetration and the current restrictions from the supply of very low sulfur fuel oil. IMO will be not only a temporary  disruption for high sulfur fuel oil, but a structural effect as well.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: We are, at the same time, reducing our carbon footprint in the whole value chain. With investment in energy  efficiency while we develop an operated profitable low carbon business, focused on both low carbon generation  and electricity commercialization. We maintain our growth path by having reached 850,000 customers. And let me  highlight that we have accomplished all of these without compromising our financial flexibility.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Related to the low carbon business, I mean, the integration has been done as expected in the plan. As I said  before, we started with 750,000 clients at the beginning of November when we started the journey. And today we  have 850,000 clients in this business. That means that in this first month not only integration has been the target,  not only let me say put in place all the systems and so on, but also we have been able to increase 100,000 clients  – the clients of our low carbon business in electricity and gas.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: And on top of that, I mean we maintain of course the target of 2.5 million clients by 2025 we'll have before. And  we are working – building the renewable capabilities – the renewable generation capabilities. And we are doing  that organically, internally. And on top of that, of course, we are – if we see or we would see any kind of let me  say as I have underlined a lot of times inorganic possibility of building capabilities. I mean not buying let me say a  huge amount of assets in operation and so on. I mean we'll do it. But the main driver is going to be this  combination of organic acquisition plus inorganic capabilities of either pipeline. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Oswald Clint
texts.profession: Analyst, Sanford C. Bernstein Ltd.
texts.text: Good afternoon, gentlemen. Thank you. I wanted to ask about your – the Upstream cash flow. You mentioned it  was up strongly I think 25% year-over-year. I just want to get a sense of which new fields are really contributing to  that. I don't – probably wasn't very much from Trinidad. So I guess it's really that your Shale plays in North  America or Colombia perhaps a little bit of the Norwegian oil – or sorry, gas condensate assets. So, I am just  wondering if you could split somehow that cash flow growth across those couple of key assets, which have been  growing.

texts.speaker: Thomas Adolff
texts.profession: Analyst, Credit Suisse Securities (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: Couple of fairly straightforward questions please. Just firstly on the 2019 production guidance of 720 KBD, I think  it initially assumed 35 KBD from Libya and 50 KBD from Venezuela. And I was wondering what the contingency  buffer was to reach that target at the start of the year? And then secondly, just going back to Refining, you've now  had two quarters in row exceeding a premium of $1 per barrel over the indicator. And I think historically, if you  take the annual average, it was around $0.4, $0.5 admittedly that also incorporated a bit more maintenance. So I  was wondering versus the historical average, should we be thinking closer to a $1 or should we be thinking about  something in between or going back to the historical average? And then finally, just on the low carbon business,  since you I don't think you've split it out, I wondered what the quarterly contribution to the net income was? Thank  you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Thank you, Thomas. I mean, first of all, let me say that today in Venezuela, we have produced in the first quarter  a bit more than expected mainly in gas production in our budget and in the fourth quarter of 2018. That's my first  approach.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: The second one is that – I mean in Libya, we are not going to win the 35,000 barrels per day but we expect to  produce around 29,000 barrels per day, 30,000 barrels per day at the average for the whole year. These  reductions could be offset by an increase of production in Colombia. I mean, we are accelerating the CPO-9 and  we are going to produce more than expected at the end of the year.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Going to low carbon business, the contribution – I mean the guidance for the EBITDA for the year will be more or  less €60 million for the current assets. We have the guidance for the EBIT of the year will be at around €30 billion.  And this quarter, the EBIT has been €4 million- I mean the expectation I mean is not exactly the first quarter  multiplied by four because we have to take into account that we are, of course, starting with the business  integrating, developing some systems and so on. But I think that today, with current assets we have in our hands,  €60 million of EBITDA and €30 million of EBIT will be a good guidance for the contribution of the low carbon  business for the whole year. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: If we take, what will happen in the future, of course, here, I am entering on a speculative analysis. We could  expect some kind of improving of gasolines in this second quarter as far as the driving season in North America  goes on. And on top of that, our expectation is that, from the third quarter on, and that is going to be clear in the  fourth quarter, and that is reflected in some way in the future markets, the effect of the IMO is going to be there.  That means that the middle distillates spread is going to increase. On the other hand, we are going to do half at  the end of the year a higher discount for fuel oil. And as consequence of that, we are going to see also a wider  spread of heavy lights at the end of the year as a consequence of the influence of the IMO.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean, I don't know, the $7.6 per barrel of IMC is going to be there for the whole year. But my expectation is that  a potential reduction taking into account that we have in April. So on what is happening now is going to impact the  average of the year, is going to be in a main way offset by a higher premium in real margin terms. And let me say,  taking into account what I'm saying now, taking into account what is happening with the oil price and so on, I  mean, I'm quite comfortable about the full-year EBITDA guidance for 2019 at around €8 billion for a whole Repsol.  But it seems to me that this effect on the IMS MC as we have seen [indiscernible] (00:41:20) in the first quarter is  going to be either partially or totally offset by the improvement of the premium.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: And the maintenance is not going to impact in a negative way. I mean, first of all, because we have maintained  three out of our four cokers in 2017 and 2018. Secondly, because we have 3, 3.5 main maintenance turnover this  year one of them the FCC of Petronor is over. I mean we completed in the first quarter, this maintenance  turnaround. The second one, the coker of Coruña, this is the smallest of our refineries is on track. And the third is  going to be the hydrotreatment area of our Cartagena in the summer. So, I mean we are a going on with this  maintenance period. Some units of Puertollano are going to be a stopping in October. But the conversion  utilization rate is going to be similar to what was in 2018. So we are not going to see, let me say a negative impact  on the premium due to this maintenance activities in our refineries. Thank you, Flora.

texts.speaker: Giacomo Romeo
texts.profession: Analyst, Macquarie Capital (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: Good afternoon. Thanks for taking my question. I'm going to ask about the headlines that came out today  suggesting that you have terminated your negotiation with KKR on X-Elio. And I'm wondering if we should read  this as a signal that you're struggling to find inorganic renewable opportunities at a price that fits your return  thresholds. And since we are on this topic, could you please remind us what sort of inorganic ambitions you have  in solar? And what's type of assets and businesses you would consider acquiring?

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Thank you, Giacomo. I mean, first of all, let me say that I don't know if I was in and I don't know if we are out now  because we don't disclose any kind of participation in any M&A operation we are or we could be potentially  involved. So, my only point is, and I have underlined in these conferences a lot of times this statement, I mean we  are going to invest inorganically only if we see real value and only if we see returns that fits with what we could  expect for an oil and gas company. I mean – and to do that in the renewable business, we have to see a clear  integration with some other businesses of Repsol. We have to see clear capabilities to develop and to take the  whole value chain in the renewable side, to build the operation and maintenance capabilities we need, and of  course, to take risk selling our main part of this production in a merchant way.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: So, we are going to invest in an inorganic way. We are going to go on struggling to find opportunities, mainly  organic opportunities and hypothetically inorganic opportunities, but only if we see clear opportunities there. On  top of that, our ambition is clear. By 2025, we have the target and the ambition to operate 4.5 gigawatts of energy  power production to be [indiscernible] (00:46:53) in the Spanish market having a 5% of the retail market, in the  gas market to have a market share of 15% in the Spanish market. And that is our ambition, it's is our target, we  are on track, and we are going to go on trying to deliver these objectives, but always under our principle, creating  value for our shareholders, trying to integrate all of that with the different businesses we have today, and with the  returns, you have to expect and you could expect from an oil and gas company. I mean, we are not going to  invest everywhere because we have investment targets. We have growth, yes, but mainly profitability targets on  track. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: And the Refining business has improved over the last 15 months, 16 months. Thanks to the digital initiative. And  the most important digital initiative in the Refining business has been the optimization using the data pool we have  in our refinery, and here I am including the feedstock, the different kinds of crude oils, the consumption in energy  terms and in hydrogen terms of these crude oils, the situation in the market, the [indiscernible] (00:51:51) unit, the  consumption of energy and hydrogen in every unit and so on.

texts.speaker: Christopher Kuplent
texts.profession: Analyst, Bank of America Merrill Lynch
texts.text: And secondly, of course, other than low carbon, this is also an area of growth that you've allocated extra budget  towards. I'm afraid I haven't spotted a huge amount of progress in terms of growing that business organically or  inorganically. So, perhaps, again, if you could update us on the status quo in that regard. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: And the second point is that we have a quite flexible capacity of putting the feedstock in our crackers. And we  have been able to feed a 40% of the feedstock of all crackers using different gases. LPG, mainly, and also ethane  coming from some streams from our refineries. So, thanks to this combination of flexible feedstock plus a quite  good performance in operational terms over the quarter, we have been able to have a good quarter.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: The low carbon business, I mean, the capital allocation we have budgeted for the pay of 2018-2020 in low carbon  business has been €2.5 billion. That was announced in our strategic update in June 2018. Up-to-date, we have  invested €1 billion, more or less, €750 million coming from Viesgo. Better said, we have on track €1 billion  because we have invested €750 million in the acquisition of Viesgo. €20 million in the acquisition of a pipeline of  Valdesolar, and we are going to invest, in coming months, €200 million, €210 million more or less to develop the  260 megawatts, 265 megawatts I think of Valdesolar, the photovoltaic project in the south-western part of Spain.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: So, the main growth we are going to push is in the retail, in the gas wholesale. On top of that, we are trying to  identify a pipeline that we may acquire and we could construct, develop, and operate with our own resources, you  have to take into account that we are recruiting people, best-class people in our market to operate our assets. In  Spain, we have great things, but one of them is that we have strong operational capabilities in the renewable  sector because the history of this country over the last 20 years. So, we are recruiting people organically and we  are combining these people with the engineering capabilities we have in the company.

texts.speaker: Matthew Lofting
texts.profession: Analyst, JPMorgan Securities Plc
texts.text: Hi, afternoon. Thanks for taking the questions. Two if I could, please. I mean first coming back refining and IMO.  You've outlined a bullish picture on IMO into 2020, to ask the question in a more forward looking way, when you  look into the second half of the year and beyond, are there any specific industrial data points or events that you'd  suggest investors look to as proof of concept to IMOs becoming a reality. And within that, when do you expect the  commercial marketing of the new very low sulfur fuel grades to take effect?

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean, the vision or the view we have about the IMO, I have expressed before this view. My point is, in some  way, supported but not the foregoer, the future markets are anticipating today. In my perception, this – I mean,  forward markets could be right, because I mean the enforcement and the compliance is going to be there. And the  most profitable – or the most logical way and the only way for some people to adapt to the newer specification in  the emerging sector is going to be to shift from fuel oil – from high sulfur fuel oil to gas oil. So, the rationale is  there. But again, we are flexible to adapt to our operation to the different realities.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean we are prepared to have a zero high sulfur fuel oil production in our Iberian system at the end of the year.  We have dispersed capacity in the cokers of Coruña and Bilbao to use either the current fuel oil production in  Bilbao or the production in Tarragona that we may transport to Coruña, sorry, to feed the coker we have in that  refinery. But at the same time, I mean we are also flexible to produce some small production of low sulfur fuel oil  using a different feedstock of crude oil and blending, in some cases, these fuel oil with gas oil. I mean we are  prepared for every situation.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: My point is that it seems to me that it's going to be more efficient, more profitable, and with more margins in the  market to produce with our full high conversion system, middle distillate when you have four cokers in five  refineries that is going to be more profitable and markets are anticipating all that that produce low sulfur fuel oil  blending your bottom of the barrel with low sulfur gas oil. So, that is my view that we are prepared for any  situation in a flexible way.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: So going to the CapEx for the rest of the year, I mean we maintain the guidance for the whole year at around €3.8  billion for the whole year. And I'm not including this year, as I said also three months ago any kind of opportunities  in the low carbon business that as you know we are using in capital allocation terms that €2.5 billion coming from  the disposal of GasNat that I consider before. But my best approach for this year, for the CapEx is €3.7 billion,  sorry, for the whole year. You know that sometimes the first quarter, and that happens almost every year, the  CapEx execution in the first quarter is a bit – is lower than the rest of the year, and we are of course rescheduling  the year. But €3.7 billion will be our first – our best guidance and approach now. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Alwyn Thomas
texts.profession: Analyst, Exane Ltd.
texts.text: Morning – sorry, afternoon now. I just wanted a quick follow up on the low carbon business. Would you consider  investing outside of Spain specifically because more areas are now starting to open up and there seem to be a  reasonable amount of opportunities available? Oh, sorry, that's it for me.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Thank you, Alwyn. My answer is yes, I mean theoretically, yes, but saying that because we are going to prioritize  returns if make sense to invest firstly in places where you have a better possibility to integrated all businesses. I  mean in Spain, we have a significant base of customers. We have 10 million clients in this country. On top of that,  we are the main gas consumer in Spain. 12% of gas production in Spain comes from our industrial sites. We  consume 1.5% of Spanish total market power. We are enactor in the power wholesale market in Spain. So, it  makes sense to start investing in Spain to develop this kind of businesses because we have a solid and a strong  position in the market. On top of that, I mean, after having the capabilities, you have a good developer, I mean,  we are ready to analyze some other developments in some other parts of the world. That, I think, that didn't make  sense starting from Spain. Thank you, Alwyn.

texts.speaker: Alwyn Thomas
texts.profession: Analyst, Exane Ltd.
texts.text: Yes. Sorry. I was just asking whether you're able to give a little bit more guidance on what your plans might be for  investments in changing your yield output in the Downstream business, Refining and Chemicals beyond IMO  2020 to 2025 sort of period.

texts.speaker: Kim Fustier
texts.profession: Analyst, HSBC Bank Plc
texts.text: Yeah. Hi. Good afternoon. I just had two questions please. The first one is just on LNG. In the last six months or  so, I noticed that you've signed a couple of LNG supply deals, one from the U.S. and the other from Russia quite  recently. And I was wondering if you could give some color on the rationale and maybe the pricing of these deals.  I assume you're planning to shift this LNG to Spain to supply your own gas and power business, but any color you  can share on that would be helpful. And just secondly, just if you could give a bit more detail on the Leon and  Moccasin developments in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico. For example, when do you expect to take FID and when you  see first oil? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Going to the gas contracts, I mean we closed a contracts with [ph] ventures (01:12:45), one BCM I remember in  the Gulf of Mexico in August that is going to – I mean to be confirmed in coming months after the confirmation of  the development of project taking that in July this year. And on top of that, we have an M-O-U, MoU to analyze  the possibility to buy 0.4 BCMs coming from the north part of Russia, from Yamal.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean you have to take into accounting that we have our consumption today in our refineries and chemical plants  of around 3.5 BCMs. And on top of that, we have a consumption that is close to 0.8 BCMs, 0.7 BCMs coming  from our CCGTs and our position in the gas market. So, all-in-all, our consumption level is at around 4.1 BCM, 4.2  BCM as a whole. We are growing in this market and the current position we have with all the contracts we have in  our hands today, I think that is 3.3 BCM, 3.4 BCM coming from the Gulf of Mexico. And we are adding to these  baskets. Let me say some other position coming from some other places.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: So, there is our rational of having a diversified basket of feedstock – not feedstocks, sorry, of gas for our industrial  sites and our market. And we have to take into account that Spain is decoupled from the European continent in  logistic gas terms. So, the real opportunities we have to feed the Spanish market, they come either from pipe  connecting Northern Africa and Spain, all the LNG plants where we have a good position as an Atlantic player  very close to the Gulf of Mexico.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: On top of that, I mean, Leon, Moccasin, first of all, we have to have the confirmation. Thanks to the – or as a  consequence of the well that is going to be drilled in coming months to appraise the Leon project. And probably  we will take the FID of the whole combined project in 2020 at around the third quarter, more or less. And the most  – I mean the closest approach I have today is will be to see the first oil in the project at around the first – at the  end of 2022 or the first quarter of 2023. The gross production of the area will be at around 35,000 barrels per day  oil. And we have a combination of stakes, 50% Leon; 30% Moccasin. So, it will take, let me say, 10,000 barrels  per day, 11,000 barrels per day, more or less, net production for Repsol. But I mean, it's still underlying. We have  to go ahead step-by-step. Thank you, Kim.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean, Jason, we have in our strategic update €11 billion for Upstream and Downstream, either sustained growth  or improvement of efficiencies targets. And we have €4 billion, €1.5 billion of them for the international expansion  of the Downstream businesses and €2.5 billion for the low carbon business.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Today, my first or my best approach, I mean I think that we could invest in the best guidance I may give you  today, €10.7 billion, €10.8 billion out of these €11 billion, we have €1.5 billion for the Downstream growth and €2.5  billion for the low carbon businesses that we are going to try to find the opportunities to invest in these areas with  the profitability we are looking for. I mean that is our best guidance today. We are not going to be far from this €15  billion figure all in all that I insist, Jason, in case of not having opportunities to invest with the return we expect, we  will proceed to an additional buyback of shares. No doubt about that. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Thank you, Jon. I mean, I say, no, in general terms that as I said or I have said over the last month, I mean if we  see opportunities of additional cash because, I mean, the oil price is above $50, that was the baseline of our  strategic update. And we see additional opportunities. I mean, we are ready to increase a bit the CapEx. The  CapEx like always looking for places or assets where we could have clear advantages. And in the case of the  Gulf of Mexico, I mean, it is clear that we have synergistic opportunities combining the Moccasin asset and Leon.  And in this case, we are combining all that with a very good operator in Deepwater in the Gulf of Mexico.

texts.speaker: Yuriy Kukhtanych
texts.profession: Analyst, Deutsche Bank AG
texts.text: Yes. Jon, thank you very much for your time. Two questions for me please. First, on Libya, could you please  comment on the lifting of crude oil production in Libya? How frequent are the cargoes currently and have you  actually shipped anything in March and in the beginning of April from the country? That's the first question. And  the second question is on very low sulfur fuel oil. You mentioned in the beginning of the call that there are some  restrictions on the market currently. Could you please elaborate on these restrictions? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: When you say the fuel oil restrictions, you are talking – sorry, so could you repeat that?

texts.speaker: Yuriy Kukhtanych
texts.profession: Analyst, Deutsche Bank AG
texts.text: Yes. I understood that you mentioned that there are currently some restrictions on the very low sulfur fuel oil  market. And I was just wondering what you mean by that in the beginning of the call.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean it seems to me that we are going to see a reduction of demand in the high sulfur fuel oil market due to the  IMO new rules. And it seems to me also that is going to be more profitable for our refiner in case of having the  units, the coking units they need to produce middle distillates, to produce low sulfur gas oil to try, let me say, to  produce for someone that has had low conversion rate in the refinery, taking their fuel oil production, use sweet  and light oils to produce a low sulfur fuel oil, blending this fuel oil with gas oil that is going to be an expensive  product due to whitening process of the middle distillates spreads. And this process is going to be possible of  course but margin for someone with strong coking capacity able to produce zero fuel oil and to maximize the  middle distillates low sulfur production, margins are going to be better in my perception than for someone using  blending to produce the product to be in specification. That is my perception take into account the reality in the  market. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Peter Low
texts.profession: Analyst, Redburn (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: Hi. Thanks. Just a quick question on refining and specifically the crude slate. texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: So, may point is that we are running our refineries using our 44% 48% of heavy oil. And of course we have the  flexibility to reduce these figures depending on the reality of the market. But today, I mean the reality of margins  and so on allow us to maintain this operation. And it seems to me that as far as the IMO effect coal impact in the  market, because this higher bottom of the barrel coming from the heavy oils, we are going to have opportunities  for feeding our refineries with heavy oil in the future. Thank you, Peter.

texts.speaker: Biraj Borkhataria
texts.profession: Analyst, RBC Europe Ltd.
texts.text: Hi, thanks for taking my questions. I just had two quick ones left. The first one is on the Downstream, there was a  fairly large negative in the other Downstream segment. I know you said Viesgo was a small positive contributor,  could you just walkthrough what drove that in Q1? texts.profession: Head-Investor Relations, Repsol SA

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Going to the gas feedstock. I mean, I remembered that in 2012, for instance, and I remember quite well because  at that time, I was running the Chemical business of the company, we could have had a maximum of 20%,  something like that, of capacity of gas feedstock. For instance, in [indiscernible] (01:32:47) all the feedstock was  NAFTA, and in Tarragona, we could have 20%, 25% and even a reduced capacity in Puertollano.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Thanks to the change of furnaces, thanks to the change of logistics and so on, and thank you also to the use of  streams coming from the refineries, the fuel gas, that [indiscernible] (01:33:13) today, we have the possibility to  increase this feedstock and let me say that we have the best of being in a European market but at the same time,  we have one of the gasiest feedstocks in the crackers in Europe. So decoupling in some way of operation from  the risk of being fully exposed to the NAFTA. Thank you, Biraj.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: Starting with the results, this quarter we release CCS adjusted net income of €485 million and a CCS adjusted  operating income of €1 billion. The main factors that explain this specific situation are the lack of production in  Libya and the strikes in Argentina.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: Higher oil and gas realization prices couldn't offset production losses from Libya and the depreciation of the U.S.  dollar. The good news for the production for next quarter will come from Shenzi in the Gulf of Mexico, since we  have drilled one development well, B-201, that is already producing, and we are currently drilling a second one. In  consequence our current production in the Gulf of Mexico, it's at the same levels we had a year ago, around 31,000  barrels per day net to Repsol.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: To finish with the second quarter results, let me highlight the main aspects of the remaining business segments.  Starting with LNG, adjusted operating income in second quarter '11 was €53 million versus €13 million posted in  the same quarter last year. The year-on-year increase was driven by higher volumes, mainly due to the start of the  Peru LNG in June 2010 and wider LNG marketing margins.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: In the downstream business, adjusted CCS operating income was €224 million, 39% down year-on-year. The year- on-year drop in earnings is mainly due to lower margins in the refining and the LPG business that could not be  offset by the recovery of the chemical business that is operating in positive terrain.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: Gas Natural Fenosa, at €188 million adjusted operating income, was in line with the same quarter of last year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: The second area I would like to cover is our exploratory program for the rest of the year. On top of our already- announced success in Guara and Carioca appraisal this year, we had a positive well in the quarter: Gavea, in  Campos 33 Block. The discovery includes two oil horizons. Drilling results are being analyzed before continuing  with the appraisal of the area.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: In the 2011 program, an additional 25 square kilometers area was chosen for a second pilot along with the 200  square kilometers of delineation. The annual program included 17 new wells and fracturing 14 existing wells of the  Loma La Lata field. During this quarter, we have had results in the area of Loma La Lata [ph] North (9:40) with  two latest vertical wells drilled in a possible natural fractured sweet spot. After fracturing the wells, they are  performing with high productivity under natural flow pressure, and rates above 500 barrels of oil per day with  capacity to produce above 1,200 barrels of oil per day. With these results, we will continue the campaign in Loma  La Lata [ph] North (10:09) with another nine wells, three of them horizontals.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: At the second part of the non-convention oil program for 2011, 13 exploratory wells would be drilled in order to  assess the potential of Vaca Muerta in other parts of the Neuquén Basin. During the quarter, YPF announced a  new shale oil discovery in the Vaca Muerta formation in the Bajada de Añelo Block. The well was 3,000 meters  depth, in which three fractures were made in 150 meters. The results of the well deliver an average production of  250 barrels flowing naturally. Such good results come from a well which does not have the best geological  conditions, low carbonate content and drilled in a rock thickness of only 135 meters. This encourage us to expect  improved results in future wells with better geology.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: We will go ahead with the exploration program in the rest of the basin in which we are close to fracturing three  wells already drilled. Before the end of the year, we will drill with our partners at least the nine additional  exploration wells.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: In Kinteroni, the appraisal campaign has been successful, with Kinteroni 2 and 3 already drilled and tested. The  construction of production and gas evacuation facilities is currently underway. First gas production of 5 million  cubic meters per day is to come onstream in second quarter of 2012 as planned. Overall project CapEx is below  budget.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: In Margarita, the first phase of the project, which include the 6 million cubic meters per day plant expansion plus  the hook up of three existing wells, is at 53% of project completion, and it's expected to start production in the  second quarter of 2012. We are already launching the second phase of the project which will increase  production by an additional 6 million cubic meters per day in the fourth quarter 2013.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: In Guara, field development is progressing well with first oil expected in first quarter 2013 as planned. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA
texts.text: In the Cardon IV project, five wells have already been drilled and the supply as well as the frontend engineering  and design for the early production facilities of up to 300 million cubic feet per day capacity has been concluded.  First gas is planned for late 2013. The option of accelerating a [ph] path for (14:48) this production to begin  output even earlier is being studied. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Repsol YPF SA

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: However, the disposal of the LNG business should not only reduce our debt but also increase our cash position  and will not have a dilutive effect. Therefore, the sale of our LNG business is our first choice. However, we will  continue working in parallel with these two alternatives to minimize the risks of not obtaining the required ratio  levels.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: During the second quarter, CCS adjusted net income was €481 million and CCS adjusted operating income was  €936 million. These results were 27% and 34% higher respectively than during the same period last year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The good results have been driven by the performance of our upstream and LNG divisions. In the upstream front,  the adjusted operating income was €518 million, 77% higher than during the same period last year. The return to  pre-conflict levels in the Libyan output and the revenues on gas realization price increase added by the startup of  the Margarita project have been the main drivers of the good results, partially offset by the amortization of the  unsuccessful exploratory wells mainly Cuba.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the LNG division, better margins resulted in an adjusted operating income of €78 million, 47% better than  during the same period last year. The increase was due to higher commercialization margins. The results were  lower than the previous quarter because of the seasonality effect mainly in our North American operations.  In the downstream business, the CCS adjusted operating income was €205 million, 5% lower than in the second  quarter of 2011. The improvement in refining margins and the increase in refined volumes could not offset the  decline of the petrochemical product demand, and the lower sales volumes of tariff retail of the market division.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The utilization rate of the refining system was 68% versus 70% in the same period in 2011. The low utilization  rates of our units was a consequence of shutdowns due to maintenance in the Puertollano and La Coruna  refineries, a catalyst change process in the Tarragona hydrocracker, and the revamp of the Petronor refinery  visbreaker. Cartagena's new hydrogen and hydrocracker plants also have shore shutdowns due to mechanical  adjustments. The ban on acquiring Iranian crude caused oil mix and operational changes in our refineries mainly  in Petronor.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Gas Natural, the adjusted operating income of €232 million was 23% higher than during the same period of last  year. The good results are a consequence of higher margins in the natural gas businesses.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Let us now move to the operational performance behind the results. Production in the upstream division within  the quarter was 320,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, 8% higher than during the second quarter of 2011. The  main variations come from Libya, Bolivia, and Trinidad and Tobago.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Libya, the production reached 47,000 barrels of oil per day, which we have reached pre-conflict petrol levels. In  Bolivia, production was 26,000 barrels per day, 24% higher than during the same period of last year due to the  start-up of Margarita phase 1. In Trinidad and Tobago, we were still affected by maintenance on the offshore  platforms and in the Atlantic LNG trains and production reached 119,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, 16%  less than during the same period in 2011.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Since early July, production is at record levels of 350,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, due to the recovery of  Trinidad and Tobago. We expect to materialize added production from Kinteroni in Peru, Russia and  Midcontinent in the U.S. in the second half of the year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Let me now review the status of the main development projects. The Margarita field project is running properly.  Phase 1 of the gas development project started up in May increasing gas delivery up to 9 million cubic meters per  day. The second phase is on track to start up in fourth quarter 2013 and reach a capacity of 14 million cubic meters  per day in 2014.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Peru, the Kinteroni project carries on as planned and we expect to reach first gas during the last quarter of  2012, with a gross production capacity of 5 million cubic meters per day plus associated liquids.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The Sapinhoa project before Guara is going as scheduled. We are currently logging the P3S well and drilling two  producing wells, P4 and P5. The installation of the Guara-Tupi gas pipeline is progressing and we expect to receive  the FPSO in December.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Lubina-Montanazo project in Spain, we are working on the subsea equipment installation and the hookup  to the Casablanca platform. We expect to start production in October.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Samples of light oil were recovered from sands above the primary objective, which is encouraging. We will be  evaluating the information of the first well both for the aforementioned presence of oil in some horizons and the  knowledge we acquired about the pressure ramps in order to consider further exploratory work.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: We have been especially active during this quarter in seismic campaigns. We finished campaigns in Indonesia,  Portugal and Alaska, and we started campaigns in Angola, Canada and Iraq. We are including in our acreage  acquisition, pending final rectification, two new important areas, Namibia and Bulgaria.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: On the LNG front, Peru LNG produced 575,000 million Btu per day, 2% more than during the same period last  year. The plant delivered during the quarter three out of 15 cargos for the Manzanillo plant in Mexico.

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Thank you, Marie. Good afternoon, everyone. Haythem Rashed from Morgan Stanley. Three quick questions, if I  may. Firstly, just to come back on the financing plan and the sort of dual approach to LNG assets plus the  preference shares, I just wondered if you could provide any updates in particular on the preference share sort of  transaction, any sort of updates in terms of timing. Is it still sort of planned for sometime in sort of late 3Q, early  4Q? Any sort of hurdles that need to be overcome before we get to that stage?

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Secondly, just sort of related to that I guess, on the LNG business, given that there's some indication around the  sort of preference for a sale there, given previously the comments about the synergies between Gas Natural and  LNG, has your view around gas not changed at all since we lost both and would you be sort of more sort of willing  to do something around that, around your stake there now given the sort of potential sale on the LNG side?

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: And my third question is just on the downstream environment, just get your view on the outlook for the second  half of this year, and specifically as well how the upgrade impact is coming through on the numbers and where you  are in relation to sort of the $2 to $3 positive impact from the Cartagena and Bilbao upgrades. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: So we'll have to see how the LNG process go on and then take decisions about the prefs. We will keep advancing  and in that sense we have the authorization of the board to keep moving with the preference shares, though the  final decision and the end of the process, it's linked to the LNG process, so difficult to assess now any detail about  the conversion of the preps.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with the second one, I'll say that before analyzing Gas Natural, let's say we are able to sell the LNG. So  for sure, it will imply many things but let's go step by step and we'll have to think about our situations if the LNG  sale goes ahead.  Finally, my outlook for the refining in Europe has not modified substantially. I think that Europe is logging  approximately 3 million barrels of distillation capacity. So I'm basically bearish about the area in the following  months until the year end. I think that the solution will never come by the demand, so some of the distillation  capacity have to be, I'll say, converted into logistic terminals or shutdown.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Basically, you have to think that it is not easy to adopt a refinery as Cartagena that was pure hydroskimming into  one of the more complex refineries in Europe, first step. Second, in relation with Bilbao, a part of the issue of the  visbreaker, you have to think that the change in the diet, in the diet closing the Iranian oils and moving into other  type of oils, which are needing more hydrogen between many other things, people need to adapt and need to know  better the behavior of this new diet we are imposing. So I think that by the year end, we will be able to reach the  range between these $2 and $3. Did I answer your question?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with the preference and the conditions, I think that every shareholder or every investor, for sure, is  concerned about dilution and that's the reason why we have to check first how the LNG business is going to evolve  and which will be the impact because things at the LNG under the agencies concept that implies a debt of €4  billion. So it will have a massive impact on the considerations of the agencies.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: So, I cannot go any forward because, first, we have to check the evolution of the LNG process and then we will  analyze the prefs. It's important to keep both projects in parallel because one thing is important, I mean what we  consider is totally necessary is to keep the investment grade. So we will see, but I cannot be more clear, okay.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: So, let's analyze first how the LNG goes in parallel, let's keep working to have everything ready, if a conversion or  if an optionality is to be given to the tenants of the preference shares and we will see afterwards. But I cannot  advance anymore than that. I mean we are working in both areas and we will see at the end, which is the best for  our shareholders and for the company.

texts.speaker: Theepan Jothilingam
texts.profession: Analyst, Nomura International Plc
texts.text: Yeah, hi, good afternoon. Thank you for taking the questions. Miguel, just coming back to the LNG business, I just  want to understand in terms of a sale process, would you consider a piecemeal sale within the LNG business? And  could you just remind us where some of that off balance sheet debt lies between the assets?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Good morning, Theepan. In relation with the LNG, our idea is to sell it as a block. I mean, we don't want  [indiscernible] (40:15) so it would be a single transaction at least initially. And in relation with what is the off- balance debt? It basically refers to all the leases of the rating agencies consider as bad debt. Basically, we're talking  of 14 tankers and all the pipelines across the U.S. and Canada which accounts for €2 billion. So basically the debt  we have is €1 billion in our balance sheet and the agencies accounted debt for €4 billion just to the fact that I  mentioned. If I have today to give you an idea for the year production and I'm always wrong with my projections,  but I think that if you take 330,000 barrels per day on a yearly basis, you will be close.

texts.speaker: Theepan Jothilingam
texts.profession: Analyst, Nomura International Plc
texts.text: Okay, perfect. And I mean coming back to the LNG business, I know it's early days but have you had – can you  indicate any level of interest in that that you've had so far in that business?

texts.speaker: Lydia R. Rainforth
texts.profession: Analyst, Barclays Capital Securities Ltd.
texts.text: Thanks and good afternoon as well. A couple of questions if I could. First one, just on the working capital side,  clearly it was quite a good release of working capital from the quarter. And then secondly, if I come back to the LNG and the preference shares issue,  clearly selling the LNG was not part of the original plan from the strategic side and I just want to understand that  if there is a maximum level of dilution that you would look out for being successful for issuing the preference  shares? texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: First one, in relation with the working capital I think we improved this year I mean this quarter, approximately  €400 million. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with the LNG and prefs, now we don't have a magic figure. I mean, we have to keep working advancing  first the LNG process to see where we are and then we will take the decision. One thing is clear, we have to keep  the investment grade and we will look, first, at the results of the LNG and, if necessary, we will go with preference  shares. So we could with both process in parallel and we will see.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean in today's financial markets and in today's – I mean, volatility is the name of the game so it's quite difficult  to assess what is going to happen in two weeks. So we will keep working on the LNG and then we will take our  decisions. This is what I can tell you. And final question was – can you repeat it, Lydia?

texts.speaker: Alastair R. Syme
texts.profession: Analyst, Citigroup Global Markets Ltd.
texts.text: Yeah, hi everyone, in the risk of laboring the same point, just on the LNG, can I just clarify whether this is an  either/or with the preference shares or would there be a scenario where you might consider doing the both? Secondly, can I  just ask – I know it's not your company, but what your thoughts are on the Sacyr situation given that you have  participated in the past? And thirdly, just to clarify on the Peru LNG cargos that you send away, where is the tax  liability paid on those arbitrage cargos? Is it paid in Peru or is it paid by corporate Repsol somewhere else? Thank  you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Thanks, Alastair. I mean, in relation with the LNG, I mean, the priority is to keep the investment grade. We are  going to move faster with the LNG and in parallel with the pref shares. If the LNG give us enough room to working  with the agencies find a status in which the investment grade is not in danger, then we will look for a solution for  the pref shares totally different from capital. I mean there are other formulas that can solve the situation of  liquidity of the preference shares not being capital.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: But having said so, I need first to know how the LNG process is going ahead. So I will solve both issues, but once –  I mean I need a variable to be solved, which is how the LNG and how the agencies will analyze the company once  the LNG is sold. Also I think it is important to mention when we talk about LNG, we are not talking about the  upstream assets linked to the LNG, okay.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: So basically, first, establish how the LNG works then let's solve the problem of the preference shares, if the rating  agencies give us comfort and we know that we can keep the investment grades. I mean their formulas to provide  liquidity to the tenants of the preference shares not affecting the capital, let's say, hybrids or many other options.  But I cannot give you more flavor today, because first I need to know how the agencies will react once we move  into the LNG process.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with Sacyr well, not much to – I mean, I don't have anything to say on that. And finally in Peru,  basically the royalties are logically paid in Peru and those royalties are dependent on the price that the LNG  reaches, basically depending on their destination, whether it's Europe, U.S. or Far East. So it's an issue of royalties  and as mentioned in, I think it was Bruno, I think that the major impact for us would be around $1 million or  something like that, okay.  Alastair R. Syme  Analyst, Citigroup Global Markets Ltd.  Q Yeah. Thank you very much.

texts.speaker: Mark A. Bloomfield
texts.profession: Analyst, Deutsche Bank AG (Prime Brokerage)
texts.text: Good afternoon. Thanks for taking for question. Assuming you've not completed the LNG sale by that point in time but you're fairly confident of doing  so hypothetically in the next two to three months, have you had conversations with rating agencies about  potentially deferring the conversion of prefs to, say, later this year going into next year, so would they give you a  period of growth to do so?

texts.speaker: Mark A. Bloomfield
texts.profession: Analyst, Deutsche Bank AG (Prime Brokerage)
texts.text: The second question is just on your divestments target. You obviously outlined the target of the strategic plan.  You've talked about looking at the LNG assets. texts.speaker: Mark A. Bloomfield
texts.profession: Analyst, Deutsche Bank AG (Prime Brokerage)
texts.text: And then, the final question is just on CapEx. I think year-to-date CapEx is coming in at around €1.5 billion for  your Gas Nat. The full year target was around €4 billion. The run rate looks a  bit light. Could you give us some  indication of whether the €4 billion target is still valid, or have you been able to make some savings on the CapEx  front? Thanks

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with the first one, I'd say that we're in permanent contract with the agency. So with one of them, for  example, we have already talked about this – this issue. And I think that time is there. I think what is important  for the agencies is to see the direction in which we are moving. And in that sense, I would say that, at least the last  meeting we've had, I ended up quite optimistic. Basically, the script was there, the initial of divestments was there.  We gain liquidity. So basically, it's not a fixed date. I think that if by September, we'll have a lot of flavor about  how the LNG process were going. Then, we will sit with the agencies. I mean – and once we speak with them, we'd  realize whether or not we have to move in one direction or the other, and this is what I can tell you.

texts.speaker: Peter W. Hutton
texts.profession: Analyst, RBC Europe Ltd. (Broker)

texts.speaker: Peter W. Hutton
texts.profession: Analyst, RBC Europe Ltd. (Broker)
texts.text: And the third one, Namibia and the action plan now that you have the three blocks of 44% off on Namibia, where  do you go from here and what's the kind of indication on when you'd assess drilling well locations and access to  rigs?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: [indiscernible] (54:14). I don't know if I have more bullets or not. But my perception is that, I think it's important  and it's always – that it is something that we always transmit to the rating agencies. I mean we have a lot of  optionality, a lot of them, both to gain liquidity and to improve the balance. And we have to pay those in what we  think is the best for our shareholders. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with the refining, two factors to be mention. Basically, in a normal year, we should produce approximately – or distillate  approximately 280 million barrels, which is 70 million barrels per quarter. So on average, this maintenance  represents roughly $0.50. But we have been distillating only 60%. This will account for a little more, let's say,  $0.75, $0.80 of dollar per barrel. Okay, Daniel?

texts.speaker: Iain A. Pyle
texts.profession: Analyst, Sanford C. Bernstein Ltd.
texts.text: Good afternoon, yeah, thanks for taking my questions. I think most of my questions have been answered, but  perhaps on the gas realizations, given that the gas realization has moved up this quarter, I wonder if you could  give some more detail on the realization you are seeing from Margarita. And secondly, I wonder if you can  comment on the progress with the shale assets you're developing with SandRidge in the U.S. And particularly,  given the low realizations we're seeing in the States at the moment, whether that has any effect on the future  development plans for that? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA

So, a good news there.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with the shale assets, the impact would be minimum this year. I think that by the year-end, on average,  it would be approximately around 2,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day with a 47% of it being oil. So, no major  impact right now. We'll keep drilling. We have right now 22 rigs operating, and we keep confident that the price  we have there is going to be a good one. And we expect to end up with more than 90 rigs and obtain the peak of  production by 2019, 2020. So right now, no more news there. And for sure, no impact at all within this year. Okay,  Iain?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Starting with the exploration, I mean, we just entered. I mean, we – I think it's – in Bulgaria, we have not received  the confirmation of the award. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Sierra Leone and Liberia, I mean we have the disappointment of Mercury-2 and our people are analyzing the –  and they're studying back all the registers we get from the wells, both Mercury-1, Mercury-2, plus the  [indiscernible] (01:04:36) and they are studying it. So I don't have any – any extra input to provide you, okay?

texts.speaker: Henry J. Morris
texts.profession: Analyst, Goldman Sachs International Ltd.
texts.text: Hi, everyone, and thanks very much, Miguel, for taking my questions. I just got three quick questions, please. First  of all, in your discussions with the rating agencies, what's the most important metric that they want you to meet in  order to maintain your investment grade rating? Second, can I just confirm what you said early on the call, that  the total debt that you can consolidated from the LNG business is €1 billion, a straight net debt plus €3 billion of  finance leases? And thirdly just on Kinteroni, I know that you're still up in the fourth quarter of this year, should I  assume that's towards the beginning of the quarter or the end of the quarter for first production? Thank you.  Miguel Martínez San Martín  Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA  A I mean, basically, the rating agencies will look for a division. They put on top of it the cash flow you generate, but  the cash flow with their considerations. I mean that is not the cash flow we normally use. And as a dividend – I'm  sorry, I mean, they divide that by a debt. And in that debt, it's not the debt that we are used to, it's also a type of  debt they consider. So in their metrics, and with that, I will answer the second question, they will consider the  leases and they calculate the present value of these leases and consider it as debt today. So in that sense, our LNG  divisions had approximately €1 billion in debt. And with the considerations of the agencies, they considered €4  billion. And the difference, this €3 billion, are due to the leases, basically the tankers and the pipelines in Canada  and in the U.S, okay?

texts.speaker: Henry J. Morris
texts.profession: Analyst, Goldman Sachs International Ltd.
texts.text: Great, thanks very much. And sorry, just to – just to follow-up quickly on LNG. Is it then your impression from  rating agencies that if you were to sell this entire business, and obviously it depends on the price you get, but that  would be enough to maintain investment grade, and you therefore wouldn't need to compare the preference  shares?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: I mean it's something we have to reach. We don't know yet which is going to be the proceeds who are going to  bank. But I think that the perspective from the rating agencies would be by far more positive if we are able to sell  the LNG. Think that the equation, they've put – and I'm talking in just by mind, but probably the EBITDA we have  in that division is approximately €600 billion. And if you divide that by the €4 billion, they are considering, as you  realize that the ratio is quite below what the agencies are asking for as investment grade. So, my perception is that  it would be an important step to keep the investment grade.

texts.speaker: Irene Himona

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Starting with the operational activity, I would like to highlight the following, in the Upstream business during this  quarter, production of hydrocarbons reached 359,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, which represents a 12%  increase year-on-year. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: From an operational standpoint Kinteroni is ready to start production. However, we are working on some  commercial arrangements. The Peruvian government decision is that gas reserves from Block 57 replace the ones  related to Block 88 as the guarantee to the Peru LNG export facility. In consequence, some contract modification  between Camisea and Peru LNG need to be made, since gas from Block 57 will be sold to Peru LNG. We are  making progress and expect to start production shortly.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation to the JV with SandRidge in the Mississippian Lime, we are reducing the production forecast. This  reduction is due to the new plants released by SandRidge after the changes in the board with a stronger focus on  value creation, rather than production volumes.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: For this year, we expect to produce in average 7,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We are in permanent  contact with the new management with the aim of approving in the following months 2014 activity.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Let me emphasize that the 10% production growth target for the year is achievable. Regarding our 2013  exploratory activity, we have already achieved the 300 million barrels of oil equivalent, annual target of  contingent resources addition.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Turning now to our seismic activity, we finished our campaign in campus BM-C-33 in Brazil and started  campaigns in Australia, Bulgaria, and Venezuela. In relation to the exploratory acreage we've got a four new  licenses in Norway in the Norwegian balance sheet where we will be the operator in two of them. We have also  acquired additional acreage in Guyana and Indonesia.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: On the LNG sale, we continue working on the closing of the transaction along with Shell. We have received all the  anti-trust approvals and we will be continuing with the initial plan to close the deal before the year end.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Let me start now with the results. This quarter we've released a CCS adjusted net income of €509 million, 6%  higher year-on-year, and a CCS adjusted operating income of €979 million, 5% higher than in the same quarter  last year. In the first half of the year we released a CCS adjusted net income of €1.2 billion, 26% higher year-on- year and a CCS adjusted operating income of €2.3 billion, 14% higher than during the first half of 2012. In absent,  the adjusted operating income during the second quarter 2013 was €514 million in line with the same quarter of  last year, mainly due to the increasing production but lower realization prices.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Repsol crude realization prices had a better performance on Brent due to higher volumes in Brazil and in the U.S.  While gas realization prices decreased year-on-year due to the sales volume mix. These two price effect have a  negative impact of €71 million. Other minor items explain the remaining differences.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving on to the LNG, adjusted operating income in the second quarter was €170 million versus €78 million  posted during the same quarter last year. We achieved higher volumes and stronger marketing margins along with  a better performance in our North American operations.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Downstream business, adjusted CCS operating income in the second quarter 2013 was €147 million, 28%  down year-on-year. The results of our resilient marketing business could not offset the lower result in the – in this  industrial businesses.
