texts.profession: Analyst, Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
texts.text: And then my second question was, looking at North America, if you were to get into either a shale play, so an  unconventional shale play in the U.S. or an oil sands play in Canada, do you feel that you've got the capability at  present to operate or would you only look at that on a non-operated basis? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And talking about capabilities to operate whether in shale or oil sands, really those are capabilities that are not  today in the Company. But this doesn't mean that operation will not be there or it will be there. We will have to  see. Right now, there is nothing on the table. So, basically, what I can tell you is that those capabilities are not in  our Company. Is that okay, Anish?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: I think that it's way too early to think of it. I don't see easy to really obtain this reversing of the pipelines. And on  top of that, there are more questions like the license to export LNG. At the end, you will end up with a huge  question mark in the table, whether or not U.S. is going to allow massive LNG exports or not. So, right now,  there's nothing there and we are not thinking in reversing pipelines. Is that okay, Richard?

file: REP - Q2 2015 Earnings Call 30July2015 700 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 31-Jul-15.pdf

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Thank you, Ángel, and thank you all for attending this conference on the second quarter 2015 results. This quarter  we're integrating the results of Talisman assets from May 8, 2015. CCS adjusted net income was €312 million and  €1.2 billion for the quarter and the first half of the year respectively.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Turning now to the market environment and main operational highlights, during the second quarter of the year  the weakness in the oil prices continued, counterweighted by a strong U.S. dollar. Brent crude prices recorded a  maximum of $66.7 per barrel in May, an average $61.9 per barrel in the quarter, an $8 per barrel increase  compared to the previous quarter.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Nevertheless, during the beginning of this third quarter, we have observed that the weakness of the oil price  continued. In relation with gas prices, they were also weak during the quarter. Henry Hub averaged $2.6 per  million Btu, a figure that compares with a $3 per million Btu of the previous quarter, and with a $4.7 million per  million Btu of second quarter 2014.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In the second half of the year, the drilling schedules composed of a less risky exploration program and will entail  lower investment than in the first half. Talking about our development projects, this quarter is worth highlighting  the progress in Brazil, Venezuela, Colombia, Canada, Vietnam and Malaysia. In Brazil we continue with the ramp- up of Sapinhoá Norte, the third well was connected to our second FPSO in place, Cidade de Ilhabela, in May. Gas  injection commenced in June allowing gross production to increase to 90,000 barrels per day in this second  platform. At the end of 2015, peak production is expected to be reached in this second FPSO, which has a gross  capacity of 150,000 barrels per day. Together with the first FPSO, the field will reach the planned plateau of  270,000 barrels per day.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Venezuela, [indiscernible] (7:00) at the end of the quarter, Repsol has started up the first producing well at the  Perla field, the largest offshore gas field in Latin America holding 17 Tcfs of gas in place. This first phase of the  development will produce 150 million of standard cubic feet per day, rising to 450 million cubic feet per day, by  the end of 2015. With the startup of this field, the eighth key growth project of our 2012-2016 (sic) [2016-2020]  (7:33) Strategic Plan has been delivered.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Colombia, the average gross production for CPO-9 block reached 10,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. The  block is operated by Ecopetrol 55% and Repsol owns 45%. We continue working on the definition of the field  development plan for the Akacias project in this block, with the final investment decision expected before year  end. Exploration activities in other areas of the block are moving forward also.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Turning to production, the average production for the quarter stood at 525,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.  This figure is 55% higher year-on-year. Production from Talisman assets has been included since May 8. Out of  the overall figure, 182,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day come from the recently acquired assets. Excluding  Talisman assets, production increased 1% year-on-year, thanks to the ramp-up of Sapinhoá in Brazil, partially  offset by the maintenance work carried out in Trinidad and Tobago. For the full year, we expect a 6% production  increase on average on an homogeneous basis. That is to say, stripping out Libya from both periods. This increase  is in line with the goal established in our Strategic Plan.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Average production in June stood at 660,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. The contribution of former  Talisman assets in June has been on average 307,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Our 660,000 barrels of  current production is split as follows: 190,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day produced in North America region.  Marcellus has averaged 73,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, and Eagle Ford 25,000 barrels of oil equivalent  per day, with Canada delivering 54,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. 108,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day  produced in Asia and Russia, most of it in the new Southeast Asia core region. 93,000 barrels of oil equivalent per  day produced in Europe, Africa, and Brazil, out of which, 40,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day come from  former Talisman positions in Norway and in the UK. Unfortunately, we still cannot produce in Libya. 269,000  barrels of oil equivalent per day produced in South America region, out of which 21,000 barrels of oil equivalent  per day come from former Talisman production in Colombia. Out of this productive areas, let me go into more  detail in Marcellus and Eagle Ford, where in June, as mentioned, we produced 73,000 barrels of oil equivalent per  day and 25,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Regarding the Marcellus, our acreage is held by production allowing us great flexibility in our CapEx decision.  This year began with two drilling rigs, but has been reduced to only one for the remainder of the year, which will  allow us to maintain a production plateau of above 400 million cubic feet per day net of royalties with self  sustained cash flow at the given current price scenario. Gas price will direct the pace of growth of this asset.  During the first half of the year, 17 development wells were drilled in our play and production from the  Friendsville area continued to ramp up following completion of gas compression facilities.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In addition, Repsol participates in a third-party non-operated program focused on the liquids-rich part of the  play. During the first half of the year, 63 new development wells were drilled in our acreage, equivalent to 19 net  wells for Repsol.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Moving now to the operational highlights in the Downstream divisions, with regard to the refining environment,  we have achieved an average margin of $9.1 per barrel, slightly above that of the previous quarter. In comparison  with the second quarter of last year, the margin improved $6 per barrel, thanks to the generalized strengthening  of the spreads of products together with lower energy cost, the high complexity of our refining system and the self- consumption efficiency program helped to capture the benefits of the existing scenario. The distillation utilization  rate was 89% during the quarter, while conversion run at full capacity.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In gas and power, sales volume decreased and the price environment in North America was tougher. The  Algonquin gas price reference averaged $2.2 per million btu in the second quarter, well below the value registered  in the second quarter of 2014, which was $4.2.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Regarding the outlook for the rest of the year, with a Brent oil price assumption of $59 per barrel in 2015 and  Henry Hub of $3, we expect to achieve an EBITDA between €5 billion and €5.5 billion for the full year. Talisman  assets will contribute with an EBITDA of €800 million. Therefore, the outlook for 2015 EBITDA, excluding the  contribution from Talisman assets is a figure in the same range as to that obtained in 2014, even in an oil price  scenario almost $40 lower than that of the previous year and having no contribution from Libya.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: I'd like to stop now to explain what we are doing in order to reduce and optimize costs and CapEx. Repsol, as  always, or especially in the current situation, applied strict cost efficiency culture and is fully committed with the  optimization of the OpEx and CapEx program. In Downstream, efforts in the last years have been focused on an  ongoing energy efficiency saving program, on optimizing oil purchases and on the maintenance and reliability  programs, all of which have led to a refining margin increase of $1.2 per barrel as compared with 2011. Efforts  continue in this area.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In relation with the Upstream CapEx, a full review of every single project is underway, stopping or delaying  investments in those which value is at risk in the current scenario. Repsol invested slightly below $4.5 billion in  Upstream CapEx including G&G and G&A in 2014. I would like to underline that in 2015, with Talisman assets  onboard since May, Repsol will maintain Upstream CapEx at the same level as 2014.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Now let's move to the second quarter 2015 earnings performance. CCS adjusted net income was €312 million, 20%  lower compared with the same period of last year. CCS adjusted net income of the first half of the year was €1.2  billion, 35% higher compared with the same period of last year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Starting with the Upstream business, adjusted net income for the second quarter was minus €48 million. This  result has been mainly affected by the drop in crude oil and gas realization prices, partially compensated by the  growth in production and the decrease in exploration costs. Excluding the impact of exploration cost, operating  income of the Upstream division would have been positive in both the second quarter and the first half of 2015.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: The year-on-year performance, excluding the effect of the consolidated of Talisman is explained as follow. Lower  crude and gas realization prices had a negative impact at the operating level of €359 million. Higher production,  thanks mainly to the ramp-up of Sapinhoá, partially offset by the maintenance works carried out in Trinidad and  Tobago, resulted in a positive impact of €37 million. Lower exploration costs lead to an increase in the operating  income of €128 million and the decreased costs were mainly due to lower amortization of dry wells. Higher  depreciation charges, due to higher production had a negative impact of €37 million. Taxes had a positive impact  of €89 million.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Turning to our Downstream division, CCS adjusted net income in the quarter was €439 million, which compares  with €162 million of the second quarter 2014. Drilling down into the quarterly results, in refining, we saw a year- on-year increase in margins from $3.1 per barrel to $9.1 per barrel, due to a generalized strengthening of the  product spreads and to lower energy costs, derived from the efforts in efficiency undertaking in the last years.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In the petrochemical business, wider margins and higher volumes allow us to improve the operating income by  €133 million. This improvement is due to the competitiveness programs implemented together with a better  market environment. In the commercial businesses, the weaker result in the LPG business was the main driver of  the €55 million decrease in the operating income. Moving to gas power and trading, this business increased their  joint operating income in €24 million. The exchange rate effect was positive by €116 million when compared year- on-year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Regarding the outlook for the full year 2015, our estimated EBITDA is figure in the same range as that obtained in  2014, even in a $40 per barrel low oil price scenario, and having no contribution from Libya.

texts.speaker: Brendan Warn
texts.profession: BMO Capital Markets Ltd.
texts.text: Yeah. Hi, guys, and thanks for the opportunity to ask a couple of questions and just two questions, if I may. Just  first question, I guess, more broadly on the acquisition and referring back to your presentation at the time of the  acquisition, slide 24, where you talked about creating value and the IRR being above WACC. Can you give us a  sense now having seen the assets and the assets being in your control, just sort of what oil price you expect IRR  would need to be for IRR to be above WACC and considering your higher synergy ability of $350 million? And  then just second question, could you just zero in on the UK North Sea assets, just in terms of how much of a drag  they are, obviously on the performance of the assets that you bought and what sort of plans you expect to take  forward to create values from those assets, please?

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: And then the final question I have is in relation to the Upstream OpEx efficiency that you'd highlighted in the  previous call. I think you've talked about a $5 per barrel reduction in Upstream costs that you were targeting. I  wonder if you could just give us a sense of whether that's still the case, whether you could maybe do more or any  update there would be very helpful. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Downstream, our refineries have launched a new CO2 reduction program, which implies better results, thanks  to the energy consumption, energy cost reduction that goes along with it. In chemicals, we have between many  other projects to reduce the cracker capacity in Puertollano, which will give us extra margins. So, the GO program  is a long one.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: And finally, in relation with the $5, I mentioned if you remember, $1 was cost reduction, $2 were due to  exploration reduction and the other $2 were due to the mix of our production because we have several projects  that are ramping up. So the extra cost of the new barrel is much lower than the once we had in the past. So the  combination of those is $5 per barrel, which is what I mentioned in the last quarter results presentation, and we  expect to improve that. I cannot tell you how much it will be, but our goal, our objective, it would be to reach the  $9 per barrel of reduction, in which I include $5 I mentioned before. So $4 extra is the objective. Whether we  reach it or not, it would be on our hands.

texts.speaker: Anish Kapadia
texts.profession: Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
texts.text: Hi. Good afternoon. I have three questions, please. First one was, could you just give us some idea of – you're  going to have a CapEx reduction in 2016. What was the impact of production – what's the impact on production of  the CapEx reduction in 2016? And would it lead to a reduction in proved reserves in North America when in a low  oil price environment?

texts.speaker: Anish Kapadia
texts.profession: Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
texts.text: Just going back to the first question. What – we're just trying to get a sense of, more in terms of North America,  and given your reducing CapEx over there, would you expect productions to fall in North America next year and  given the reduction in CapEx and low oil prices, would you expect reserves to have to be de-booked?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: I mean, first, I'd say that a possible reduction in production in North America, which is possible because as we  mentioned in the speech, we are going to drill for cash and free cash could be a reduction, but it's not our main  concern. I mean, globally production will grow, and in North America, we'll drive for those – as much as the  scenario allowed us to. In the existing scenario, probably would be CapEx reduction and reduction of the main  production. But I don't see it as a major concern. Okay, Anish? Anish?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: And with the addition of Talisman, really the reserves figure is something that will appear once we end our budget  work, but our concern today it's totally focused on free cash generation and not in size. I mean, as mentioned, with  the organic capabilities of Talisman assets and Repsol assets, we'd be reaching more than 900,000 barrels of oil  equivalent as production per day, and this is not the objective. This is also one advantage we have right now  because we don't have any need as others may have to maintain our production. I mean, it's not our goal anymore.  We are looking for value, not for size. Okay?

texts.speaker: Filipe Rosa
texts.profession: Banco Espirito Santo de Investimento SA (Broker)
texts.text: My second question relates to Downstream and the strength in refining and in the chemicals business. You have  done a significant restructuring in the chemicals division. Refining margins are – I don't know, I think that  everybody is surprised by their resilience. Going into 2016, are you assuming a reduction of your profitability in  the Downstream in a scenario of stabilization of oil price, or do you think that in a scenario of stable oil price at  the current level, your industrial businesses in Downstream could maintain their profitability? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Thanks Jon. I don't know if I have the answer for the first one. Sometimes, the refining beats the index, sometimes  it doesn't, and I don't have the slightest idea on why last quarter they improved by I think it was something like  $0.60 or something like that index while in this quarter, they have been almost at the same level. I think they're  something like $0.10 below. But I don't have the slightest, I mean – I don't have answer other than the – that in  Bilbao in Petronor there was a maintenance for something like 15 days that may have affected the CCS margin that  we have reached this quarter, but it's the only reason that I can think of right now.

texts.speaker: Matt P. Lofting
texts.profession: Nomura International Plc
texts.text: Perfect. Thanks Ángel. Thanks for your comments, Miguel. Just two things, if I could. Firstly just on the cash flow  and the cash cycle, if you could just add any sort of comments in terms of how you see that the cash cycle on an  underlying basis this year and then perhaps next year at current forward curve oil prices given the sort of  additional comments you made around CapEx plans, assuming I guess in the background that you continue to  sort of look to utilize the scrip on the dividend side.

texts.speaker: Marc B. Kofler
texts.profession: Jefferies International Ltd.
texts.text: [indiscernible] (01:14:00) Miguel, thanks very much for the presentation. Just two questions from me, please. And  I suppose the first one is sort of building on the previous question. Acknowledging your comments around the  current scenario and weathering the storm so to speak, are you able to put a timeout there as to when you think  the Talisman assets can be free cash flow generative? And then secondly, this one is probably more mechanical,  given the strategic update plans early November, should we expect some potential divestments before that  update? Thanks.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Well, I was starting to get concerned, because nobody was asking anything about Gas Natural. Thank you Nitin for  your call. I was starting to become nervous. I mean, our idea is to keep Gas Natural. Gas Natural is a great asset. It  gives us a very good [indiscernible] (01:21:19) and only, only and put that in – I mean only, if it's totally necessary  to maintain the investment grade, we will think of divesting Gas Natural, okay. So it would be somehow the silver  bullet if you want to call it that way.

file: REP - Q2 2016 Earnings Call 28July2016 700 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 28-Jul-16.pdf

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Thank you, Paul, and thank you to those online for attending this conference call on our second quarter 2016  results. CCS adjusted net income was €345 million and €917 million for the quarter and the first half of 2016  respectively.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Let's now continue with an update on our progress towards the delivery of our strategic objectives. Moving on to  our efficiency and synergy program, we continue to make good progress in 2016 and are on track to deliver the  cost savings targets set out in our strategic plan.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: More generally, the implementation of cost saving initiative across all parts of our business has progressed as  expected in the second quarter, with highlights that follows. In Upstream, in the first half of the year, we have  achieved more than 50% of our full year objective. And by year-end we expect to be well above the OpEx and  CapEx reduction targets that we have set for the year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Looking forward, although oil price improved in the second quarter compared to the lower levels observed early in  the year, we remain cautious on the short term recovery of commodities and continue to focus our efforts on  achieving cost neutrality at around $40 price level.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Before going into detail on the results, let me now describe the market environment and main operational  highlights in the quarter. At the macro level, during the second quarter, oil price recovered marginally and Brent  crude averaged $45 per barrel compared to $62 in the second quarter of 2015, and to $34 in the first quarter of  the year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Gas price were stable in the quarter with Henry Hub average $2 per million BTU, lower than the $2.6 of observed  in the second quarter of 2015. In recent weeks, there's has been a change in this trend with Henry Hub near more  future contracts seeing some support and averaging around $2.8 per million BTU.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Turning now to the operational activity, let me start with the Upstream. Average production in the quarter stood at  697,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. This is 33% higher year-on-year mainly due to a full quarter of volumes  from acquired assets versus only a partial contribution in the second quarter of last year. Together with the ramp- up of Cardon in Venezuela, Sapinhoá in Brazil, and contribution from Gudrun in Norway, along with higher  production in Peru.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: These effects were partially offset by the ramp-up of Sapinhoá and higher gas production in Peru. In the month of  July, production has continued in line with the second quarter.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Brazil, the hookup of the PFCO (sic) [FPSO] (11:05) at Lapa has been concluded. And the installation of flow  lines is currently ongoing. According to the operator, first oil is expected in the third quarter, one quarter ahead of  schedule.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In the UK, we continued to reduce our lifting costs with CapEx and OpEx below plan, and production ahead of  schedule, while development projects, MonArb and Flyndre and Cawdor progressed towards first oil in the first  half of 2017.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In North America, production in the Marcellus has increased year-on-year while reducing drilling activity to one rig  with a cash breakeven close to the $2 per million BTU. This asset is cash generative at gas price levels observed  since the end of the quarter.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Moving to Latin America, in Peru, the gross production from Kinteroni increased in April to 160 million square  cubic feet of gas per day. The development of the Sagari discovery is continuing with first gas planned for 2018.  This development will raise total production from Block 57 above 200 million square feet of gas per day once on- stream.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Trinidad and Tobago, the execution of projects to increase production is ongoing. The development of Juniper  is reaching its final stages and a startup is planned for 2017. This offshore shallow water project will reach a peak  production of 95,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day and is 100% owned and operated by our BPTT joint venture  where Repsol holds a 30% stake.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Now let's move on the second quarter earnings performance. Second quarter 2016 CCS adjusted net income was  €345 million, 100% higher compared to the second quarter of last year. CCS adjusted net income of the first half  of the year was €917 million, 26% lower compared to the same period of last year that include significant post -tax  gain coming from the exchange rate positions due to the net long cash position in dollars held for the acquisition  of Talisman.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Looking at the results by division, starting with the Upstream business. Adjusted net income for the second  quarter was €46 million positive, €94 million higher than in the same period of 2015. Overall, compared to the  same period in 2015, lower oil and gas price realization in the second quarter of 2016 were offset by the impact of  higher volumes, lower cost resulting from our efficiency project and lower exploration expenses.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: As a result of lower exploration activity, principally due to lower amortization of dry wells, the operating income  increased by €144 million, excluding the exchange rate effect. Lower crude oil and gas price, net of royalties, had  a negative impact on the operating income of €372 million.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Turning to the Downstream division, CCS adjusted net income in the quarter was €378 million, 14% lower than in  the second quarter of last year. Drilling down into the quarterly results in Refining. Lower utilization rates along  with lower refining margins due to the planned maintenance reduced operating income by €224 million. The  refining margin indicators declined in the period compared to the second quarter of 2015 due to narrower middle  distillate and light-heavy crude spreads, partially offset by lower energy costs.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: With regards to Gas Natural Fenosa, adjusted net income in the second quarter of 2016 amounted to €96 million,  9% lower year-on-year, mainly due to the lower profits in the gas commercialization business attributable to the  current price environment.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: To conclude, we remain cautious on the pace of long-term commodity price recovery, and expect further volatility  going forward. That framework, we will continue to strength our balance sheet through portfolio actions whilst  maturing synergies and implementing self-help measures that will reduce the group cash neutrality breakeven to  our $40 objective.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Second, the gasoline spreads that were quite nice, I would say, in the first half of the year has shrink which makes  sense due to the end of the driving season for the refiners. And we have not seen yet the increase in the diesel  spreads. So, all in, right now it's true that refining margins are a little low.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Having say so, I think that the main factor is going to be the weather in the fourth quarter. And also one thing we  have realized since June when we finished both the maintenance in Cartagena and Tarragona is that we are well  above the index.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: I mean, the improvement in operational capabilities, plus the energy efficiency we have gained with this  maintenance is giving us an extra room. And then, we will have to see. But this is what I can tell you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: So, I may say that the first two can be a range and the third one is something we may guess based on the price  finally – final price of oil you have in your estimates. But one thing is clear, I think that we should shrink that figure  before the year ends.

texts.speaker: Anish Kapadia
texts.profession: Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
texts.text: Secondly, just wondering if you'd talk a bit more about petchems. It's interesting they were saying kind of different  dynamic it seems in terms of petchem demand versus the refining demand for the gasoline and middle distillates. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The strength of North American unconventional production together with the recovery of Libyan and Nigerian  volumes put pressure on oil price despite the decision by OPEC to extend its production restrictions.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The Chemical business continued to benefit from investments in energy and operational efficiency and generated  record levels of EBIT based on our sustained improvement in the trading environment. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Let me now go into detail on the main operational highlights from the quarter. Starting with the Upstream division,  quarterly production averaged 677,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, a 2% decrease versus first quarter, but in  line with guidance for 2017.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The sale of Ogan Komering and fluctuating gas demand in Indonesia was partially offset by higher than budget  production in Libya. In the UK North Sea, we delivered first production  from MonArb redevelopment project with the startup of the Shaw and Cayley fields. Repsol holds a 30% net stake  in this project and the redevelopment will extend the life of the MonArb fields beyond 2030.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Brazil, the ramp up of Lapa progresses on track and the hookup of an additional production well in July has put  gross production at 60,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. In Trinidad and Tobago, we expect to achieve the first  gas from Juniper in the third quarter. The joint ventures partners also approved the FID of Angelin in June with an  expected startup of production in 2019.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving now to exploration; higher activity quarter-on-quarter resulted in the completion of five exploratory and  one appraisal wells, with two of the exploratory and the appraisal wells being declared positive. The Savannah  and Macadamia discoveries in Trinidad and Tobago have unlocked approximately 2 Tcf of gas in place that will  support ongoing deliveries and the production plateau of our joint venture.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Now, moving on to the financial results, I'll briefly summarize the principal outcomes for the quarter. Second  quarter 2017 CCS adjusted net income was €496 million, €151 million higher than in the same period of 2016.  The EBITDA at CCS stood at €1.5 billion, €300 million increase year-on-year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Downstream, CCS adjusted net income was €429 million, €51 million higher than in the second quarter of  2016, principally due to better results in Trading and Gas & Power, growth in petrochemical margins, higher  distillation volumes in Refining and higher margins in Peru. These were offset by a lower Refining margin indicator  and then lower contribution from LPG following disposals last year.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Our lower capital guidance allows us to maintain production whilst supporting the ongoing development of future  projects. In fact, the current Upstream portfolio of projects on production and in development included the recently  sanctioned Red Emperor and Buckskin projects are capable of maintaining a plateau at around 700,000 barrels a  day through 2022. Future major projects identified, but not yet sanctioned have the potential to stand this plateau  or raise overall production volumes.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: So I may say that one-third has been efficiencies and two-thirds refer to the market, basically, the improvement,  not only in the naphtha price, but also in the dual feedstock that we have achieved for our system with LPGs on  naphtha being used alternatively. So I would say two-thirds for the market, one-third, which implies that if we turn  back to the lower part of the cycle instead of being zero or a little below zero, we'd be around €200 million EBIT;  this in relation with Chemicals.

texts.text: Thanks, Paul. Good afternoon. I just had a couple of questions, please. First of all, Venezuela, if you could  possibly remind us of what is your exposure. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA

texts.speaker: Anish Kapadia
texts.profession: Analyst, Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
texts.text: And then the second one is switching to the U.S., in your Northeast gas position in the U.S., I think the capital  allocation there is obviously quite gas price sensitive and I think you've talked about potentially hedging some of  your gas price exposure in the Northeast. texts.profession: Analyst, Bank of America Merrill Lynch

texts.profession: Analyst, Goldman Sachs International
texts.text: Thank you, Paul. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And as mentioned, we have a small area in the north of Spain which we already can charge our electric vehicles  there. Okay, Michele?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: So, basically, I may say that both in Cardon, the system we have agreed with the authorities to monetize our gas,  and in Petroquiriquire with the [indiscernible] (54:05) account, both systems are working, not at a perfect level, I  may say Quiriquire is doing quite well, and, in the case of Cardon, more or less we are recovering about 60% –  high 50s, 57% of our billing. texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And in relation with the quantity, well, right now, what we pretend is to be in the first quartile, both in the oil sector  with our peers in oil and also being in the first quartile in the Ibex 35%. So this is more or less where we want to  be in relation with the quantity.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In addition, Luis Cabra has been appointed new Executive Managing Director of Technology Development,  Resources and Sustainability. texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Our 2018 to 2020 investment budget increases to €15 billion, a 35% rise compared to the previous three years  period. A total of €11 billion will be invested in the core upstream and downstream portfolios, and an additional €4  billion will be devoted to expanding the downstream and to building a new low carbon gas and power business.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: The expected €2.5 billion investment in low carbon to 2020 includes the €750 million acquisition of the hydro and  CCGT generation assets, and of course, the retail business of Viesgo. The transaction is expected to be  completed in the fourth quarter of the year, once all regulatory approval has been received.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: On the development side, work has continued at Bunga Pakma in Malaysia, which achieved first gas early two or  three weeks ago. This project is expected to produce around 150 million gross standard cubic feet of gas per day,  enabling the PM3 asset in Malaysia to meet its gas delivery commitments for the coming years. In exploration, a  total of five wells were finished in the quarter, of which three were declared successful, while the remaining two  were deemed negative.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving on now to the financial results, I will summarize the main figures for the second quarter of the year and  how they compare with the same period of 2017. Second quarter 2018 CCS adjusted net income was €549  million, €104 million higher than in the same period in 2017. Upstream adjusted net income was €360 million, a  €245 million increase compared to the second quarter in 2017, driven mainly by higher realized prices, in the oil  case, higher production volumes, and lower amortization rates, partially offset by higher taxes and a negative  exchange rate effect.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Downstream division, the CCS adjusted net income was €337 million in the quarter, €92 million lower than  in the same period of 2017, mostly due to lower results in Chemicals, affected by the shutdown of the Sines  cracker, lower margins in Peru, and the negative exchange rate effect. These impacts were partially offset by  better results in refining in Europe, marketing and trading.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Finally, let me now finish with some comments on the outlook for the remainder of the year. Our revised CapEx  forecast for 2018 amounts to around €4 billion, of which around €2.3 billion, and $2.7 billion – $2.8 billion will be  invested in Upstream; €0.9 billion in Downstream and €0.8 billion in the new low carbon business before the end  of the year. Upstream production is expected to stay at around 715,000 net barrels per day, 720,000 net barrels  per day, subject to the fluctuations in Libya.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Downstream business, we are expecting the refining margin indicator to stay around $7 on average for  2018, and with all planned maintenance for the year already completed. This quarter, our Refining system will  benefit from having all this distillation and conversion capacity available and our current forecast expects to  generate a premium in the real CCS margin during the second half of the year.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In conclusion, based on our performance in the first half of the year, we remain on track to deliver on our targets  for 2018, while working on the updated strategic objectives through 2020. During the next three years, we aim to  deliver value growth based on improved shareholder returns, increase the profitability across our portfolio, and we  expect to build our low carbon gas and power business funded by organic cash flow and the proceeds received  from the disposal of our stake in Gas Nat. Under a conservative Brent price scenario, we will be able to increase  our CapEx, grow our shareholder remuneration by 8% annually and implement a share buyback program to offset  the dilution associated with the scrip.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Looking into our full year 2018 results, with no more major maintenance plan in industrial businesses, we expect a  stronger contribution from the Downstream in the second half of the year, while the Upstream continues to benefit  from the recovery in crude oil prices.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Talking about the capital investment, and if you remember a lot of you that in the road show last month, I  underlined the message that these additional cash coming from the oil price was going to be offset by the building  of the inventory related to these new prices. texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Talking about the $70, I mean, first of all, we have to see growth happen. But let me say, I'm going to be very  prudent, in any case, in the capital discipline of this company. texts.profession: Analyst, RBC Europe Ltd.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA

Jason Kenney  Analyst, Banco Santander SA (London Branch)  Q  My question for the resources on, with the Viesgo acquisition, do you think you'll separate out the gas power and  renewables division at some point? And secondly, on the roadmap for return on capital employed, can  you just remind us of the upside for return on capital employed over the coming strategic plan period, please?

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: So, thank you, Jason. I mean, of course, in the coming months after closing the deal, we'll decide the whole  organization and incorporate in the corporate level and in the business level of Viesgo. Today, we don't have a  decision about that. But let me say that what we have in Viesgo today is gas and power business.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: And going to the power, what we have is the combined cycle side that is fully integrated in the gas chain, and we  have the hydraulic link to the pumping that is, let me say, perhaps [indiscernible] (51:35) technical terms, but is  more a today a trading tool for power, taking into account the volatility we have in the Spanish [indiscernible]  (51:47) price over the whole day than our pure production asset. So, I mean, that's going to be decided after the  closing of Viesgo. But the driver of the decision is going to be to optimize our position in the market, extracting the  maximum value of the assets we are acquiring. You will be able to track the results, of course, at the end of the  year.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Looking at the capital employed increase during the strategic plan, I mean I maintain the guidance. We commit  and we define when we presented in June the strategic plan. I mean, €11 billion for the whole three years period  2018, 2019, 2020 in the Downstream and Upstream businesses. On top of that, we are going to invest an  additional €1.5 billion in the new growing activities in the Downstream. I'm talking about the lubricants, trade-in,  the international expansion of the service station business and so on. And as I said before, this €2.5 billion  applied to the low carbon business is going to be decided depending the profitability and the return we could  expect from this project. And as I said in June, I'm going to prioritize the return over any need to develop or to  deploy or to invest this capital in the renewable side. Thank you, Jason.

texts.speaker: Operator

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: With regards to another growth project included in our strategic plan, Carbon 4 in Venezuela, on August 15, we  officially declared commerciality. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Third, we continue with the process to dispose our LNG division. Due to the confidentiality agreement we have  signed with the participant companies, we will make no further comments or answer any questions about the  process until a decision on the sale is made by the year end.

texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Let me share with you, the process is evolving according to our expectations. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving into the quarterly results, third quarter CCS adjusted net income was €496 million and CCS adjusted  operating income was €1.2 million (sic) [€1.2 billion] (12:39). texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the LNG division, the adjusted operating income was €189 million, 75% better than during the same period last  year. The increase was due to higher commercialization margins. The good performance comes  mainly from the refining business, where the gasoline and middle distillate differentials as well as the lowest  quality of the new crude in place and product deals due to the Cartagena and Bilbao new units have delivered an  average margin of $6.4 per barrel during the quarter.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The LPG results and higher volumes in the wholesale marketing of petroleum products partially offset the  decreasing margins and the 12% decrease in volumes in the retail marketing division, delivering an overall stable  result.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation to Gas Natural, the adjusted operating income of €231 million was 16% higher than during the same  period last year. The increase is due to improved results in the Latin America operations and better margins from  the natural gas sales.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Details from the Cartagena and Bilbao projects were smaller than we thought. So, we have some CapEx saves  there. So basically, I would say CapEx will be totally in line with estimates in the upstream division and  the shortfall would be between €200 million and €250 million in the downstream division.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Starting with the second one, I mean, for sure, it's only my opinion. So, the final decision would on the board. But  in my perception, the treasury shares will go into the scrip dividend. So basically, we will increase capital and  reduce at the same time the treasury stock. This is our initial idea and the one we will present to the board  meeting. texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA

Basically, we keep attached to the plan, but it's way too early. I mean, it's  only five months since we presented the strategic plan. So, I don't know what else can I comment to you. Simply  that probably next year, we'd be around 6,000 barrels oil per day that we'll keep working.

file: REP - Q3 2013 Earnings Call 7November2013 700 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 07-Nov-13.pdf

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Starting with the results, in this quarter, the results were affected by a tough environment due to three factors:  disruptions in Libya, weak international refining margins and the dollar depreciation. As a consequence, we  obtained a CCS adjusted net income of €387  million, 22% lower year -on-year, and a CCS adjusted operating  income of €840 million, 33% lower than in the same quarter last year. In the first nine months of the year, CCS  adjusted net income amounted to €1.6 billion, 9% higher year-on-year and a CCS adjusted operating income of  €3.1 billion, 4% lower than in the first months of 2012.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Exploration costs were in line this quarter if compared to a same period last year. Higher G&A and geology cost  were compensated by lower cost of the dry wells. The increase in depreciation charges and in operating cost of the  new projects are still ramping up, together with increased maintenance cost and the absence of the revenue that  we booked last year for the lease of the Scarabeo-9 rig had a total negative impact of €140 million. Other minor  items such as the exchange rates explain the remaining differences.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving on to the LNG, adjusted operating income in the third quarter of 2013 was €129 million, versus €189  million posted during the same quarter last year because of the increase in the number of cargo sold to Manzanillo  which are linked to Henry Hub prices.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Downstream business, adjusted CCS operating income in the second quarter of 2013 was €143 million, 53%  down year-on-year. In the refining business, we were able to run our combustion units at full capacity even though  we continue suffering weak margins in Europe. The decrease in margins year-on-year was mainly due to narrower  international products spreads versus Brent, partially offset by the wider light heavy crude spread.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: The CCS refining margin in the quarter reached $3.30 per barrel. The decrease in refining margins caused a  negative impact of €163 million. In the chemicals division, a better environment in prices and higher volumes had  a positive impact of €20 million.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: During the third quarter, the production of hydrocarbons reached an average of 344,000 barrels of oil equivalent  per day, a 1% increase compared to the third quarter of 2012. Throughout the quarter, we suffered disruptions of  our production in Libya due to the shutdown by activist groups of the pipeline that transport the crude oil to the  Zawiyah export terminal. The effect of the disruptions in the quarter was that production fell by 20,000 barrels of  oil per day. We maintain committed and confident to achieve our expected 7 % compound annual production  growth rate between 2012 and 2016.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Peru, we are in the process of closing the commercial contracts needed to replace the gas reserves from Block  88 in Camisea, as a guarantee for the Peru LNG export facility with those from Kinteroni in Block 57 .

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Bolivia, the second phase of the Margarita-Huacaya project came on stream on budget and one month ahead of  schedule. The project will add 5,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day to our production. The potential of the  Margarita and Huacaya field is huge and we are starting to consider a third phase that could be executed in  a short  timeframe to deliver up to 18 million cubic meters per day by 2016, provided that the additional  commercialization volumes can be secured.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Brazil, covering production from the first well of the Sapinhoá field is above the initial expectations at around  30,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. If the productivity of the wells follows this pattern, we will only need four  wells instead of the initial estimate of five in order to fulfill the total capacity of the first FPSO of 120,000 barrels  of oil equivalent per day.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Due to the adverse weather conditions, we had a delay in installing the submersible buoy system. We expect to  connect the next well to the FPSO in Sapinhoá in February and at least two more wells during the first half of  2014. This delay will have only a minor impact, taking into consideration that we expect to connect the second and  third well in October and November, respectively. The second FPSO, Cidade de Ilhabela, is expected to arrive on  time in the second half of 2014.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving on to Carioca, a new well has proven the prospectivity of the southwest flank. Furthermore, last week, a  letter of intent to charter an FPSO for a period of 20 years was signed. Expected to start producing in the second  half of 2016, this platform will have a processing capacity of up to 100,000 barrels of oil per day and 5 million  cubic meters per day of natural gas.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In Campos 33, the Ocean Mylos Rig arrived to the drilling location and will be prepared to spud the first well in  the coming days. This rig has been contracted for a three-year period and can be extended by one or two  additional years, if needed. It will start drilling in Seat, where we see potential upsell in the addition of contingent  resources and will continue in Pão de Açúcar, which is the first target for the development, being the biggest  structure in the block.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Let us now cover our 2013 exploratory activity. During the first nine months of the year, 10 out of the 20  exploratory wells found hydrocarbons. These good results allow us to achieve the resources addition target that we  had in our strategic plan. We announced recently our related discovery, which corresponds to a high quality oil  well in Libya, very close to our producing assets in the Murzuq Basin.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation to the exploration acreage, during 2013, we have been acquiring further acreage to secure a su bstantial  future growth. We have strengthened our portfolio this year by acquiring more acreage in OECD countries like  Canada, U.S. and Norway, extending our exposure to carbonates, following the Perla play in Aruba, Colombia and  Nicaragua. And increasing our exposure in West Africa, where we were the highest bidders of the offshore Block  E13 in Gabon, where the formal approval – where the formal award is still pending.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Turning now to M&A in the LNG business, we would like to mention that the sale process to Shell continues  progressing as expected, in line with the estimated timetable for completion. Finally, in Peru and regarding the  potential divestment of our Downstream assets, the final binding offers have not fulfilled our expectations. So we  have ended the sale process.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In summary, the tough environment affected the quarterly results, mainly due to three factors. The disruptions in  Libya, the weak international refining margins and the dollar depreciation. Notwithstanding these factors in the  quarter, we were able to release a resilient set of results on a cumulative basis, with a 9% increase in our CCS  adjusted net income.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with Kinteroni, the situation is complex in Kinteroni. I mean, the whole facility is ready and it was  ready on budget and on time. But the government of Peru wants the Block 88, which was the backup of the LNG  facility, their production would be sent to the internal markets. So the Block 57 , which is the one in which  Kinteroni is located, is going to be the one that will back up the LNG facility.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: So in order to start production, we have to reach agreement, commercials agreement, in which we hav e the six  partners of Camisea involved. We also have the four partners of the LNG processing plant involved. We have the  lenders of the LNG facility also involved. And on top of that, in Block 57  where Kinteroni is located, our partner  Petrobras is selling right now its stake. So we also have to take this, the entrance of the new partner, in agreement.  And on top of that, we have the government of Peru. So it's quite difficult to assess a date for when Kinteroni will  start because, as you can see, we have more than 15 parts involved in the negotiation.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: Having said so, I think that things are moving, slowly but moving, and probably the closing and the start -up of  Kinteroni will be more or less at the same time that the closing of the LNG sale.

texts.speaker: Jason S. Kenney
texts.profession: Analyst, Banco Santander SA (London Branch)
texts.text: And then secondly on Gas Nat, I know there's been a lot of press speculation about this. Are you able to say  whether Temasek or Sinopec have indeed expressed an interest in your Gas Nat stake and potential timing for  divestment of Gas Nat presumably after the LNG sale?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: And in relation with the Gas Nat, I think that – I'd say that right now, we are starting to study which counterparts  or which companies would be interested in the stake, but it's way too early to provide you any color. I mean,  Gas  Natural is a great company. We are quite comfortable in our stake. It's true that the rationale behind the  operational activity, once we sell the LNG business, faint. And in that sense we have to study all possible  alternatives in relation with our portfolio and Gas Natural is part of it.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: We are not in a hurry and we are starting to study which transaction could improve our, I would say global  portfolio distribution. And only when we analyze which is the right move to do, we will do it, because other than  that, if we don't find an alternative for Gas Natural, we will keep the stake because I mean it's a very good  company and we have a positive covering of more than 47 0 basis point. That's all I can tell you, Jason.

texts.speaker: Filipe Rosa
texts.profession: Analyst, Banco Espirito Santo de Investimento SA (Broker)
texts.text: Hi, good morning, everyone. Three questions, if I may. The first one on CapEx, the accumulated CapEx in Q3  seems to be running well below the run rate for you to reach your target for the full year and then excluding Gas  Natural, I believe that Downstream is the division where the CapEx is running below. I don't know if you could  update your target for the full year for the CapEx ex -Gas Nat?

texts.speaker: Filipe Rosa
texts.profession: Analyst, Banco Espirito Santo de Investimento SA (Broker)
texts.text: And my final question relates to your relationship with Pemex, we talked about Gas Natural, we talked about  Sacyr, I don't know, could you give us your view on how do you see this potential interest of Pemex in setting up a  partnership with Y PF and would you adopt the same stance that you have adopted so far with other companies  that have signed partnerships with Y PF? Thank you very much.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Repsol SA
texts.text: In relation with the first one, the needed to desulfur the diesel and gasoline productions in Peru, at least the initial  estimate is approximately $7 50 million. We have a stake of $51 million. So basically, half of it would be on our  side. So we are talking about $37 5 million for a three-year period. So it's not that big, to say something.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Thank you, Ángel and good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Today I would like to discuss something which I  think is very material if somewhat unusual. It was a great loss for Total, the energy industry and those people everywhere trying to find solutions in a  complicated world.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: With regard to the refining environment, we saw a recovery of the refining margin indicators throughout Europe.  Thanks to the weaker oil prices and a strong maintenance season in the U.S. from which we benefit. In the last few  weeks, the downward trend in Brent crude prices has continued, reaching the lowest levels since November 2010.  Sustained improved refining margins are protecting us in the short term from this situation.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In the Gulf of Mexico, we have good news from two wells. León, our operated ultra-deepwater well where we have  found good quality oil sands with a net pay above 150 meters, we are currently evaluat ing the discovery.  Additionally, we have also completed appraisal work at the Buckskin and expect to move into front -end  engineering and design in 2015.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Brazil, in Campos 33, Seat 2 is programmed to run a test following the drilling of Pão de Açúcar, w hich we are  re-spudding now, after encountering a healthy oil column. A test was performed in the Sagitário well in Block 50  of Santos, confirming that this feature is a significant discovery.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Russia, we have three positive wells. 31-P and 32-P in the Karabashsky second block and K-3 well in the  Karabashsky third block in West Siberia. We carry out production test this year that confirm last year positive  results. In Alaska, we are finalizing the definition of two to three paths for the first development. We'll have  additional definition and potential confirmed from next winter drilling campaign.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Turning to production activity, during the quarter we reached an average of 366,000 barrels of oil equivalent per  day. The production was 6% higher year-on-year, and 8% if Libya is stripped out from both years. In Libya, we  resumed production on the 7th of July and we were able to produce at 50% of our full capacity during the  remaining part of the quarter.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Brazil, we have reached production of 100,000 barrels per day in gross terms with the first FPSO, and we are  expecting to have first oil from the second FPSO this month. This second FPSO is already in location. Sapinhoá  field will reach plateau for both FPSOs in the second half of 201 5.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Finally, I would like to briefly explain the recent acquisition of the Chilean company Compañía General de  Electricidad, CGE, by Gas Natural Fenosa. This acquisition reinforces the leadership of Gas Natural Fenosa in gas  distribution in Latin America, with the entrance in a stable and growing economy where Gas Natural Fenosa did  not have a presence; providing a platform for the consolidation for power distribution in LatAm and further  growth in power generation in Chile. This transaction is co nsistent with Gas Natural Fenosa's strategic priorities,  which aim to increase its international diversification.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In Gas Natural Fenosa, the €92 million adjusted net income in the third quarter of 2014 was 13% lower year on  year. This lower results are mainly explained by the lower results in the gas commercialization business, due to the  new regulation approved this year in Spain and the sale of the telecom business carried out during the second  quarter of 2014.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Additionally, I'd like to take this opportunity to underline the resilience of our earnings to this weaker crude oil  price environment. Since Repsol production is still 60% gassy, the quality and relative size of our Downstream  assets protect us along with a better performance of the spread of those pro ducts not indexed to crude oil prices.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: The negative correlation between oil prices and dollar-euro exchange rate also provides a hedge and the solid and  stable results from Gas Natural Fenosa are not affected by Brent price. Finally, we continue analyzing the market  in order to pursue a possible inorganic transaction and probably as a result of the new macroeconomic scenario  better opportunities could arise.

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Thanks, Ángel. Good afternoon. Thank you, Miguel, for the presentation as well. I actually would love to pick up  on the last point that you made around the inorganic sort of opportunities you're pursuing and just with regards to  the current environment. Clearly, as you say, lower oil price may allow you to acquire something at a more  attractive price; however, I just wanted to understand how you're finding the evolution of bid/ask spreads  effectively with sellers. Are you finding that sellers are willing to discuss valuations at lower oil prices or is that  actually potentially providing some challenge with regards to executing on a transaction?

texts.speaker: Filipe Rosa
texts.profession: Banco Espirito Santo de Investimento SA (Broker)
texts.text: And my second question relates to what is your outlook in terms of – in terms of oil prices, what is your  perception? Is that affecting the way you're looking at your CapEx plan? Y ou probably need to revise it soon. Do  you see any potential investments at risk with the new backdrop of oil prices?

texts.speaker: Filipe Rosa
texts.profession: Banco Espirito Santo de Investimento SA (Broker)
texts.text: And coming back to your intention to make an acquisition, are you revising downwards your long-term  assumption for oil prices or do you think that you now will be able to make an acquisition at the previous  valuations you were expecting because the sellers will adjust their prices to your new level or to your valuation?  Thank you very much.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In relation with outlook for oil prices, I mean sure that they will fluctuate, as a first comment. In relation with the  CapEx, I would say I will not touch the – and we will not modify our plan for exploration. I mean, if we start  exploring today, probably first oil would arrive in eight years. So, we have to look more on exploration as buying  an option. And buying an option is something that has proved quite – we have achieved good results through our  model which basically implies putting at risk and penalizing short-term our P&L of $7 per barrel produced and we  will keep attached to that.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: And finally, in the acquisition, for sure, we are revisiting long-term oil prices and really having a wide band, I  would say between $70 and $100, to analyze any possible acquisition. Did I answer you Filipe?

texts.speaker: Oswald C. Clint
texts.profession: Sanford C. Bernstein Ltd.
texts.text: Thank you very much. Yeah, maybe – I think you made a comment that all of your production was economic at  these prices. Could you just talk about your Mid-Continent volumes? Is that also true for that portion of the  Upstream in the third quarter? And what happens here at these oil prices going forward? And how should we  think about that volume growth into 2015?

texts.speaker: Anish Kapadia
texts.profession: Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
texts.text: The second question is relating to Angola, we've seen kind of, just generally in the industry, quite a few  unsuccessful wells in the pre-salt in Angola. It seems like, on your two wells in Angola, the commerciality is highly  questionable. Just wondering how you think about your Angola pre-salt exploration strategy going forward?

texts.speaker: Irene Himona
texts.profession: Société Générale SA (Broker)
texts.text: And my second question on the Downstream, obviously, a key strength this quarter. Can yo u talk a little bit about  the trends you're seeing in Spanish and European oil products demand? Are things getting a little bit better?  Thank you.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Taking this into account, what I do expect for the fourth quarter. I would say that dependent on Libya, with Libya  in a like-for-like basis, I think we should do a little better than we have done in this quarter. Refining margins are  little better. Cold weather helps. Gas oils will have to increase margins. We'll have the full speed Sapinhoá. So my  estimate – and Gas & Power would do better in the U.S. So I'm a little optimistic in comparison with the third  quarter. Okay, Irene?

texts.speaker: Hamish W. Clegg
texts.profession: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
texts.text: Good afternoon, guys. It must be good to be Repsol, one of the only companies to benefit from or at least be less  impacted by lower oil prices, given your mix. But one of the questions asked on many of the other calls has been  what's the sort of rough rule of thumb leverage to oil prices for you, which is something that all companies have  been answering us?

texts.speaker: Hamish W. Clegg
texts.profession: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
texts.text: Second question is just on your drilling and M&A. One of the things you mentioned is the lead time on drilling –  having a successful drilling campaign, finding oil and coming into the portfolio. How much would you consider  using your successful drilling operations as a means to generating cash flow? It might not be organic, but by  selling stakes in some of your discoveries that could definitely help bolster your cash po sition in terms of kind of  cash coming into the business.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Thanks for your question, Hamish. In relation with oil price sensitivity, I'll give you something more than the oil  price sensitivity. Basically, after tax, $1 fall affects us approximately in €18 million at after-tax result. A 10%  increase in the dollar increases our [ph] DDI (43:40), our EPS by 12%. And normally, oil price and dollar moves in  the opposite direction. So, we have somehow a coverage there.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In relation with the flexibility, no major changes and we're always active managing oil supply basket. So the  flexibility, I would say is more on our refining system and we take the advantage of that and we [ph] permanently  (47 :43) look at every type of crudes that are available.

texts.speaker: Alastair R. Syme
texts.profession: Citigroup Global Markets Ltd.
texts.text: Okay, thank you. Yeah, on the crude feedstock question, I guess my point was, you're seeing an increasing  availability of lighter crudes as things get backed out of the U.S. market, can you take advantage of that in the  system?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: I would say that increase in light crudes will not help us much, as a basic rule. I mean, part of our advantage is the  – in-between the spread on heavy and light. So, if there's more light crude in the market, the spread between  heavy and light would be lower. I mean, we are handling today – our diet include 45% of heavy stuff. So basically,  we'd like to have a wider spread. So if the increase of light crude comes in, logically it will not help us. It's okay,  Alastair?

texts.speaker: Joshua E. Stone
texts.profession: Barclays Capital Securities Ltd.
texts.text: Hi. Good afternoon. Very well, thanks. Given the fall in the oil price, I just wanted to clarify on your acquisition  priorities. You previously talked about a need for liquids, and wanting to get more liquid in the portfolio. But also  mentioning the advantage of having gas in a falling oil price environment. Are those priorities unchanged? Or are  you perhaps willing to maybe settle for a little bit more gas, if the opportunity presents itself?

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Thanks for your questions, Joshua. In relation with the first one, I would say liquids or gas is not precisely the  most critical factor in the acquisition. We'll look more for really value and possibilities to generate value and also  in stable scenarios. I mean, meaning that – by that, that portfolio tuck-in, we need to be more in stable countries.  If you want my opinion, I think that there's more downside today in liquids than in gas, but it's just an op inion.

texts.speaker: Miguel Martínez San Martín
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In relation with Gas & Power, it's quite difficult to make an assessment. Seeing that Algonquin last year, which is  the reference price at a given moment, reached $80, so it's very much dependent on how the weather will affect  the East Coast during the fourth quarter. So really difficult to assess how the weather is going to be in the East  Coast of the U.S. Sorry about that.
