texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Let's start with the main events of 2014. We end 2013 and began 2014 with a closing, as you can remember, of the  disposal of our LNG assets to Shell as planned. During the first week of 2014, we were able to close the settlement  with the Argentinian Government in relation to the controlling stake of the Repsol Group in Y PF and Y PF GAS.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Now, let's move to the fourth quarter and full-year 2014 results. Fourth quarter 2014, CCS adjusted net income  was €37 0 million and CCS adjusted operating income was €626 million. These results were 201% and 197%  higher, respectively, compared with the same period of last year, thanks mainly to the good results obtained in the  Downstream business. 2014 CCS adjusted net income was €1.7 billion and CCS adjusted operating income was  €2.4 billion, at 27 % and 12% higher, respectively, c ompared with the same period of last year.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Production reached 371,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day during the fourth quarter, a 16% increase year -on- year. When we look at the full year, we reached an average 355,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, a 2% growth  compared with 2013, despite lower output coming from Libya. If we compare – let me compare both years without  Libya, production growth would have reached 8%.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Second factor, lower crude and gas realization prices that had a negative impact at the operating level of €232  million. I have to add higher depreciation charges – some higher depreciation charges due to higher production  that had a negative impact of €106 million. Also, lower exploration costs that led to an increase in the operating  income of €77 million, mainly due to lower amortization of wells and lower G&A and G&G.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Our full-year net adjusted result in Upstream was €589 million, a 40% decline due to lower production in Libya,  for security reasons as you know, and lower prices. Discussing about our Upstream division performance, I'd like  to end with our reserve replacement ratio that was 118% for 2014. We finished the year, the year 2014 I mean,  with a total of 1.54 billion barrels of oil equivalent of net proven reserves. And rolling average over the last five  years has been of 198%.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Turning to our Downstream division, adjusted net income in the quarter was €370 million, which compares with  the €21 million of the fourth quarter of 2013. Full-year net adjusted income stood at more than €1 billion, a 111%  increase compared to 2013. Drilling down – even being in Downstream business, let me say drilling down into the  quarterly results, in Refining, we saw a year-on-year increase in margin from $4.1 to $5.5 per barrel, due mainly to  lower energy cost, wider spreads between the products, mainly gasoline and middle distillates and Brent.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Moving to Gas & Power, operating income in the quarter was €102 million higher year-on-year, and the results of  the North American operation were driven mainly by higher volumes and price, together with the positive impact  of marking-to-market of the contractual commitments for the natural gas compensations in North America.  Results in trading and other activities explain the remaining difference.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In Gas Natural Fenosa, the €67 million adjusted net income in the fourth quarter of 2014 was 32% lower year -on- year. And these lower results are mainly explained by the provision for impairment that Gas Natural Fenosa  did of  the Egyptian LNG plant of Damietta.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: To sum up, this quarter, we have delivered a fair set of results with improved performance of our Downstream  business offsetting the lower results of the Upstream division. Due to the current environment of lower crude oil  prices, we've been able to generate positive free cash flow before divestments during the year. And even in a low  crude oil scenario, the integrated model we have designed allow us to remain resilient.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: The different investment cycles and cash generation of the Upstream and Downstream businesses contribute to a  greater stability of our results. And let me say that, additionally, the increased U.S. dollar strength and the  significant portion of our gas production not linked to oil prices provide further stillness. On top of that, we have  the likelihood of the dividend flow and results of our affiliate, Gas Natural Fenosa, a stake that provides further  optionality to protect the company in any possible scenario.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And let me now speak about what we should expect for 2015. Pending closing, we can't speak at present of the  figures of the future merged company, but we'll have the opportunity to do it in coming weeks. On a standalone  basis, within Repsol, we are revisiting or reviewing our investment program, including our exploration budget, in  light of the current environment, together with the implementation of efficiency and cost-cutting measures.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Our Downstream business investment will be applied basically to maintenance and to our programs to reduce  CO2 emissions, increasing profit through energy consumption reduction at our industrial plants, and giving more  steps of the new specifications project in our refinery in Peru. During the year, we will review all of our supply  chain and the relationship with our suppliers and service providers in o rder to reduce costs. We have already  started and we have seen price reductions arising from them.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Sustainability, safety, governance – good governance, and environmental management at the highest standards  will remain at the core of our operation.

texts.speaker: Filipe Rosa
texts.profession: Banco Espirito Santo de Investimento SA (Broker)
texts.text: My second question relates to your guidance in terms of CapEx. So you guided for Upstream. I don't know if you,  apart from exploration, where do – are you cutting any projects from your pipeline? Are you delaying any project  so that you managed to reduce your CapEx so significantly? And if you could provide us a guidance for the overall  company for 2015 in terms of CapEx?

texts.speaker: Filipe Rosa
texts.profession: Banco Espirito Santo de Investimento SA (Broker)
texts.text: And finally, on exploration, you are reducing your budget, but 2014 was a record year in terms of investment.  Could you just let us know what are the main highlights in terms of wells or in terms of exploration for 2015?  What are the wells that we should look at? Thank you very much.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Excuse me. I forgot it. I have here notes about your questions, and I forgot to answer the last one. In the same  spirit of the current strategic and oil price situation, we are going to be prudent regarding our exploration  campaign. That means that we have more appraisal wells than frontier wells.

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Thank you, Ángel. Good afternoon, gentlemen. A couple of questions from my side, please. Firstly, just on the  North American gas business and the good results you've had there. I just wondered if you could give us a sense of  how repeatable that will be in 2015. And it seems to be an area where it delivered over and above sort of  expectations reasonably consistently. Is there something you can tell us about how much of that sort of  performance is something that we can see continue into 2015 and help you through the sort of weaker oil price  environment?

texts.speaker: Haythem M. Rashed
texts.profession: Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Secondly, I have a question on the CapEx guidance that you gave for 2015. But, specifically, what you're basing  your assumptions or estimates on particularly with regard to the oil price? So is the 20% reduction in CapEx a  reflection of the – does that sort of assume your base price that I think you talked about before of $85 2015, $93  2016, or are you looking at a different oil price scenario with that CapEx rate in mind?

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Y es. First of all, starting for Gas & Power business in North America, I mean, as I said in my speech, we are – the  factor of the mark-to-market positions we have in the fourth quarter. Of course, we are going to do our best to  repeat these results in the future, but I have to say to you that we depend in a close way from weather, for  instance, because you know that we took advantage of the high prices in New England and in the Northeastern  American coast. And in these scenarios, our Canaport plant and our Commercialization business in North  America is more profitable.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: So, I can't deliver, of course, anything regarding the first quarter of this year. But I could say that that is going to  depend in a strong way from the weather in North America and, of course, the mark-to-market positions we have.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Regarding the CapEx reduction, I mean, first of all, we have a long-term price – a scenario of price deck. And in  our opinion, I mean, the rig count drop in unconventional production, the natural decline of wells and the long - term slowdown across the sector will translate into a tightening of the supply-demand balance that will bring  prices up. That is our view regarding our price scenario in our deck. But, of course, we are not here to forecast the  oil price scenario, but to manage the current scenario.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: So my duty is to manage this company in any scenario where the Brent price is $60 per barrel. Regarding this  scenario of $60 per barrel, we have to be able, even in this current scenario, to have as Repsol – I'm talking, of  course, about the Repsol standalone company. I can't deliver any figure regarding Talisman, as you know, before  the closing – is to have a free-cash-flow-neutral scenario at the current oil prices. So, to achieve this objective, I  mean, we are being very prudent regarding our CapEx in our Upstream business. And, of course, we are trying to  promote efficiency in every business of Repsol.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Regarding your last question, portfolio management, first of all, we are not in a hurry to divest anything. First of  all, we have the cash we need now to pay the Talisman transaction. And it's true. I mean, we announced to the  market that 12 months after the closing, we are going to be able to divest €1 billion assets in the market, that is, I  mean, a 3%, 2% of the total assets of Repsol, is not too much. And, of course, we are going to take account the oil  scenario price in this policy. And in that case, I mean, we will try to divest in assets not directly linked to the oil  price.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: I mean, and regarding GasNat, you know that GasNat is always an alternative, but today's enviro nment reinforces  the integrated model with the strong cash generation coming from Downstream and Gas Natural Fenosa. And Gas  Natural Fenosa brings a cash dividend with a much higher yield than the marginal cost of debt after tax. So we are  not in a hurry to do anything regarding divestment. We'll do it, but in the right moment.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you very much, Bruno. Let's start by Venezuela. Let me say that we are operating in Venezuela in a normal  way and we are developing our projects in Venezuela in a normal way. And let me also say that I know that there  are companies or sectors that could have less or more difficulties in Venezuela. You also have to take into account  that the oil and gas sector is very particular in Venezuela, because it's a key factor for the economic sustainability  of a country. And so the environment where we operate is different from the environment in business terms, I  mean, where some other sectors or companies operate.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Regarding the – I mean, the influence of risk of devaluation in accounts in Venezuela, I mean, the last exchange  rate for the sector, as you know, contemplates the official exchange of VEF6.3 per US$1. So there is not a ny impact  on the oil and gas sector companies.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Potential investment in Canaport. Sorry. I mean, as you know, Canaport was outside the perimeter in the sa le of  our LNG business to Shell. And, of course, our goal is now to maximize the value of that plant, analyzing, studying  and trying to implement different alternatives. I mean, it's true that in the market, you know that there is a  growing interest in exporting LNG from United States, from the Eastern and Pacific Coast of Canada. And we are  trying to take these steps in this direction, I mean, in order to know if this option to be open and to be valuable for  Repsol.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: So the idea is to design an attractive project for Repsol and for third parties in order to – I mean to be able to  attract investment. But let me say – let me underline that Repsol doesn't contemplate under any scenario to make  a significant investment in Canaport. So, in terms of CapEx for Repsol, it's going to be near zero. And now, we are  looking for permits. We are analyzing the engineering of the project, and we are going to try – I mean, to be able  to – we could have the possibility to analyze a different alternative. And I think that it's okay.

texts.speaker: Lydia R. Rainforth
texts.profession: Barclays Capital Securities Ltd.
texts.text: Thanks, Ángel, and good afternoon. I'll stick to three questions, if I could. Can you just tell us where you are  regarding the thinking on the hybrid bonds and whether you need to get that done before the deal closes, or  whether that is done in the second half of the year? And then, secondly, and partly linked to that, the oil price at  the moment is below what? I think you considered the acid test when you did the Talisman deal. Is there any  implication on that in terms of what you think you might have to do in terms of the credit rating agencies and just  outline any discussions you might have had with them on that?

texts.speaker: Lydia R. Rainforth
texts.profession: Barclays Capital Securities Ltd.
texts.text: And then, just a final question – actually two, if I could. Third question, just on the cost optimization space. How  much are you looking for that being – and this is just for Repsol itself, how much are you looking for that to be  self-help and I think efficiency improvement, versus what you're looking for from the suppliers' side? And just a  very quick clarification question. The conversion capacity utilization of 105%, is that the maximum that you think  you can get to or can that be pushed any higher at all? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And let me say, we have many tools to react. We have, of course, the cash we have in our pockets, we have, of  course, the hybrid bonds issuing process, we have the portfolio management, we have the reduction of CapEx of  further divestments now linked to oil prices assets. So – but our financial cushion is really wide to ensure that we  are going to maintain our rating grade.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Second question, cost optimization, I mean, more or less when I was talking about our reduction of $1.1 billion in  CapEx terms in our Upstream business, I said 55% more or less, I remember the figure, comes from the  exploration activity and 45% from our development programs. So let me say that more or less from this last figure,  that could be $450 million, 50% could come from – I mean, in some way, slowing down some running  investments or things like that, 50% comes from efficiency. That could be $200 million, $250 million in our  Upstream activity and that means more or less 6%, 7 % of the full CapEx.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And I'm talking, of course, about CapEx in Upstream regarding this efficiency of cost optimization. That is, more  or less, fits in our current way what is happening, what some older companies of the sector are delivering now.  And, of course, you know that we continue improving the efficiency of our Downstream businesses mainly  through the reduction, thanks to our CO2 program, the reduction of our energy cost.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And you know that in our refineries and in some way, perhaps a bit less, of course, in this last case of the  petrochemicals, but in our refineries 65% of the total cost is energy. And last year, we have been able to r educe in  450,000 tons our emissions of CO2 of the company, mainly in our refining and petrochemical businesses, also a  part in the Upstream business. And thanks to these CO2 reductions, we have reduced in a huge way our energy  cost in refining.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And, second one, you also have to take into account that in some processes, mainly cokers, and we have four  cokers, we don't operate in continuous terms, but we operate in batch. That means that if we are able to reduce the  time of the full cycle of the coker, that means that we are able to increase the conversion utilization rate of our  system. Theoretically, I mean, we could say that 108%, 110% could be the maximum. But be sure that we are going  to do our best to overcome this figure.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And now, I'm going to give you the figure regarding Repsol standalone. At the current $60 per barrel oil price, let  me say that our forecast is that we are going to be neutral for the current Repsol in 2015 in terms of free cash flow,  after paying, of course – after financial expenses, after CapEx logically, and after dividend.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Let me only, I mean, underline the exception of Mid-Continent. As you know, the unconventional environment is  quite different. And in the current oil price scenario, we are slowing down our investment in Mid - Continent. I'm not going to deliver more about this issue because, I mean, I have to respect the operator,  SandRidge, that tomorrow is going to deliver the full figures regarding what is happening in Mid -Continent.

Hamish Clegg  Bank of America Merrill Lynch  Q  Okay.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Over the course of this year, 2015, we achieved the successful integration of the two companies and we identified  the potential synergies between both organizations, deploying a new organizational structure to include all the  combined assets and operation of both companies. This integration of Talisman was, let me say,  complete under  an increasingly difficult and volatile macro scenario, as you can see on this slide with the drop of oil gas prices.  And once the integration was complete, we release our new Strategic Plan whose main objective is to provide value  and to provide resilience under any price scenario.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Portfolio management and efficiency, together with the strength of our integrated model and/or the operational  improvements already implemented in previous years, allow us to provide value even in this low price  environment. And as you can see in this slide that you have now in front of you, with Brent being down by almost  $50 per barrel in 2015, we have been able to keep our EBITDA CCS at a similar level to the previous year.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Repsol is able to achieve all that, thanks to our Tier 1 Downstream division and the right balance of Downstream  versus Upstream portfolio. As you can see on the slide, Repsol is the company in which our profitable  Downstream division contributes most to the reduction of the company's global bre akeven. The rate of our  Downstream business in relation to our Upstream overall and liquids production, as you could see in this slide, is  the highest within our peer group.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Our Upstream division has also made this contribution to cash neutrality in 2015 and in a year marked by the  Talisman integration and price turmoil compare to 2014 and considering Talisman for the full year, our Upstream  has reduced CapEx by more than 50% and OpEx by 12% or by 13% if we take a per barrel basis.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And at this point, let me discuss our Strategic Plan in more depth. In our projections, we used two sets of planning  assumptions, as you could remember, because we had the opportunity to explain all that in October and to see  most of you in the road show that followed that presentation, I mean we used a set of planning assumptions and  our base case and as stress case reflected the metrics of the plan under a $50 flat scenario. But considering the  continued price weakness, we have carried out an exercise to review the projections of our base and stress cases,  revisiting them under an even lower oil and gas prices scenario.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Our revised base cases start with a Brent price of $50 in 2016, $55, $65, $75 ramps up to $85 by 2020. Our  updated stress case goes down to $40 in 2016, $40 in 2017, and remains flat at $50 for the rest of the period. And  with regard to gas prices, our revised base case starts with a Henry Hub $2.6. And our updated stress case is  reduced to $2.6 per million of Btus in 2016 and 2017, while remaining flat at $3.5 for the rest of the period. We  keep our refining margin assumptions in line with our strategic projections. And as you can see, we are adapting  and adjusting quickly but of course maintaining our strategic drivers untouched.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Our CapEx for 2016 is reduced to €3.9 billion. We are also anticipating the achievement of our efficiency  objective. Our target is to capture €1.1 billion from efficiencies plus synergies in 2016 and this figure, as you could  remember, is more than half of our objective in the Strategic Plan period. We expect to maintain this effort in  2017, keeping our investment at the same level as in 2016. Overall, we are reducing the Group's cumulative  investment for 2016 and 2017 by around €1 billion of which €300 million correspond to efficiency measures.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We expect to achieve at $40 Brent per barrel cash neutrality in the next two years after paying our dividends and  our interest. To achieve this figure, we are only including the Downstream cash-in coming from the announced  piped LPG sale, but we are not including any of the divestments that are going to be made or done in the period  2016, 2017.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: This objective will be achieved through CapEx optimization and implementation of our efficiency measures. Most  of this optimization in CapEx comes from our Upstream for we expect to invest around €3 billion in 2016  excluding these figures, G&G and G&A.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: The reduction arises from a combination of lower exploration, our efficiency program with the OpEx and CapEx  optimization associated to this efficiency program, a non-inflation capture, as well as deferring non-critical  investment in development and producing assets, while keeping at the same time our production level at around  7 00,000 barrels per day.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: More than 50% of efficiency plus synergies target in 2018, as I said before, will be achieved in 2016. And all -in-all,  we will reduce our Upstream OpEx in per barrel terms by more than 13% in 2016 comparing this figure with the  cost – with the OpEx in 2015.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: First, I'm glad at this morning, and let me say that was this morning because when we closed the deal last night,  we announced the sale of our offshore wind power business in the UK for around €240 million. This is a new  milestone in the progress of our divestment program.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We also reached an agreement with Armstrong, our partner in the Alaska project to dilute our position in the  North Slope, generating a positive impact on our cash flow of around €7 00 million as we are avoiding carrying  Armstrong for that amount. And I think at this point is important because, I mean, I'd like to underline that this is  a good example of win-win transaction that we can undertake to optimize our E&P portfolio even under the  current low price scenario.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Let's speak briefly about our projects for 2016. On the development side, the ramp of the second FPSO in  Sapinhoá north in Brazil – in Brazil, sorry, will be complete in March with our production in Brazil thus reaching  around 45,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day net to Repsol.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Also in block BMS-9 in the Santos area, the development of Lapa is progressing on the schedule and the FPSO  Cidade de Caraguatatuba is expected to be in location by mid-year with first oil planned for the fourth quarter.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In the UK, we continue advancing with redevelopment of Mon-Arb and Flyndre Cawdor, with advances to  accelerate first oil expected early in 2017. And at the same time, we are going to go on reducing CapEx in order to  have further improving in per barrel performance in our North Sea assets.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In Peru, this Sagari project have received the environmental approval, and development work continues as  planned for first gas in 2018. In Columbia, we'll continue with appraisal campaign in Akacias. In Algeria, the  execution of Reganne progresses with first gas maintained for 2017, while the conceptualization of Sud-Est-Illizi  continues in parallel with the successful appraisal phase which is leading to material resource base.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And with regard to our Downstream business, Downstream businesses, as I said, this year, we expect to further  improve the resilience of our margins through this battery of measures. First, a reduction in losses, consumptions,  and CO2 emissions in our refineries and in our crackers coupled with additional efficiency measures. At the same  time, we are going to enhance and to increase the reliability of our plants in order to increase utilization of the  conversion capacity of our refineries. And we are going to boost the improvement of our differentiation program  in our chemical business thanks to our metallocene plant in Tarragona. And finally, the revamp our La Pampilla  refinery in Peru is progressing as schedule.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Now, let's move on the fourth quarter and full year results and the main operational highlights. Fourth quarter  CCS adjusted net income was €461 million, 25% higher compare with the same period of last year and 189%  higher than in the third quarter. Full-year 2015 CCS adjusted net income was €1.86 billion, a 9% increase compare  with full-year 2014 results. These results were impacted by low oil and gas prices in the Upstream, and all that was  offset by a very strong Downstream performance, especially in refining and chemicals.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Despite the challenging and difficult context we are living, the strength of our Downstream has more than offset  the continued decrease in crude oil and gas prices. As you may see in the slide, this resilience of our result is quite  exceptional within our peer group. The Repsol Group's cash flow from operations amounted to €5.4 billion in  2015, of course. I'd like to stress the fact that the outstanding performance of our Downstream division that  contribute more than €4 billion to this figure.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Looking at the result by division, starting with the Upstream business. Adjusted net income for the fourth quarter  was minus €27 6 million to €180 million lower than in the same period of 2014. All in all, the Upstream results  were mainly impacted by lower realization prices with a bigger E&P asset base partially offset by lower exploration  and other costs. Production reached an average of 697,000 barrels per day in oil equivalent terms in the quarter  higher than the third quarter, thanks to the ramp-ups in Sapinhoá in Brazil, in Cardón in Venezuela, and the  production increase in the UK, where you know that we are reversing the decline.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Current production is over 700,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day and the reserve replacement ratio for 2015  has been 500%, of course, taking into account inorganic part of this ratio. Excluding the acquisition of Talisman  and other inorganic transactions, our organic reserve replacement ratio was 159% ending the year with 2.4 billion  of proved reserves. This ratio is impacted by the increase in our stake in Venezuela, as well as from reserve  increases in Trinidad and Tobago North America and Bolivia.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Y ear-on-year performance excluding the contributions of Libya and Talisman is explained as follows, lower crude  oil and gas realization prices, as you know, and all that has a negative impact at the breakeven level of €307  million. Lower exploration expenses led to an increase in the operating income of €89 million. Lower depreciation  and amortization charges increased the operating income by €52 million, as a consequence of lower amortizations  in the U.S. and Russia and lower production in Trinidad and Tobago, partially compensated by the increase in  production in Brazil and Venezuela.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Finally, I'd like to mention that in the current environment of low crude oil and gas prices, th e board of directors  of Repsol has agreed in application of the most rigorous and prudent financial criteria to apply extraordinary  impairments totaling approximately €2.9 billion to its 2015 earnings of which €2.4 billion have been booked in  the fourth quarter of 2015. These provisions can be of course reversed in future accounts when the price outlook  changes.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Turning to our Downstream division, CCS adjusted net income in the quarter was €495 million, significantly  higher than the €37 0 million of the fourth quarter of 2014. Full year adjusted net income was €2.2 billion, 113%  higher year-on-year, and this improvement is mainly driven by better by better refining and chemical margins and  enhanced performance in the trading business, partially offset by lower results in gas and power and LPG.  Quarterly performance was underpinned by very strong chemical results that, let me say, that continue in the first  quarter of 2016. And I hope that the same thing could happen over the whole year.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: The Refining Margin Indicator was down quarter-on-quarter but still average at a healthy $7.3 per barrel, 33%  higher than the same period of 2014. We have entered 2016 with a robust refining margin operating around –  above $7 per barrel, thanks to a strong gasoline spreads offset in some way by the weaker diesel spreads due to the  mild winter. We continue to see heavy light spreads [indiscernible] looking forward.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In the commercial businesses, the operating income was €29 million lower year -on-year, mainly due to lower LPG  margins in Spain. Moving to gas and power and trading. The operating income was €8 million lower than that of  the fourth quarter of 2014, but nevertheless and even in this mild winter we have positive results in our gas and  power American business which is always good news. The exchange rate and other effect year-on-year was €27   million. Result from equity affiliates and non-controlling interests and taxes and so on, explain the remaining  difference.

texts.speaker: Filipe Rosa
texts.profession: Haitong Bank, S.A. (Broker)
texts.text: My second question relates to your strong liquidity position and the fact that your hybrid bonds, they are trading  at a quite high yield. I know that probably this not the best time, but historically, you have compared the deal of  your Gas Natural investment with the cost of debt. Now, you have quite expensive debt that you could rebuy – you  could buy again – buy back selling your Gas Natural stake. Could you just elaborate a little bit on how you are  seeing your cost of debt and whether you could have some sort of measures to optimize at the level?

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We have a track record of delivery. We are executing more than €3 billion either of divestment or CapEx reduction  that are linked to M&A operation and we have developed this effort in four months. We have, of course, overcome  that objective we have of €1 billion agreed previously with the credit rating agencies. We are going to go on  delivering and I think that all that should be enough to maintain the investment grade.

texts.speaker: Irene Himona
texts.profession: Société Générale SA (Broker)
texts.text: And my second question, in the October strategy plan for 2016 to 2020, apart from OpEx, CapEx, et cetera, you  had included a €6 billion asset disposal plan. Today, you adjusted the CapEx, OpEx and dividends, but you have  made no reference to what asset disposals are still required to deliver the plan and protect the investment grade.  So I wonder if you can clarify, do you need more than the €6 billion. And in the context – in light of the $30 oil  and your adjusted stress case, how is the board thinking about the Gas Natural holding? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: At the same time, at this oil low prices and I'm assuming in this $40 per barrel scenario that we are goin g to go on  in this scenario over the year. The competition of the chemicals based in the American ethane is over for our  system. Our competitive position is better. And let me also say and it could be a quite, that we are in some way  capturing the strong efficiency measures we put in place two years, three years ago in our petrochemical  businesses.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And we have shown last time this morning, our capability to crystallize hidden value from many businesses that,  let me say, a market is not, in my opinion, perhaps sufficiently taken into account. We have outside on our E&P  business many assets that are not related to the oil and gas prices and we could extract and capture this hidden  value.  Ángel Bautista  Director-Investor Relations  A  Thank you, Irene.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Others. Gas Nat, there wasn't any kind of decision in our board related to this issue. And let me say, we are not  putting any focus in any specific asset. We have €42 billion, €43 billion in assets. Don't forget that 25% of these  assets are Downstream assets, that even the E&P we have shown over the last four months like we are able to  deliver disposals in this tough scenario and that we could have a 30% of our Upstream assets that are not directly  related to the commodity prices either because they have a fixed price contract or because they are B and C  contracts and so on.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We are going to reduce more or less the reserves replacement ratio this year in a 9% or 10% due to these CapEx  defers – deferrals, sorry. But in this oil and gas price scenario, my duty is to preserve the value of the company.  And I think that this reduction of 9 points, 8 points 10 points in the reserves replacement ratio mainly when – as  you could see, we have an organic replacement of 159% last year and taking in organic terms 500% growth are  good figures.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: So that is the real reason of this coherency, Jason, in delivering our Strategic Plan. We are maintaining the same  main targets, but our duty because this scenario is different. We are not at $50 per barrel, so I can't maintain. I  can put on the table the same kind of measures we had when we were at $50 per barrel scenario. And that was the  average in 2015.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you, Jason. I mean, you are right. We are maintaining our main priority, that is that after paying the   dividend of Repsol, reducing our debt. And this figure is representing what you are saying. And to achieve and to  deliver this figure, we are going to increase the efficiency, the OpEx reduction, the CapEx reduction we have in our  hands and we are going to be active trying to capture value for our M&A operation. Thank you, Jason.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: What are the production implications, you said, of this CapEx reduction? Zero. I mean, zero in next two, three,  four years because we are always talking about projects that we're not going to see the first oil, either first oil or  first gas before 2020. So now, we're zero.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We have increased our production in Norway, thanks to the Gudrun swap. Cardón, the ramp -up is also there and  so on. So I presume that the total production this year is going to be net average of 7 00,000 barrels per day and  the impact in the [indiscernible] Strategic Plan of this measure is going to be almost zero.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you, Haythem. First of all, related to La Pampilla, I'm not going to put, of course, any name to any asset as I  said before. But our committed with the La Pampilla East this year by July more or less to fulfill the middle  distillates hydro-desulphurization project to adapt ourselves to the new regulation in Peru.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: At the same time, of course, we are also revisiting every Downstream business and every Downstream assets also  in terms of efficiency. We are now making a lot of money in our Downstream businesses, but it is always time to  try to be more efficient. And as you could see in our Strategic Plan, we are going to reduce our cost in  our  Downstream businesses in a figure above €200 million this year, 2016, thanks to the addition of all these  efficiency measures.

texts.speaker: Flora Trindade
texts.profession: Banco Português de Investimento SA (Broker)
texts.text: And then secondly, just trying to see if you could give us a sense of what could be the level of free cash flow you  expect this year considering the current oil price scenario and the adjustments you have given in terms of CapEx  and deficiencies with and without the divestments you have in the meantime announced? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you, Flora. Let me underline again related to the rating agencies. We have €43 billion of assets in our  hands, a relevant part of them are not related to the oil price. So, we are going to take advantage of this basket to  play, to increase the value for the company, and we are not going to deliver any specific measure.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: I know what I have to do but my duty's to stay here, of course, and not to follow given any kind of more  information related to the assets of the company. 2016, our aim – our target this year is to reduce the debt level of  the company even at these oil prices. And as you know, we are taking a deck for the year of $40 per barrel Brent  and $2.6 per million of BTUs in Henry Hub price. Even in this scenario, our target is to reduce in quite a  significant way the debt level of the company.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Let me stress the fact that to reduce our debt this year, the first way we have is the free cash flow generated by our  businesses even in this tough scenario. With that complement coming from the CapEx  reduction I stressed before  and the efficiency measures that, let me say, we are increasing these measures everyday and is not wishful  thinking, I have a commitment with you and the commitment is that every quarter, I am going to deliver to the  market, so to you, what is the fulfillment level of the efficiency measures in OpEx in our corporate level, in OpEx  for our E&P business and the OpEx of our Downstream businesses. And I'm going to do that at the day I will  present the results of the first quarter of the year.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And secondly, we are going to go on trying to extract a captured value for the company through our M&A. We have  a basket of assets that are seasoned in some way and I'm sure we are going to be able to crystallize them as we  were able yesterday closing the disposal of the wind farms in the North Sea. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Hamish Clegg
texts.profession: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
texts.text: Second thing relating to the same thing, really. CapEx, could you give us a split between Upstream and  Downstream following the recent reductions? Is most of that in the Upstream or the Downstream? It'll be quite  useful to know.

texts.speaker: Hamish Clegg
texts.profession: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
texts.text: And then just finally, I know you're sick of hearing about the agencies, but could you tell us a little bit about the  sort of options you have? So, number one, just confirm that you are committed to investment grade. Secondly,  there's a lot of talk about Gas Natural, but could you confirm that actually you get a one-notch modifier for owning  Gas Natural anyway, and therefore, it wouldn't make sense to sell it because it does contribute very, very stable  cash flow? And finally, why would you not do an exchangeable bond ahead of selling a brilliant asset like Gas  Natural?

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: So in the Downstream business, as you know, we are putting all our effort in two kind of projects. First of all,  guaranteeing the reliability and the correct and right maintenance of our plants. And secondly, all the efficiency  programs we are boosting in our industrial plants. And on top of that, of course, we can't forget the hydro- desulphurization project in La Pampilla as I mentioned before.

texts.speaker: Lydia R. Rainforth
texts.profession: Barclays Capital Securities Ltd.
texts.text: And then the third one, just to take it away from the credit metrics. So coming back to refining the Downstream  side, clearly there does seem to be a longer term shift away from diesel and towards gasoline. I'm just wondering  in terms of, we spend a lot of time thinking about the future of the Upstream, but around that future of the  Downstream business within Spain, how you look at again moving back towards those sort of more gasoline-based  model within that? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Cash operating cost, I presume, Lydia, that you were talking about the Upstream. In 2014, we have an operating  cost – an OpEx cost per barrel of $21.5 per barrel. We reduced this figure to $18.7 per barrel in 2015. It's an  important decrease mainly due to the OpEx cuts plus the production growth and our guideline, our target for this  year 2016 is to reduce a 16% further our OpEx per barrel to $15.7 per barrel. That means it's a huge effort.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We are reducing from $21.5 per barrel in 2014 to $15.7 per barrel in 2016. And let me say these figures are, in any  case, affected by the high cost of our North Sea operations that I'm not going to hide this fact. And without these  figures, we could be at around $12, $12.5 per barrel, but the reality the average, the target for our Upstream  business for this year is $15.7 per barrel.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Future of Downstream, let me say, we are in a strong importer diesel market and at the same time, we are  exporting gasoline every day. A third, 35%, 40%, depending on the seasons of our gasoline are exported mainly to  North America and Latin America, mainly North America. Any shifting from diesel to gasoline that could happen,  I presume that in a moderate way because we can't forget that the inertia of the market is very high, we will be  able to maintain our position as diesel producer in a strong diesel importer market. And let me underline that the  figure of the import in Europe could at around 50 million tons of diesel per year and at the same time, we could  reduce our gasoline export to North America, and that would be good news.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you, Brendan. I said to you, to the market in October that I have at that time – I suppose at that time that  we could have a flexibility of 20% to 25% in our CapEx. I hope we are today, in some way, conforming on  delivering what could be at that time only an expectation. I have to realize that today is – it could be, in some way,  more difficult. I'm sure that we could have some additional flexibility coming mainly if we stay in this low oil price  scenario, let me say, of $30 per barrel, I presume that the deflation of costs could be higher than we are  forecasting now in our company – in the sector, sorry.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Perhaps, if we go on and we stay at $30 per barrel in six, seven, eight months, perhaps we could have some FID  decisions that we could take or perhaps to defer. That could be an option. Today, we are thinking of other  possibility to take it because it's a way to create value for the company in coming years. But let me say if we are in  a $30 per barrel scenario in one year from on, perhaps we could change our mind.

texts.speaker: Alastair R. Syme
texts.profession: Citigroup Global Markets Ltd.
texts.text: Thanks, Ángel. Couple of quick questions. When you made the Talisman acquisition, under the purchase price  accounting, you started decommissioning liability. I just wonder given the impairments you've taken, whether  you've made any changes in that decommissioning assumption given the low oil prices?

texts.speaker: Alastair R. Syme
texts.profession: Citigroup Global Markets Ltd.
texts.text: And secondly, can you just talk about the investment decisions you're making? I was particularly thinking about  Red Emperor and Akacias in Colombia. Can you talk about what sort of oil prices you require to meet hurdle rates  on those investments? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you. There is no, at the moment and with the information I have now in my hand, no relevant change  related to the commission and liabilities in the North Sea, but there are quite relevant operational OpEx cuts,  CapEx cut and we are reversing at the same the decline in oil production, increasing the oil production in 2015.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Y es, when we are taking – let me say I think I have more or less my – the figures in the mind, so perhaps you  could check this figures with Ángel later. But I think Red Emperor at $40 per barrel, it could be a profitable  project and Akacias at $50 barrel more or less could be profitable. So – but let me say, I have to see this project  that could have the first oil in 2017 or 2018 in a quite broad perspective. I can't see all the prices in 2016 to take  this kind of decision because in that case my risk – I have the risk of having the – or taking the wrong decisions.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And wrong decisions could be about any kind of concern about the current oil price we living today, but  at the  same time, I have also to maintain some kind of light over the future of the oil prices. So, I think the two projects  that could be profitable at $40 or even $50 per barrel, we have to consider them and take the right decision.  Thank you.

texts.speaker: Jon Rigby
texts.profession: UBS Ltd. (Broker)
texts.text: And then just second question, just for one final point of clarification, I hope, is in your stress scenario or  something like that, is a disposal or sale of Gas Natural credit positive or credit negative do you think? Thanks.

texts.speaker: Anish Kapadia
texts.profession: Tudor, Pickering, Holt & Co. International LLP
texts.text: And then, finally on the cash flow; just wanted to get an idea of how you see your Upstream cash flow trending  over the next few years, if you assume a flat oil price scenario? So, just really trying to get an idea of how your cash  margins evolve in the Upstream over the next few years if you take commodity prices out of the equation. Thank  you.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you, Anish. CapEx, it's true, but if we look at our North American assets today after reducing our CapEx in  Marcellus, for instance, where we are only operating with one rig now, we are maintaining a quite flat gas  production operation at around 400 – 500, better said, millions of cubic meters per day. I see this CapEx levels,  this production, stable in coming two years.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: So, if we are able to go on in this path of increasing the EBITDA of the company and at the same time we are able  to deliver this debt reduction we target for 2016, this year, that changes both figures, we are going to be able to  reduce in accurate way this figure I said before. Thank you. And as I said before, we have considered and we have  analyzed our battery of measures and a lot of measures are included. We'll take in our opinion the right decisions  and of course without announcing them before as we did this morning with the wind offshore project. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Oswald Clint
texts.profession: Sanford C. Bernstein Ltd.
texts.text: All right. Thank you very much. Yes, if I think about the Talisman, the negative €200 million contribution last  year and I think about the Statoil joint venture, the operatorship of Statoil, their reduction in Marcellus costs, the  kind of OpEx reduction in North America, but also your reduction in your gas price and your oil price, does that  number materially change as we think about 2016, net-net is it going to be the same or should it worsen on to the  scenario you're kind of talking about today? And then secondly, just quickly maybe just an update on Libya, the  status of your operations there and if anything is included in 2016 or 2017 from that country? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Q
texts.profession: Okay. Thanks for that. Just as a side comment and I'll close here. The reason I'm say ing this is because recent
texts.text: rating action in the natural resources sector have been particularly extreme, that's why I wanted to...

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Y es, your point is a good point but respecting the work of everything and of course respecting the work and the job  of the rating agencies because they have to protect their technical targets and aims. But let me say that our  position as a company is also quite different from a mining or a pure extractive oil and gas company. It's not usual  in our sector or in the extractive sector, let me say, to see a company able to maintain the EBITDA in 2015 with  this low commodity prices, at the same time, being able to reduce the debt in their hands.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And about the maintenance, I have – first of all, let me say that the first part was done, that was the maintenance  of the hydrocracker of Cartagena because we have to change the catalyst. texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: The Upstream division deliver an impact of more than €800 million by the end of the year, contributing to a  reduction in free cash flow breakeven, which, for the Upstream alone, now stands at $61 per barrel. Synergy  projects have delivered more than €300 million in sustainable reductions in 2016. And by yearend, 85% of the  projects require to capture $400 million of synergies by 2020 had already been implemented. All in all, compared  to our pro forma full year in 2015, we have reduced our total Upstream operating expenditures by 20% in 2016,  and by 24% on a per barrel basis.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In exploration, a more focused drilling program, together with our portfolio targeting lower risk, contributed  towards lower overall CapEx spend. The organic reserve replacement ratio in 2016 was 124%, reinforcing  confidence in the long-term sustainability of our resource base.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Downstream division, we complete [ph] our trades (05:30) and restarted the low-sulfur diesel unit at our La  Pampilla refinery in Peru. And let me say that this investment not only allow us to meet tightening sulfur  regulations, but it also delivers an increase in our utilization rate. The project is expected to deliver a return on  capital of over 15% during its lifetime.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Now, for the main operational highlights for the quarter, starting with the Upstream division, fourth quarter  production average 679,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, a slight decrease year-on-year. Quarterly production  was impacted by planned maintenance in several assets and the sale of Tangguh and TSP, partially offset by  higher volumes in Brazil, thanks to the start-up of Lapa and the ramp-up of Sapinhoá. Average production for the  year was within our guidance range of 690,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Looking now to the Downstream division, in Refining, the margin indicator averages $7.20 per barrel in the  quarter. Margins recover materially versus third quarter mostly due to [indiscernible] (09:11-09:14), together with a  widening of the heavy [ph] crude (09:16) differentials due to an active maintenance season in Latin and North  America. Processed crude oil volumes increased by 8% compared to the previous quarter, thanks to higher  utilization in both distillation and conversion. Actual CCS margin generated a premium through the indicator of  around €0.60 per barrel.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: And going to the figures for the full year, the Refining margin indicator was in line with our long-term assumptions  of $6.30, with actual CCS margin averaging also $0.60 over the mark. The Chemicals business maintained its  strong performance in the fourth quarter, thanks to steady volumes, good margins, helped by global demand  growth and lower feedstock costs.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Moving on now to financial results, I will briefly summarize the principal outcomes from the quarter and the year.  Fourth quarter 2016 CCS adjusted net income was €698 million, €245 million higher than in the fourth quarter of  2015. Full-year 2016 CCS adjusted net income was €1.9 billion, €70 million higher compare with full-year 2015  results. EBITDA CCS stood at €5 billion for the year, in line with 2015. At the net income level, we closed 2016  with a positive result of €1.7 billion, a €3 billion increase compared to 2015, and mostly due to impairments  applied in that year.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: We are planning short stoppages in Puertollano in March, and Cartagena during the second quarter as part of our  multiyear planned maintenance schedule. In the case of Cartagena, we are talking about the hydrocrack. We are  focused on improving our cost and energy efficiency, gaining flexibility in our product mix and through our five  interconnected refineries in Spain, optimizing product delivery.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the Chemicals business, in 2016, we finished the installation of a new splitter in Tarragona. That will allow us to  process 35% LPG content in our cracker delivery, flexibility, and resilience over a wider range of feedstock prices.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Additionally, we are developing projects with two main goals in the Chemicals business: first, targeting higher  margin non-commodity products; and, second, developing petrochemical products that fit within a low-carbon  feature such as CO2 polyols, CO2 as raw materials, just a few in propylene oxide or bio polyol [indiscernible]  (17:16).

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: In the retail business, we are following a strategy that is core in Repsol, transforming while performing. This  means while maintaining our current performance, we are also developing initiatives to respond to current and  future challenges. With our strong focus on customers, we are adding services and products based on new  consumer behaviors, for example, personalized offers or [ph] shared economy (18:04) service. Additionally, we  are addressing change in energy demands through the provision of charging points for electric cars and the  supply of LPG or auto gas.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: We have a strong retail network that is a starting point for the creation of further competitive advantages,  partnering with Amazon to provide flexible delivery and collection points. This idea that we call transforming while  performing will allow us to create a retail business to supply energy products and related services not only for  2017 but for the next decade and beyond.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Our company [ph] morphed (20:01) in our process of performing while transforming. We're thinking every process  to be leaner, lowering our corporate cost and streamlining our decision-making processes; a company that will  organically breakeven approaching $40 per barrel after paying dividends and financial commitments; a company  committed to the scenario defined under COP21 in Paris, developing our own road map to be part of the solution  underway to the 2 degrees Celsius objective; a company fully focused on energy efficiency as the first driver to  reduce emissions.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: And let me say that over the last 10 years, Repsol has already reduced by 4 million tons its annual CO2 emission  from our industrial activity. And we will decrease by a further 1 million tons by 2020 while improving our  competitiveness.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Repsol is a company already prepared to contribute to our low emissions future with a significant presence in  natural gas representing 65% of our production today and 75% of our current reserves. We are a company also  committed to the reduction of [ph] design (21:23) leakage and we have committed, promoted by the World Bank,  of having a Zero Routine Flaring by 2030; a company with a portfolio of Upstream assets that will allow us to  consolidate our growth and maintain our reference production level of 700,000 barrels per day until 2020 from  current reserves under development, while increasing value through higher margins per barrel; a company that  can sustain this production level to 2025 from contingent resources, whose development projects will mature in  2018 and 2019, all while maintaining our 100% replacement ratio to 2020 and our long-term sustainable average  with shelf life of between 8 to 9 years, a bit higher [ph] in gas and in oil (22:22), giving us the flexibility to adopt  worldwide variety of macroeconomic scenarios, improving margins, and generating value in the company.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Under current oil prices, we have a clear commitment to take investment decisions only where projects generate  value above capital cost, a [ph] top (22:45) Brent price of $55 per barrel even in a scenario of rising commodity  prices, therefore, giving us the necessary resilience to thrive in a time of energy transition and continued volatility.  We have a portfolio of Downstream assets that sit at the top of the first quartile in terms of margin in Europe,  delivering resilience and competitiveness across a wide variety of economic scenarios over the next two decades,  and consistent with our support of the commitments made in Paris during COP21.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: We have a set of commercial businesses focused on the customer and providing services, allowing us to position  our business for growth in newer scenarios for mobility and energy. Repsol has a multi-energy approach, with  experience and knowledge that comes from [indiscernible] (23:39-23:41), in the manufacturing of biofuels, for  instance, and, more recently, in the services of recharging electric vehicles born out of our experiences providing  energy through natural gas and LPG.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: As I look into the future, let me say, I see a sustainable Repsol with flexibility and choice. This commitment and  this capacity to be resilient and competitive in a changing energy landscape gives me confidence about the future.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: Let me conclude by saying that we set our strategy and we have demonstrated our full commitment and ability to  deliver the goals identified within it. This is the path we took in 2016 and will be the path we will continue in 2017.  Delivering and performing, that is our clear [ph] unmet (24:37) road map; but, at the same time, transforming the  company to be prepared to take our part in future mobility and energy scenarios less intensive in carbon.

texts.speaker: Josu Jon Imaz San Miguel
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Repsol SA
texts.text: And going to your last question about the North American assets.
