texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, Rio Tinto Plc
texts.text: But we – as I said, we'll have an hybrid solution where there will be an element of coal fire and there will be an  element of renewables that is being worked out. The government is supportive on this one. So, in that context is –  do I feel uncomfortable where we are? The answer is No.

texts.speaker: Lyndon Fagan
texts.profession: Analyst, JPMorgan Securities Australia Ltd.
texts.text: Thanks very much. Look, I'll just try again on Iron Ore, are you – is your system fully balanced at 360 million  tonnes by the end of this year in terms of mine port and rail once AutoHaul is fully up and running and running  efficiently? I think that's what you said before. Is that still the case? And it just would be good to see whether you  could confirm that. And then the second one is more on the market. If we have just lost 50 million tonnes out of  the market, I think you said 245 million tonnes was domestic China production from last year. Just wondering how  you would see that gap being filled in terms of destocking of inventory, potentially more scrap usage, and whether  you had a surplus in your base case supply-demand model for this year anyway? Thanks.

texts.speaker: Jean-Sébastien Jacques
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, Rio Tinto Plc
texts.text: Now, in terms of your question on Iron Ore is we had the seminar last year in June when we took some of you on  site, and we were virtually at that point in time that we should be balanced in terms of run rate at the end of this  year, around 260 million tonnes. The position has not changed. So I can only repeat so many times the same  thing here. So, the guidance for this year is 238 million tonnes to 250 million tonnes. For sure, we will look at all  opportunities to meet the market requirement. But as Simon said, I mean it's simple than that, we don't [ph]  downgrade (00:57:14) the quality of our product and so on and so forth. So, we'll explore all opportunities to help  our customers. But we're not going to do anything stupid. That's what I'm saying.

texts.speaker: Jakob Stausholm
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Director, Rio Tinto Plc
texts.text: If you look at the Copper & Diamonds business, then return is actually quite attractive. But, right now, there are  some projects that are under construction and doesn't produce anything yet. So, it's less meaningful to look at  that. It actually looks pretty attractive the picture there. And the third area outside Iron Ore, Energy & Minerals. I  think you have to recognize that it was not the best year last year. We have guided for higher production this year;  and therefore, we also expect higher profitability this year. So, overall, I remain quite positive about the whole  portfolio not just the high profitability in Iron Ore.

texts.speaker: Jean-Sébastien Jacques
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, Rio Tinto Plc
texts.text: The challenge in exploration it takes 20 years, 30 years; it's a long term investment and so on and so forth. But  are we looking at all options? The answer is yes, organic and M&A. But M&A, we have a watching brief. The truth  of the matter is, if you look at the last 20 years, not only in mining business, but in other industries, most of the  M&A transaction destroy value, okay? And the same time, in the context of the mining business, if you don't grow  starting by the replacement offsetting the depletion, you have a problem.

texts.speaker: Jean-Sébastien Jacques

texts.text: Following the KCDC announcement, Oxy RB immediately began to withdraw its product from the market. In  November 2012 the KCDC Investigation Committee was formed to review all reported cases of death or injury  from the exposure to HS products and to categorize the cases on the basis of the evidence linking their lung  condition with HS product use. This classification has been undertaken in a series of rounds, the first two of which  are complete. The third and fourth rounds are planned but not yet complete.

texts.speaker: Adrian N. Hennah
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In addition to categorizing cases according to the likelihood of a link between an individual's injury and the use of  an HS product, the KCDC has also made findings based on an environmental survey as to which manufacturer's  HS product was used.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Moving from Hygiene quickly to Home. Let's start with the Air Wick brand, where we've truly upped the innovation  engine over the past 18 months or so. This is Air Wick Pure Essentials. You will recall that we had launched a  range of aerosols with the Pure sub brand. The Pure sub brand, very successfully actually, has done very, very  well in all the markets where we launched that Pure range of aerosols.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: This Pure range addresses really the key aerosol performance gap, which is, when you spray it, the spray really  does not last that long. The fragrance experience does not really last in an aerosol. What is different about this  range is that it comes not just with essential oils, it delivers a superior experience, a fragrance experience that is  formulated so that not a single drop of water is added. And the fragrance is fresher and it's purer and lasts longer.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Moving from Air Wick Pure Essentials to Vanish. Now as people, we know that dried-in stains are the torture test  for stain removals. If it works on those, it will work on everything. And this is our best Vanish ever, with the  ultimate performance claim of 30-second stain removal, even on a 7-day dried-in stain. And that comes under the  Vanish Gold platform. And we are going to roll it out across Vanish markets.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: But you know what? We have to deliver it consistently now that we are at a stage where we are achieving  Hygiene at the top end of the 3% to 5%. So that's how I would say it.

texts.speaker: Charles J. Pick
texts.profession: Numis Securities Ltd.
texts.text: And finally, regarding the Scholl Wet & Dry product, what is the future of that? Are you intending to sort of  relaunch it in different format? And why specifically has it been something of a failure? And actually also, if  possible, can you quantify the sales shortfall from that, vis-à-vis your budgeted aim?

texts.speaker: Adrian N. Hennah
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you. Well, in terms of quantifying the input cost tailwinds and then headwinds. No, Charles, it won't surprise  you to know we're not going to give you a precise number for that. It's safe to say that it has been a material  contributor over recent times to the tailwind and we do not expect that to go through the second half. And we do  expect it to be adverse by the time you get into 2017. But a magnitude of that, not going to give specific guidance.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: What are we going to do about this? As much as our ambition talks about and will actually keep thinking about  innovation – in fact I presented two of them this morning – we are all over how to actually get the parent issue of  Wet & Dry. We launched Wet & Dry with the assumption that some women want their dry skin product to work  even with their wet feet. And perhaps either it's not resonated as well as we would have expected.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: We continue to invest in the long-term growth and health of our brands. You will see that BEI as a percentage of  net revenue has declined by 40 basis points in the quarter. This principally reflects a reduction in our BEI onshore  as we have cut the non-return-generating investment behind the Wet & Dry Pedi.

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: The increased A&P spend was planned and is focused in China and the United States. It was a necessary  correction. The increase in SG&A was in large part the result of reduction in focus on MJN's Fuel for Growth cost  reduction program in the face of the transaction, coupled with the top line reduction.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: But just to remind you all that we have four very interesting size brands in our BMS portfolio. We have, of course,  MegaRed that we've talked about, But we also have Airborne, we have Move Free and we have Digestive  Advantage. And actually, they're all four off a good growth potential, because they all four serve very interesting  benefit platforms. So now, we are introducing – as I just said, just come to our three other innovations, we just  talked about Digestive Advantage, we are introducing Digestive Advantage chocolate bites.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: But anyway, so let's move from Adrian's eating habits to the next innovation, which is about category creation and  a new brand launch. I think we haven't talked about new brand launches and new category creation but I think this  is very exciting. So, I want to talk to you about a category which fits in health and one that addresses a major  unmet need. And all of you who live in London and maybe elsewhere probably think that air pollution is all about  China, but it's not because it's clearly becoming a pressing health issue on a global scale. And it's not just in  China or even New Delhi or India. It's in many other countries and major urban centers including London.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: Pollution impacts consumer health as we can understand but also the way we live our lives. For example, fear of  pollution can make parents in China and even other markets reluctant to let their kids play outdoors with obvious  impacts on physical health. This issue of pollution level is also not understood properly because pollution levels  vary greatly. For example, in local areas, let alone within urban centers; for example, indoor air quality is different  than outdoor air quality. It could be two times more pollution inside a tube station versus just outside one. Inside a  room or a car could be a very different level of pollution, air quality versus on outside.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So, the fact of the matter is current outdoor air pollution solutions in the market are generally limited to masks.  And that offers limited flexibility and also addresses the needs of the consumers in a very limited way.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So, what are we doing? We are introducing SiTi, a new brand endorsed by Dettol, a range of products designed  to protect consumers against out of home form pollution. We have developed a new brand for this category, SiTi,  to ensure it's seen as an expert, that it has the credibility. It develops the partnerships to succeed in the long term  in this very important area.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: Now, because pollution levels as I explained vary by location, we also need local measurement. And because all  air pollution is not visible, this measurement is a very important element of enabling consumers to monitor their  own personal spaces. So, I think most of us think that air pollution can be seen and you will see this haze and this  black mist around you and that is pollution. But in many times, in a clear day, you might have a very high level of  pollution. And therefore, this measurement of pollution whether it's on a personal space or outdoors requires  monitoring and measurement. And then people can decide what to do with the protection that they need. So, first  in a range of city products is a sensor. Now, this sensor connects you to your [ph] stock (45:40) smartphone, and  constantly monitors air pollution where you are, indoor or outdoor. And if it goes into the yellow or the red zone, it  will send you an alert asking you to take action. So, you've got the first starting point is a monitor whic h is a  connected device with attachment to your personal smartphone.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: Now, to protect against this pollution sensing that you will get to know from your monitor, we are launching two  other products. The first one is a mask, but this is no ordinary mask. It is the most sophisticated and high-quality  mask in the market and also contains a micro vent for maximum breathability. Because if you wear mask for a  long period of time, you also worried about whether or not you're inhaling your own carbon dioxide, and  particularly for young children, so what we have provided in this mask is not only the maximum protection from a  PM2.5 point of view, but also breathability through this micro filter, so that you or your children can wear this mask  for long periods.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: The third product in the range are nose filters. You can simply put these inside you. They are very discreet and  you can do that – and takes 98% of the air pollution out. So, it's a very, very effective nose filter. You can – if you  wear one, nobody can see that happening. So, next time you want to run or a morning walk and you think the  pollution outside is high, you just wear it and move forward.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: And that's the reason why RB has developed a dishwash tablet specifically designed for the compact desktop  Chinese dishwashers. And therefore, this all-in-one compact tablet is not just a smaller version, if you want, of the  larger tablet. It is a completely different technology. The composition is free of phosphates, is designed for faster  dissolution, contains the right balance of bleach and enzymes and has the right ingredients actually to tackle  China's specific food soil challenges very effectively.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So moving to and as the last example of the day before I get to targets and interesting things like that is on Air  Wick. So, the product is called VIPoo and you'll soon know why. And with the launch of VIPoo, we are effectively  creating a new segment in air care and that's called toilet perfumes. I encourage you to see this extremely  interesting campaign for Air Wick VIPoo on your YouTube if you have time. And the insight and the reason why  it's called VIPoo is this, that even VIPs have to use the toilet. And the idea that others would walk in just after you  and smell something nasty is rather embarrassing. And VIPoo is not just a traditional post-poo spray. It's actually  a pre-poo spray. It contains natural essential oils that traps the nasty smells and releases pleasant aromas.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: Just add a few sprays in the bowl before you use the toilet and it will create an essential oil barrier, which traps  embarrassing smells before they hit the air. I hope you got it. So, no one really gets to know what really happened  in the toilet.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: And there is no question, the traditional environment is tougher. The macro traditional environment is tougher, but  we have to drive our strategy therefore differently. And that's what we are doing. These two transactions that we  have done, added together, changed quite significantly the shape of RB and positioned us in a very different way  moving forward. And I think that, really, if you ask me what's the headline of half one, the headline of half one is a  strategic transformation of RB's portfolio.

Those of you who are connected to  this, what I'm just talking about, Swachh Bharat. It's one of the biggest programs of the government. And RB  through Dettol and Harpic has been the number one partner in this program, actually, and we're very proud of the  work we are doing to make sure that we can bring hygiene, and sanitation, and education on diarrhea, and other  things like this, and handwashing.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Executive Director & President, RB Health Business Unit, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: Moving on to Finish, the reason I talk about this innovation is that we knew always that, in Finish, cleaning your  dishwashers, not dishes only, cleaning your dishwasher is an important thing to do. But actually to clean  dishwashers, until now has meant that you have to unload the dishwasher and use it empty. Because of one  simple reason, the technology of the dishwasher cleaner, which is acidic, actually neutralizes the technology of  the detergent which is alkaline.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Executive Director & President, RB Health Business Unit, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: And, therefore, you cannot use them together. What does that mean? People get lazy, don't use them that  frequently. And secondly, you need more water and energy actually when you use a dishwasher on empty. This  has been a technology challenge for quite some time; something that we knew of because we actually, of course,  are front-runners in this [ph] area (01:07:43).

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Executive Director & President, RB Health Business Unit, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: This is the first product which actually works in an alkaline environment. So that actually, first of all, it provides a  synergistic benefit to cleaner dishes but also has a cleaner dishwashing. So you don't have to use your  dishwasher empty. You can actually put with every dish wash cleaning. Detergent, you can also choose to put a  dishwasher cleaner, so that is very, very interesting here, and that's why I chose to actually point it out.

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Executive Director & President, RB Health Business Unit, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: On SBP, a brand that we own in Brazil, actually it's the market-leading brand by a distance. So, I think that is quite interesting about this innovation,  and we are the first to market in SBP also.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So let me talk first talk about Cillit Bang. So Cillit Bang will be the brand to carry this is Europe. And what we are  doing is we have formulated a product, again, not an easy task from a technical point of view, which works as a  complete kitchen system. The kitchen system really here is that not only it cleans your dishes and therefore cuts  through the grease, but the foam also can be used to actually clean the kitchen surfaces and the foam is just the  right amount so that it does not cause streaking. So it's a pretty technically difficult thing to achieve this balance of  amazing grease cutting and right amount of foam, but also having no streaks on your surfaces. So it's a complete  kitchen system. It's a versatile product. It's a concentrated product. So the amount of product in every drop is  much more concentrated than the normal dishwash washing-up liquids that you find around Europe.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: Right. This is a very, very interesting idea which we are launching. Now, when we talk to moms, they tell us they  want to actually have perfectly clean – and they tell us they have – they want great cleaning, great stain removal,  but they don't like the idea of harsh chemicals. Now, I'm sure some of you can also agree with that.  But people think there's always going a to be trade-off between tough cleaning and safety, like if I give you  something safe, it could not be as good in terms of cleaning or the other way around. What we've managed to do is  to create a product with hydrogen peroxide as its centerpiece that allows consumers to have the same tough  cleaning that a bleach can give you without the necessary harsh chemicals associated with it. And what happens  here is that hydrogen peroxide when coming into contact breaks down into water and oxygen so it does not leave  any harsh residues.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: And people don't use Clearasil – they're worried about using Clearasil more than they need to because they think  it could cause drying. But we also know that if they don't use enough of it, it's not going to work as well. So you've  got to get the right balance. What we've given through this device is just the perfect dose of product which is  required to get to visibly clearer skin. So this a perfect dose product. That's point one.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So, that's really the idea, to combine air and fabric use all under one product, but now with a technology actually  which works for several hours. Actually, it works for 12 hours. So it's a 12-hour microencapsulation technology  and we're launching with this initiative also a number of other interesting initiatives with Air Wick. I don't think  we will have time to take you all through all our innovations, but there are quite a lot of interesting ideas on Air  Wick, which we are taking to the market also at the same time.

texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: And last one, I cannot finish this presentation without talking about Durex because you never let me go. What we have introduced is the first Durex silicon-based lubricant  which has three times longer lasting effect. It's also much better to use in terms of in feel and so on and so forth.  And I'm sure actual use is much better than words here, so I would just leave it at that.

texts.profession: QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION
texts.text: And then two, in terms of raw materials, what's your outlook for this year, given oil remains persistently high, will  you get some relief at all? And what can the cost savings be for Squeeze and X-Trim and SSL?

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc

texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So starting with gross margin, we're launching today a new project to deliver gross margin expansion and it's  called Project Fuel and it's this year's squeeze program. texts.speaker: Mary Elizabeth Doherty
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: Secondly, we have new programs to drive reduction in costs. Our margin strategy is about creating the fuel for our  future growth. texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: 2007 we said we wanted to reduce our carbon footprint per unit dose by 20%, and that was an end-to-end, a  cradle-to-grave impact, which means even including the amount of heat and energy that is deployed in using  dishwashers in homes of consumers, to take ownership of that carbon footprint, too. texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: And then this whole issue of social contribution, and we have increased just last year our social contribution with  our primary partners of Save the Children by 60%. texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Health, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So I talked about sustainable growth, and I talked about how RB 2.0 has set us up so that we can deliver and  drive sustainable growth. texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Health, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So, Gaviscon is the one on the left here and you've got an ordinary antacid on the right. And then on top, what Gaviscon does is it creates this raft, this white raft that  you see on top. This raft comes from a very special ingredient known as alginate. texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc

texts.speaker: Robert de Groot
texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: When you start doing laundry, you don't have a lot of disposable income, you probably have a soap bar and you  do the laundry that way. Then you move up to laundry powder. texts.speaker: Robert de Groot
texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So also here you see that the premium segment is growing much faster than value. texts.speaker: Robert de Groot
texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: These innovations and these decisions of what segments you play, they also have an impact on the margin. texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: And therefore, we started working on a vision, a vision that supports that purpose, that company purpose. And  this is the vision, is create a cleaner world. texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So it's eliminating dirt, pests, germs, odors that impact your health and your happiness. But then if you have this  beautiful product portfolio, what else can you do with that? texts.speaker: Robert de Groot
texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: The third mission is about delivering sustainable outperformance and outperformance is something that I think it  will not be a surprise. texts.speaker: Robert de Groot
texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: Another example that we're super excited about, to really stop diseases that are borne by mosquitoes, and this is  a Brazil example. texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: But also our big brands have bigger innovation in 2019 and some of them are displayed here, so you can have a  look later. texts.speaker: Robert de Groot
texts.profession: President-Hygiene Home, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: But we're also serving new needs; new needs like consumers want to have absence of harshness, absence of  harsh ingredients. texts.speaker: Rakesh Kapoor
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc
texts.text: So, we monitor all that and I have to say that we are – it is actually really very much on predicted grounds and  therefore we feel very comfortable as we go into 2019 in terms of what we expect the impact to be and it's all  again baked into the targets. texts.speaker: Dominique Thormann
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Good morning, everyone. As you all have already seen from the headlines, the group's financial results for the first  half of 2011 show that the first six months of our mid-term plan are in line with its objectives considering the  harsher environment that we operated in.

texts.speaker: Dominique Thormann
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: The cost of raw materials caused a negative impact of €313 million. This impact is worse than our initial guidance  in February, which is something that I pointed out to you as a risk when I presented Q1 revenues. This on-cost  relates to the steel contracts signed in July 1, 2010, which took a further increase on January 1 of this year, as well  as higher impacts from indexed raw materials and oil-based products.

texts.speaker: Dominique Thormann
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: For the next part of the walk down, we have grouped four items which together form the major part of our  Monozukuri cost reduction efforts announced during the strategic plan presentation Renault '16 – Drive The  Change.

texts.speaker: Dominique Thormann
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: As our sales mix outside of Europe expands, this is increasing the level of natural stock due to the longer supply  chain. However, this does not completely explain the difference above and beyond the one-time impact, such as  our new distribution scheme in China, inventory management was negatively impacted by the tsunami.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Of course, on the downside, the quake that hit Japan in March has had a disastrous impact on the car industry  and has aggravated pre-existing supply constraints impacting our company. These constraints have in return  impacted negatively our European commercial performance where we have not been able to produce enough cars  to meet the demand. It has also forced us to adjust the mix of models produced, namely gasoline versus diesel and  increased incentives in order to align demand levels to what we could supply.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: We estimate that the lost opportunity totaled 50,000 units, and in order to maintain the production levels, we  choose to distort our mix by producing cars where the supply of components were not limited. I would like to take  the example of the 1.5 diesel engine, which normally accounts for 84% of Clio sales in France.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: The tsunami also increased our upstream logistic costs in order to find quick replacement alternatives to provide  our plans with the missing parts. For the full year, we estimate that the tsunami and impact – will impact our  profits by €200 million. That tsunami was also impacted working capital due to a rise of inventories. As the  shutdown period for many industrial sites have been brought forward in July, we have had to build stock to cover  the vacation period.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Stock of petrol versions is also higher, as when factories restart, the mix will heavily shift back to diesel. In  addition, there was also an overstocking of 20,000 vehicles due to the teams concentrating on parts availability  rather than strict stock control.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: In 2012, capacity investments should reach €150 million enabling a 3.2 million unit capacity per year. Three- quarters of this investments will help increase the powertrain capacity with the remaining quarter of our – for our  vehicle production capacity.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Let me give you a concrete example. In order to improve our response to the strong 1.5 dCi powertrain demand,  we have increased our production by 100,000 units per year in the last three years, from 900,000 units in 2008 to  an expected 1,200,000 engines in 2011. In 2012, we expect our output to increase by another 70,000 units.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: The €279 million savings in the first half are the result of thousands of improvements of part processes, product  content across our line-up. Each single action helps reduce our TDC by a few cents of euros per vehicle. For  instance, on Scénic, the Douai plant decided to integrate the anti-corrosion treatment of several [indiscernible]  parts. It leads to a cost increase of €0.65 per vehicle for the plant. But it also allows a €5 per car purchase cost  reduction since the suppliers no longer need to process these parts through anti-corrosion. For the full year, the

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: We are expecting a similarly high success as the one we enjoy in Europe. By the end of next year, we will also have  localized production in Russia, India and Colombia. The second half of 2011 will mark a real breakthrough in the  automotive industry with the first ever electric vehicle sold at the same price as the diesel equivalent. Kangoo ZE  will start sales in October, Fluence ZE in November and Twizy in December. EV is not a bet, it's an insurance for  the future, insurance to be the best in CO2 emission, insurance to have a proper answer to further certain oil price  increases, insurance to stand years ahead of competition in terms of mastering the technology and its costs.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: A few hundred electric vehicles are already in customers' hands in Europe for testing, and the feedback we have  from old users is very supportive. Great driving pleasure, little range anxiety, practicality of the home or office  recharging, feeling of doing the right thing for the planet, and this without paying more than a traditional internal  combustion engine.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Raw material prices should remain above the level initially expected in February, taking the full year impact to  €600 million. Additional risks could emerge from further Forex deterioration and the concern on the euro zone  situation.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: So, that's the most important thing I would like to tell you is, I think people are deeply committed to the company  and there is high level of passion to do the best possible things. There is the sense of dilution of energy that is,  from my perspective, one of my priorities is to refocus the company on the business objectives.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: For the supply question, I think it's fair to answer by breaking down in two parts first to recognize that there was  during the financial crisis an extremely tight and frugal management of our investment related to capacity. And by  the end of the previous year, we obviously under-called the TIV in France, where of course the mix of diesel is very  high. This is why we were short of supply even before that tsunami came in. When the tsunami came in, we were  already very tight in terms of ability to meet the diesel mix in France, because we under-called the TIV in a  situation where the frugality of investment, capacity investment, management didn't give any room to capture an  upside coming from the market. That tsunami came in and made the situation worse with very well-known  specific supply of chips coming from Japan and from there we were trying to breakdown the available chips across  the different customers, as you may imagine.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: So, I would like to just mention the fact that tsunami is part of the problem. We had already this very tight  situation in terms of capacity and this is the reason why two weeks ago we decided to invest €150 million in  powertrain capacity, which historically has been a very tight bottleneck of the company. And we can connect this  to what I said about the powertrains. I believe Renault has one of the best diesel engine line-ups of the industry  and we need to leverage this strength.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: With the investment we have done of €150 million in powertrain and some other [indiscernible] parts, we are  bringing now the total capacity of the company to 3.2 million, and this includes some mix variation between  gasoline and diesel to make sure that we can continue to capture some upside in the markets if they appear.

texts.speaker: Dominique Thormann
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Okay. Why don't I take – no on the segment breakdown for the first half, but it's nothing – that's not the issue.  The issue is that's not the concern. The concern is we try to explain is mostly the diesel-petrol distortion that we  created deliberately because of the supply availability and constraints. So, that's what caused the imbalance and  because also don't forget we shifted our manufacturing patterns so that we closed plants earlier, so we ended up  pulling things forward when we shouldn't have had on-ground inventory.

texts.speaker: Dominique Thormann
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: But we'll be – so, we're shut now and we were shut already last week on the uncertain parts, and we'll be staring  earlier than plan. So, the manufacturing team have done a – a lot of – and it's not easy when you start disrupting  your manufacturing, your shift patterns, you disrupt your whole supply chain. So, that's what caused – so there's  timing and then there is petrol-diesel mix, but not inter segment, that's not the – that's not so much the concern.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: I think it's going to be top level competitiveness in terms of fuel efficiency on the car which is already very much  appreciated for the functionalities and for everything that makes life easy in this car. So, I am quite bullish about  increasing the sales overseas on mostly Mégane. Scénic will remain a more European product, but enhanced by  very competitive powertrains.

texts.speaker: Carlos Tavares
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Yeah, we don't see anything that could be a surprise for us on LCVs, I still consider that, it remains an upside in  profit mostly because we are not manufacturing as many cars as the market demand. So, anything that we will  improve namely in Batilly through the month of August in the efficiency of our assembly workshop for body-in- white will be immediately produced to the market. So, I see LCVs still as an opportunity for upside rather than the  reverse.

texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Nissan Motor Co., Ltd.

texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Nissan Motor Co., Ltd.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Nissan Motor Co., Ltd.
texts.text: And I think the companies with a smaller scale, who will not have this leverage, are going to be confronting a very,  putting the Espace on a common platform of the Alliance while it was a specific platform for Renault, Laguna, et  cetera, we see how much cost reduction and investment reduction is massive. texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Nissan Motor Co., Ltd.
texts.text: And for ZOE, I want you to know that all the R&D is already expensed. We have – we had the policy on electric  cars to – everything we can expense, we expense it. texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The success of all these activities allow us to meet one of our Drive the Change midterm objectives sooner than  forecasted, namely delivering an operating margin in excess of 5 %. texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Before moving to 2016, I would like to say a few words about the alliance stability covenant that was signed with  the French government and Nissan in December, and the recent controversy surrounding emission levels from  diesel-powered vehicles. There is a  shared understanding amongst all party that the alliance need to continue to prosper and generate growing  synergies. For the last 17 years, the alliance has enabled both Renault and Nissan to grow profitably in a  sustainable way.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: As regards emissions, at the risk of stating the obvious, there is no fraud or cheating at Renault. This has been  independently verified by government appointed commission in France that concluded that our vehicles are not  equipped with any fraudulent software. A ll our vehicles are compliant with existing regulation in all markets  where the group operates.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: That being said, we are working to further improve our performance in emissions. We already made an  announcement in December stating that the specific engineering taskforce had been put in place and that we  would roll out enhancements for better emissions performance.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We are confident in our own strengths, yet we are also aware of the challenges surrounding the industry. Let me  illustrate a few. Given commodities and energy price trends, we are not expecting that demand will improve in  some key emerging markets anytime soon. This is especially the case for Russia and Brazil, where we expect  further declines this year by 12% for Russia and 6% for Brazil. We remain convinced then these markets will  recover at some point and will be ready when this happens. However, for the time being, we have to continue the  hard work or keeping our businesses healthy in these markets.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Emissions regulations are nothing new. But following what happened last year to one of our competitors and the  confusions surrounding this issue, we will address this topic in a more demanding, clear, and stringent manner.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: 2016 will also be a year during which we will be framing the controls of our next business plan. Much of the  upstream work has already started and will lead to specific targets to be achieved in the future. texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The electrification of powertrains and the place of zero emission vehicles will gain an importance in the coming  years. texts.profession: Oddo & Cie SCA (Broker)
texts.text: So, I would like to understand, as a representative of the automotive industry and as the Chairman of Renault and  Nissan, what you intend to do to recreate the trust, the confidence, of investors and of customers, especially in  terms of a transparency? texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: I think it's a good solution, taking one independent entity, whatever it is, to test your cars. When you can test any  car today in any condition and find 5, 10, 15 times more emission than what is written. You think it's a solution?

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: No. Because what is important is, emission – I'm going to tell you exactly what we think about the problem, then  tell you what we're doing about it, okay? Anybody can do that, okay? And there is no way anybody c an have real driving emission standard that reflects the  way you're going to use your car, no way, because there are billions ways to use a car.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: And when you satisfy your customer, you need to understand what he wants, okay? Obviously, he wants a car  which is [ph] normed, (44:30) in the norms, but he wants a car which is cost-competitive, he wants a car with  good fuel efficiency, and frankly, he doesn't care only about NOx, he cares also about CO2, and he cares about  many other things. texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We're talking about NOx, diesel, Euro 6, that's all. But you can't open a Pandora box, where you say, what? Y ou  know what? I'm going to test the car on something else. I'm not going to take NOx. I'm going to take something  else. I'm going to take CO2. I'm going to take fuel efficiency. And you can here find any carmaker, any models, and  just say, you guys are cheating because, what I'm seeing on my car is not what you [ph] have announced it. (45:10)

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Our cars follow the norms. Yeah, you want to test our car, you're going to find 5, 10, 15 times, et cetera. Thank you  for having interest in Renault, but you can test any other car, not only on NOx, but how about testing on CO2 and  testing in other things? Y ou're going to find these kind of things, okay? So, the first thing is calming down and  telling the truth and the facts. We've done it, first with the officials. We had, from the official, clear statement  saying, these guys are not cheating.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Second, all our vehicles are on the norm. Third, but you can improve your performance on emission outside this.  Okay. Very good. Everybody can improve, et cetera, and we're going to do that. But we're going to have to do that  putting it in perspective. We're talking about diesel, NOx, Euro 6. How about the rest? Okay. After NOx, you're  going to have another emission, and then you're going to have CO2 and then you're going to have fuel efficiency.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We need to ask ourselves the question because, at the end of the day, our job is to make sure that our cars are  attractive. And they are competitive, still following the norms, still following the norms. And by the way, when we  say we have – some of your competitors are better than you because – yeah, maybe. But they've over-invested in a  certain way in diesel, which is a strategic decision, which I understand.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Well, you worry about emission, buy electric car. You worry about the emission, buy electric car, and we are the  leaders in electric car. If really your first concern is emission, well, we have the perfect car for your concern, buy  electric, buy ZOE, buy KANGOO electric, and we have other products coming.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: And we think that the answer – if this growth is emission growth, the answer is going to be zero emission. In zero  emission, we are the leaders. So, in a certain way, you have, from one side, to make sure you get out from the  debate; there's cheat, you don't respect the norms because everybody recognizing today that this is not the case. If  there is a problem, there are not enough norms, fine. Bring the norms.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Let's see how the norms going to do for the technology, by the way, because whe n the consumer are going to start  to see that diesel costing more and more money, they may be tempted to switch to gasoline or switch to electric –  which is fine for us, by the way, because we are very strong in these two categories. We obviously have a  communication to do a lot of public relation, and we're talking about it.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So, the idea of saying, okay, can we take an NGO and tell them to test our cars? Frankly, my opinion, it doesn't  resist five minutes analysis, okay? First, the question about, why an NGO will test your car for one carmaker, why?  Okay. NGO are not to test the car of one carmaker. They are to eventually save the world or resolve the emission.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: And second, no matter what test you're going to do, you can always come with an experience showing that you are  not respecting the norm because in the consumer mind, you need to tell them that you can use a car in a way  where emission are going to be no matter what, 5 times, 10 times much higher because even in Euro 6d, which has  been decided by the European Parliament, real driving condition, it's norm. Very specific condition on whic h the  car are going to be tested.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: And I can bet you that anybody who's going to go take a car, test it in a completely different condition, you're  going to get 2 times, 3 times, 5 times. I'm going say, hey, this is not my real driving condition. So, we ha ve to be  very careful about the emission, be very transparent. Make sure that we don't bullshit anybody about it. It's a  complicated issue. And this is an issue which is going to stay with us for many years to come.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Today, concentration is on NOx diesel because there was a cheat discovered, et cetera. But tomorrow, it may be  CO2. It may be fuel efficiency. It may be something else. And I bet you, because of the attention about that, you're  going to have a lot of media excited about, okay, let's go test cars into different condition. Emission problem have  one solution; it's zero emission. There's nothing – we don't emit anything. We have it.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Now, on where we are testing, we have to recognize, you are always going to get an emission different from what is  tested because you can always use a car in a way where you're going to obtain a completely different performance  than what is norm because you're never going to test the car exactly the way it has been norm even with the real  driving emission which has been delivered. So, that's why I'm very prudent on this, very prudent on this because  of the confusion and not to promise anything that we cannot deliver, and not promise anything which is against  the nature of our product.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: This is an important question about – but we are communicating. We're putting all the data. We have a  continuous engineering working with the French government in other country. We are making a lot of interview  with specialized press to try to explain the problem and also telling them, first, we have electric cars. Y ou  worry  about emission? Buy electric car.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Second, by the way, on CO2, we're one of the best car company in the world in term of emissions, fuel efficiencies  and CO2, which is global warming, by the way, which is the main concern of COP21. And then, you hav e the  specific emission on which we say, please norm, put the norms because when you put the norm, that's important.  And then, after the norm is being reached, then we can give the consumer what he wants.

texts.speaker: Georges Dieng
texts.profession: Natixis SA (Broker)
texts.text: Okay. Thanks for the reminder. Georges Dieng. Natixis. Two questions. First one on the CapEx cycle, with what  you said in terms of product renewal, the need to invest more related to emissions and the future projects  regarding autonomous driving, et cetera, should we see a surge or an uptick in the CapEx cycle or will you still  remain at a 9% CapEx to R&D ratio cap? That's my first question.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: But the question to your answer, we will – at no moment, will be higher than 9% in the foreseeable future and we  are capping the investment, not by avoiding doing projects, by particularly doing them in a different way. A lot of  cost reduction, a lot of sharing with Nissan, sharing with Daimler, this is the best way to cap the investment, and  at the same time, continue to have a very strong output of new products and new engines.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Okay. Well, we had, but for internal purposes, I've been told we cannot use it outside because you guys are too  curious. So, every time we show you something, you want more. So, we have a very simple chart where I put the  regions and the products and we put circles, green circle is profit, red circle is losses. And then we were product by  product, region by region, putting all these circles on the map. What's interesting that in 2005, there was one big  green circle on C segment Europe, a small green circle on LCV, light commercial vehicle Europe, and practically  everything else was red and small. That was [indiscernible] (1:05:27) 2005.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Today, when you look at this map, you have big green circle practically everywhere in Europe except for D, E,  which will be green this year. And then, you have most of the region green, okay? So, my question – what I want to  tell you is when I tell you it's a different company, it's – that mean we have invested and developed the product  and established a presence in markets where we can tell you, for the next two years to three years, you should see  much more contribution to profit coming from the different regions.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Up? He's asking for more cars and more engine. That's the situation in Europe. You have the situation in China,  obviously in China. But again, in China it's easy for us, because it's just – we're going up because we're starting  with practically zero.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: And you know very well that the day energy price start to move up, commodity price start to  move up, this market  is [ph] going flat (1:15:35), particularly that it went down. It went down 50%. To come back to the same level, it  will go up 100%. Okay?

file: RNO - Q4 2016 Earnings Call 10February2017 200 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 10-Feb-17.pdf

texts.speaker: Clotilde Delbos
texts.profession: Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Executive Officer - RCI Banque, Renault SA
texts.text: Let's see this in more detail. Slide 9 shows the main variance that explains this increase. I will start the walk down  reading left to right. Cost reduction activities contributed positively for €72 million. As we told you when we  published our Q3 results, our Monozukuri activities impacting positively €184 million for the full year have been  penalized by costs related to overheated demand and launch costs. In addition, we have decided to increase our  R&D spending both in terms of new technologies and additional products.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Beyond 2017, I would like to share a few brief thoughts. Our industry, as you know, is going to witness a lot of  disruptions, both in terms of products and services, and consequently, also in term of organization and  management. By 2030, a lot are expecting electric vehicle to account for 25% of new cars sold in urban areas.  And virtually, all vehicles will be connected to the Internet. It's no surprise for you if I say that the car of the future  will be electric, autonomous, and connected.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: The next mid-term plan is about sustainability of Renault. Sustainability of Renault means at the beginning it's top  level of quality and reliability of the cars. So, there is a real mindset transformation in term of quality. This has a  cost, it's an investment, it starts with additional costs that we are seeing here. Obviously, this is also combined  with the launch of a new product. But very likely what you should see in 2017 and 2018 is this number should go  down. Okay? I'm giving you trends here. These numbers will not go down. R&D will not go down because we are  multiplying – I mean I want to use the full scale of the Alliance to install a technological power of the Alliance.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: So, we are ahead in electric cars. It's clear today. We want to be ahead in autonomous cars. We want to be  ahead in connected cars and we're going to go ahead also with services. We're one of the most credible group  today in this field and we think this field is of nature changing the industry. We want to play our role so you can  expect this to continue.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Manufacturing and logistics, this should go down for a very simple reason is we have optimized the production in  order to catch every single opportunity of sales, which mean additional shifts, freight, et cetera. We had air  freights, et cetera. We had a lot of over-costs that we assumed to sustain our growth. But I can tell you in 2017  and 2018, I don't think we're going to have another 13% growth of our sales. So, this should go down.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: So, frankly, this is all absolutely not founded. We have all the elements to say it, because for you, it's important to  understand that this is about sustainability. I'm not after a peak performance in 2016 and the hell with 2017. I'm  not after peak performance in 2017 and the hell with it. So, we know that if we want to build sustainability, we're  going to have to be very disciplined but very reasonable also in term of pricing, and that's what we're pursuing.

texts.speaker: Georges Dieng
texts.profession: Analyst, Natixis SA
texts.text: Yes. Good morning. Georges Dieng, Natixis. Two questions, if I may. First question on diesel, could you share  your views on what could be the penetration of diesel in Europe and your own sales? And in terms of mix, what  could be the possible implications in terms of the margins? And second question on EVs, in general. Is this  business profitable as we speak? What's the breakeven point? And what would be, let's say, the combined  investment for both the Alliance and Renault standalone for the next EVs generation?

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Okay. Well, first about diesel; well, diesel is going to go down, it goes down in our sales, it's going to down with all  car manufacturers, it's going down country-by-country. And frankly, it's very logical. With the diesel bashing that is  taking place practically everywhere with the half-truths said about diesel, well, it can only go down. Plus, the  unfortunate event that happened with one of our competitors is not going to help a lot, because now there is  suspicion about all carmakers doing something fishy about diesel, which you know very well is not the case,  because so far only one carmaker has been clearly designated as having cheating device.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: All the others are investigation, maybe allusion that maybe something, but frankly, nothing has been determined.  And I can tell you, we have been investigated in France, in Germany, in Britain, in Korea, et cetera. Nobody has  so far, which we knew from the beginning because we stated from the beginning, there is no cheating device. But  what's going to happen is with the fact that they want to regulate emission in any conditions, well, this is going to  become more expensive; on top of the fact that the image of diesel is being bashed all the time.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: So, you're going to have a negative marketing campaign going on, including political campaign, plus, objectively,  the diesel cost is going to go up because you're going to have to put a lot of devices to reduce the emission in a  kind of utilization that, frankly, consumers don't even care about. So, this is going to go down. This is going to go  down in our sales. It's going to go down at the level of the industry.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Now, the question is how far it's going to go down. We think it's going to disappear from small cars. It may remain  a little bit on the higher level. Okay? So, which means premium, et cetera, some SUVs. That's what we think, but  we can be wrong also. I'm afraid I may be too optimistic also even with this. So, we are preparing for this. We are  preparing for this.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Obviously, as you know, we have a significant offer in gasoline, particularly thanks to the Alliance. And we are the  big player with electric car. So, we're going to continue to invest in diesel to make sure that – I'm not saying  investing to expand the diesel offer but investing to make sure that our diesels are more competitive both in  emissions and in term of performance. But at the same time, we know that this percent is going to decrease, so  we are heavily investing in gasoline engine and particularly with electric cars.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Electric cars, we have the clear intention to continue to be the leader, even though a lot of carmakers now are  coming to the electric car and recognizing the fact that this industry cannot perform without electric cars. We have  an extensive experience. We are today in a positive marginal profit on electric cars, I can tell you – because the  problem of profitability is how much of the research and the development you have made, you put in your cars.  So, I don't want to get into this debate. I consider this as a one-time fixed cost that I've already paid, okay, I don't  want to reimburse for that. It's already paid. It's buried in the past of Renault.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: I'm analyzing – we're pushing people to sell electric cars with marginal profit. And I can't tell you marginal profit on  electric car today is positive for Renault, which is obviously an advantage. We are encouraged to sell electric  cars, while most of the other carmaker are still in negative territory. And we want to advance as much as possible  the volume, because this is going to be the virtuous circle where the more you sell, the more you make profit, and  the more you have an advantage.

texts.speaker: Georges Dieng
texts.profession: Analyst, Natixis SA
texts.text: Yes. Just the first step of the EVs, I think the combined investment was around €4 billion for the Alliance?

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Well, from now on, the investments for electric cars are not different from investments for other cars. So, don't  think that it's going to – for us, it's going to require much more investment to develop a new electric car compared  to another car, particularly that as you know for the batteries. Today, we don't have to invest so much in batteries,  because there are so much offers in batteries and there is competition in batteries. One of the reasons for which  we started our own battery in 2008, 2009, there was no battery available for electric cars at that moment.

texts.speaker: José Asumendi
texts.profession: Analyst, JPMorgan Securities Plc
texts.text: And then, maybe a bit more strategically for Carlos, please. Your French competitor is basically saying that  they're going to comply with real-driving emission standards already three years ahead of time. So, maybe if you  could please talk about – a little bit about the implementation of [ph] RCR (00:01:17) across the fleet? And where  do you stand on real-driving emission standards?

texts.speaker: Clotilde Delbos
texts.profession: Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Executive Officer - RCI Banque, Renault SA
texts.text: In terms of raw material, as Mr. Ghosn mentioned in his speech, we are today facing huge upward trend on the  raw material that we haven't seen the impact until 2016, even though it has started in 2016 for many reasons. The  first one being that we have semiannual or annual contract in steel, so 2016 was protected for these increases.  And for the rest of the commodities between the small hedges that we make and the time it flows through our  P&L, it did not impact 2016.

texts.speaker: Clotilde Delbos
texts.profession: Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Executive Officer - RCI Banque, Renault SA
texts.text: So, for 2017, we forecast a few hundred millions. Yes, I think you can take as a first assumption that it might  reverse the positive impact that we have had this year and it might even be more than that, but we cannot make  any prognostic. Obviously, commodity is very volatile. Anything could make it go back down. And we're trying to  make sure that we negotiate the best contracts with our steel suppliers.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Yeah. Well, obviously, as you know, there is a lot of discussion taking place about the new emissions, when  they're going to be applied. Will there be enough capacity to validate all the new homologation, because what you  don't see today is all carmakers are going to have to re-homologate all their cars and with the new engines. And  the workload for the people who are going to be in the homologation is huge. We don't know how they're going to  be able to deal with this.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: So, there is a risk here, but this is a risk for the industry no matter how advanced you are in term of technology  and no matter how much investments you've made to make your diesel extremely performance in terms of  emission. We are seeing this bottleneck. We are discussing with the authorities by telling them, you have to be  careful, because if everybody needs to come and homologate before a certain date, you guys want to face a huge  workload. We don't know how you're going to do it. This is number one risk, but for the whole industry.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Second, yes, some carmakers are more advanced than others about really driving performance, because  depending about how much they invested in diesel before. Okay? It's true. Some carmakers are more advanced,  and some makers has issue. But they're going to be more advanced if the segment of the market is going down.  Let's not forget.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: And we are balancing our effort into not only improving our diesel performance, but we are keeping our eyes on  the fact that we need to have a strong gasoline offer and we have to have a strong electric car offer. So, we are  maintaining this balance, keeping an eye on the fact that the market is shifting. For the moment, the shift is very  clear.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: So, we want to maintain our diesel engines competitive, but we are preparing for a battle, in our opinion, is going  to be much more on gasoline engine, electric cars, and plug-in hybrid. But carmakers are not at the same level in  terms of emission, because the investments in technology has been very different. For some carmaker, diesel  was at the center of their powertrain technology. For other, it's one between different technology. But I'm glad  we're in the second category.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: So, moving from 63 to 90 is going to be a substantial improvement in cost from the French plants. This is not  going to position the French plant at the top level of the Alliance, but this is going to reduce a lot some of the  handicaps that we have been facing in the past with the production from the French plants. But for us, the  sustainability also for Renault – again, I come back to the sustainability of the performance, means we need to  transform France into a powerhouse as much as possible and to reduce the gap existing in productivity between  the French plants and some of the other plants of the Alliance.

file: RNO - Q4 2017 Earnings Call 16February2018 200 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 16-Feb-18.pdf

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: In 2017, we strengthened our leadership in the electric vehicle market. Our worldwide sales were up 38% versus  2016. Our best seller, the ZOE, is the number one electric vehicle sold in Europe, offering the best autonomy at  the best level of price for the fifth year running. Despite growing competition, more than 90,000 ZOE have been  sold so far. Last year, Renault-Nissan and Dongfeng formed eGT New Energy Automotive, a joint venture  designed to manufacture competitive and affordable electric vehicles for the Chinese market.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: From the risk side, the first one is obviously raw materials. We expect pricing headwinds throughout the year. The  second is uncertainty around ForEx exchange rate, particularly due to a surging euro. And, finally, the volatility in  mature markets due to stock market instability, rising interest rates, changing environmental and safety regulation,  consumer behavior will be particularly difficult to predict.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Okay. So, when you have a €122 billion purchasing bill, you better manage it well. 1%, 0.5%, 2% can make a big  difference and this is where the Alliance plays a role that in – when we see the cost of the technology that we  need to develop in terms of autonomous, in term of electric, et cetera, you can't duplicate. You can't afford to  duplicate. This is where the Alliance plays a role. So, hopefully, this answers some of your question. Maybe not –  are you okay? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Georges Dieng
texts.profession: Analyst, Natixis SA
texts.text: Yes. A question on emerging market, a follow-up, and maybe a focus on China in particular. I know that the  current situation you're starting from a low point doubling volumes. And obviously, there's a lot of challenges  ahead in terms of EVs. And I was wondering how you intend to address the situation in China. Will the JV you just  setup be enough to meet the new requirements starting in 2019?

texts.speaker: Francois Provost
texts.profession: Chairman-Asia Pacific Region, Renault SA
texts.text: Yes. For China, so the first step was to start the operation in DRAC, so we launched successfully the two first  SUVs, Kadjar and Koleos. We doubled the sales. Moreover, we already reached 87% of localization, thanks to  the Alliance. And in terms of quality, we already got a lot of awards, which is encouraging for the future. We  release our DRAC midterm plan, which is the contribution to drive the future for China passenger vehicles,  400,000 cars, nine localized models, of which three EVs. So, to answer to your question, we have the plan. We  have also the visibility to cope with regulation in terms of electric cars.

texts.speaker: Gianluca De Ficchy
texts.profession: Senior Vice President - Senior Vice President, Chief Executive Officer RCI Bank and Services, Renault SA
texts.text: Third component is that we have invested a lot on the strategy on the used car vehicle financing. We have  reached an exceptional result in 2017 with more than 300 vehicles financed. We were below 200,000 just a few  years ago. And this strategy will continue and the quality also of the portfolio for the used car financing is positive  today, it will remain positive in the incoming years.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Now, we can be anywhere between 6% to 7%, if we have very, very favorable conditions, we can be – that's why  I'm not telling you we're going to be below, I'm not going to tell you that we're going to be above, I frankly don't  know. It's going to depend a lot on factors which are independent of our view. Obviously, if the European market  performs at plus 6% this year versus 1%, it's a different story. It's a completely different story. So, I don't know  where the euro is going to be versus we are very sensitive to the pound, we are very sensitive to the Argentinean  peso, we are very sensitive to the ruble. So, that's why we are being cautious. This cautious doesn't mean we're  cautious about our own performance. We feel very strong about our own performance in 2018, but we are a little  bit careful with the environment around us.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Now, the question you're asking about how the consumers are reacting in front of everything coming on  regulation. It's very interesting. Consumers are running out of diesel. What you're seeing today in term of  percentage of dieselization is artificial. Why? Because if you go to the retail and you go to specific customers, the  percentage of request on gasoline is much bigger than what we are selling. The problem is that the industry is not  able to follow instantly the shift between diesel and gasoline, and this is something which is going to stay with us.

texts.speaker: Carlos Ghosn
texts.profession: Chairman, President & Chief Executive Officer, Renault SA
texts.text: Now, to make it more complicated in different function of the segments. If you are into the D-segment, for  example, the shift from diesel to gasoline is less visible. But when you go to the lower segment, it's obvious. And  we have to look at it category by category, fleet versus retail, because you may have big shifts when you consider  that. But I mean, this is something which is interesting is, today – I'll ask you one question. The car which is the  most sold in retail in Europe, the number one cars most sold in retail, forget fleet, forget the registration, forget  anything else, is today the Sandero, the number one car most sold in Europe. So, again, and that's one of the  beauty of Dacia is we're trying to focus mainly on retail.
