texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Let me start with a brief review of 2011. Last year, it was marked by Germany's new energy policy, the  government's sudden decision to phase out nuclear power, resulted in significant one-off burdens, overshadowing  our financial performance. As anticipated, all major financial performance indicators were down on the previous  year, although we slightly outperformed our own expectations.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Our efficiency program is also on track. We are actually ahead in our plans and managed to achieve more than the  envisioned €900 million for 2011. The program will come to a close by the end of this year, with cumulative  savings of €1.5 billion compared to the base year 2006. But we are not resting on our laurels. You know you won't  wear them on the wrong spot on your body if you're resting on them. We have already kicked off a new program,  which together with the additional efficiencies of the current program, target to further efficiency enhancement of  all together €1 billion compared to 2012.  Finally, we have also made progress in the renegotiation of our long term oil-indexed gas contracts. With three gas  suppliers, by the larger number of contracts, we were able to remove the gas-to-oil spread risk by either moving to  gas wholesale price indexation or early termination of the contracts by mutual agreement.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Ladies and gentlemen, one of the cornerstones of our strategy to transform RWE into a more international, more  sustainable and more robust company is our new built program of thermal power plants. By 2014, we will have  renewed more than one quarter of our generation fleet. At that point, we have – we will have invested  approximately €12 billion to operate one of the most modern thermal generation portfolios in Europe.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: This program reduces specific CO2 emissions conservatively. The replacement of our old 150 megawatt lignite  blocks of which we still have 12 at the end of 2011, with the new BoA which is the new improved lignite fire  technique will also – will alone reduce our annual CO2 emissions by 6 million tons per year.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Where do we stand in this program? At the end of last year, we had 2.6 gigawatts of new capacity connected to the  grid. For the year 2012, we expect five power plants with a total of 6.8 gigawatts to enter into operation in rapid  succession.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: In January and February, the two gas combined cycle gas turbines, Claus C and Moerdijk, were commissioned. At  the end of March, our lignite plant in Neurath will come into operation, followed by the CCGTs in Pembroke, U.K.  and Denizli, Turkey in the second half of the year. Next year, we will start operations at our hard coal power plant  in Hamm, Germany. The program will be finalized in 2014, with the commissioning of the Dutch hard coal plant  in Eemshaven.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: I'm happy to report that we are finally coming to an end of this huge program successfully, the biggest in the  history of RWE. I would also like to compliment the skills and experience of our engineers. You might have heard  about the problems that other players in the market have faced concerning the new T24 steel grades used in coal  plants, mainly the occurrence of hydrogen-induced stress corrosion cracking, Spannungsrisskorrosion in German,  which leads to significant delays and cost overruns. Thanks to the sophisticated ramp-up project developed by  RWE technology, we have been able to exclude any such problems on our project so far, knock on wood.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: On the other hand, we were able to profit from trial runs of our new Neurath lignite plant precisely at the height of  the cold temperatures, while we still have our traditional 150 megawatt blocks in operation, 12 of them. This  enabled us to have 11,500 megawatt, 11,503 to be correct, of lignite power connected to the grid in the middle of  February, which was a new record production.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: When I came onboard almost five years ago, I knew that I would have a big task at hand to change the course of a  supertanker such as RWE, to make it more sustainable, more international and more robust. In addition to the  financial crisis and the economic downturn, politicians did their bit to make the sea rougher. But as a hobby  sailor, I know that you sometimes have to adjust course due to stormy weather without losing sight of the final  destination.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: I believe that we have prepared the group for the radical changes in the energy sector by initiating and executing  the biggest investment program in RWE's history. We were not deterred by external or internal setbacks and are  just starting to reap the benefits.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Four out of nine new power plants are already operational. These replace older less-efficient plants, provide more  flexibility and lower CO2 emissions. With the foundation of RWE Innogy, renewable energy became an integral  part of the group strategy. By 2014, we will have 4.5 gigawatts in operation or under construction, contributing to  €500 million of operating results. By 2020, we are targeting 20% of renewable and generation capacity.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: RWE Dea has become and will remain a core growth area of the company. Despite the planned disposals, our  upstream business will increase production to more than 40 million barrels of oil equivalent per year and reach  €800 million in operating results by 2014.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: With our CCGT project in Turkey, we also stepped into new growth regions for our traditional electricity and gas  activities. There are further opportunities to grow in Central Eastern and South Eastern Europe, and RWE is well- positioned to make use of its expertise and skills.  Over the last four years, we also doubled our research and development expenditures. We put major emphasis on  finding solutions to prevent carbon dioxide from power plants entering into the atmosphere. With our innovative  pilot projects, I believe we are one of the pioneers in this field.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Finally, the bundling of our gas procurement contract allows us to proactively manage the gas portfolio with the  commercial expertise and knowledge of RWE Supply & Trading and seeks structural solutions to fundamental  market changes in the sector. So whilst the selling conditions have not always been as favorable as I would have  liked, I believe that as I prepare to hand over to the new captain, RWE is well-positioned for the voyage ahead.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Ladies and gentlemen, let me start with the headline numbers for the group. External revenue was slightly down  by 3%, mainly as a result of lower external sales from own electricity generation via RWE Supply & Trading.  Jürgen has already mentioned the performance for our key earnings numbers, EBITDA and operating result. I'll  come to the details in a minute.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: The non-operating result declined by approximately €400 million, mainly due to restructuring measures. We had  one-off burdens of approximately €500 million for staff reduction matters in our German Generation and Sales  and Distribution businesses. Peter will give you more information on our further efficiency targets in a minute. In  addition, we suffered from impairments on our Dutch Generation portfolio and on the former Essent gas storage  activities.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Slide 10 gives you an overview of the development of the operating result by division. The new German energy  policy has left its mark on the German Power Generation business unit, with the reduction of the nuclear lifetime,  the introduction of the nuclear fuel tax and earlier closure of our nuclear power plant at Biblis.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: In the period under review, we had about €1.3 billion of burdens from the new German energy policy and the  nuclear fuel tax. In addition, the Power Generation division suffered from lower realized spreads. Take together,  these factors led to a decrease in operating result of 33%.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: The second negative factor is the development in our Trading/Gas Midstream division. The division has been  particularly hit by the impact of the negative gas-to-oil-spread. In addition, the performance of the Trading  business has been much weaker than usual.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: As expected, our Dutch business, Essent, couldn't repeat the results from last year, mainly due to the transfer of  gas midstream activities to our Trading/Gas Midstream division. Weather conditions were also less favorable than  last year.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Our CEE/SEE division reports a reduction in operating result of 5%. In the Czech market, we faced decreasing  grid margins and lower gas sales. In addition, in Hungary, we suffered from burdens from regulation and  declining electricity sales due to tough competition.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Our Renewables business benefited from increased generation volumes and more favorable quotes of prices.  Furthermore, liquidated damages from our share in the wind offshore project, Greater Gabbard, had a positive  impact.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Our Upstream business strongly increased its operating result to €558 million. Higher gas and oil prices and  improved oil production are the main drivers.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Ladies and gentlemen, let's have a look at what we are expecting for the individual divisions of this year before  Peter will give you an update on the overall group outlook for 2012 and 2013 later. The German Power Generation  business unit is expected to close above 2011. Major driver is the commissioning of the new lignite-fired power  plant in Neurath.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Furthermore, expect the positive contribution from the change of nuclear provisions and lower maintenance and  operating costs. This will more than offset declining generation margins and a higher nuclear fuel tax. Although  first court rulings on the nuclear tax were in our favor, we still have to book the costs in the P&L.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: We see our German Distribution and Sales business unit on par with the last year. On the one hand, we will  benefit from our efficiency improvements. On the other hand, we expect lower income from participations and the  absence of positive one-offs from the first-time consolidation of NEW in 2010.  The Netherlands/Belgium division had fallen significantly below the previous year. Declining gas midstream and  electricity generation margins cannot be fully offset by further efficiency gains.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Before the fire at our Tilbury site on February 27, we expected a further significant increase in RWE npower's  operating result year-on-year, particularly as a result of our ongoing efficiency improvement and the  commissioning of our Tilbury biomass plant. This will now be dependent on the extent of the damage from the  fire.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: In the Retail business, we are expecting progress on the squeezed domestic margins. Again, this Power Generation  business will suffer from declining from declining generation spreads.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: The CEE/SEE division is expected to show decline in operating result compared to 2011. This is mainly due to  expected lower gas sales and good margins in the Czech business. Continuous commissioning of new projects in  our Renewables division will lead to an increase in operating earnings in 2012.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: In the current year, we expect our Upstream Gas & Oil division to show a further strong earnings increase. The  start of production in new gas fields, higher gas prices and lower exploration costs will be the main drivers.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: The development in our Trading/Gas Midstream activities are still dominated by the negative gas-to-oil spread  and our ongoing price reviews. We do expect further improvements during the course of the year, but we only  anticipate significant relief to come from 2013 onwards. For that reason, the operating results might even fall  significantly below the negative number of 2011, as we are still paying the high contract prices to our suppliers but  achieved only traded wholesale prices with our customers.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Ladies and gentlemen, let me take the opportunity to give you a brief update on the situation with our long-term  oil-indexed gas contracts. Total procurement portfolio is approximately 45 bcm. This is approximately 2 bcm less  than last year. Long-term oil-indexed contracts account approximately 20 bcm compared to 24 bcm at the  beginning of 2011, after we settled first renegotiations at the end of last year of which some were transitioned to  fully-traded wholesale market indexation in the next years, some moved already to fully-traded wholesale market  prices.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: But the volume of our oil-indexed gas contracts to end clients fell from approximately 4 bcm to approximately 2  bcm. As a result, our net exposure declined to 18 bcm as of February this year. We are still in renegotiations for  nine out of our 17 contracts and are optimistic that we will solve this issue during the course of 2013.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: Last but not least, we also did announce new efficiency targets. By 2014, we want to improve our underlying  earnings by €1 billion, of which approximately €750 million should already be realized next year.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: So let me quickly run through this. In terms of regional strategy, we continue to remain focused on our core  electricity and gas markets in Central Europe. However, our growth areas of Renewables, Upstream Gas & Oil as  well as Central Eastern and South Eastern Europe will be broadening our geographical exposure, and thereby  diversifying specific country risks, predominantly those of regulatory and political nature. To this end, more than  60% of our investments between 2012 and 2014 will be outside Germany.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: The same holds true for our Generation business. Our broad generation mix is less exposed to single isolated  commodity price movements. The best example is the combination of our lignite and gas generation fleet, but the  combined risk is much lower than the individual risk position.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: At present, we are benefiting from the fate of our clean brown spreads. The geographical-diversified Renewables  business is also better suited to balance better patterns in different regions. In addition, investments in the most  economic renewable technologies reduce these future regulatory risks.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Our Distribution and Renewables businesses provide a regulated and stable income stream. Disposals of regulated  network companies will be compensated for by the increase in contribution from regulated renewables. Our  Upstream business offers exposure to global unregulated commodity prices.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Becoming more sustainable remains at the top of our agenda. Here, we are working I three different areas. First,  we want to lower our specific CO2 emissions by more than 20% by 2020 compared to 2005. Although CO2 has  become less prominent in the realms of the financial market, but at least because of the steep decline in costs for  emission certificates, CO2 reduction remains a key priority for Germany and Europe. We don't see this changing  in the foreseeable future or in relation to any new carbon mitigation regulation post 2020.  Our target, therefore, is to reduce the specific CO2 emission factor physically to 0.62 tons per megawatt hour by  2020. Including financial measures, it will even come down to 0.5. More details on our current CO2 position and  reduction path can be found in the back-up section.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Second, with the nuclear phase out in Germany, renewable energy plays an even bigger role. It's important to see  that the trend for more renewables has decoupled from the goal to simply reduce CO2 emissions.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Firstly, renewable technologies such as wind and biomass are expected to become even more economical in the  long run. Secondly, they support the desire to be less dependent on the traditional primary energy sources. We  have, therefore, set ourselves a target of increasing our renewable capacity to at least 20% by 2020, from  approximately 8% at the end of 2011. We will focus on those technologies which are most economic and therefore  be – they have the lowest risks for political intervention.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Thirdly, last but not the least, we promote the efficient use of energy, not only through more efficient power plants  but also by developing and offering energy-saving products to our customers; products as micro cogenerated –  cogeneration units and heat plants.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: To our smartphone offering, we standardize and encourage the customers to use less energy. And with our  investments in the charging infrastructure, we facilitate the use of electric cars, not only in Germany but for  example also in the Netherlands. The city of Amsterdam ordered last year at least 125 charging stations to support  their project of 10,000 electric vehicles by 2015.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: With this in mind, let's have a look at our capital expenditure on slide 19. As you can see, we have passed the peak  of our investment program. For this year, we expect investments of some €6 billion. This includes the completion  of a number of conventional power plants projects which we haven't mentioned before.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: From 2013 onwards, our investments will come in line with more sustainable CapEx levels, which we see between  €4 billion and €5 billion. This includes day-to-day CapEx of approximately €2 billion to €2.5 billion. And for 2012  and 2013, the majority of investments are already committed. For 2014 onwards, there is more flexibility to adjust  CapEx levels which will be used for our financial discipline if required.  On slide 20, you can see how much we will be spending in our key growth areas. Some €6 billion is earmarked  from Renewables, Upstream Gas & Oil in Central Eastern and South Eastern Europe until 2014. This does not  include the day-to-day investments in these divisions.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: We will invest more than €1 billion per annum in our Renewables activities, focusing mainly on offshore and  onshore wins as well as biomass projects. We can't confirm our capacity target of 4.5 gigawatts in operation or  under construction by 2014 as well as operating earnings targets and €500 million for the same year.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: With a number of projects currently under development and said to start production over the next three years, we  have decided to provide you with a nearer-term target. It shows that successful growth path developed RWE Dea.  The target is to increase production to more than 40 million barrels of oil equivalents by 2014 with an operating  result of approximately €800 million.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: However, despite the planned asset disposals, we are still confident in the longer-term growth post-2014. RWE  Dea has continued its successful exploration track record, increasing its resources and options for further  developments, for example, in its Titan and Zidane projects in Norway. On this basis, we will still expect Dea to be  able to double its production to 70 million barrel oil equivalents in the course of this decade.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: In Central Eastern and South Eastern Europe, we see growth opportunities in Generation, especially in Turkey  and Poland. Please bear in mind, slide 20 gives you the divisional split of the planned CapEx. From a regional  point of view, there is, of course, an overlap. Investments from the Renewables and Upstream division can also  take place in Central Eastern and South Eastern European markets.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we have already initiated the next efficiency program. For 2013 and 2014, we are targeting  further efficiency enhancements of approximately €1 billion per annum compared to 2012. On the one hand,  already existing measures will lead to additional efficiencies of €500 million from 2013 onwards compared to  2012. On the other hand, we are working on completely new measures of approximately €500 million.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Out of the new measures, a total of approximately €250 million is expected for 2013. All of this will help to offset  the pressure we are facing from the full auctioning of CO2 certificates which will hit us from 2013 onwards.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: We have identified the major synergies between generation portfolios of the group and have started to realize  them. Take for instance our fleets of state-of-the-art CCGTs in Germany, the U.K. and the Netherlands. In terms  of where we operate, 14 identical machines of Alstom, type GT 26 gas turbines in all of these plants. In the future,  we can benefit by sharing our experience and having a common maintenance strategy across the national  companies. This provides synergies over a double-digit million euro amount.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: This brings us to our outlook for 2012 and 2013. Corporate call press already provided you with the divisional  outlook for this year. For 2012, overall, we expect EBITDA operating results and recurrent net income to be in the  order of 2011. This means that we are able to mitigate the full-year dilution effects from our disposals of Amprion,  Thyssengas and the Rostock hard coal power plants.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Moving out to 2013, we now anticipate to not only offset the dilution from further disposals, but also the impact of  full auctioning of carbon certificates, so we are confident that we will avoid the infamous carbon cliff. Our new  efficiency program is one major reason for the improved outlook. Last August, our outlook did not yet include the  centrally decided measures we are currently working on.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: For EBITDA, we even expect to be above last year's level. However, you have to bear in mind that our new power  plants will lead to an increase in depreciation charges.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: With regard to the gas-to-oil spread situation, we updated our expectations in mid-February. We also anticipate  some successful results for our gas contract negotiations.

texts.speaker: Vincent P. Gilles
texts.profession: Analyst, Credit Suisse Securities (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: And my second question is a need of clarification on what you hinted at regarding the renegotiation also of some  of your gas contracts. You used the word some contracts and some renegotiation. It would be interesting to  understand what you actually achieved here. Is it a price cut, sort of P&L cut? Is it an element of flexibility on part  of the contracts you renegotiated or is it a full flexibility on some other contracts? Thank you very much.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: With respect to the gas contracts, I think that is nothing new. We already, in the Q3 call last year, told the market  that we were able to remove the gas-to-oil spread risks by either moving to get wholesale price indexation or early  termination of these contracts by mutual agreement. So it's not only a simple P&L adjustment, but it's really that  what is our final goal that is reducing our exposure to the gas-to-oil spread.

texts.speaker: Peter Wirtz
texts.profession: Analyst, Westlb AG (Broker)
texts.text: Yeah, hi, good afternoon. First question on gas also; on top – in terms of your guidance 2013, how much has  changed compared to six months ago in terms of including a goal for the gas business in this 2013 assumption?  Because the feeling that some of the rulings seem to postpone into the year 2013, 2014, which means there's  probably a bit more pressure here. And the second question, regarding the dividend policy; in terms of your target  to cover investments and dividends with operating cash flow, it seems to indicate that you are not prepared to  raise the payout ratio to a level of 60% in the foreseeable future.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: I think I take the first question, that is very simple straightforward, there is essentially no change to the  assumption this time compared to the assumptions we have made in August with respect to the outcome of the  gas-to-oil price revisions.

texts.speaker: Patrick Hummel
texts.profession: Analyst, UBS AG (Broker)
texts.text: Yes, good afternoon, everybody. Patrick Hummel from UBS. Also two questions from my side, first one regarding  the profitability outlook for your coal and gas generation business. I mean your peers have been quite cautious  here on the outlook given the spreads where they are and also pressure on operating hours due to ongoing  Renewables growth, potentially declining demand, et cetera. I just wanted to pick your brain, what your thoughts  – your latest thoughts are on the profitability of your hard coal and gas stations and in that context, how are you  thinking about closures and when you think you will have finalized decisions about potential closures or  mothballing.

texts.speaker: Patrick Hummel
texts.profession: Analyst, UBS AG (Broker)
texts.text: And the second question is simply to understand the situation at the Tilbury plant in the UK. When do you think  we will have clarity in terms of the maintenance shutdown? How long it will take and whether or not the biomass  firing could be delayed by that incident?

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Well, Patrick, let me address your questions. The easier one is Tilbury, we expect about four months maximum  delay. And we have to be very careful to determine the cause of the fire. We are using several different types of  wood pellets and we have to see whether there was a flaw in the manufacturing of the wood pellets in the storage  and so on. And we want to make certain that this doesn't happen again. Luckily, none of the vital components of  the actual power station was destroyed. It was only the storage facility.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Second, Patrick, that is your first question. We have – when we embarked on our investment program,  emphasized the flexibility of the new plant and the CO2 reduction, and we have always, and this was in some cases  even a prerequisite to obtain the permission to build and operate, dam closures, plant closures, we mentioned the  16 150-megawatt blocks, of which four were closed until the end of last year. But this year we were just lucky, we  had a windfall that they were still operational when the new BoA was already in its trial so we could sell a lot more  electricity in the past month and a half than we had planned for. But those 12 150-megawatts lignites will go out in  – by the end of the year.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: In general, some other thermal power stations are – I should call it under scrutiny. We haven't decided yet what to  close. In fact when we decided then we had a local outcry and we found very interesting solutions, for example in  Saar that we handed the power station over to another operator who got CO2 credits for it and that made it viable  again. Some of the thermal power stations will stay in a, let's say half year cold reserve. But we still think that with  our fleet, particularly with the lignite-based power stations in the present market conditions, still taking into  account the CO2 price, the emissions price and so on, our present fleet is well-positioned and we are not  announcing further closures.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Patrick, may I add to that, that in 2012, we have 1.4 gigawatts of spare capacity that's contract in which will be  going out and that is rather old hot coal capacity which will probably not be in the money and is being replaced  with some of the newer assets that we have invested in.

texts.speaker: Alexander Karnick
texts.profession: Analyst, Deutsche Bank GmbH (Broker)
texts.text: Yes, good afternoon. Just one question or two questions rather. One is on gas again, obviously, you reduced your  net exposure in terms of bcm to 18 from 20 last year, in your positive contribution outlook, is it now possible for  you to – sort of, give an indication, sort of what a exposure assumption could still be in there? I'm trying to gauge  how much of a positive contribution could we actually underline ongoing operational whatever you want to call it  and how much could be actually a one-off contribution for settlement of earlier closures?

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Alex, are you sure you're right in the investment business? You are phrasing your questions so diplomatically. I  think you could also work elsewhere but to the first question, I will address the first one, second one will go to  Peter Terium because he is designing the new efficiency programs.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: The first one is no, we will not give you any further. It's a nice try, you're asking so politely and kindly but we will  not give you anything further than just that we managed to reduce the exposure by 2 billion cubic meters per year  from last year to this year. This is all the information we can give on this.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Yeah. On the section with €650 million, we have already indicated earlier that €500 million out of that was  already included in existing midterm planning. We now updated it and added another €150 million. The €500  million is backed up by individual programs like efficiency improvements in the retail and downstream areas,  plans in Generation division where we put a new modern fleet in and take old power plants out that has a head  count effect certainly. All of it has already been taken care of in the last year's numbers. We also had some of the  provisions for that already in H1 and I've indicated in August that that was already taken for.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Part of that is also the result of the head count reduction due to the nuclear phase-down, the immediate  decommissioning we have, so the immediate stoppage we had last year. And also included in the €500 million is  Netherlands because it has now become a "division of a larger enterprise" rather than a standalone company on its  own. All of that adds up and this is including efficiencies in retail sales area where we benchmark individual sales  activities in each of the countries that adds up to the €500 million. The additional €150 which comes on top of  that is a further program which we are currently working through and that is a combination of increased  efficiencies, cost reductions also in IT and in procurement and also as a result of more efficient working and the  result of the energy transition that we will reduce head count at the end of today. We don't know exactly how  much at this moment in time but we're confident that we can deliver the social acceptable way.

texts.speaker: Peter A. Bisztyga
texts.profession: Analyst, Barclays Capital Securities Ltd.
texts.text: And then my second question is your 46 gigawatts of capacity that you're targeting for 2020, does that include any  new fossil fuel or nuclear build beyond your existing program to 2014?

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: On the 40 gigawatts by 2020, that does not include any further investments – 46 gigawatts, it does not include  any further investments in fossil or nuclear power plants.

texts.speaker: Benjamin Leyre
texts.profession: Analyst, Exane BNP Paribas SA
texts.text: Yes, thank you and good afternoon. Two questions, please. First one on the CO2 regulation, I was curious to see  your opinion of the likely outcome of current discussions at the EU level to [reiterate] the ETS and also if the UK  issue or perceive a possibility that the CO2 price floor may be revised down? And the second question, curious to  see if you were hearing any remark about taxation on lignite in Germany or nuclear in the Netherlands? Thank  you.

texts.speaker: Stephan Lowis
texts.profession: Vice President-Investor Relations, RWE AG
texts.text: Benjamin, I think we didn't get your first question right. You asked something about our CO2 target or on the  European level, the CO2 target?

texts.speaker: Benjamin Leyre
texts.profession: Analyst, Exane BNP Paribas SA
texts.text: At the European level, if there is any – what is your view on the evolution of regulation on CO2 at the EU level?

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Well, let me address the first one or maybe even the second one since – well, I mean, Peter, the political  connections are your responsibility now but I think if you like – as to the first one, I think that the European  Commission and the European government are realizing that it is an illusion if only 14% of the world's CO2  emissions are regulated by a cap-and-trade. To make those 14% even more and more expensive, that may reduce  them but the total CO2 exposure in the world will continue and so that there were some press reports lately that  even some hardcore environmentalists say that it does not help just to make CO2 more expensive here but we  need global other arrangements for this.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: As to the second one, energy security also, that is the second one was the taxation of lignite. I see no risks, at least  not for the four or five years ahead of us that lignite is taxed. That is my personal, of course, my personal view and  the major political parties in Germany will not tax our domestic fuel because this brings energy security.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Okay. Let me add to that and confirm that. Even various recent talks I've had on both the national or country level  as well as on federational level with politicians and ministers do not give an indication of an actual plan for  awareness that maybe the energy transition that they have initiated could come to an additional, quite  considerable additional burden for both the consumers as well as the industries. So there is some hesitation to put  any further additional cost in the energy system. And the last one you've asked of, nuclear taxation in Netherlands,  I'm not aware of any concrete plans in that nation and I don't think they are very realistic.

texts.speaker: Sofia Savvantidou
texts.profession: Analyst, Citigroup Global Markets Ltd.
texts.text: And just the second question, sorry to come back on the gas contracts. The 2 bcm that you have reduced your  exposure to with regards to the oil-to-gas spread, is that a permanent reduction, i.e., is this forever or is it just for  2012 and it might go back up to 20 bcm or 19 bcm or whatever in 2013 or 2014? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Andreas Thielen
texts.profession: Analyst, MainFirst Bank AG (Broker)
texts.text: Yes, good afternoon. Firstly, I'd like to understand with respect to 2013, how you treat the CO2 certificates which  you have secured over the past years, in order to cover your position there as presumably prices, they locked in at  – were higher than current market prices. And secondly, with respect to your targets for offshore wind growth, we  heard a lot about problems with grid connection and I just wonder how much of your project pipeline is related to  Rolf Pohlig  Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG  A May I start with respect to the CO2 position, I think you're referring to the strategic CO2 position which we have  built up over the recent past. You're absolutely right that prevailing CO2 prices currently are below the level at  which we on average acquired those certificates. The answer is relatively simple. All these certificates which we  bought will be used during the time horizon of 2013 until 2020, i.e. during the course of the third compliance  period. And that is also with respect how they are used, they are used on the straight line which means that in each  of the following years, one-eighth of the overall certificates which we bought will be used and then we will see that  financial burden by one-eighth per year.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: Then on the delay, potential delay in offshore wind projects, this is within our view in – one project that we have  in the planning, it's Nordsee Ost, that is having a potential delay of up to a year and it will delay from mid of 2013  until the end of 2013, beginning of 2014, talking about 295 megawatts, so given this time window, it will not  impact the outlook that we have given to you on 2013.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: Yeah, Andreas, the majority of our offshore wind projects at the moment is outside of Germany, not within  Germany.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: These three projects under construction, two are in the UK, Gwynt y Môr and Greater Gabbard and the third one  is Nordsee Ost in Germany, the already mentioned 295 megawatts. UK offshore wind parks are much larger, they  are 576 megawatts and 504 megawatts.

texts.speaker: Bobby Chada
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Hi, good afternoon, everybody. First question is about Tilbury. If it's offline for a certain period this year, my  understanding is under the Large Combustion Plant Directive, the running hours are limited. Is it right to think  that any running hours that you do not use in 2012, you can then use in 2013 instead, so effectively, we could see a  shifting of the margin from 2012 to 2013?

texts.speaker: Bobby Chada
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: And then second question is on slide 47 of the presentation pack, where you helpfully set out the EBITDA and  operating results from the 2012 through 2014 CapEx plan. Looking at the various big projects in thermal  generation, E&P and Renewables, it seems that a reasonable piece of this €1 billion is likely to come after 2013.  Could you add any color to that, or?

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: And there are two additional issues. As you know, Tilbury will then be fully converted to biomass and then it will  fall under the Large Combustion Plant Directive. And also, at the moment we were definitely suffering a certain  damage. Luckily, no personal injuries incurred but after sometime then we also have our insurance for disruption  of operations. So financially, it's not quite clear how this accident and this fire really impacts us. But it's, let's say,  low, low, low double-digit...

texts.speaker: Bobby Chada
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: Is it possible to ask a follow-up on the biomass piece?

texts.speaker: Bobby Chada
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc
texts.text: You talked about not really being sure of the cause of the problem. Is there anything to make you question the  technical basis for burning biomass at Tilbury or is it really just a very cautious statement?

texts.speaker: Jürgen Großmann
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG
texts.text: It's a cautious statement, there is nothing that we worry. There's nothing fundamentally wrong with burning  biomass, we – this is well -tested. But still we have to find out what caused this fire.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: But we know out of experience, Bobby, in the Netherlands, with Essent is that, it takes quite some time to really  get the procedures and the routines around the handling of biomass correct. So it's an element of training,  experience and also the fine-tuning of the equipment locally. And that takes some time and we need to investigate  exactly where it went wrong but there's nothing fundamentally against using biomass in such large volumes.

texts.speaker: Vincent De Blic
texts.profession: Analyst, JPMorgan Securities Ltd.
texts.text: Yes, good afternoon, two questions, please. The first one was on asset disposals. Your indication of potential  valuation is obviously much more bullish than in others. I wanted to know how confident you were in the  valuations you've used? And also if you could just remind us of which non-producing effects we should be thinking  of, whether it's just E&P or also potentially some power plants being built. That was the first question.

texts.speaker: Vincent De Blic
texts.profession: Analyst, JPMorgan Securities Ltd.
texts.text: The second one is on gas. Is there any major difference, that from the terms of the contract you have re negotiated  and those are the contracts you haven't renegotiated in terms of are they awarded in terms of as they are worded  or is it just a question that there were different partners and some partners are easier to deal with in a way than  others? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Tanja B. Markloff
texts.profession: Analyst, Commerzbank AG (Broker)
texts.text: Yeah. Good afternoon. I have a question on the – I would be interested on which gas and oil price you achieved in  2011 and what kind of price level you used for your guidance 2012 and 2014? And the second question would be  on the investments that might become necessary to increase your volumes from 40 million boe to 70 million boe  after 2014?

texts.speaker: Tanja B. Markloff
texts.profession: Analyst, Commerzbank AG (Broker)
texts.text: For Dea in 2014, originally it was €1 billion but oil and gas prices increased. So what would it be excluding the  disposals, excluding the dilution?

texts.speaker: Karin Brinkmann
texts.profession: Analyst, Baader Bank AG
texts.text: Good morning. It's Karin Brinkmann from Baader Bank in Munich. I have two questions. The first one, you are  still a stakeholder in Amprion. So if we have to invest in the grid and Amprion plans to invest more than €3  billion, with your share of these investments, is it already included in your targets or will it be, is equity not visible  to us? What is your stand on the further grid investments in a more overall view? And the next question is a very,  a bigger question on the implementation cost for the efficiency programs, do we see further implementation cost  in 2012 and 2013 or is it more or less all in the provision in 2011? Thanks.  Jürgen Großmann  President & Chief Executive Officer, RWE AG  A Let me start with the latter one, it's the easier one. It's more or less all included, no additional cost.

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: And with respect to Amprion, Amprion is meanwhile financing itself on a standalone basis so the company has its  own credit lines, has its own rating so we do not expect that for the further grid investment, there will be any  financial burden on ourselves.

texts.speaker: Matthias Heck
texts.profession: Analyst, Macquarie Capital (Europe) Ltd. Germany
texts.text: And the second question is again on the gas-to-oil spreads, sorry for that, could you give us at least an indication  whether in the trading and Gas Midstream business in 2011, there was a positive earnings contribution from the  Prop Trading or it was net loss making as well? It's just to understand where we are coming from in 2011?

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: No, sorry. Unfortunately not but if you take the major projects, you see that by the end of 2013, the biggest  projects are already finalized only on the energy side and one bigger power plant is still under construction. So the  bulk of that is already then finalized.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: And Hamm is only decommissioned during the course of the year 2013.

texts.speaker: Vincent P. Gilles
texts.profession: Analyst, Credit Suisse Securities (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: Yes, hi. A very simple question is on the impairment on your Generation assets in The Netherlands, €270 million,  if I read all the documents rightly. Can you help us understand the power price assumption behind this? I guess  it's the power plants at the end of the year, but you can take many power prices. And also, if you could share with  us your assumptions regarding the next few months in line with the guidance that you gave a bit earlier to deal  with The Netherlands? Thank you.  Rolf Pohlig  Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG  A Vincent, with respect to the impairment to this asset and with impairment tests for all subsidiaries or assets, we  usually take for the liquid period, the forward commodity prices and, of course, then the real signs and hard starts  with our longer-term expectations. But we will not share with you what our longer-term expectations because that  is quite obviously a price-sensitive information also to our competitors. So for the liquid period, that is three years  or so. You simply take the market intelligence, i.e., the forward market prices from the market, and thereon then,  we have our fundamental analysis, what should be longer-term equilibrium prices for commodities in the market.

texts.speaker: Deborah B. Wilkens
texts.profession: Analyst, Goldman Sachs International Ltd.
texts.text: Yes, good afternoon. This is a question for Peter Terium, if you need to provide for further financial headroom  beyond what you're looking to achieve through these new targets, what would you look to first, the cost control or  will you go back to a larger disposal program? And the second question is for the 2013 guidance, what does it  reflect in terms of the mix of carbon you have pre-bought, and the market forward?

texts.speaker: Alberto Ponti
texts.profession: Analyst, Société Générale Corporate & Investment Banking (Italy)
texts.text: Yeah. Good afternoon. The first question is on Innogy. You are reiterating the target of €400 million by 2014 and  4.5 gigawatts but you had the same target last year or a year before. So what is causing the delay? We're also  hearing on newspapers of difficulties in connections for offshore wind parks. So if you can update us on that?

texts.speaker: Rolf Pohlig
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Executive Vice President, RWE AG
texts.text: And to you first question. The energy targets, we didn't change anything, it was always 2014 €500 million  operating results and the 4.5 gigawatts in construction or in operation. So there is no change.

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: With respect to the first question, I think we have told the market, what [in the U.S.] assets we have on the  agenda. So for example, we are selling a specific E&P Upstream asset, they are fully consolidated to the extent we  are selling and that is our intention or Net for gas in the Czech Republic that is a fully consolidated asset. I think  on the other side, we have some situations where we are selling down, the companies there, we have a majority  down to a simple majority. One example is what we only achieved the other week or two weeks ago that the  regional distribution company, VSE in the Saar region.

texts.speaker: Tatsiana Harelyshava
texts.profession: Analyst, Commerzbank
texts.text: Yeah, good afternoon. Thank you very much for taking my question. I have two questions, firstly on working  capital. How sustainable the decline is in 2011. And my second question is on compensation payments on gas  contracts in 2011, can you just comment on that, what do you expect for 2012?

texts.speaker: Peter Terium
texts.profession: Deputy Chairman, RWE AG
texts.text: It's difficult to say because if you take for example, how we sort sold our CO2 certificates, either on the OTC  that's a sustainable number. It differentiates between year-on-year on the decision the traders make, where they  sort the CO2 for example. So therefore, we can't be, say, this is the precise number for the next couple of years.

texts.speaker: Stephan Lowis
texts.profession: Vice President-Investor Relations, RWE AG
texts.text: But looking forward, as we already commented in the first call, one of the biggest driver in the future, of course,  will be the sourcing of the CO2 certificates, if they affect variation margins or not which means either you do it by  the OTC market or via the exchange market.  Andrew F. Moulder  Analyst, CreditSights Ltd.  Q Right. Okay, thank you.

texts.speaker: Stephan Lowis
texts.profession: Vice President-Investor Relations, RWE AG
texts.text: The second driver, of course, is the new efficiency program which we released today for 2013 and onwards. And  my final comment, what hasn't really changed is the commodity price environment. If you compare it to last  August, there were bits and pieces going up but also bits and pieces going down, so that's more or less unchanged.  So here are the two major changes, being more concrete in our disposal thinking and having also the cost  efficiency program in place.

texts.speaker: James Sparrow
texts.profession: Analyst, BNP Paribas
texts.text: Okay. Thanks. Yes, that's helpful. And there again, I assume no change in the gas contract position?

texts.profession: Analyst, AGF Investments, Inc.

texts.speaker: Stephan Lowis
texts.profession: Vice President-Investor Relations, RWE AG
texts.text: With respect to the gas contract, I can't be more specific here to be honest because what I'm saying is, as Rolf said  earlier on, this call is public. So whatever we say about the current gas contracts, our counterparts will carefully  listen to that. So I would like to stick to what I've said. We are assuming that the bulk of these contracts will bring  us a significant relief from 2013 onwards.

texts.speaker: Neil J. Beddall
texts.profession: Analyst, FIL Investments International
texts.text: Thanks. Me again, coming up behind Andrew again. I apologize for this, because I'm going to return to gas  contracts. And I know you sort of say you're going to renegotiate the vast majority of these by 2013, but when can  we expect to see positive margin on all the contracts? I mean, I'm assuming you're making a loss of over €800  million per annum or certainly in 2011 based on the previous conference call where you said trading generated a  profit, so presumably the loss is due to the gas contracts. I'm just wondering how long is it going to take to turn  around that €800 million plus? I don't know whether it's €800 million or €1 billion or €1.2 billion or what the  figure is, but can you just give a bit of guidance on that please?
