texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Member-Executive Board, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah, thank you for the questions. CapEx, yeah. 2017 is, in many ways, a transition year. It is true for the CapEx  number as well. We have a lower CapEx number than last year, but still higher than in an average year. We had  some shifts from Legacy due to the incident. It was difficult to precisely predict what can we finish in 2016 and  what is going to – has to be done in 2017. So the CapEx for Legacy will be higher than the €200 million that you  mentioned and this 2017 is a year of high CapEx in our KCF plant and some other environmental investments. So  the number will be higher than the €600 million that you mentioned would be the guidance for the CapEx in 2017.  €40 million is the number for that impact that we had in the first quarter on the Werra situation. We can give you a  rule of thumb. It's a bit more than €1 million impact per production standstill day in Hattorf. Then you surely  wonder why it's €40 million on 25 days because we have additional costs for our measures that we use. So it's  the roughly €1 million per day and we have 55 days in our forecast, and some €20 million, €30 million for  additional measures all over the – for the full year. Then you should have the impact based on normalized  weather situation for the rest of the year.

texts.speaker: Thorsten Boeckers
texts.profession: Head-Investor Relations, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah, hi, Markus. It's Thorsten here. So we have seen 64 million tons in our world, i.e., including the specialties in  2016 and we expect a slight increase on that number. When you deduct the 4 million tons, you see that we are  not far away from what the whole market is expecting there. You asked also about the pricing I think in potash  [indiscernible] (34:34), we – you see price, a positive price effect because of the volume mix. Because when we  expect normal weather conditions for the rest of the year, Burkhard elaborated on our volume expectations  earlier. This means also we can't reduce more specialties and this means our ASP is not as depressed as it was  last year. And this is what we have factored into our guidance.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Member-Executive Board, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah, that's the right base. On that base, we've lost in 2016 roughly 800,000 tons. And if we only lose the 55  days, we would lose 200,000 tons out of this roughly 6.9 million tons.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Member-Executive Board, K+S AG
texts.text: Of course the full 500,000 tons, but that will ramp up to the 500,000 tons that we have agreed with Koch.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Member-Executive Board, K+S AG
texts.text: We are working on more than the six pads. The six pads are now completely available for us for starting the  production, and of course, we have very precise idea of the quality of the product. And we are very happy with the  quality of the product and we are not waiting for the outcome out of the pads. We have a lot of geological  research work to make sure what is the quality of the deposit, and where to position our wells. So we are very –  we shouldn't have a surprise out of that.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Member-Executive Board, K+S AG
texts.text: The Fit project was logistic and administration and these are the same areas we are going to work on for the  additional cost savings.

texts.speaker: Andreas Heine
texts.profession: Analyst, MainFirst Bank AG
texts.text: Yeah, thank you for taking my question. The first quickly a little bit elaborate how you see the potash pricing  environment in spring now in Europe, your most important area? And then I would like to understand where you  would think that your unit cost and good condition in 2018 will be with the cost savings in place and the KCF plant  coming on stream? And then lastly, it was very helpful that you have given us what your best guess is on the  production level with this Hattorf issue. Would you also provide what, let's say, a worst case scenario under very  dry conditions could be? So what is, let's say, the range we have to think of if the weather becomes nice and hot  in the summer which would obviously not be fun for you, potentially for me, that would be helpful.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Member-Executive Board, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah, worst case weather, this is almost impossible to answer. I only said every single day and we're only talking  about Hattorf. Because we believe with our additional measures, we are able to keep all the other two sites  running. That was not the case in 2016. We had closedowns, not only in Hattorf last year, this year we expect it  can only impact Hattorf, so we expect an impact of roughly €1 million and now it's up to you to mention how dry a  year can be. We are safe for the next couple of weeks, but what's going to happen after that, I don't know. I'm  sorry, will not be able to give you a worst case number.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Member-Executive Board, K+S AG
texts.text: Why I shouldn't always see the downside, it could rain more and then we are not – then we have some upside  here.

texts.speaker: Andreas Heine
texts.profession: Analyst, MainFirst Bank AG
texts.text: Well, the completely is just I would like to have a flavor what your unit cost will be if everything is solved in 2018.  So with the KCF plant in operation and no issue anymore with this water flow level of the Werra. Will that still be  on this level of €216 per ton mentioned for 2015 and normalized 2016 or would it be different?

texts.speaker: Oliver Schwarz
texts.profession: Analyst, Warburg Research GmbH
texts.text: Yeah, thank you. I'll cope with your demand and go one-by-one. In regards to the measures, wastewater removal  from the mines, are there additional measures to come or are you satisfied with the measures in place?

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Member-Executive Board, K+S AG
texts.text: No, we are working on additional measures. For example currently, we are only allowed to bring our waters from  the stockpiles into Bergmannssegen-Hugo. We hope that we will be able pretty soon to bring our production  waters into that old mine as well. That would have a meaningful impact because there's a big volume available  there and the next big one is [ph] beautiful water (51:05), another old mine with a meaningful available volume.  We hope to get a permit to dispose waters there in the second half of this year. These are the most important  further steps in addition to what we have in hand already.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Member-Executive Board, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah. Thank you very much for joining us today with many interesting and important questions. I think it was clear  that 2016 was difficult. We believe 2017 will be better, but could still be bumpy. Of course, we still are dependent  on the weather situation, but we are very optimistic for the future, Legacy will kick in, we will finish our KCF plant,  Salt 2020 is on track. So good reasons to be positive. And if you have further questions, please contact our  Investor Relations department and have a great day and we are looking forward to see you soon again. Bye-bye.

file: SDF - Q4 2017 Earnings Call 15March2018 400 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 15-Mar-18.pdf

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Our dividend proposal of €0.35 per share is in line with our policy to cash out 40% to 50% of the adjusted net  income. The proposed increase of €0.05 also reflects our optimism for 2018. Now, let's have a closer look at the  most important topics on slide 4. Let's start with Potash. Due to our improved wastewater management in the  Werra region, we reported only 25 outage days. This was not only a huge improvement on 2016 but also better  than previously guided. The product mix in Potash nicely improved. However, we are still facing some challenges  at our Werra plant after the turbulent times and the trouble we had with our wastewater back in 2016.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: As a result, the motivation of our workforce was low and illness is still high. In addition, it hasn't been easy to fill  vacancies. This has left a mark, and we've lost some production in addition to the outage days. It is our focus to  fix our environmental challenges and improve the motivation of our people. On top of this, we have implemented a  new management team at the Werra, and we are once again hiring people to strengthen our workforce. At the  same time, the decision to close down Sigmundshall by the end of 2018 was not easy for us, but diminishing  volumes and vanishing profitability triggered this step. Last but not least, we have taken the first important ramp- up step at Bethune.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Let's move to the Salt division. Volumes were up by 1 million tons. However, overall prices came down as  expected on the back of the inventory situation at the end of last year's winter season. Nevertheless, we remain  on a very good track to deliver on our Salt 2020 target of a normalized EBITDA of at least €400 million.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Let's move to slide 5 to talk about the environmental and regulatory topics. As you already know, our  environmental challenges and easing environmental tensions are quite close to my heart, and I'm personally  deeply involved in these matters. What have we achieved so far, and what is yet to come? We have improved our  wastewater management and reduced the outage days in 2017 to a level below even our previous guidance. With  the KCF commissioning, which reduces our wastewater by another 20%, we are pretty optimistic that there's only  a very limited risk of further outage days in the Werra region.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: We are currently working on the tailings pile extension, and I'm happy to again confirm that this project remains on  time. We have now received the permission to prepare the ground. Of equal importance, of the settlements we  have reached with Gerstungen and the BUND long lasting disputes have finally come to an end.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: So, what happened in Salt, please turn to slide 7. Let's start with an update on our non-de-icing activities.  Volumes in the final quarter were up on last year's achievements, driven by good demand from chemical  customers in Europe as well as higher industrial salt volumes in Latin America. However, the average selling price  of €110 per ton in Q4 was below last year's level due to adverse currency effects but also on the back of further  improved copper-leaching activities. The profit contribution of copper leaching is remarkable, but low pricing has a  softening impact on our average portfolio price. Our de-icing business reported a tangible volume increase in Q4.  Overall, the mild weather in North America was more than compensated by Europe, again, a nice proof of our  regional hedge. Prices in de-icing were down as expected. This was mainly due to the inventory situation in North  America at the end of last year's winter season.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah. It's always difficult to predict something which we have seen in one quarter for the future because our Salt  business is so volatile. I would rather like to elaborate a little bit on how we started into the New Year. And we had  seen several nice events that started very early this year with a nice snowstorm at the East Coast.

texts.speaker: Thorsten Boeckers
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Director, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah, Christian, there is, from an underlying market trends point of view, nothing to worry about, but you  remember that we had this disastrous Hurricane Irma last year, and this affected especially also these segments  we have, in this area, which was widely affected. People do not longer buy food salt or water softening products.  And on the other hand – so, this was a volume effect and on the other hand because of the emergency – agency  [indiscernible] (00:19:35) taking away most of the trucks we need for logistics in order to deal with the disaster, we  had also a shortage in logistics and also rising costs, what we call nonstandard sourcing costs.

texts.speaker: Neil Christopher Tyler
texts.profession: Analyst, Redburn (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: Okay. And the third question, you talked about the tailings pile management in Germany. Should we anticipate  anything meaningful in terms of either CapEx or OpEx in 2018, 2019 versus the 2017 baseline?

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah. Good question. Exactly this we are working on. We wanted to convince as many people as possible to  move from Sigmundshall to the Werra. And I'm quite hopeful that we will be able to do so. Of course, in parallel,  we have already started hiring people from the market. I think the most important is you need to understand that  we had 220 outage days in 2016. We didn't know how it would – how the near future would look like. We had  some outage days in 2017. Now, we have solved all environmental topics and we can offer them a long-lasting  future. And I'm convinced that in the course of this year, we will settle all problems at Werra.

texts.speaker: Thomas Swoboda
texts.profession: Analyst, Société Générale SA (Germany)
texts.text: Right. My second question is on Salt. We haven't seen normalized de-icing salt levels for quite some time. So,  could you remind us what do you think did the current normalize Q1 level should be? I'm not asking of what you're  seeing in Q1. I'm just asking about normalized level.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: So, as you know, we have storage facilities in Bethune and in Vancouver. And the current inventory is pretty  much what a normal fill of these storage facilities will be in the future. Yeah, so, there's no further increase and no  significant decrease of that volume to be expected.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah, of course, inventory levels came down a bit. And that is always a good implication for the bidding season of  the following or the next bidding season. But it's by far too early to be more precise on that, and the winter is not  over yet. There's more snow to come at the East Coast and we are expecting at least a couple of more wintry  days here in Europe. So let's wait what the final outcome of this season will be.

texts.speaker: Thorsten Boeckers
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer & Director, K+S AG
texts.text: Hinkel, we see basically they're in part a relation to the MOP prices. So, if we have a positive movement in the  MOP price, we also see industrial prices going up. When you're referring to specialties – this is why I'm currently a  bit confused, when you refer to specialties, you mean probably SOP, right?

texts.speaker: Chetan Udeshi
texts.profession: Analyst, JPMorgan Securities Plc
texts.text: Understood. And do you have any view on, of course, there have been some plan new capacity additions out of  Russia. Have you seen them on the market yet, at least in terms of offers, or being talked about in the market in  terms of availability at all? Thank you.  Burkhard Lohr  Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG  A  The only new capacity is – which entered the market is Bethune, and we have seen in the period where we have  delivered into the market with our new volumes that prices went up. So, obviously, the environment is very  healthy currently.

texts.speaker: Joel Jackson
texts.profession: Analyst, BMO Capital Markets (Canada)
texts.text: Okay. And is it reasonable for 2018 that you would sell more than 8 million tons in the Potash and Magnesium  segment this year?

texts.speaker: Marc Gabriel
texts.profession: Analyst, Bankhaus Lampe KG
texts.text: And once again, on Salt, if I quite remember, that was in 2013, 2014, the winter was a normal winter, what you  would call a normal winter for the de-icing salt. Then you had some volumes of 13.1 million tons over the two  winter quarters. And afterwards, prices rose by 20%. Now, we haven't seen that strong volume compared to the  Q4 2013, but is that something which you would expect as a normal winter, this 13 million tons?

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: I would expect the 13 million tons as a normal winter, and the most important quarter is the first quarter. And this  first quarter was very close to a normal winter. So, we're optimistic.

file: SDF - Q4 2018 Earnings Call 14March2019 400 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 14-Mar-19.pdf

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Thank you, operator. Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to our full-year 2018 conference call. Let me start with  some general thoughts on last year's performance. 2018 was a demanding year for us. We had to face  extraordinary factors like the extreme drought in Germany. As a result, we were forced to temporarily stop  production at our Werra potash plant in September and again at the end of the year.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Just a few years ago, these interruptions would have caused earnings to slump dramatically. Today, however,  K+S is stable enough that despite all headwinds, the slightly improved EBITDA can be reported. We made  progress with our German production and met our Bethune-related profitability targets. We added additional  buffer capacities at our Werra sites. And without our improved water management, we would have had to report  shutdowns in June already instead of September.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: However, we are working hard in becoming even more robust against weather-related disruptions and to deliver  on our Shaping 2030 related promises. We are making progress and are on a very good track to achieving our  targets.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: And now please open slide number 1 (sic) [3] (00:02:08). We have increased our group revenues by 11% and our  EBITDA by 5%. A positive pricing environment mainly in potash, but also increased volumes across all segments  were quite supportive. In Salt, we shipped more than 3 million additional tonnes as a result of the harsh winter at  the start of 2018. Furthermore, we increased our Canadian potash production and achieved 1.4 million tonnes,  which is almost half of the total capacity.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Due to the drought, we had to stop production at our three Werra sites, which resulted in 64 outage days.  Moreover, we were focused and forced to use additional shipments of saline wastewater for off-site disposal. On  top of this, the unusual low water levels had a negative impact on freight rates, which increase substantially.  Keeping in mind, that already back in 2017, the Potash division has to carry a weather related EBITDA impact of  about €40 million. The burden year-on-year was therefore additional €70 million.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Let us have a closer look at the market conditions in our Potash businesses on slide 4. Overall, last year Potash  market was quite supportive. Global demand increased to a good 71 million tonnes from our under 70 million  tonnes in 2017. At [ph] year-end (00:04:30) most producers were sold out into Q1 2019, which also let to robust  MOP pricing, especially, in our overseas business. Please keep in mind that more than half of our revenues were  generated in Europe and with Specialty products having a more resilient price development and have recently  also started to pick up. Our average selling price for our Potash and Magnesium Product portfolio of €264 per  tonne is therefore still lagging behind to describe market environment.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: So let's move to slide 5 to give you an update on our potash production. In 2018 we work very hard to tackle our  production challenges. However, adjusted for outage days in December, we missed our target by almost 100,000  tonnes in Q4. In total, we achieved an annual production of 7.5 million tonnes. And bear in minds, we had  addressed all issues which crossed last year's headwinds and overall product availability has already improved.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Unfortunately at our Neuhof plant, the low roof stability reoccurred despite counter measures installed in Q3. For  safety reasons we stopped mining in that sector, which is one of the three fields we are active. We are working on  solutions to continue in that area. In the meantime, our production is moved to the other mining sectors, which  takes time and effort. As a result, last year's production fell short of our initial planning by the abovementioned  100,000 tonnes and will also be burdened by additional 100,000 tonnes in 2019 year-on-year.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Looking at Bethune, production is continuously increasing. To further increase product quality, we are going to  install a grinder pump in the first half of 2019 and some cooling equipment in the second half of the year as  discussed.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: On slide 6, we would like to talk about the weather impact. As already mentioned, our outage days with a negative  EBITDA effect of €110 million. To improve the situation, we expanded our basin capacities by more than 10% to  about 600,000 cubic meters last year already and also expanded our logistics for off-sites disposal. In early  summer 2019, we intend to further expand our capacities to store saline wastewater underground on-site by up to  400,000 cubic meters. This will make us even more robust this year. The good message is there is a high  probability to have no weather-related standstills in 2019.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Let me give you an update on our potash production target for 2019 on slide 7. This slide is already quite familiar  to you. You can see we will get back the volume's lost by the weather related outage days and from our  production issues at the Werra site which are now resolved. However, the performance of our Neuhof site also  has an impact on this year's production. Nevertheless, we will regain about 500,000 tonnes of production in total.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: While in Europe, the wintry weather conditions at the beginning of 2019 caused a slightly above average demand  for de-icing salt, the business in North America was still a bit below our expectations, but catched up in the last  weeks. However, in total, we are on schedule so far this year. Demand for our non-de-icing product is solid with  increasing sales volumes.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Now, let's come to our outlook for 2019 based on our new external reporting structure on slide 9. Based on what  we have discussed when introducing our group, Shaping 2030 strategy, we are working hard to breakdown silos  and build one company. The implementation of our Shaping 2030 strategy is advancing with visible results. In  2018, we started to make our administrative functions more efficient and focused on delivering customer value.  Initial synergy effects have already been achieved in procurement, production, as well as sales and marketing.  The reorganization is progressing well.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: We see a good market environment for fertilizers. After the robust demand we experienced in 2018, we expect  global potash demand to remain at least stable. The positive environment of 2018 should therefore also favorably  reach into 2019. We see a further increase of our Canadian production and there is a high probability to have no  weather related standstills in 2019. Rising cost inflation is likely to soften some positive effects from potash  pricing. The adjusted free cash flow will improve significantly and turn positive in this year. This is the most  important target for all of us in the quarters to come.

texts.speaker: Christian Faitz
texts.profession: Analyst, Kepler Cheuvreux SA (Germany)
texts.text: Yes. Good morning, gentlemen. Couple of questions. So, first question surrounding your ongoing production  issues. Can you put a bit meat to the bone on what's going on in Neuhof and also the lower K2O content in  Unterbreizbach? And related to that, potash-wise, why do you still have caking issues in Bethune?

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Okay. Let's start with the German sites that we are running through an area with lower K2O content as previously  expected that we have reported in Unterbreizbach. We have reported last year and we have already indicated  that we will see effect of that in 2019 as well. We should be through that area and we know that we get a higher  content in – K2O content after we are done. So, in 2020, we are hopeful to see a positive turnaround of the  situation.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: And the last remaining bigger issue is at Neuhof plant, where we have still not fixed the situation with our roof  stability. We thought we could fix it with another anchor situation, stronger, longer, but that didn't work. We have  really an extraordinary geologic here in this area. And now we believe the solution will be to narrow the space  between the piles – the pillars, and that requires a lot of pre-work and adjustments. And that's why we believe we  will be able to do so and go back into that area, which by the way has the highest [ph] K2O (00:19:51) content.  That's why we want to desperately find a solution for it. But that will be most probably not done before the end of  this year. That's why we have decided to take out the additional 200,000 tonnes. So, if you take 2018 and 2019,  we'll lose 200,000 tonnes compared to our original plans for Neuhof. But it is all baked into our guidance.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Once we have prepared that, the cost is not significantly higher. But we will take out less out of this area. That is  the most [ph] – that's the higher (00:20:45) consequence. That means we cannot mine all the volumes that we  would have liked to mine in this area. But that has no effect – immediate effect and the higher cost is not  meaningful. Coming back to Bethune, that was your last part of the first question. There's no surprise. We  indicated to have the perfect quality we need to install this grinder pump that will happen pretty soon. And at the  end of the day, we need to have this cooling facilities, and that will be installed by the end of the year. And we see  now in the cold period, it works better. But there will be a summer of course to come without this cooling facility,  and that's why we have modeled this effect that we most probably will see into the volume expectation for 2019.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Yeah. Thanks for that question. We have started last year already. No big volumes, but we have started the  process and we have seen it works. And that's why we are very sure to be able to deliver the 100,000 to 200,000  tonnes secondary mining. And as you know, that is very low-cost production, and we are very happy to see that  ramping up now.

texts.speaker: Patrick Rafaisz
texts.profession: Analyst, UBS AG
texts.text: And following up on this, your cash unit costs guidance for over €200 due to cost inflation, could that change if the  secondary mining comes in at the upper end, so at 200,000 tonnes, or is that independent of this?

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Now, first of all, I would like to use the opportunity to indicate that Bethune with only 50% of the capacity has a  cost per tonne number which is below our German number. So, it has already a positive impact. So, it indicates  what is ahead of us in the future. But the 100,000 – if we talk about the upper [ph] end of 100,000 tonne  (00:29:13) secondary mining at the upper end is not big enough to really turn the needle.

texts.speaker: Patrick Rafaisz
texts.profession: Analyst, UBS AG
texts.text: Will you still be showing potash numbers separately within that segment or will it all be mixed up with the Europe  Salt business?

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: We will show potash – agricultural potash numbers. So, it is even more transparent for you, because we show  which is the – what is the development of potash which goes into our customer segment – or is sold in our  customer segment, agriculture, and the rest is industries. So, in the past, we have always blended these  numbers, although we have completely different customers and partially the dynamics are different. That is the  good news for you.

texts.speaker: Thomas P. Wrigglesworth
texts.profession: Analyst, Citigroup Global Markets Ltd.
texts.text: No, no, just exceptional kind of in terms of the – obviously, you've got the cost saving, the 2030 plan cost savings.  You've got maybe other costs that might become exceptional through the course of the year. Outside – I'm not  looking at obviously the weather-related.

texts.speaker: Burkhard Lohr
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman, K+S AG
texts.text: Okay. Yeah, of course, together with our Shaping 2030 initiative, I mentioned one positive effect, but there are of  course extraordinary effects. texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Good afternoon and welcome to this Investor Day. I hope those who have been able to join us this morning in La  DuPont have enjoyed their visit. First of all, I'd like to say that we have not chosen the date of this meeting  according to the French Presidential Elections, but obviously, following the results, I'm more optimistic on France  than I watched some months ago. I expect a recovery of our first market to gather momentum and the program of  our new president on energy renovation is promising. Although, as always, we will need to know more about the  details of its implementation.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Concerning the third axis, management priorities, we have pushed further our cost saving programs. I think we  can say we have become a CSR reference. We have delivered attractive returns for shareholders, and we have  maintained a solid financial structure. But more globally than just the targets of 2013, when I look backward at the  last few years, I think we have achieved a lot on a number of fronts. I will select six topics.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Tom Kinisky has replaced John Crowe as Head of our U.S. Operation at the beginning of this year. Before that,  he was in-charge of our very successful plastic business and I will say over the years, he has worked in most of  our HPM activities.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: At the other extreme, on the left of the slide, we can talk about the evolution of the automotive industry. Comfort  requirements become more and more important for end users; vibration control, noise reduction. Durability are  becoming critical to the OEMs even for the very small parts. This is where we can add value, for example, to our  performance plastic bearings, parts in door assembly or seats, and there are many of them in each car.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: If I take acoustical solution, the example in the middle, the products will be sold more and more with a specific  service to help, to design the best combination to reduce noise in a given environment. Those trend we see them  everywhere at work. And it makes us very confident that our uniqueness will be a true positive differentiation  factor in the future.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: To take a few more specific examples, in the marine industry, we sell many products, insulation, glass, or even a  lot of plumbing and heating through our distribution network. We have decided several years ago to coordinate  our efforts toward this market, and to put in common the strengths and knowledge of all our businesses, on the  innovative material side, on the construction product side, and on the distribution side.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, last but not the least of the topics where we have transformed the group over the last three years is our  corporate social responsibility activities in all their dimensions. These achievements have been recently  recognized through our inclusion for the first time into the Dow Jones Sustainability Index in 2016. And at the  same time, we enter immediately at the first track in Europe, and the second one in the world in our sector.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In the field of governance, we strive to achieve the highest standards. Our board has reviewed and improved  practices consistently in line with best practices. We have now a board committee reviewing our CSR policies.  This year, the board has appointed a lead independent director, Jean-Dominique Senard, the CEO of Michelin,  who will start his office from this general shareholders' meeting next month.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: From an environmental standpoint, Saint-Gobain is committed to reduce the impact and we have taken strong  commitments to that effect whether it concerns CO2 emissions, water consumption or waste, as you see in this  chart. We are following methodically our action plans with strict measurements in all our facilities. These actions  are all the more important as Saint-Gobain is an important actor in the fight against climate change.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Our products and solutions are key to the reduction of the emissions of CO2 in buildings, which is the biggest  sector in terms of global emissions. We have calculated with independent international consultants that although  we are a significant emitter, our solutions, when installed, have a very positive effect. In fact, during their lifetime,  they allowed to avoid 90 times the emissions that have been necessary for their production.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Many of you know my personal commitment in that field because of personal convictions, but also because it is a  big opportunity for Saint-Gobain. In terms, the group should be leading the way towards a de-carbonized world.  The only tool going forward will be, in my view, a price of carbon. And in weighting political decisions, we have  decided to setup an internal price of carbon within the group to step up the mobilization of our businesses and to  encourage disruptive innovation.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In a nutshell in Saint-Gobain, CSR is not just a set of practices to comply with international standard, it is an  integral part of our strategy. So, this is, with all the aspect, where I think that we can see that Saint-Gobain has  been transformed over the last three years. And now, I will let Guillaume answer the question about the  macroeconomic environment.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In automotive, for example, the need for more comfort is creating opportunities for, for example, our coated  glasses or for our performance plastic parts, Pierre-André was talking about that. The progression of electric  vehicles is creating in general more constraints, for example, weight constraints and therefore more opportunities  for all of our businesses. In the aeronautic sector, same holds true, for example the CO2 constraints on a smaller,  but still quite important scale, in-flight Wi-Fi development, for example, is generating additional business in our  high-performance materials sector. And finally, in the healthcare industry, the move towards disposable tailor- made, high-tech systems is clear good news both for the patients first of all, but also for our high-performance  plastics business. But Tom will elaborate a little bit more about that right after my presentation.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, benefiting from markets tailwind is clearly a positive for the company but long term what you are probably also  interested in as investors is whether we can go faster than the wind. And this is going to be the topic of the next  few presentations and I will now hand over to Tom Kinisky who will start to address this important question. Thank  you.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Whether you're talking about autonomous cars, aging population, the need for healthcare, air transport growth, all  of these are having an impact across all of our businesses and sectors, but the real question isn't the underlying  market trends. It's actually how can we find and identify those trends that are – those markets or submarkets  inside of these trends that are growing faster.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: On a personal level, I think we all want in our homes a positive outcome for our families, whether that's to reduce  the noise of the neighbors next door, whether that's to improve the air quality inside of our home, maybe by  lowering the VOCs, and we actually have products that can do that today. We have noise blocking gypsum board  for example to keep the noise out from the neighbors. We have gypsum board that absorbs VOCs to make a  better air and quality environment for our family. So those are our offerings today.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And I have another direct example, 18 months ago we moved the North American headquarters into a new – well  it's not a new facility, it was a 20-year-old building, but newly renovated. And what we did as we did that was we  put the building science behind the building. So it's got our materials in it, but it also has dynamic – it has sensors  and dynamic controls in which we are controlling the acoustics, the light, the ventilation system, the temperature,  we have electrochromic SageGlass for example in the building and it's all controlled sensor – where we are  actually now measuring the outcomes of the people inside of our building as well as their well being.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: To give you one specific, we have a customer service center in the building. So 18 months ago, we moved in, and  of course we are controlling through sensors all of their environment and what we discovered after 18 months is  that the productive in that call center has gone up 180% and it stayed there now over six months to sustainable.  And it's all because we're impacting the well-being of the employees' environment. As a result of that, it's having a  positive outcome. That same group of building, scientists we're using them to design the next generation building  of the future and we have building scientists not just in North America, but across the entire world working on this  question of correlating comfort well-being with building science.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: We want to have an impact on this. Guillaume mentioned, for example of that there is a potential labor shortage in  the U.S. and many of the mature countries. If we can impact productivity, we can also help to relieve that issue.  Here are three examples of how we're doing that. Pierre-André touched on this already with prefab. But if you look  at just bathrooms. If you take the bathroom module and make it an industrial environment, we've reduced the cost  by 50% and changed completely the amount of onsite work labor required, reducing it by 99%.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The same thing is true with lightweight materials. If they're easier to handle on the job site, we can make people  more productive. If we can change the curing time and the drying time significantly and these are examples with  our mortar products, we can dramatically change again the amount of labor time on the site.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And the last one, and this is a kind of interface between new technology that's happening in building, modeling,  information systems as well as what we can do in advance, because we're getting sp precise, we can bring precut  materials on to a job site. They fit immediately, you're not cutting on the job site, and you're not generating waste  on the job site. And these are just three examples of many of other solutions that we're offering today.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: On the far right, and this was already mentioned by Guillaume, but I'll elaborate on it. In the case of  biopharmaceutical manufacturing, the advent of personalized medicine, what's happening now is the  pharmaceutical companies which used to manufacture in large stainless steel reactors are now doing things in  small scale for personalized [ph] and (46:33) disposable plastics, which are impacting our plastics business. And  these are just a couple of examples that we have across our business.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So I want to conclude by saying that this combination of what we're trying to do in terms of science, high efficiency  manufacturing and service is all supported by what we're doing with open innovation inside of these industrial as  well as construction markets.

texts.speaker: Thomas G. Kinisky
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, General Delegate for North America, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In the case of high performance materials, two thirds of what we manufacture there either customized products or  co-developed products and we're inviting our customers, we're inviting our suppliers, we're inviting other partners,  universities into our innovation across the entire group around the world. One example of that is fablabs. These  are small labs that have been set up in a variety of our plants across the plastics business in which we have our  employees collaborating with outsiders to create innovation.

texts.speaker: Benoît Bazin
texts.profession: Senior Vice President & President-Construction Products Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Second priority for growth, innovation. Our product innovation is closely connected to the markets. If I take the  example of insulation, we start from the customer needs, the market needs and we have developed over the  years, the multi material offer, fire resistance with stone wool, thermal and acoustic performance with glass wool,  wood fibers, for the ecological customers who prefer wood, PIR with the Celotex acquisition from a few years ago  for thin and high thermal performance and also traded goods and accessories again to make the products easier  and faster to install.

texts.speaker: Benoît Bazin
texts.profession: Senior Vice President & President-Construction Products Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: But innovation is also in services, like in the pipe business, where we have developed sensors for either leakage  or corrosion detection or in mortars where we have trucks to deliver on multi-storied job sites.

texts.speaker: Benoît Bazin
texts.profession: Senior Vice President & President-Construction Products Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Some of you have seen [indiscernible] (53:06) this morning our new friendly glass wool. I hope you had the  opportunity to touch it which triggered a very positive customer reaction. We have seen also Habito. Habito is a  revolutionary plasterboard with high fixing capability, high durability and also high acoustic performance. A very  great solution for better and stronger wool for both the residential and the commercial markets.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Let me give you a few examples. The surface treatment of my cell phone has been made with zirconia beads and  probably your cell phone has been made with zirconia beads of Saint-Gobain. If you have an accident tomorrow,  probably we will be able to give you and to provide you all the needed product for the repair of your car body,  refinishing and after that for protection of your car. Last time you took a taxi or you took your car, it's highly likely  that it was equipped with our bearings providing noise reduction and friction reduction and giving you intimately a  better comfort.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Let me give you few promising examples. So first example, coated veil is a product that we developed in co- development with Gypsum Activity. This is coated veil that is protecting the plasterboard from humidity and from  UV during the construction. Second example, an example more between new products and new market, we  developed a refractory product lines which is called wool for installation furnaces with recycled material, not only  we manage to find a solution with recycling of waste of our customers, which is a problem for our customers, but  we also got a cheap source of raw material to enter with a competitive product on this market.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Third example, more new markets entering in the new market segment, sandwich radomes. A radome is a  weatherproof dome that is protecting the weather antenna. It's a growing market. We developed an innovative  technology panels incorporating 3G fibers between the two, in and outer, surfaces avoiding the delimination  issues that is encountered by our competitor's position. On top of that, it facilitates the assembly and the  maintenance of the system.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And fourth, application an example, ceramic filters. We developed a ceramic filter in co-development with our  customers to address the growing market of the water and beverage filtration, but also water treatment and the  pollution. So the second lever is to focus on development of new application end markets.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: I would like to focus on five axes to show you how we can outperform our markets. First is innovation in the  material, the glass material itself. The second is to focus of offer onto high-performance glazing for building in  which we can combine the different capabilities that we have. I could mention, for instance, the combination  between comfort and thermal efficiency or the integrations of blinds into IGU for hospital for cleanliness services.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The third element is the excellence in developing system for the automotive segments. Integrating high-level  technical customer requests. I can use the example of the heated windshield for commercial aircraft cockpits or  the lamination of sensor or the integrations of antenna of invisible camera on the sidelights or backlights. The  fourth axis is the execution in emerging countries, where in most of the case, we have leadership position. Finally,  the integration of the sustainability problematic from the conceptions of the lifecycle management to the process  or efficiency – energetic and efficiency. So let's elaborate on these five levers for growth.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: We do not only develop product. We also spend one-third of our R&D efforts to process improvements like, for  instance, cost management or focus on energy, reduction on energy or CO2 or improvement of the capability or  tolerances of our products. And finally, in terms of excellence of operational excellence, the float business and the  Sekurit business are really [indiscernible] (01:18:30) our industry in the rollout of Industry 4.0 digital processes.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, I'd like to give you two example, one is the SageGlass product, which is the activation of electrochromic  technology for glass that can tint on demand. The second recent innovations that is under way is the joint  ventures that we have set up with the American glass manufacturer Corning in order to be able to produce extra  glazing windshield for electrical vehicles.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The second example is something quite new. We have developed very high-sized coated glass panels. Those are  18-meter glass panel with extreme glass neutrality, very, very clear, for very iconic projects that you can  sometimes recognize. This is a new facility that we have set up in Germany and we are just starting in [ph] here  (01:20:23) as well. We will export all over the world this kind of a very specific, specific product.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The second example is the smart windshield. This is a [ph] visionary (01:21:35) front glass that integrates on  enabled new features for the new generation of cars like electrical vehicles, like for autonomous driving or  infotainment. Here, we are in discussion with several players of the market in order to bring those techno  solutions like OLEDs, or LED, or sensors, or HUD-compatible windshields that we really integrate in the  windshields. So, as we can see here, it really goes beyond the pure material. Let's have an illustration with the  following video.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: What do we offer here? Here we offer reflective glass, which is [ph] Lorenzo of (01:26:07) coated glass for  residential. We processed facades and now we do it out of India, very complex facades. We offer advanced  coatings for the different solar control applications from India, from Korea, from Mexico. We provide as well  through digital channels a series of service and adjacent product like foams, sealant, spacers and different  accessories. So most of those markets are fast growing and in most of them, we are as a number one or number  two position. Our next target is now to go to Africa after what we have done recently in the Middle East.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Finally, I would like to elaborate a little bit on the fifth lever, which is the sustainability. I have a strong belief that  sustainability is not only an economical calculation for the customer but this is more and more a customer request  and experience where environment and well-being are really the two key motivations for them. And at Saint- Gobain, we want to have our technology and our product range saving the planet. So as we mention often, as an  example, double glazing units that we produce and that emit CO2, this CO2 is offset within three months after the  installation of this double glazing.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: But still, we continue permanently to reduce our footprint with very clear plans, with very clear technological and  operational roadmaps and we really – you can believe me that this objective of CO2 emissions, our reduction of  emission in our plant really matters for our customers. So as you can see here on the example, our very thin glass  like you can see here is saving, is providing for electrical vehicles, savings of rate of 30%, which as well saved  energy. And this segment of the electrical cars is going to grow, is predicted to grow 40% in average in the future  for the next decade, so it's really material [indiscernible] (01:28:20) right segment.

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The other example is the electrochromic glass, we spoke about, SageGlass systems. Here as well we can reduce  emission and energy by 20%, but also it brings a tremendous feelings of comfort of well-being, so we really  combine the quantity and the quality and the comfort. Here as well, let's have a look of what SageGlass is made  of...

texts.speaker: Patrick Dupin
texts.profession: Senior Vice-President in charge of the Flat Glass Activity, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: As a conclusion, I'm really convinced that we have the right approach, the right organization, but also the right  team to amplify the market growth through focus on innovation, through business approach in building and in the  mobility segment, increasing our position in emerging country, where we have really a very robust position and  sustainability-enhancing solutions.

texts.speaker: Fabrice Didier
texts.profession: Vice President-Marketing, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: KANDU, for example, proposes noise reduction solution to restaurant owners based on data analysis and  measured by a simple smartphone. PAM with a start-up Echologics offers and sells leak detection and  maintenance services for the drinking water network to municipalities or to the contractors. And Kåre will develop  Homly You, maybe our most emblematic project.

texts.speaker: Fabrice Didier
texts.profession: Vice President-Marketing, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: You may have seen in the press our future headquarters that will be built only in 2019. It's a virtual picture you  have seen. The tool that has been used by Valode et Pistre, the architect, to choose type of glass they wanted.  And it is all over the world used by our sales team in glass to suggest to our partners how their future buildings  will look like.

texts.speaker: Kåre Ivar Olsen Malo
texts.profession: Senior Vice President-Building Distribution Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Prefab solution, which was rightly mentioned early today, will be a part of our buildings for the future. It's also  increasing significantly and both from the industry side, but also we, in distribution, we'll play a significant role  within this area.

texts.speaker: Kåre Ivar Olsen Malo
texts.profession: Senior Vice President-Building Distribution Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Communication costs have also dropped dramatically and a good quality Wi-Fi today on the plant has the power  of close to 1 giga per second.

texts.speaker: Kåre Ivar Olsen Malo
texts.profession: Senior Vice President-Building Distribution Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So I will now show you a few examples of how these technologies work in Saint-Gobain. We here see on an  automotive glass production line that the extension of the number of sensors and the integration of the machines  can better control the process, reduce [indiscernible] (02:00:58) and decrease reject and material cost. The  overall equipment efficiency of the line can improve 2% to 5%.

texts.speaker: Kåre Ivar Olsen Malo
texts.profession: Senior Vice President-Building Distribution Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The automated guided vehicles, also called AGV, are getting a new life. They do not depend on fixed pass on the  floor like tramways in the old days. They are now more like autonomous cars with beacon radar vision system,  which allow very good self positioning. These vehicles adopt to changing environment in order to take over the  bulk of transport in some of the warehouse. So productivity jump associated is over 50%. The cobots that we  have described earlier can handle complex tasks, relieves the operator from physical load and have very friendly  interface, easy to program.

texts.speaker: Kåre Ivar Olsen Malo
texts.profession: Senior Vice President-Building Distribution Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Without even waiting for the end of the current saving plan, we have decided to launch a new one which would be  longer by one year and where the saving target is increased from €267 million per year to €300 million per year.  This is an important change compared to the recent evolution in which the yearly saving figure was decreasing  with time. But this is a commitment and we are comfortable given the number of opportunities that we see  opening, thanks to new manufacturing technologies. Thank you very much.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: [ph] Secondly, part (02:07:42) of this is that we are able to pass through raw materials and energy cost in our  prices. We have a good track records of doing this, but it is every year a renewed challenge. And the third  assumption is that the mix of businesses on our products is relatively constant. So, this is only – is it only the  theory or can we hope to turn it into reality.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, usually the next question we get in road shows is about the potential normative margins in our businesses.  On the next three slides, we'll try to answer this question with ranges knowing that we don't give specific time  frames. But this is a good indication of what we think we can achieve in what we should call a normal environment  knowing that we would qualify the last few years as probably unfavorable and 2016 and 2017 as recovery.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Restructuring costs have gone down and, as volumes recover, they should stand the tight control. Asbestos has  been stable in the recent years. Ideally, I would like to be able to tell you today that we are going to trend soon  downwards, but it's still too early to make such a statement.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The tax rate is also in line which is [ph] little (02:13:37) talked about despite its important impact on the cash flow  generation. It has also gone down steadily from 34% to 27% in 2016. This is due to the overall environment  obviously, which is more favorable as well as through our optimization efforts. And if the announcements that we  see in some countries and in particular in the U.S. in terms of political changes are aligned with what has been  announced, it would be good news for our ability to maintain and maybe improve this good track record.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: I would like to illustrate maybe, first, all the engineering work, which is behind this structural reduction of CapEx  needs by taking two examples of things which are totally comparable because we are talking the same object on  the same side each time.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: On the left side, this is an example of what we were able to do on maintenance CapEx, which remains a  significant part of our envelope, with the successful rebuild of the same insulation furnace. And you can see that  we reduced by more than 50% the costs per output.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: To illustrates this strategy, I will use the example of our Performance Plastic business within HPM. Starting with a  very good tubing product in our historical portfolio, which is used in many different industries, requiring high purity  and resistance characteristic, we have found application in the medical sector where there is a growing trend for  single-use disposable systems. You've seen the [ph] video (02:25:17) in the last presentation. Progressively and  through six acquisition until now, we have built a very nice business with very quick value creation.

texts.speaker: Q
texts.profession: Hi, [indiscernible] (02:46:12). Follow-up questions on the Industry 4.0, could you be a bit more specific on the
texts.text: And last question not directly linked to this presentation, but you said that Emmanuel Macron election is positive  for you, could you be a bit more specific? And also maybe a comment on the nomination of Nicolas Hulot as  Minister for Ecology.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Then there is a fact which is also something specific to us. And from that standpoint among the various  candidates, the Macron is the one who [indiscernible] (02:51:33) in terms of energy, renovation and all that, the  most important program. So that's good news for us, whether this is going – this particular point is going to  translate for us soon into additional sales? I don't know. And this may take time. But I think the psychology will be  there very quickly, that's my – I may be wrong, but that's my assessment.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Then concerning the new minister, it's – I learned that 20 minutes ago and it's a bit early, but it can only reinforce  the push towards more efficiency, energy efficiency actions in buildings, because there is a very strong  consensus that if you want to do more in terms of environment, CO2 emissions, the obvious easiest target is  building. So from that standpoint, if the government is more driven in that direction through the new minister of  environment, it will help. I don't know whether this is going to be major, but it's going, all that is pointing into the  right direction.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So I repeat it once again. Amazon, I think that the time where Amazon will ship plasterboard, insulation of cement  has not come in my view and I don't think it will come. There is a specificity that you may have seen this morning  on what we do. Then – and I think, but there is – there maybe – Amazon may come into some tooling or things  like that and we have our answer with, for instance, with [indiscernible] (02:55:32) and all our logistic center would  be [ph] good (02:55:35).

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: On the second point, it's two different topics. On Flat Glass in Europe, what I have said, what I wanted is first to  reduce the capital intensity and to have more downstream than upstream instead of having, in the past, more  upstream than downstream. We are getting there. In fact, at the moment, we are buying glass for our  downstream, more – we are buying glass. And the fact that the glass we buy is more of a commodity side and we  intend to continue to do that. So, I think we have got, from that standpoint, where we wanted to be, largely.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Yeah. I will take the questions. First of all, when I say normative margins, I think I explained in my comments that  it was – those were margins that we expect to be able to deliver in a normal environment, which means not a  peak environment. At peak environment, we will maybe be able to do better. But the correlation and the  multiplicative factor between the peak environment and the normal environment is something that I wouldn't risk  myself in trying to predict.

texts.speaker: Eric A. Lemarié
texts.profession: Analyst, Bryan, Garnier & Co Ltd. (France)
texts.text: And the last question regarding the ecologic service you mentioned in the presentation to assess the pipe quality  system, I don't know if you've got a point of view of the quality system of the pipe in France, the pipe system  especially at local authorities level, do you think pipe network is in a good shape or not. And if it's not in a good  shape, do you see here an opportunity for you? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: I think last one, on pipe I think that [ph] overall, (03:10:49) all over Europe our – the pipe network is quite old and  the leak level is very high. I think the UK is highest, I think it's 30% to 40% leaks. So, as price of water goes up,  the incentive to improve plus the health issues, which can arrive and then we have some places where it starts to  happen, means that the prospects are good. Now, the question is at between the prospects and the realization,  it's clearly an item where, historically, you cannot say that it's going to happen in the next day. So, I think it's going  to take time because of the financial situation of a lot of local authorities, not only in France but everywhere in  Europe. And that has been hurting us in the last two, three years and I see it will take a little bit more time.

texts.speaker: Q
texts.profession: I've got two questions, if I could. First one, I'd like to just push you a little bit more on the main theme seems to be
texts.text: And I guess, what I'm trying to understand is, I can understand it for HPM but I'm struggling a bit more for the  Building Distribution and the Construction Products giving your market shares in some of these markets as to  what the scope is to outperform. And then the second question is on carbon that you mentioned, I think, and  correct me if I'm wrong, you're doing an internal charge for carbon when you look at some of these projects. Two- part question, what you are assuming is the charge for carbon [indiscernible] (03:18:56) or a longer-term charge?  And why are you doing that, is it because you think that the charge is going to go way-up in the future, or is it just  because of the CSR positives?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And on carbon. Yes, on carbon, in fact, we have – I have put in – it's an internal price and in fact we have put two  prices. We have one for our CapEx, so it's up to charging of cost is just doing our calculation on CapEx as if there  was a price of carbon and then we [indiscernible] (03:21:22) but it changes the way we do the CapEx, and we  have [ph] an array (03:21:27) two or three places where we have added – we have changed what we would have  done because of the price of carbon. We have added some expenses, in fact, the CapEx has been a bit higher  because if there was a price of carbon in that country at the level we have internally we would have – it would  have made sense. So, we have two price of carbon.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And the second price of carbon which is much higher, the first one I can say is around €30. The second one  which is closer to €100 is for R&D. And then [indiscernible] (03:22:05) open the box for disruptive ideas  [indiscernible] (03:22:13) if there was a price of carbon a much higher one. So, why I have done that? I've done  that mostly because I believe that it's going to happen. And as we are – I mean, when we do a CapEx, we don't  do it for the next three years. So, I'm trying to anticipate what could happen. The issue is that when I anticipate  the price of carbon for our CapEx in India, maybe what I'm doing is not going to happen, before the CapEx has  been depreciated. But we have decided to have a worldwide approach.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, Lapeyre we've had a lot of reorganization. I think that we are seeing in the last few months some encouraging  trends and Lapeyre is – in the framework of what [indiscernible] (03:26:05) explained and my answer in terms of  these B2C, B2B environment it's – I think that it's potentially adding a lot to our thinking and our portfolio. So, I  don't – but we need to improve the profitability of Lapeyre, which has not been good.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now in this context, the main points that concern Saint-Gobain's results are very good organically, up 6.7% over  the first half after a first quarter which we told you was rather extraordinary because of a very mild weather in  Europe whereas the weather had in 2010 – during the same period in 2010 had been not fair at all.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now for distribution prices that went 2% over the first quarter have gone up to 3% over the second quarter,  because – and this is important, because most of our raw material prices, of course, are in our industrial activity  and so we had to pass across the 3% hike in raw materials to offset the price in raw materials and energy.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: As Pierre-André told you we have started capital expenditure again and as you can see it's up 48% since between  H1 2010 and H1 this year. You remember, of course, that we have a seasonal variation between the first half and  second half of every year, but we haven't had a sharp upturn in our first half of this year, a little over €200 million,  actually €209 million. And the breakdown is about €100 million, which increases our CapEx in Asia and in  emerging countries at about €60 million, that's 30%. That is devoted to energy efficiency and to solar power. If  you add up the two that is about 80% of the increase in our CapEx, which is actually has – actually increased our  production capacity in emerging countries and is based on energy efficiency and solar power, which is what we  had announced last year.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Construction products 4.9%, with 3.7% for – over the second quarter. So, that was good. Building distribution up  by 7.3% throughout the first half of the year, 4.5% over the second quarter, which means it has continued to  improve, because the first quarter was, of course, suffered from the consequences of the weather conditions over  the first quarter. Then Verallia plus 4.2% of growth throughout the half, that was 2.2% over the first – the second  quarter, sorry.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now a little more detail, Flat Glass plus 8.2% of growth and this was also pulled up, continued to be pulled up by  emerging countries, but also by building in Europe. Over the second quarter in Europe, the figure was up 8%,  because of energy efficiency and value-added product, such as triple glazing and the penetration of triple glazing  in Germany, last year the figure was 25% and this year the figure is 33%. So, there has been a significant impact in  the product – in the sales of value-added products here in this particular business sector. And in the second  quarter, we did have a slight shrinkage of this activity.  Now prices continued to improve in Flat Glass, because over the local quarter, we are up by 4% and we will have  another increase in the month of September. High-performance Materials, as you can see, the sales figures would  seem stable compared to last year in absolute terms, you must not forget that we did sell-off Advanced Ceramics at  the end of 2010. So, in terms of organic growth plus 9.3% over the first half of this year. Strong growth also in  plastics which is linked more to industrial consumption.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now, if we look at EBITDA and CapEx, you can see once again it was at €615 million last year, €842 million this  year and investments have more than doubled in this particular business activity, and have gone up to €323  million with a lot of investments that we have made in the Float line in India and in Brazil as well and investments  in high value-added products for example in coating – coated glass in Europe and solar power as well.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now, building – construction products, sorry, you can see that is 4.9% up over the whole half of year. And this has  been pulled up by emerging countries but also through energy efficiency solutions in Europe. And overall we've  had an increase of 6.4% in Western Europe.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The prices in these activities have also increased especially for Interior Solutions plus 3% over the second half –  second quarter sorry. And this was necessary to cover the rise in costs of raw materials and energy and for  insulating materials such as foam and for certain products there.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now plus 4.1% in the – over the half year for exterior solutions with mortar doing well and in activities for exterior  solutions in the United States because of weather that has pushed up our activity. On the other hand, we have had  a negative impact for pipes as I told you earlier especially in Europe but also for exports to the Middle East.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In terms of profitability, you can see compared to last year for Interior Solutions we have once again, increased  our profitability plus 1.1%, it's gone from 6.8% to 7.9%. Thanks to the improvement in our prices, which offsets the  cost of raw materials and energy and here we have the impact of the leverage effect that we can have on our  Exterior Solutions – Interior Solutions, sorry, mostly in Europe.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: As for building distribution, you can see there is a growth of 8% this center in H1. texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: There you've got the performance of innovative materials, industrial materials, which are improving. However the  basis for comparison is becoming more difficult.
