texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And just to finish, EBITDA and CapEx by geographic area. There once again you can see that we've been keeping a  slight lid on CapEx for France. Nevertheless we have invested in Europe. We  have invested quite heavily there with investment in proppants and in emerging countries a major priority of the  Group.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: What does this mean for the Group? For innovative material first of all, we think there will be a robust momentum  across all geographic areas with good levels of margins. In mature countries we will continue to develop slowly. texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: What are our priorities for H2, 2011? Given our investment policy, well we will continue with this but, of course,  being very clear cut on our financials. We want, first of all, to give the priority to the sales price. We've already  been doing this. We have price increases across the board in most of our activities, which are going to be  continuing to be rolling throughout the year. We have to cover the rises in energy cost, of course. I think the  pricing power of Saint-Gobain which has been clearly demonstrated over the past months really gives us reason  for confidence for the rest of the year.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: A second major thrust in terms of growth is energy efficiency and solar power. Here we've started to build a  factory in electrochromic in glazing. And we have also launched the two Avancis plants, one in Germany and another one in South Korea, with high  performance levels, which are still improving in our pilot factory, which gives us a great confidence in our  technology compared with that of our competitors.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: We are taking advantage of our excellent strategic positioning in emerging countries which have strong growth  plus good positioning in the mature countries. I showed you back in February, we took the example of France.  Looking at the new measures on energy savings and these measures have really been positive. We stated back then  that we're going to build a new rock wool factory in France and this is similar to what we are doing in Japan, a  country where energy savings measures are going to be very strong, very robust in the next years for obvious  reasons. So, we have, as I said, good positioning on developed and developing countries.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: We're doing very well in terms of keeping a cap on our costs. Our road map is designed to keep our savings at  50%. 50% savings were in line for that Saint-Gobain has demonstrated that it is fully able to increase its sales  price in an inflationary context. This has to do with the cost of raw materials, energy cost, of course and we are  now in a very strong financial position, which means that we continue to expand and we can seize opportunities as  they arise in different fields across the board.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Over and above the H2 of this year our growth priorities are in the emerging countries on energy savings  measures. These focuses really put us on the right path I believe for growth in the future. And I think you can see  that from the figures our performance is validating our targets and our strategy. We are fully in line with what we  said we'd do and we are on the right path to hit the figures and the targets which I have planned previously for  2015.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: So these results have been achieved within the framework of an economic climate that obviously was much  tougher than that of H1, 2011, and that they clearly did worse in the, compared to the first quarter of 2012, which  was more or less satisfactory and was in line with the economic scenario that we thought would play out at the  beginning of the year. The deterioration was especially bad over the last two months, especially in Europe.  In North America, we have continued to have a good level of activity, as far as our industrial sectors are concerned  and we have seen a very, very gradual recovery in residential constructions in North America and, therefore, the  signals for the months to come also are green.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: And so, in the – it is true that the global economic climate has deteriorated with sharper deterioration in the last  two months. Now, of course, the basis for comparison was very difficult, because although we did have a negative  calendar impact in the second quarter in Europe, as I mentioned, I'm not going to talk about this very much but  it's quite clear that the weather conditions in Europe over the second quarter were really not very good.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: We've also had a significant impact of the rise of cost of raw materials and energy, especially in flat glass, because  that is an activity that has really suffered from all the unfavorable conditions, and that is why our results have not  been good in flat glass, both in Europe and in emerging countries. I'll come back to that in more detail later on.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: So, given this deterioration in the economic climate, just as the group has done in the past, we reacted very  strongly and very quickly, as well with, and we took a number of measures. First of all, we have decided to  maintain and I believe that this is very important, although results have been rather patchy from one sector to  another, we have continued to focus, as a priority, on our sales prices, given the increase in the cost of energy and  raw materials.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: We launched new cost cutting program and from the first half of this year, we've already seen the primary results  come up and, especially, we've had specific program in the flat glass division.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now for flat glass, we've seen a sharp downturn in demand in most of the countries where we are present. In  automotive glass in Europe, which has been accentuated by, of course, fallen inventory throughout the assembly  line and we've also seen a shrinkage in the solar market and for non-residential sectors in Europe, as well. And in  Asia and in Brazil, we have markets that were not a positive for the first half of the year and, above all, we've had –  there is a lot of overcapacity in China and, of course, this has led to short-term high exports that, of course,  impacted prices, both in Brazil and in Korea.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Some of these stoppages, of course, are final stoppages we did in the first half of the year. We stopped two other  floats in France and Germany and also we have sold two half floats, one in Italy and one in France. In Brazil, we  started up a new float, but we had to stop one of the other floats for repairs and, in Asia, we stopped one in China,  two temporarily in South Korea and another one in China that was for the solar market.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Of course, we had to restructure and downsize our solar business, given that although the market for solar panels  continues to grow in Europe, as far as the mid-term trends are concerned, but as you know there was a bubble in  2010, 2011 and, therefore, this year we've had a relative downturn. And given the actions that have been gathered  by the Chinese, our European customers, especially Germany's customers, have had a difficult time and, therefore,  we've had to restructure our activities in solar.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, given all these elements and you'll see that we are going to – we've had made the lot of investments, but we  have frozen any new investments and we've decided to sharply reduce inventory in flat glass in order to ensure  that we are in line with the reduction of demand. Of course, the actions we've taken are not limited to flat glass.  I'm going to look at the two – so the two main examples of this are Spain and Portugal. I'm sorry, I don't think we  can continue says Mr. de Chalendar.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, for the first half of the year, given the deterioration in the economic climate in Europe and in emerging  countries, especially over the last two months, we have launched an action plan with new measures that have to  adapt to the changing economic climate.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: You can see 2.6% rise, two-thirds of the positive contribution to sales and from distribution with the Build Center  and Brossette acquisitions. Brossette was consolidated as of the 1 of April, but the remaining third is made up of  the acquisitions made in performance materials, in energy efficiency, with Solar Gard and in construction  materials essentially on emerging markets.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Regarding disposal gains, you can see €66 million, essentially due to the main item, which is gains that we reaped  in from the disposal of a half float, an independent, [ph] Mr. Reulle (16:42). Assets depreciation, €193 million –  asset write-downs were €193 million. Depreciations in two main areas: first of all, write-downs in flat glass with  our float activities and in our solar activities, as well and, on the other hand, there was goodwill depreciation in  distribution in Spain. So, on the whole, operating income dropped 20.8%. That's the business income item.  So, a word about asbestos-related claims in the US, which is customary – situation was stable. Regarding the  number of claims, we're at 2,000 claims in the first half. Claim settled, slightly rising, but there are swings on that  number. As you know, when stocks are dropping at the end of the period, we were at 47,000 claims. Settlements  over the 12 month signing period are down, €70 million.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Moving on to cash generation, let me begin with EBITDA, you can see a 7.9% drop. It remains at a very high level,  €2,284 million. There was a rise in CapEx in the first half, because we initiated investments in 2011 notably on  emerging markets. As you can see, nearly 50% of our industrial investments were made in Asia and in emerging  countries. And you can see that the growth CapEx and development CapEx have an 80-20 split. Well it's 80-20 if  you'll include energy efficiency. With regard to Europe, that is 80-20 between Asia and Europe.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now moving on to free cash flow plus change in operating working capital requirement, so you see cash  generation proper. Actually, you see quite an improvement against a pretty difficult backdrop. You see a 21% rise  in cash generation, which confirms the priority that we clearly set out on cash generation for the half year.  There were a few acquisitions in the half year. The top two are Brossette, obviously, which we integrated on April 1  and SAGE, which is our specialized glass. This is in energy efficiency. With respect to last year's half year, you see  that we're more cautious in acquisitions, because we spent €277 million versus €520 million in H2 2011. And the  acquisitions are essentially in line with commitments made in 2011. As Pierre-André suggested, we postponed any  new acquisition projects that we had.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Conversely, regarding High Performance Materials, you see the prices performed well, thereby driving H1 growth,  so greater than the volume performance and it pretty much offset the volume situation. In terms of the numbers,  you see the impact of the integration of Solar Gard and a positive FX impact.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Regarding EBITDA and CapEx, you can see that CapEx in Innovative Materials remains high with significant  investments made on the emerging markets for automotive glass and for flat glass in Columbia, Brazil, India, but  we also invested in energy efficiency in SAGE in the US. EBITDA minus investments, €326 million over the  period.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Regarding exterior solutions, you see a minus 1.2% there. This is essentially due to pipe, as previously announced,  because pipe is at minus 12% over the period. Other activities in exterior solutions, mortar and exterior business  in the US are still in positive territory.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: So I'll hand it over back to Pierre-André, who is going to tell us about the outlook and the action plan moving  Pierre-André de Chalendar  Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA  Well, first, let's take a look at the economic outlook for H2. Although, we know that the economic climate is not  going to be easy to forecast, what we've decided to go with is that in Western Europe, conditions are going to  remain difficult in the automotive market.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: The context may be slightly different, but the worse the economic climate gets and the worse the prices of energy  and raw material may get – of course, they may soften. These prices may soften little bit, although we don't see  that happening yet. And therefore, we need to pass through the increases in the prices of raw material and energy  into our sales prices in a varied manner, depending on the sector.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, if we look at the cost savings by business sector, you can see that this concerns every business sector. Of  course, the flat glass activity is going to contribute the most, but all of our business sectors are concerned. Now, if  we take a look at the type of costs we're going to cut, first of all, overheads in which we believe, we should be able  to make a cost saving of about €100 million.  Here we see that the programs that we launched three to four years ago have already given us certain savings and  now make it possible for us to launch new reductions by basing ourselves on the centralization of support  functions that we done earlier. And therefore, we can continue to cut our overheads and general structural costs in  our businesses.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: I've already talked about the main points for the first half. We will continue to restructure in flat glass. We've  already done a lot of work there. But other measures have to come in the second half as well as in pipes.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, in these investments, we are going to do, all we can, to preserve our investments in emerging countries, and  concerning energy efficiency, which will actually ensure – which will actually account for 80% of our totaled  annual growth CapEx this year.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Sales prices that are – plans are to be increased in insulation, as well as in our exterior solutions products. The  situation, however, is going to be much more uncertain and much more patchy in Western Europe depending on  how different markets evolves and how construction and renovation markets evolved.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: However, we will have a favorable impact on these sectors of our cost cutting action plan. And as you know, it is a  fluctuation in – and the gap between the price and the cost of raw materials and energy is the most sensitive there  for us and, therefore, it might be more in our favor in the second half of the year.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: So, in this context, given that the economic climate has continued to deteriorate since the beginning of the year,  given the scenario, the objectives that we have fixed for ourselves for the second half of the year is, of course, to  continue to raise our sales prices in a measured manner. We consider that we will continue to have declines in our  sales volumes. So we hope to limit them as much as possible. And the operating income for H2 will, of course, be  impacted by the decline in sales volumes and, therefore, should be slightly reduced compared to H1, 2012. And, of  course, we will continue to keep a very sharp eye on our free cash flow and we hope to have a very high level of free  cash flow and a very strong financial structure just as we have today.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: Now, short-term prospects, that clearly are going to be impacted by the international economic climate and by the  economic outlook in our sectors, but that will not affect the very solid fundamentals of the group with a very well- balanced business portfolio and very well-balanced geographically as well.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: And we believe that we would be resilient and as we have been so far, very clearly, the group is very responsive one  with – we manage to take selective measures and we hope that this capacity to react will help us to very quickly  adapt to the economic climate. But I can't really talk about a strong recovery although, of course, that will happen  once the activity starts to improve.

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: And, of course, the group will continue to have a strong financial structure. And these advantages, in spite, of the  rather negative economic climate, does give me a lot of hope for the future of the group.  So this is the end of my presentation, and Laurent and I will take your questions, of course. And first we'll take  questions from the room, then the questions by phone, and then the questions by – through the Internet.

texts.profession: SECTION
texts.text: Q Yes. Hello. I have a few questions if you don't mind. The first question concerns gypsum and insulation in the  United States, which have had quite a significant loss for you. So, do you think that you can reduce that loss this  year? Do you think that you could break even this year, if that's envisageable?

texts.speaker: SECTION
texts.profession: SECTION
texts.text: Second question, could you give us figures for the evolution of the costs of raw materials and energy for the first  half of the year, at least more or less an idea? And the second element, concerning the Achilles heel of the group  that is flat glass, the EBITDA, which hasn't done very well. Is that only in emerging countries, or has that also been  the case in Europe? What is – what are the figures more or less of the price of 4-millimeter glass till the end year- to-date to the end of June?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now for insulation, price rises came later. They are ongoing right now. And so, of course, the situation is going to  improve more gradually than was the case for gypsum.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: As I told you, we had production capacity in Europe that outstripped demand and certain number of players on  the market which is often the case in flat glass, if you have production capacity, you have to use it all the time.  And, therefore, we had a level of inventory that was high. And we had a reduction in inventory that went beyond –  that goes beyond the reduction capacity, but of course that takes a lot of time. And that's why the price rises that  we tried to push through in the month of May were not sustainable.  And Laurent will tell you about the cost of raw materials and energy.

texts.speaker: Josep Pujal
texts.profession: Analyst, Kepler Capital Markets SA
texts.text: Josep Pujal with Kepler. So to echo the last question on the cost of raw materials and energy, do you believe that  your price rises have been enough to offset that? And if you look at the difference between the different sectors  and if you exclude flat glass, because I imagine that of course flat glass has pulled you down sharply this year.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Okay. I'll answer your first question concerning the gap between costs and prices. It's quite clear throughout the  group, we are slightly below. We have not been able to pass through all the costs of raw material and energy, the  increase in the cost of raw material and energy throughout the group. As you've pointed out yourself, there is one  sector that is quite negative, which is flat glass, where prices have gone down, whereas costs actually have  increased more than – in that activity than in the other activities of the group.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now for flat glass, today in terms of price for the 4 millimeter float that Pierre-André talked about, if I remove the  inflation of raw materials and energy from that, we are at a historic low point, which we already reached in 2009.  And in 2009, the capacity was closed down and the prices went up slightly. So if I look at the prices over the last  10 years, really this is a historic low point for prices there. And we hope that that is proof that we can only move  upwards from here. And as Pierre-André said, we hope the price rises will be able to be pushed through from  August onwards.

texts.speaker: A
texts.profession: Well, for flat glass, we have to make the difference between the building sector and the automotive sector. If you
texts.text: As far as the building sector is concerned, we have to look at the situation country by country. In China of course  there is far too much over capacity. texts.text: Regarding second question on solar, solar amounted to a little over €300 million. Essentially for glass and some  activities in High Performance Materials, the drop in sales in solar should be around 50%, very significant drop.  But sales are not that substantial at group level.

texts.profession: Hello, I am with Cheuvreux. I have questions on flat glass. I'm sorry I'm emphasizing. So you spoke about small

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: We announced a price hike in August not due to energy. And as I say, I'm hopeful. I may have seemed cautious  but, cautious on the experience we had in May. But history has shown that when capacity is back in line with  demand, prices rise. And now we're at a very low point as we speak. Now, our competitors also announced price  hikes. I don't have competitive intelligence that would allow me to tell you about their cash cost levels; take a look  at the results publications of our two Japanese competitors. In the last two quarters, their results were pretty –  were not very good, showing that Saint-Gobain is not that poorly managed after all. Muriel Fellous.

texts.speaker: Muriel Fellous
texts.profession: Analyst, SG Securities (Paris) SAS
texts.text: Muriel Fellous from SocGen. I have three questions, if I may. My first question has to do with insulation. Looking  at the second quarter interior solutions, I see a deterioration. Could you give us some explanations about that?  That was my first question.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: I am expecting measures that will bolster renovation, notably for energy efficiency reasons. Measures have not yet  been taken. And I do hope that government will give us some news, and that will be good measures. That being  said, as far as building starts are concerned, the market trends are not good, but the rollout of RT 2012, and this  was beyond Building Distribution has to be taken into consideration. The weight of energy efficiency is rising  every year. And that should have a quite positive impact over the next few months, as far as building starts are  concerned.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So you see, I believe that the good margin levels we have in High Performance Materials essentially stem from a  portfolio. We've stepped up our R&D efforts. All the technological niches we operate in are very promising. So I  have no significant worries about the sustainability of margins. They should remain well above historical levels.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Regarding the markets served by High Performance Materials, well, as I said in the presentation I don't have any  specific worries. There is a lot of diversity on these markets. Some of these markets are very buoyant –  aeronautics, energy, healthcare, even when it comes to energy efficiency proper, the business we acquired last  year, is growing strong in sales. So I have no specific concerns.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And also we have structural programs, world-class manufacturing, WCM, we call that and that makes possible to  reduce specific energy consumption and for structural gains as well. So if you take the one third of structural cost  savings, overheads and purchases that is, and the operational cost savings on the other hand, it's fair to estimate  that roughly 50% of the €750 million are structural and the other half has to do with the economic situation. Very  roughly speaking, I mean, we're just orders of magnitude, right.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Glass by the way is not a global business. Transport costs are very high. Glass travels better than gypsum or  insulation materials, but glass transport costs are very high. So, economically speaking, it can't be structural,  especially not as far as Brazil is concerned. Question from the floor?

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: No, Laurent Guillot speaking. Given the uncertainty we have on the financial markets, having a solid balance sheet  and preserving a robust financial situation is of the essence. So it calls for investment adjustments and acquisition  adjustments, you know. But nevertheless, we are focusing our CapEx on energy efficiency in emerging market and  we're still investing on those two fronts. So, it calls for efforts, more maintenance investments in western  countries. you see.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Regarding the US, the change from Q1 to Q2 essentially concerned exterior solutions. These are just as we  experienced in the past. And that was bloated or swollen by weather conditions which were very favorable in the  US

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, you have to take a look at the average. As a matter of fact, we said so in the conference call in Q1, we said that  there was the weather impact. And as we speak, I think the trend for H1 is a pretty truthful  reflection of what's going on in the US, given that as far as exterior products are concerned and renovation was  concerned, regarding interior solutions is more for building starts. And there, in terms of volume and building  starts in the past few months, there should be a gradual improvement in volume.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now, if we turn to flat glass prices, I don't have any more comments to make. I'm not expecting any deterioration  in prices in glass solutions. That should answer your questions.

texts.profession: Analyst, HSBC Bank Plc (Broker)
texts.text: Two questions please, the first on your energy efficiency products. So could you update on Q2 for Isover please, and any other energy efficiency  products that you care to give an update on.

texts.speaker: A
texts.profession: Regarding energy efficiency, I haven't mentioned it. Well, I broached upon it. At one point, I did say that sales in
texts.text: Europe and France, up from the construction market. So I think we still have a positive effect due to our product  mix. Take Isover sales in the half year, and there is a 6% increase, far better than what we have on average. Also  you had a question on France. There's a lot of export from France. So if your question has to do with the French  market, however, let me say this, the French market is probably one of the best performing markets in Europe.  And it's moving in the right direction, as far as volume is concerned. As far as prices in pipe are concerned, there is  not much to report on, apart from the fact there were major raw material and energy price hikes and we have not  passed them on in Europe, although things are improving little by little.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: But given the measures that we've already taken to cut costs, the situation of flat glass over H2 should not have  any losses anyway. Okay, is that all?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: I have three other sheets of paper here. Mr. Rosenberger from UBS. Can you explain the increase in margins in  Building Distribution? Is it purchasing and cuts or is it? Well, as Benoît Bazin told you, it's a little bit of all of this.  What is the inflation of other costs than raw materials and energy? For example, wage inflation? Well wage  inflation is significant because, of course, it's very high in emerging countries. So in Europe and in US, it has been  limited. But in emerging countries it is high. And it is quite clear that as we can pass through, as Laurent told you,  the costs of raw materials and energy into our prices, this was – we were not able to do that to enough to cover  wage inflation.

texts.speaker: Q
texts.profession: So Madam Rousseau, you confirmed your guidance for 2012. Why are you reducing it today?  Well as I've told you,
texts.text: the way the months of May and June panned out, they did not move in the direction we expected them to. And  therefore, we are more pessimistic about the economic climate than I was two months ago.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And so the program that we've launched for this year is a program that will make it possible for us to really face a  very challenging situation. If we have any pleasant surprises in autumn, well in that case, we will do even better  than I expect. And I believe that these programs will make it possible for us to position ourselves well for 2013, no  matter how the economic climate changes. And that will give us a very good recovery point when things improve,  and it is going to improve. I believe that the fundamentals of the group will have been preserved, and they will be  very positive for us for the years to come. So, I wanted to make that point before I concluded it.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So these results are overall in line with what we were expecting in particular taking account of the first quarter  where we had the impact of the adverse weather condition of course. So overall, the market conditions, trading  conditions as expected were harsh even though they were contrasting conditions from one business area and one  region to another. There was an important calendar impact in the first quarter that was not corrected in the  second quarter, so far all of the half year; we had a calendar impact that represents 1.4%, which will be corrected  as time goes on in the third quarter.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So we had weather conditions that were really adverse in Europe. In some countries, those conditions, Central  Europe went on right until the end of the first half, because in Germany for example for the Saint-Gobain  business, it was good news in the medium term. But the flooding that took place, disastrous flooding Germany in  June of course had an impact that continued right till the end of the first half. And also there were unfavorable  impacts in the Northern part of the United States, where it always cold there but it lasted longer than usual,  especially as last year there was a – the weather conditions were very mild.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So outside of the weather conditions, certain business areas, of course, they have considerable impacts, but in  North America, good news that we were expecting we saw clearly that the construction industry for residential  buildings so it turnaround well, it's running at a good level in Asia and the emerging world. As expected, the  dynamics are a bit different from one area to the other there, but we saw a return to growth gradually, very much  returned to growth for flat glass for Saint-Gobain. And in Western Europe, overall, we encountered still difficult  trading conditions with the slowdown in industry and in construction at the same time as we expected even  though we see a fledgling recovery from the end of the first quarter onwards – the first half onwards sorry in the  U.K.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Another important point, and you know this is always first a priority for Saint Gobain, we continue to see an  increase in our selling prices about 1% in the first half against a stable backdrop for raw materials and energy  prices. Also, we kept at close watch on our cash. Our CapEx in the first half down by over €200 million compared  – in euro of course – compared with the previous year. We were very prudent about acquisitions too, which we  limited to just about €40 million in the first half, but that didn't prevent us from doing targeted development in  key growth areas for our group, there are three of them, that's the emerging countries and Asia. Energy efficiency  – energy and the environment, EEE, as we call it, and then consolidation in building – the building distribution  sector and in Construction Products.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So we started off a coating line so as to upgrade our possibilities in Flat Glass in Brazil then we pursued our efforts  to grow in Mexico and China, which are really buoyant markets of course. And we're starting off right now too –  roughly the CapEx took place at this start of this year. We're starting off a plant, a proppant plant in the U.S., a  ceramic beads that's for the hydrocarbon market. And among the acquisitions we made, there is a small amount  for that, but nonetheless it's an important acquisition will be worthwhile in the long – in the medium-term, it's an  acquisition of plastics in Brazil.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: We are currently gradually restructuring, as I've said regarding the components, the components in the solar – for  the solar industry, we discontinued a line in Poland and we pruned down our business activity level in Germany.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And if you separate out the first and the second quarters, the impact of the scope effect in the second quarter is  negative to the tune of minus 3. – minus 3.3%. So that's the trend that will be sustained for the full year in terms  of the contribution to the group's sales for the full year. You see a minus 3.2% on like-for-like basis here. So the  price effect is up 1%. That's a good price increase given the fact that there is steadying up of energy and raw  material prices minus 4.2% then for volume. That's quite an improvement compared with the first quarter,  because we said, 6.3% – minus 6.3% in the first quarter.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So the operating income, as you see on the screen going to €1.26 billion this year. So that's down of course, down  15.7% the group margin, 6.1% that is slightly shrinking compared to 6.9% figure we had last year. Good resilience  though of our non-distribution businesses, the margin grows from 8.9% and 9% in spite of the drop in volumes in  Europe because of the adverse weather condition in the first quarter. In particular, thanks to the improvement of  the gap between price and cost in certain areas, especially in Exterior Solutions.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The non-operating items here between the operating income and the business income, I'll go back to the provision  for asbestos-related litigation later and that's stable as you see. You see the other expenses going up quite  substantially here between last year and this year that's because of the restructuring plans that we're pursuing  within the group. Almost 50% of that sum devoted to the restructuring within the Flat Glass with a lot of  restructuring in our float glass areas but also in Sekurit, an arbitrage in Spain, but we're doing also in The  Netherlands of course so and in solar panel glass. So we're spending a lot of money at the moment to turn around  the Flat Glass business of course, that's reflected there.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: These are the trends that you can see on this slide that's due to weather conditions and the number of work days  during the first quarter, 1.2% for the quarter. During the second quarter, we had a slight improvement of Flat  Glass that's positive and also Interior Solutions as well and distribution as well in the U.K.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: On the contrary, there is still a negative impact of our volumes all in all in Europe. And also, if you look at Exterior  Solutions, as you can see we have a negative 4.1 for this first half that's for Exterior Solutions, that's due to a  reduced stocks on the side of our clients in the U.S.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now if you look at all of these business sectors and that's very important our price performance is good. All of our  prices are positive, if we look at each and every single business sector. Well, it's less the case for Flat Glass. We  reached, well, zero versus last year. Yet we're positive in emerging countries and slightly in the red in Europe, that  is negative in Europe. This will not offset the cost of energy and raw materials plus 2% of Packaging, for instance.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And here is another breakdown, that's the sales breakdown and industrial assets breakdown. As you probably  know, what we do usually to appraise the profitability of each business line and long-term trends on these  businesses what we look at is industrial assets. We have Innovative Materials and Construction Products, that's  one-third of our portfolio more or less and then there is building distribution which totals approximately 22%, it's  less capital intensive.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now, during the second quarter, we have improved. Europe is still in a negative position, but less than before due  to the weather conditions during the first quarter, and the U.S. are up. There is an interesting growth in prices and  volumes, a two-digit type of growth in the U.S.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Then Building Distribution, internally, we have grown, but it's been difficult, minus 4.6%. This really shows that  this business is very much exposed in Europe. Europe was very negative during the first quarter, minus 9% in  volumes in Europe, that's for Building Distribution in Europe during Q1. And then during Q2, volumes gap is  minus 1.7%, therefore, you see the impact of the weather conditions during Q1, which was a major impact on our  businesses.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Even though the weather conditions – even though that was still difficult, there were floodings, for instance, in  June in Germany, yet our business is down, still down, but they've improved compared with Q1 that is minus 2%  and Scandinavian countries that's a big geography for us. That's stable now at 0.6%. And the trends are quite  favorable in the U.K. Our sales in the U.K. are up 8% against – from last year, when – so that really shows that we  improved considerably during the second quarter.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Finally, we'll have look at Packaging. There is a drop in sales that is 2.9% for this half with an interesting price  increase that is plus 2.1%, slightly below the figure we had during H1. But this is due mainly to the comparison  basis last year that is up 2.1% that's the price increase. This is more than the price of energy and raw materials and  therefore, the spread for us is increasing and that's positive for us, if we look at operating income.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now, we will speed up and we will talk about our geographic areas. This is a pie chart that shows the different  areas, geographic areas and the trends. As you can see, we have drops in sales in France and in Western Europe,  which show that the Q1 had a big impact and progressively, Scandinavia is improving and Germany as well, even  though we have seen the major impacts of floodings during the second quarter.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So in China, gradual improvement. The first half was marked by slower progression than what we expected. There  was the price effect that was negative given the raw materials and energy price importance in our business areas,  especially in pipes. So we expect to see the pursuit of, let's say, a softer recovery, a bit slower than what we  expected, but that will continue in China and good momentum in Southwest Asia.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So in Western Europe, industrial markets should stabilize we think, particularly automotive connected with the  trend in automotive production figures. And there will be ongoing difficulties, of course, in construction, we think  given the fact that the situation varies in certain countries, but we should note that it is more favorable in the U.K.  of course. So we think the upturn in the U.K. and Germany should take hold. Thermal renovation also is an  important thing these days, so energy retrofits should shore up our trading.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The construction market, as such, isn't a dynamic market, that's the least you can say, but we should be shored up  quite a bit by these energy retrofits, refurbishment and so on going on. So if we take out the weather related items  and weather related impact, independently of that, there is an improvement in the second quarter that we've seen  that should be sustained into the second half of the year, but for the moment, depending on the countries, the  situation, of course, vary and somewhere slightly negative. So for the second half, we think we should continue  ramping up our action plan.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So we're continuing to keep a tight rate on our cash, keeping a close watch, therefore, on cash management and we  want to keep our capital expenditures, of course, in check. As we said, the net debt should be reduced and we will  be keeping a tight rate too on our working capital requirement. But we were trying to work in a selective manner  and strategic areas with energy efficiency being a focus also Asia and emerging countries and we hope to  consolidate in Construction Products and Building Distribution.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And energy efficiency should drop the markets there, but there will be a gradual improvement we think in Asia,  particularly in pipes. And we should see an improvement in the price/cost spread compared to 2012 in  Construction Products. Our sales price have continued to go up and as raw materials and energy are leveling out  in price, that spread should, therefore, improve compared with last year.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So France, we've seen there an attenuation of the drop. We've gained market shares with Point.P, and also, we saw  the impact of energy efficiency measures for Point.P is ramping up its efforts and setting up now dedicated outlets  so as to meet the needs of our clients.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And we'll continue to see moderate organic growth and solid profitability. Now, the drop we saw in the second  quarter, we think, was a bit higher than the trend we see on the side of our clients. So we should see a slight  improvement in the volume trends going forward. So if we sum it all up, we're expecting operating income to  recover in the second half. As I said in February, we were expecting to bottom out between mid-2012 and mid- 2013 now 20 – we consider for in the light of the figures we now have to hand that we bottomed out in the first  half of 2013, aggravated, of course, by the bad weather condition in the first quarter and we think it's starting to  turn on.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Well, on Flat Glass, on the price/cost spread, we have good news compared with what we're expecting at the start  of the year on the trend in the cost of raw materials and energy. However, on prices, there's still things that are  uncertain. The prices went up in the second quarter, bit less than we anticipated, but it's harder to put across price  hikes than what we were hoping to do.

texts.speaker: Josep Pujal
texts.profession: Analyst, Kepler Cheuvreux
texts.text: So each time, I mean anyone and the other. So we heard about the adverse weather conditions in the first quarter,  but then what's the reason for the low volumes in the second quarter because it wasn't the weather?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Benoît will answer the third question. I'll answer the first two. First the price, inflation increases. Price increase  was 1% during the first half, which is what I said before that is inflation for raw materials and energy is something  that is being reduced progressively. This is something that existed out during the past, that is we had an inflation  during the first quarter or first half. It's going to be less the case during the second half. And therefore, more or  less we offset increase in raw materials and energy during the first half.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And if we look at the different businesses, the situation varies, which is what I said that is the spread is negative. If  we look at Flat Glass, the spread is rather positive and is increasing for High-Performance Materials and then the  spread is slightly negative, yet it's more and more stable for Interior Solutions, and we have a positive spread for  Exterior Solutions and also Packaging.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And Benoît will answer the final question, the third question.  Benoît Bazin  SVP & President-Building Distribution Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA  A  Well about the U.K., there is no price war. I was mentioning a competitor that posted their figures this morning,  they have the same explanations and the weather conditions had a major impact in the U.K. for the first time,  because usually, there is an increase in sales prices systematically, for the first time, they went down in the U.K.  The trend is changing a lot, because Q2 is – Q – quarter one we had increases in volumes and we're running short  of some families of products. So this is quite exceptional in the U.K. and also there is something more specific to  us is that we are actively working on this so that we could increase the margins for Build Center. As you know,  their margins were not as good as the other margins we have in the U.K.

texts.speaker: Muriel Fellous
texts.profession: Analyst, SG Securities (Paris) SAS
texts.text: And number three, the cost of energy, could you perhaps tell us what the increase was for this half year versus last  year's? And my third or rather fourth question has to do with Building Distribution in the United Kingdom. I'd  like to understand something; you mentioned an 8% increase, does that include the scope effect for Build Center?

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now, I'll answer the other first three questions. First the cost of energy. Well, the cost of energy is still decreasing.  For instance, this year, we think that raw material and energy prices will go up €100 million and that's for the first  half, mainly, more than the second half.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Well my answer is that, if we look at Exterior Solutions in the U.S., the market is such that it includes a number of  things, that is, new build, but also renovation and it's mainly renovation. And therefore, the weather conditions  have a major impact. First, the positive weather conditions for Saint-Gobain that is when there is a storm and  spring, for instance, or hurricane perhaps in fall, autumn and then negative things for us, when there is no storm,  but when the weather is not nice in winter, and therefore, it's a late season for us. So it's all of these phenomena  that we have to remember.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now what I can tell you is something about this exceptional item, well, the storm that is and the hurricane, if we  look at spring, well, this season was not as good as last year's and lower than the average we usually have. I don't  know about the hurricane season in September, who knows? But anyway not March, this being said, there is a  negative effect, that is, as I said, it was very cold in the U.S. more than usual and therefore, the season started later  unusual. That's for this market.

texts.speaker: Arnaud Palliez
texts.profession: Analyst, Raymond James Euro Equities SAS
texts.text: Could you tell us more about what's – that is newbuild and renovation?

texts.speaker: Arnaud Palliez
texts.profession: Analyst, Raymond James Euro Equities SAS
texts.text: Well, I have a new question therefore about Interior Solutions. What about the price increases that you posted for  plasterboards or insulation products in the U.S.? We have big increases during Q1 and at the end of last year, it  was discontinued during Q2.

texts.speaker: A
texts.profession: Well, as far as your assumptions are concerned, you are asking us to confirm what we said. Yes, we confirm that
texts.text: Yes, for H1, Mike for H1, there was a big drop in volumes. Well, that's for the whole half year that it's 5% more or  less for this H1. Well, it varies depending on the business lines, depending on our geographies and their  contribution is different. That is, we have a contribution in the Nordic countries that suffered a lot. They suffered  due to the foul weather conditions during the H1. And their contribution is big in terms of percentage compared  with other countries like the countries in the southern part of Europe.

texts.speaker: Will Morgan
texts.profession: Analyst, Goldman Sachs International
texts.text: My bad. I had three questions please. The first one is regarding your cost cutting. I think you have said at the full  year results that you expected – sorry, not cost cutting, your energy and raw materials inflation, I think you said at  the full year results you expected impact of €300 million to €350 million for the full year. Is that something you  are still sticking to or are you – it seems like from what you are saying you might be looking for a number lower  than that?

texts.speaker: A
texts.profession: Yeah. So three points. Considering the first one, the cost cutting, to answer the first question, the first question
texts.text: Now the breakdown per business line or for the whole year. Given what we've done with Flat Glass, well this  business will have a big impact on our cost reduction or cost cutting program. All in all, if you look at Innovative  Materials that is Flat Glass plus High Performance Materials, this represents more or less – well, let's say, 45% for  this business and the rest is, let me say, more for construction materials that is 30%, 35% and the rest is  distribution – building distribution and to a lesser extent Packaging – well, demand for Packaging if we remember  the trends we have in terms of sales in the southern countries.

texts.speaker: A
texts.profession: My answer it that, well, these new laws are for the new build, the new construction sector in France. That is in
texts.text: France, as you probably know as you are in France, there are discussions at present within the framework of what  we call the energy transition government plan. And by the way, I took part in these discussions. There was a  hearing on this and I think that we should move towards renovation, we should have more laws in renovation as  well.

texts.speaker: A
texts.profession: My answer it that, well, these new laws are for the new build, the new construction sector in France. That is in
texts.text: Now, if you look at our markets in Saint-Gobain, we are supported by the fact that the thermal regulation in new  construction is good for us, that is ART 2012 and the sales of [indiscernible] (01:33:48) during the first half in  France have decreased slightly, almost zero decrease, therefore a lot better than the rest of the construction  market, which means that this is good for our business in general. And when the market decreases a lot, it means  that we decreased less than the market. I'd rather have a market that's slightly positive so that we would increase  more. But you see this is the type of impact it has on our group.

texts.speaker: John S. Fraser-Andrews
texts.profession: Analyst, HSBC Bank Plc (Broker)
texts.text: Yes. Thank you. Just coming back to the question on energy and raw materials which I didn't hear an answer  around the guidance. I heard also it's that the full year was plus €300 million to €350 million for this year which  is about one and a bit percent increase. Did I hear earlier that you've reduced that to about €100 million and so  your energy and raw material position would be very low, cost inflation. And that would imply that your price to  cost balance should be favorable if you can continue the half one price run rate. Could you just clarify that, please?

texts.speaker: A
texts.profession: Yes. I do recall what I said, I said we were expecting an inflation of the raw materials and energy prices. We were
texts.text: So what we should look at here is not so much the price hike as such and the raw materials price hike – but price  cost spread. So we've 1% of a price hike for the group as a whole in the first half and there again we've got to apply  that hike and just keep it on – but for the industrial part because that's where the energy and raw materials price  hikes are taking place opposite it. So in the light of all this especially for the second half we should have a positive  spread that should help us, it wouldn't be just €143 billion minus one hundred, it might be a bit less than that.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In North America, both the construction and industrial markets proved buoyant despite a slow start given the very  severe weather, contrary to what we had in Europe. But the overall U.S. economy is going strongly as you saw  yesterday with the data on the second quarter.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Concerning – it's coming also from High-Performance Materials, from 12.9% last year to 13.3% last year with a  good performance, which is also above second half last year. It's despite we have volume stabilization in Ceramics,  but we have a negative mix effect in term of products in Ceramics which is weighting on the profitability. But  despite that, this has been more than compensated by the improvement we had in the other businesses in  Abrasives and Textile Solutions and Plastics due to the volume, but also overall due to the cost reduction in HPM.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Exterior Solutions is up 3.9% in internal growth. The second quarter is at 3.8%. The first quarter, you  remembered, suffered from the weak volumes we had in our Exterior Products in the U.S. The volumes were a  little bit better in Q2 on a weak comparison basis last year, but we are not compensating for the difficult  performance due to the weather conditions in Q1.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The U.S., to finish with, U.S. you remember that Q1 was clearly affected by the weather conditions. We were  negative at 1.4% growth. The second quarter posted a 6.5% growth helped, boosted by our performance both in  Interior Solutions where we have double-digit performance and in High-Performance Materials.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Second item related to this goal. We wanted to reduce the capital intensity in developed countries. We set up a  goal to decrease that between 2013 and 2018 by five points to seven points. The comparison between June and  December is not relevant, so I compared to June. And between June last year and June this year, we are two  points below. So we are also moving probably faster than what we had in mind towards this goal through tight  rein on investments in those regions and better saturation of our production capacities.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Second strategic goal is which is to increase differentiation, to increase a part our activities which are more value- added and more specific to specific customer needs. This is firstly done through R&D efforts and more innovation.  So just a few examples of the innovation that we have launched on the market; new Flat Glass products which  nearly completely, 95%, eliminate condensation while keeping the same type of insulation. This is very promising.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Some new external wall systems combining insulation, Mortars and Flat Glass panels, and others that you see on  this slide. We have continued to work on sustainable habitat where we see there is very strong potential, and we  are working on – we have finalized work with two British universities which are very interesting to model with real  [ph] terms (43:53) the behavior of solution construction in building different types of construction within a kind  of a real bubble where you can have the climate you want for the time you want. And we are getting some very  interesting lessons from that and speeding up our training programs. These are just a few examples.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now, in terms of the outlook and action plan for the second half of 2014, which is my last point. How do we see  the economic climate for the second half?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: We think that we have been gaining and we will continue to gain share, so we expect just not to be strongly  penalized by that. But the market in France will not be good in the new housing starts. In renovation market,  which is more important, there may be progressively good impacts from the measures taken by the government in  terms of energy efficiency, but this is probably more in the latter part of the year.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So in this overall framework, what are our priorities? First and like usual, I am not going to change that, and I  think it has been the constant characteristic and we have achieved good results. Saint-Gobain will continue to put  priority on increasing sales prices, even though, as Laurent mentioned, the rise in raw material and energy cost is  getting much smaller.

texts.speaker: Arnaud Palliez
texts.profession: Analyst, Raymond James Euro Equities SAS
texts.text: Good morning. Arnaud Palliez with Raymond James. I have three questions, if I may. The first one is on your raw  material and energy deal. Can you give us an update about the kind of inflation you expect for this year? You  mentioned that you have stronger inflation on several materials, but maybe at the same time on energy it is going  down. So do you change the guidance you previously gave for this year?

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Concerning raw material and energy, yes, we stay with the same guidance we've given at the beginning of the year,  which is slightly below €100 million impact of raw material and energy cost. In fact, when I say raw material and  energy, energy is stable with some energy cost going down in, let's say western countries, but at the same time, as  always in emerging countries where we have one-third of our assets, energy prices that are usually distributed by  monopolies are going up.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: On the raw material, on the other side, we have some raw materials that are going up, mainly for glass businesses  or cullet and soda ash and for gypsum vis-à-vis paper. On the other side, we have all the costs that are going down  especially iron ore and coke for the Pipe division. But overall, the ore impact is maintained at a slightly below  €100 million for the full Group for the full year.

texts.speaker: Will R. Jones
texts.profession: Analyst, Redburn (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: Good morning. I had a few, please, if I could. First, just on energy and raw materials. Since you've given the  guidance for the full year, could you just outline what you think the first half, second half split is there? And  overall, do you think that there's scope for a better price-cost spread in the second half than the first?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: When you look at the second quarter, we were a bit surprised not to see that after a bad first quarter there would  be a pick-up. But for the whole year, it's a bit early, but we think that this should compensate normally, and we  should be – have around flat volumes during the year. It's mostly renovation and there is also the storm impact  which has not been very good this year like it was not also very good last year. But it's mostly renovation, so  roofing doesn't get impact from significant increase in new housing that we have in Interior Solutions.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And you see at the moment quite different trends in the U.S. depending on the geography. The regions are not  behaving exactly the same way. And for various reasons, there is dynamics of the weather which have been very  different and depending, then you have the impacts of storms which are not normal weather. So you have different  dynamics.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: You need to remember that the Construction Products activities of Saint-Gobain are generally outperforming, and  that's our strategy; are outperforming the general construction level. And clearly, have nothing to do with what  you see in cement for those of you, and there are many who are following cement. texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: From a pricing perspective, Interior Solutions operated in a more challenging environment due to the competitive  nature of the business, as well as to the fact that it is also one of those businesses which is benefiting the most on  the other side from the reduction in raw materials and energy bill, which is true for us as well as for competitors.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So a few words now about the outlook and our action plan. In terms of the economic climate, we have seen  stabilizing trends in France. texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar

texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Good they were in terms of our cost saving programs. We delivered €170 million during the first half. We are also  speeding up our program of small and medium-sized acquisitions. texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And as you remember, we had said that at the beginning of the year, this was a particularly important challenge  for us as we were facing increasing cost of raw materials and energy. I mentioned in Q1 that we expected our  build to increase by at least €250 million due to price. I now expect a figure more around or above the €300  million mark. Things seems to be stabilizing, however, on the purchasing side. So a great pricing achievement  which was not a given entering the year.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Flat glass delivered solid results in the first half, with 5.6% internal growth including 2.7% of volume, and 2.9% of  price. This good price appreciation, which was steady over the two quarters, allowed us to more than cover the  raw materials and energy evolution.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Moving to Construction Products, where we saw organic growth of 3.7% for the first half, driven by volumes and  particularly pricing at 2.8%. This pricing achievement was important as Construction Products is a business sector  where we see the majority of the raw materials and energy inflation this year. So, this is good news even though  we need to continue to push in this direction.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In interior solutions, interior solutions grew 4.1% with an increase in both volumes and price against the backdrop  of the strong inflationary environment in raw materials and energy costs. A few example of cost increases that we  have seen would be, for example, steel profiles, paper, but also gypsum, and this deserves particular explanation  because what's happening here is that we are progressively shifting the supply of our plasterboard plants from  using synthetic gypsum, which is a byproduct from coal plants, progressively being shut down in some countries,  to natural gypsum, resulting in some additional costs in those plants which were using desulfurized gypsum. All  the industry is experiencing the same trends, but this adds to the imperative of pushing price overall.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In pipes, prices increased against the backdrop of rising raw materials and energy costs, but in terms of volumes,  we continue to suffer from the lack of large export contracts. As a reminder, this continues to particularly impact  France and the France sales figures as they are accounted by country of production.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, in this framework, our priorities remain constant, as I explained at the beginning of the year. Clearly, we'll  focus on the sales price. You've seen that we have done a good job of increasing prices. As you saw also, it's not  enough in all our divisions because of this increased bill in energy and raw material prices that Guillaume  described.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In terms of cost of raw materials and energy, as I said, we are now estimating that the price effect on the full year  is going to be €300 million. And for the first half, we think that at the group level, we were able to offset the cost of  – the inflation of cost of raw materials and energy by price. That being said, the situation is very different from  business to business, as I mentioned, probably positive in flat glass and more difficult in Construction Products,  which experienced the biggest part of the inflation of raw materials and energy.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Maybe I would say on a spot basis, we are a bit more confident than we were a few weeks ago on energy, but not  on raw material. But as you've seen, this changes very quickly. Next question. Yeah.

texts.profession: Analyst, Redburn (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: And then the last one was just if you can help us understand expectations for U.S. roofing for the remainder of the  year?
