texts.text: I think we answered to that question, we expect, if the weather conditions are good in March, we expect a positive  evolution of volumes in the first half of the year. And clearly, we have a trend for the time being concerning  emerging countries and the U.S. that are positive and the stabilization in Europe. And the cost spread as always is  a significant strategy, and as someone remind us before, we have 10 years of track record in terms of passing the  cost increase to our customer in Saint-Gobain.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: I think I already answered in terms of the UK where we are positive and we are also positive in terms of volume  and pricing in Germany, but to a lesser extent than to the UK. By the way, Germany is truly benefiting in more  than other countries by the better weather in the first two months of 2014.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Well, when you look at France, you'll see some macroeconomic data especially in construction which are quite  depressing. And when you look at Saint-Gobain sales, you don't seem to see the impact of those yet, but I think  this is going to continue to be the case in 2014. I think the market in France for us is not – the macroeconomic  environment is not very positive, but I think it's not at all as bad as you could think and so we are not expecting  necessarily an improvement in France. There will be an impact of the weather positive at the beginning of the  year, but we are not, on the other end, very negative on France as far as we are concerned for 2014.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Well, roofing activity during 2013 has seen very strong upswings from one quarter to the next. We had a very  strong first quarter. We had a very bad second quarter because of destocking. We had a very good third quarter  and we have more disappointing for fourth quarter. Overall, it has not been a great year also, as Laurent explained  earlier, mostly because of the impact of storms and weather which there were very few storms in 2013 compared  to the average and especially compared to the year before which had an impact to our volumes where overall for  the year not positive in roofing in 2013.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: For 2014, if we can expect a more normalized weather but that's very difficult to assess, we should see some  growth which is not very easy to quantify. To remind you the roofing market is mostly renovation. So, the impact  of what's going on new construction is limited compared to our Interior Solutions business, gypsum solutions  which are strongly benefiting from the upswing in new construction in the U.S. So, probably more positive in 2014  on roofing but magnitude is not clear.

file: SGO - Q4 2014 Earnings Call 26February2015 230 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 26-Feb-15.pdf

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: So, as you can see in this – on this slide, an evolution of Construction Products that has been clearly very different  between H1 and H2. H1 was very strong, boosted by Q1 on weather conditions. H2, at plus 0.4%, slower than H1,  definitely, due to the reduction of the prices in the roofing business in the U.S., but also due to the slowdown of  the macroeconomic situation in Continental Europe, France and Germany.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: In line with that, another metric was to reduce the capital intensity of Saint-Gobain, especially in developed  countries, with a specific focus on Flat Glass. Here also we have made a progress towards our objective. So, the  first metric which is for the overall industrial assets, we have reduced from 32% to 31%, in line with our 28%  objective for 2018.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Now, I would like to give you a few elements about our outlook for this year. In terms of economic climate, there  will be a gradual recovery in Western Europe, which will be nevertheless hampered by the fact that the  construction market are going to stay depressed in France for at least a significant part of this year.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: In Construction Products, we will continue to see good momentum in Interior Solutions, and we expect the  situation in roofing to stabilize. And in Building Distribution, we will have a mix depending on the evolution of the  different countries, but overall, the organic growth will be reduced by the downturn that is still going to be the  case in France. And clearly, the first half comparison will not be easy with the first half of 2014, also because of  some weather impact. In Packaging, we expect a good level of operating income, and clearly a continuous  improvement.

texts.speaker: Josep Pujal
texts.profession: Kepler Cheuvreux
texts.text: Josep Pujal from Kepler Cheuvreux. I have three questions, if I may. The first one is on the price cost gap. How did  it went in 2014? Were you able to recover, through prices increases, more than your cost inflation or not? How do  you see 2015, given what is happening to energy costs? And also, how should we read the – what seems an  acceleration of the prices in Q4? Is it – is there a one-off there?

texts.speaker: Josep Pujal
texts.profession: Kepler Cheuvreux
texts.text: I have two other questions. Do you want them now? Y es? My second question is on the volume trends. 2014 was  polluted by weather conditions, very strong in H1, very favorable. But if you try to strip this, what can you say  about the underlying trends? Do you see an improvement or a stabilization or still a deterioration? And,  particularly in your guidance, and if we focus on France, in your guidance, France remains a negative, whereas we  see some leading indicators, like building permits, which stop deteriorating in Q3 – end of Q3 last year. So, do you  think that in the second part of the year, it will start to show in your figures?

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Y es. Concerning the price cost spread in 2014. Clearly, as I guided in July, we remain with approximately €100  million headwind in the cost of raw material and energy for the full year 2014. And you've seen that, over the full  year, we've managed to get 1.1% prices overall, including Building Distribution material resale business. So, you  should count that a little bit differently. So yes, we were able to pass the cost of raw material and energy to the  customers. But clearly, at the same time, this is not taking into account the inflation that we have on all other cost   than raw material and energy.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: If you look at 2015, clearly we have, on the opposite, if we stay at the current prices of energy, we should have a  tailwind coming from energy which is also around €100 million impact. On the opposite, in some raw material,  we  have increasing prices. For example in soda ash, and this represents probably to the – as of today, and if the price  stay at the level they are today, approximately a  €50 million headwind. So, the net of the two is, I would say, a  €50 million tailwind, perhaps a little bit more, if we continue to have good evolution of, let's say, or a stable  evolution, of energy, energy prices. But that's the order of magnitude.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: So, very difficult to say to you what will be the spread through the year. And as Pierre-André said, our target will  be to keep – or to keep the prices up as much as possible, and to benefit from this change of energy prices that is  beneficial to us in 2015.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Concerning renovation, I'm also very optimistic medium-term on France. I consider that the law, which is being  passed on the energy transition in France will be very positive for us. But this law has not been yet voted. It takes  quite some time. And I don't expect that it will have a positive impact for Saint-Gobain before the second half of  this year.

texts.speaker: Yassine Touahri
texts.profession: Exane Ltd.
texts.text: Y eah. Good morning. Yassine Touahri from Exane BNP Paribas. So three questions. First on the roofing in the  United States, could you give us a bit more color about the outlook? And to what extent could you keep the decline  in cost that is likely to happen because of the recent collapse of oil prices. Is there a scenario in which margin  could expand as much as in 2009?

texts.speaker: John Crowe
texts.profession: Senior Vice President
texts.text: From an energy standpoint, obviously, asphalt is our largest raw material, and with the drop in oil prices, we are  seeing a pretty significant reduction of asphalt prices. So we would expect that to be a favorable raw material cost  input for the year versus what we've seen in the past year.

texts.speaker: Arnaud Lehmann
texts.profession: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
texts.text: And lastly, regarding the pricing outlook for building products. One of your competitor in insulation was referring  to, let's say, some limited downside risk to prices obviously in the context of limited or some deflation in energy  costs. Do you believe you'll be able to increase prices in Europe in Building Products? Thank you.

texts.speaker: John S. Fraser-Andrews
texts.profession: HSBC Bank Plc (Broker)
texts.text: Thank you. My question is regarding France and – particularly France, where you've in the second half reported a  volume fall of 6% to 7 %, I think you said. Could you differentiate between energy efficient products and non- energy efficient? And perhaps you could use also that as an example and get the volume in that space.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: And the same order of magnitude that we – the difference is the same order of magnitude that's a few percentage  between what do in energy-efficient products and the markets.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: So that's but it's the second time effect. In construction, the impact will be much more diffused and long-term. I  think that the economy of Europe is going to progressively impact, but it will take more time in construction. For  pipe, it's clearly good news.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So globally, I am optimistic on Poland, especially on the construction. And that's where – it's more precise for me  than what I said. There has been a reduction of the growth in the second half because of the weather on the first. I  think that this is going to be good.

texts.speaker: Laurent Guillot
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: I think I answered this question already. And in term of energy, we expect deflation of around €100 million in  terms of raw material, on the opposite, we expect inflation of around €50 million.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: And I have another question on the impact of the evolution of oil price on our projects, for HPM particularly, and  for the energy transition on buildings?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: First of all, I think that the evolution of oil prices is globally, in terms of our initial impact, good news for our P&L.  I believe this fall is not going to last. I don't know when, but I don't think it's going to last very long, even though  it's one year, two years.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: I am very impressed by the speed at which the oil production in the U.S. is falling. The adjustments are absolutely  massive at the moment. We have a small business of proppants, where we also have reacted very quickly. We have  already reduced our capacity by half last month, and we can reopen if it's [ph] power but new (1:30:55)  adjustments are [ph] varied (1:30:57). So exploration in the U.S. at the moment is extremely low. Production is  falling. This, at some point, will have an impact on the overall worldwide oil prices.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So I don't think it changes the prospects for renovation, especially which is a question for our energy savings  program in buildings, which are growing especially in Europe, to remain for many years, in most countries, a  strong priority. So I think it's more a short-term subject.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Concerning the businesses we have in HPM, this business of ceramic proppants is going to be affected. It's not a  huge business for Saint-Gobain. It's going to be affected short-term, but we have seen this business being, in the  past, also quite cyclical. And I believe that oil exploration will come back. For the rest of HPM, this issue of oil  prices is not a major driver of our projects.

texts.speaker: Q
texts.profession: [indiscernible] (1:34:18) just a little question on U.S., you mentioned that building materials had a good dynamic
texts.text: in North America except for roofing. So what happened for roofing in volumes and prices?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: There is another point that, yeah, we may not have mentioned that this year, but this business in roofing has one  particular dynamic, which doesn't – we don't have in our other businesses, which is a significant activity exist or  doesn't exist depending on the level of storm activity, which has been very low in the last two, three years, and  which has, last year, also had a negative impact because – and you need to know that roofing is mostly renovation  and the storm factor is important.

file: SGO - Q4 2015 Earnings Call 26February2016 230 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 26-Feb-16.pdf

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: In the industry activities in the U.S., which is a big part of our HPM businesses, we have been clearly hit. But what  happened in the oil and gas market, especially with our proppants division, some of our industrial activity has  remained solid.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Organic growth was positive 0.4%. Prices were up plus 0.3%, showing once again the group's ability to drive prices  even if the environment became increasingly deflationary during the year. Volumes edged up by 0.1%, and this  performance was achieved despite the adverse effects of oil and gas-related businesses and the strong slowdown  experienced in our Pipes business. Those two businesses represent more than one-third of a point of negative  volume growth this year on the group.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: As Pierre-André mentioned previously, excellent working capital performance, as we co ntinue to harvest the  benefits of a very strict cash discipline. This is a historical low, and this is substantially better than what had been  guided previously as a long-term objective, partly helped by good weather conditions at the end of the year which  led to a busy month of December. So two days improvement compared to 2014, with approximately one of those  two days coming from exchange rate.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, let's now move to sector-by-sector and regions-by-regions comments. So, Innovative Materials had a solid  year, with a strong contribution of Flat Glass of plus 5.1%, driven by a strong [ph] Sika rate (21:08) but with a  solid upstream, too. High-Performance Materials showed a good resilience despite the effect of oil-and-gas- related businesses.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Construction Products is growing overall by 0.5%, with Interior Solutions at plus 1.9%, which is a growth entirely  linked on the full year to volumes. Exterior Solutions was lower and weighed on the average, mostly because of the  difficult environment in the Pipes business in the second half. In this activity, I'm talking about Exterior Solutions,  the volumes were positive for the year, however, with a negative price effect of 1.8%, also impacted by the roofing  asphalt price decrease.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: High-Performance Materials was impacted by the decrease in ceramics, which is itself mostly the effect of oil and  gas-related businesses, especially North America. All other activities of HPM, abrasives, plastics and textile  solutions, are growing. And without proppants, HPM growth would have been around 1.5%.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: A substantial part of the CapEx is one-time heavy plant maintenance, for example, in Interior Solutions in the U.S.  Another important investment is our new roofing plant in Missouri, to be started in the second quarter of 2016.  This will help us improve our geographical footprint, our service level, and our logistic cost in a profitable  business.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Looking at the results by geographical area, you can see that all areas have improved this year on both semesters.  The only exception being France. North America, which was helped by exchange rate on one side, could have been  better had it not been for the oil and gas effect, first, and start-up cost in the second half of the year.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In terms of margin percentage, substantial progression in Western Europe reaching 5.9% profitability in the  second half; strong improvement also in emerging countries in the second half to 10.7% profitability despite Brazil  slowing down. And France and North America, a little bit less positive for reasons which were already explained  namely volumes and Pipe in France on one hand and oil-and-gas-related businesses in the U.S. on the other hand.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Okay. Now, I'd like to give you a quick update on our strategy and the outlook for 2016. So, our ambition remains  the same, building on our worldwide leadership on sustainable habitat. We aim to create and deliver innovative  and high-performance solutions to enhance our habitat and our daily life. And following the divesture of Verallia,  we are concentrated on our three pillars to serve our main construction market and an additional industrial niche  markets around with each of our three sectors bringing specificities, Innovative Materials, Distribution, and  Construction Products, and leveraging strong synergies between them.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So, second priority is to answer the major trends in our markets. If we look at what's going on in the construction  markets, I think I would say three things. First, there is a change in the respective role of the various players, of  the key decision makers in the construction industry. And this is boosted by the digital evolution. Globally, the  user, the final user is much more involved. The boundaries between the final users, what is called also B2C  approach and the traditional approach, are reshuffled to some extent with digital with the user focusing more and  more as growth and well developed on making sure it gets more comfort in many areas whether it is acoustic,  whether it is thermal – it's more thermal comfort than energy savings – whether it's visual. And I think this is a  very important trend.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We expect a slight growth to continue in North America, with some uncertainty in some industrial market. I think  – and we have – we should not underestimate the importance of the energy sector in the U.S. And I think the oil  and gas issue is spilling over to a number of industrial sectors in the U.S. At the same time, there are others which  are quite positive. But I think there are some – there is clearly a slowdown in industrial activity in the U.S.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Okay. So, I will take the first one on cost savings. So, the €360 million of savings, as you say on the other side, on  the other side to that, there are some cost inflations. For example, the salary inflation. I remind you that our salary  mass is approximately a little bit less than €8 billion. So, there was cost inflation there. And on the other hand,  there are also a few other costs linked to, for example, SG&A or to maintenance or to  occupation costs, which are  increasing also. But overall for the year, the cost savings we have, and the benefit of the reduction of raw materials  and energy cost, are offsetting those additional costs. And I think the second part of the question was about the  magnitude – okay.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Y eah. So, on the second one – on Pipe, I will say that you have first an impact, which has to be taken out to some  extent, which is the price impact, which is relatively similar to the impact in Roofing, the raw materials, you know,  iron ore have all gone down significantly, and our pricing has gone – has had to come down as well. So, that  explain part of the drop in prices.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: As far as Europe is concerned, and a lot of that is in France, we have both bad markets in infrastructure in Europe,  and especially in France. And we have an impact of both very good before last year, at the beginning of last year,  and very – but now, number of contracts mostly to the Middle East, which has been always an area where there is  – it's a good market, but there is oil and no water. But you need oil to finance the water, so we are at a low – even  though we see some orders for the end of the year, we are at a low at the moment. So, it means to give you a  [indiscernible] (55:21) the last quarter, our sales in that division all together were 20% down, so it has been quite  significant. And we expect that the first half will still be difficult.

texts.speaker: Josep Pujal
texts.profession: Kepler Cheuvreux
texts.text: And my third question is about the delta price costs in 2015. So, your costs – sorry. Your prices increased by 0.3%.  I don't know what did the raw materials and energy, but at the end, what was the positive or negative delta for  you?

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Y eah. The third question was about the price cost spread. If I understand well, on the cost of raw materials and  energy we had this year, thanks to – I mean, there were – energy obviously went down overall. And some of our  raw materials went down also, which was compensated by some other raw materials which are still in an inflation  mode. But overall, on the overall bill, we had savings linked to the price reductions of approximately €100 million.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: On the issue in – sorry. Your question in the U.S., as Guillaume said, we have had some pressure on pricing in the  second half in Interior Solutions. So, pricing were slightly down. I think we hope to have a price increase in  insulation. And in plasterboard, it's a little bit early to say whether we'll have the price increase at the beginning of  the year or a little bit later during the year. But as I told you that our priority is always to try to get price increase  when we can get those price increase.

texts.speaker: Eric A. Lemarié
texts.profession: Bryan, Garnier & Co Ltd. (France)
texts.text: Hello. Eric Lemarié from Bryan, Garnier. Just to come back on Lapeyre, I understood that the last time we talked  about Lapeyre, you said that Lapeyre was beneficiated from the energy and renovation trends in France, with  people changing their windows. Is it still the case now?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Renovation, yeah. Well, Lapeyre sells windows but also kitchens, bathrooms generally. We have had historically  strong volatility. It's true on windows given the tax credits which have been changing. There are new tax credits  which have been put in place, but as you know, they are more complicated than the one which existed before and  are linked to – you don't need – in order to get this tax credit, you don't need to change only your windows. You  need to have complete renovation projects. And so it's less efficient just on windows than the one which existed a  few years ago, which has disappeared, and the new one which has been put in place is less but it's a positive.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Overall, I would say that I am still very hopeful that the renovation and the energy transition law will get some  positive impact for Saint-Gobain, but the law has not yet been completely translated into decrees which are  necessary. It's happening at the moment. It has been slower than expected.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Second question. How difficult will it be to find new contracts in Pipe given weakness in oil-dependent market  especially in Middle East?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: In fact, when you look at history, it's not just black and white. The oil price in Middle East is bad, and we don't  have prices high and we have contracts. We have – I think we have good prospect but not before a number of  months. And because we had some very good contracts to expire, we have a very difficult comparison at the  moment and the low activity.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Germany, we had a good fourth quarter, in fact, and we had a slow start, I would say. But in Germany, the months  between November-December and February-March are, one, relatively low months, and second, the weather  makes a big impact. So, I don't – I wouldn't draw too much. I expect a reasonable growth in Germany better than  last year.  Guillaume Texier  Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA  A  So, I think your last question was about Q4 internal growth and the breakdown between price and volume. So,  going with Flat Glass, Flat Glass in Q4 had a growth of 3.3%, out of which, 2.2% was coming from volume. HPM,  minus 1% in alignment with the year, out of which minus 2% was volume and plus 1% was price.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Well, it's clear that on some of the oil-and-gas activity, and especially proppants, the comps is going to get much  easier. It's already much easier in – it will be much easier in Q1. So, yes, all in all, this would mean, as you've said,  it was the 2% negative weight on HPM for 2015, which is going to nearly disappear this year. So, that's quite clear.

texts.speaker: Will R. Jones
texts.profession: Redburn (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: Thanks. The first, please, is just around energy and raw materials. If you could just update on what you think the  [ph] travel bill (1:25:51) might move by this year compared to, I think, the €100 million or so downwards you  referred to last year. The second just on Flat Glass. I think the sort of pricing data we can see that sug gests some  resilience in pricing over the winter months in European upstream. Is that true outside of [ph] just (1:26:08)  Germany or perhaps just an update there around Flat Glass pricing? And while we're on pricing in Europe,  perhaps, as well, you could just update us on how you see plasterboard and insulation pricing moving in the  context of costs?

texts.speaker: Will R. Jones
texts.profession: Redburn (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: And the last one was just more general, around, with energy prices falling, are you seeing any countries where  either government or consumers are less willing to undertake energy efficiency-related renovation as a result of  the drop in energy costs? Thanks.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The first one I understood, I think it was the price effect for next year on raw materials and energy, and this one I  can answer. So there was, last year, €100 million positive on raw materials and energy. For next year, we're going  to – if things were to be frozen at today's prices, we would see an additional positive impact on our energy bill, as  well as on some raw materials.

file: SGO - Q4 2016 Earnings Call 24February2017 230 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 24-Feb-17.pdf

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: We invested in niche technologies and new services. For example, we bought a tapes company in Italy, which  complements our successful performance plastics portfolio. In Flat Glass, we continued to invest downstream with  a windshield replacement network in France, an interesting asset-light and services oriented business. In  insulation, other example, we continue to diversify our materials portfolio with the Isonat acquisition in wood-fiber- based insulation.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And in the High-Performance Materials, the CapEx are more granular in nature, but I will mention our investment  to sustain the fast growth our plastics business in the U.S. or our capacity expansion to produce technical glass  fabrics for various construction related applications in Czech Republic.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In North America, we had a very dynamic H1. Our H2 was less booming but still growing. Here, again, prices  were under pressure in 2016 on the back, however, of low energy and raw materials cost which benefited our  P&L.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In terms of the outlook, and first the economic climate, we are forecasting a gradual improvement in France,  driven by a good growth in new-build, and despite a still uncertain renovation market, even though we start to see  some early sign that this could improve. Further growth in other Western European countries, despite less  visibility, as Guillaume already mentioned, in the UK, but good growth overall in all our other countries.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In Construction Products, we will have better volumes and further cost saving, which should offset – more than  offset – sorry, not offset – more than offset the exceptional weather impacts of Roofing in 2016. We can't predict  the weather, but we have in mind that it was a significant impact in 2016. And Building Distribution should benefit  from what I said from better volume growth in Western Europe and, as you know Distribution, if pricing overall  gets better, Distribution benefits clearly from a bit of more price inflation.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So in terms of our priorities, our number one priority, I repeat myself, but the environment changed and this year  it's a very important topic. We are seeing a change in our raw material and energy situation, which went down  significantly in 2016. This trend is reversing and we need to have an upturn in price. You have seen the fourth  quarter. So, this bodes well for 2016, but it is clearly a strong priority to change from a deflationary environment to  some price increase for all our businesses.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Okay. On the pricing effect, you saw the positive pricing figures of Q4 with plus 0.8%. On the last year, 2016, we  had a price to cost of raw materials and energy gap. We had a price overall at 0% and our bill of raw materials  and energy, the price effect was a benefit of approximately €260 million overall.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Now, as we said during the presentation, we are entering a different environment, where we are seeing inflation of  raw materials and energy. And at this stage, our calculation is that this price of raw materials and energy effect is  probably going to be north of €100 million for next year.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Well, I don't – I have not seen central platform from competition, except in the UK. But in the UK we have a little  bit different strategy, but we are – we have moved in that direction in sanitary, plumbing and heating. We are not  convinced on some – on large – adjusting logistic platform in terms of heavy-side, we are not completely  convinced. We are setting up a platform in Germany and I think we will be the first one. In France, we are clearly  ahead of competition on that and Nordics also. But our logistics platform are mostly on sanitary, plumbing and  heating and some special – so light-side part of our Building Materials area, mostly.

texts.speaker: Eric A. Lemarié
texts.profession: Analyst, Bryan, Garnier & Co Ltd. (France)
texts.text: I've got a second question on Pipes. You have mentioned some delay regarding the export contracts. But do you  expect new additional contracts from – to the Middle East, thanks to the oil price increase of last year? Are you  optimistic regarding that? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Yeah. In terms of Roofing, we don't give divisional details. As I mentioned, we had a great year in terms of growth  in Exterior Products in the U.S., including Roofing and Siding, a two-digit growth. And in terms of profitability, what  we usually say is that we are in the same order of magnitude as our competitors in terms of profitability, but I will  not say much more. We benefited in the second quarter like the oil markets of the effect of storms. But what I  have to say is that on top of that, the underlying market in terms of new construction and renovation in the U.S.  was also quite good and steady over the full year.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: In terms of – your second question was about cost inflation. And I think I said a little bit during – when I was  answering the first question. Although, last year, we benefited from €260 million of cost – of price reduction of our  raw materials and energy. And approximately, you find half of that in the cost savings program because we  consider that those are our savings on top of the market price evolution, and half of this would be deflation,  market deflation.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: For next year, as I said, things are turning fast with a lot of raw materials and energy prices going the other  direction. And at this stage, our best estimate is that we are going to see an opposite effect of a little bit more – of  more than €100 million.

texts.speaker: Elodie Rall
texts.profession: Analyst, JPMorgan Securities Plc
texts.text: The second question is on fixed cost inflation. I know we talked a lot about raw materials and energy prices, but  what kind of fixed cost inflations are you seeing in your businesses. What was it in 2016 and should we expect a  similar increase in 2017?

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Okay. So, the first one about Roofing. Roofing, it's very difficult to quantify the effect of storms on Roofing, but  clearly we benefited from a higher than average storm season in 2016. What we say that a very large year, I  mean between a very low year and a very large year, you can have up to one month of effect in terms of volume.  Obviously, we don't know what 2017 is going to be like in terms of Roofing.

texts.speaker: Gregor Kuglitsch
texts.profession: Analyst, UBS Ltd.
texts.text: So, the second part is as a percentage of sale, what is the sustainable run rate? Whichever way you like to  quantify?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Well, I have seen some – what I have seen from industrial activity is – I have not seen as positive as [ph] you're  seeing (59:59) when I look at in the markets where we are. I think it depends very much on the market.  Automotive has been good, aeronautics has been good, health has been good, everything which has been linked  with oil and gas and that has expanded to general industrial has been clearly less good in the last few months. I  would say that the trend of the last few weeks has been better. But I remain cautious. There is some uncertainties  in the U.S. about the general environment, I would say. So, it's becoming more positive, but in my view, it's still a  little bit uncertain. Next question.

texts.speaker: Manish Beria
texts.profession: Analyst, Societe Generale Global Solution Centre Pvt Ltd.
texts.text: Yeah. Good morning. I have three questions. The first one is we have seen gross margin expanding in last few  years in an environment of low energy and commodity prices. So I just want to understand your pricing going  forward. So, will you look at getting some kind of pricing, which will keep on enhancing your gross margin or you  will just aspire to maintain your gross margins? This is my first question.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Clearly [indiscernible] (01:08:04) weather is a biggest upside in the next few years, it is in France. That's one of  the countries in Europe now where we have add this biggest drop in volume in the last few years without – and  we have had no recovery, very slight recovery in 2016. The difference with the other European countries that we  have started to recover and we have seen very good leverage in the other European countries in the last year  starting. So I clearly expect that to happen in France. In France, our main issue in the last years has been very  significant drop in terms of volume. So, I expect the leverage to be significant in France in the next few years.  Okay. Any other question? You wanted to say something now. No? No, I don't think there are other questions.

file: SGO - Q4 2017 Earnings Call 23February2018 230 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 23-Feb-18.pdf

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, a good performance but this performance was absolutely necessary because of the context of increasing cost  in raw materials and energy that we faced with inflation of those costs ending up amounting to over €500 million  for the year.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: I'll now turn to each one of those businesses, the High-Performance Materials and Flat Glass, to give you a little  bit more details. So, in Flat Glass, Flat Glass delivered good results with organic growth of 5.2% driven both by  2.5% of volume and a price effect of 2.7%. The good pricing over the year allowed us to achieve a positive spread  versus raw materials and energy costs.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The operating margin went down to 9.5% compared to 10.3% last year, hit mainly by the inflation in raw materials  and energy cost over the course of the year. A number of the materials that we have seen the most inflation on in  2017 are using the Interior Solutions sector. For example, steel profiles, paper and gypsum, with the move  towards natural gypsum and away from synthetic gypsum, resulting in some additional costs across industry as I  explained in the first half results.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Interior Solutions is also the area where our teams push price the hardest with good success, with prices up 3.1%  for the year, 3.5% in the second half and even 4.1% in the last quarter. So, we are seeing momentum here even  though we experienced a time lag at the start compared to the raw materials and energy inflation.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Exterior Solutions delivered organic growth of 6.7% over the year, with an acceleration to 10.1% in the second  half. This acceleration was driven by an improvement in all three businesses, but in particular, Exterior Products  in the U.S. This business benefited from additional weather-related demand resulting from repairs after the  hurricane in the U.S., and also of the very good construction and renovation activity in the U.S., overall.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Despite the raw material and energy cost inflation, we managed to achieve a wider margin of 8.4% for the year,  up from 7.9% in 2016.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: North America, we mentioned that already when we talk about High-Performance Materials and when we talked  about Construction Products. North America grew by 6% like-for-like over the year, with 9.8% growth in the  second half. In Construction, volume continued to trend well and was boosted by additional weather-related  demand in the second half. And I mentioned earlier that in the industry, we saw a good volume improvement  overall and particularly in Ceramics.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: We should have a good progression of other Western European countries, whether it is in the south, whether it is  in the north and in Germany. There is one country where there are some uncertainties, which is clearly the UK  given the very uncertain process of the Brexit, which is more creating uncertainties on the market than having a  direct impact because Saint-Gobain, we buy and what we produce in the UK is sold in the UK. So it's more – we  are not going to be affected strongly by what's going on between Europe and the UK, but the general climate in  the UK is uncertain at the moment.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The environment is getting a bit more supportive, but in some cases, we are clearly to take some risk in terms of  short term, in terms of our market share. We are ready to do that. In some cases, the industry is having the same  pressure on cost and also is acting. It is a clear focus for Saint-Gobain.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Yes. I think that it is clear from the trend you have seen quarter-after-quarter that we are getting out of this  situation you described, which mean that our environment is now realizing that we are back to not a huge  inflationary mode, but we are out of the recession. And it's clear that the first one are the raw materials and it's  coming through the chain.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And on the elimination, in fact, what you're talking about is what we call the holdings, which is what is centrally  accounted for in operating profit. And it's true that it's higher this year and there are several reasons. One of them  being insurances because you know that we are self-insured and we had, for example, an earthquake in Mexico  where we suffered damages in our Flat Glass installations. All of that is accounted for in holdings.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And there are three components as I mentioned here. There is the asbestos costs, which are relatively stable, in  fact very stable. Then there is a restructuring costs and as I mentioned, we are trending down in terms of  restructuring costs. We continue to have restructuring costs as it's part of our optimization programs, but as our  activities getting better, we are doing a little bit less of large restructuring. And then, there is the litigation and  environmental costs, which are quite variable year-on-year.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, this year, we are in a relatively high year with, for example, legal fees linked to the fact that we are one of  dozens of parties involved in the Grenfell Tower inquiry in the UK or in the U.S., our voluntary efforts to remediate  water pollution around three of our former existing sites in High-Performance Materials.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The fourth quarter was better. We have launched significant actions to reduce our cost base in France. But the  French business of Pipe has been affected by, clearly, a very significant drop of our exports for both, I would say,  reasons which are the fact that the oil countries which have been historically buying a lot of pipes are – don't  have, given the price of oil over the last two, three years, have had a drop in their orders. This is starting slowly  better, but in fact the recovery has been behind what I was expecting.

texts.speaker: Eric A. Lemarié
texts.profession: Analyst, Bryan, Garnier & Co Ltd. (France)
texts.text: Yes, hello. Eric Lemarié, Bryan, Garnier. I got three questions, if I may please. The first one on raw materials and  energy, Pierre mentioned it but I missed that. Could you remind us what was the impact of raw materials and  energy last year, and what could be your guidance for 2018?

texts.speaker: Elodie Rall
texts.profession: Analyst, JPMorgan Securities Plc
texts.text: Second, on roofing, you said volumes were supported by strong storm activity in 2017. So, what is your  expectations for 2018? I think Owens Corning has guided for a mid-single-digit decline for 2018. Is that what you  expect as well?

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: On roofing, yes, we saw what Owens Corning said about the outlook for next year. First of all, as I mentioned  rightly, it depends very much, like always, on the weather situation, which I'm even less able to predict than the  exchange rate. But I would say that overall, because of our geographical footprint, we are a little bit less exposed  to storms, it doesn't mean that we are not exposed to storms, but we are a little bit less exposed to storms than  Owens Corning. So, because of that, I think we will have a slightly more optimistic vision of 2018 and we expect  at this stage to see a flattish market in 2018, given the fact that in 2017, we benefited, indeed, from some storms.

texts.speaker: Guillaume Jean Philippe Texier
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, I don't know if it's a complete answer, but we are pushing as hard as possible on the cost saving side to offset  the overall cost increase that we see every year.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: If there is no more question on the phone, we move to the Internet. So, we have a question first from Paul Roger  from Exane. Our new price increases plan in U.S. wallboard insulation and roofing, and will the price/cost spread  be stable for the Interior Solution division overall this year.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: So, I can give you the announcement we have done in the U.S. in terms of pricing, which doesn't mean that we  will have this price realization. But we have announced significant price increase in insulation, between 12% and  15% in February, in gypsum in January also 15%, and in roofing around 3%. This may be the timing of those is at  the beginning of the year, which is usual in the U.S. I cannot tell you at this point that we are really pushing hard  on this price increase.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Do you expect the recent trend of insulation companies expanding in stone wool to continue? How could the  penetration of different type of insulation change post the Grenfell tragedy? Maybe, Benoit, you want to answer  that question. Benoit Bazin, heading our Construction Products sector.

texts.speaker: Benoit Bazin
texts.profession: Senior Vice President & President-Construction Products Sector, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Well, clearly ,there is a strong insulation market overall. On many applications, stone wool is, of course, one of the  materials. We have also our stone wool offer and we see also glass wool coming back on some new applications  like façade, like external insulation on façade and also flat roof. So for each application, there are several  solutions, stone wool being part of the offer, glass wool as well and other materials which varies according to the  regulations, according to the countries, according to marketing that – or the insulation players have done. So,  yeah, stone wool is growing. We are investing in stone wool and overall the insulation market is quite strong right  now.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Yeah. Well, I would say that in the Nordics, we have a relatively good competitive situation with a stronger  competitor in our plumbing and heating business. Overall, I think we are doing – more or less, as where they are,  we are doing better than competition in the building materials side in Nordics, clearly.

file: SGO - Q4 2018 Earnings Call 22February2019 230 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 22-Feb-19.pdf

texts.speaker: Sreedhar Natarajan
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The cost inflation for the year from the raw materials and energy was around €600 million with most of the  inflation seen in Construction Products but also in HPM and Glass.

texts.speaker: Sreedhar Natarajan
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: The inflation in energy and transportation was quite significant. Looking forward to 2019, we still not have the full  visibility at the beginning of the year on raw materials and energy inflation, but it is likely to stay at a high level  even though probably a bit lower than 2018.

texts.speaker: Benoit Bazin
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Innovation is also a strong pillar for growth. We are pleased to be for the eighth consecutive year within the top  100 most innovative companies globally. We leverage the critical mass of our spend, €450 million last year, and we'll  continue to do that in 2019. We share joint labs, could be on thermal or acoustic labs that are spread in our major  regions. We leverage also common technologies, [indiscernible] (00:37:28) or polymer extrusion, for instance,  across all kinds of product lines and markets. We leverage material platforms such as ceramic, plaster, plastic, or  glass whether it's glass for [indiscernible] (00:37:41) insulation or automotive or building glass, and we'll continue  to invest on innovation.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Second, we want to enter new countries, and that we can do it either with greenfield or through acquisition. And  third, about the local leadership, and that's where we will have what I said in terms of country analysis, and we will  take more of that into account. So that means that in some countries, we will grow certain businesses which are  linked with the portfolio. For instance, one of our most important acquisition in 2018 was in distribution in Norway.  We are building a very strong position, with very good synergies.

texts.speaker: Nabil Ahmed
texts.profession: Analyst, Barclays Capital, Inc.
texts.text: The second question is on the cost inflation. I mean, you seem to be guiding on similar energy and raw materials  cost inflation in 2019 than in 2018. I mean, we saw some deflation in energy prices here and there. So, I was  wondering why you're seeing that. Is that related to the comparison base of H1 2018 while you're still seeing a lot  of inflation? Is that related to your hedging strategies? Is that related to raw materials and inventories, which  means that we're not going to see a lot of deflation into your numbers in 2019?

texts.speaker: Benoit Bazin
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Raw materials and energy, yes, we could have a bit of positive surprise in 2019 versus what we had in terms of  inflation in 2018. texts.speaker: Benoit Bazin
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And second, bear in mind also that we have a lot of electricity and natural gas in our energy bill. So, it's not only  oil or totally directly oil related. So, yes, we could have a bit better or bit less inflation but still a significant inflation  in 2019. So far, we start the year with a good price momentum and good price cost spread. Let's see how the  year develops, but, yes, it might be slightly easier than what we faced in 2018.

texts.speaker: Sreedhar Natarajan
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Yeah. I'll just add, if you look at and you all keep track of the trend of price, the oil price, 2017 the average was  $52 and it went up to $72. And then in October it went up to $86 and then it came back $50 in December. It's  really, really volatile. And now, it's hovering around $65 per barrel.

texts.speaker: Q
texts.profession: Good morning. It's [ph] Glynis Johnson (01:30:12) from Jefferies here. Just one if I may and it's just in terms of
texts.text: cost inflation. I appreciate that you don't want to necessary pin down with your cost inflation. But can I just check  that your general guidance [indiscernible] (01:30:25)? Does that include your energy cost as well? And also, can  you give us a little bit in terms of wage inflation?

texts.speaker: Sreedhar Natarajan
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Yes. So, yes, when I say €600 million for 2018, it does include the inflation of energy cost. And so, coming to  wage inflation, we had a wage inflation in the range of 3% to 3.5% for the whole group. Again, it varies from  region to region. So, that's my...

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: And there is no more question on the phone. So, then we have question on the Internet. Okay. So, questions from  Paul Roger from Exane BNP Paribas. What impact could Phase 4 of the carbon emission trading scheme have  on your manufacturing footprint in Europe?

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Well, this is a very technical question. But, as you know, I am quite interested and committed in this question of  climate change. And Saint-Gobain has taken some very strong commitment to reduce in the environmental  footprint. We are in line to do that in terms of CO2. So, we have targets which are going to some extent to reduce  the importance of this topic, and this is a goal.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: I would say that the new phase of the European carbon emission, which means an update of the allocation rule,  [ph] will positively link (01:39:27) to a reduction of the allocations. But concerning cost for Saint-Gobain for the  next few years, we don't see an impact. This could bite in not before five, six years and then we should have had  a reduction of our CO2 emission.

texts.speaker: Pierre-André de Chalendar
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: Then we have questions from a [ph] Glynis Johnson (01:40:32) from Jefferies. Can you tell us what raw material  costs are actually increased by in full-year 2018 and guidance for full-year 2019? What should be we anticipate  from other cost items such as wage inflation and energy cost inflation?

texts.speaker: Sreedhar Natarajan
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Compagnie de Saint-Gobain SA
texts.text: If you just take the overall target we have given in 2017 Investors Day of €1 billion, out of that till now, if you take  into account the silicon carbide, which we have signed and yet to close and also the money, part of the money we  need to receive from the China transaction, which should happen very soon. So, if you take all these into account,  we have close to 50% of our target is already done.

file: SGROL - Q2 2012 Earnings Call 2August2012 400 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 02-Aug-12.pdf

texts.speaker: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.profession: MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION
texts.text: So before handing out over Justin to run through the financials, I just want to make a few opening remarks, if I  may, give you my take on the half year. Operationally, I think we've delivered good results despite what is clearly a  very challenging macroeconomic climate. And we're very pleased to have EPRA earnings up just over 5% for the  half year. Secondly, since the strategy announcement in November last year, we've made some very encouraging  at this stage in the process. We have taken some further write-down in terms of NAV, largely as a result of the  lower valuation of the Neckermann site and the other large non-strategic assets, which I think reflects the  relatively illiquid nature of such assets in today's difficult market environment. So more encouragingly, the core  portfolio has performed well, both operationally and in terms of capital value, and those core assets now represent  81% of our total portfolio compared with 69% when we announced the strategy. So overall, I'm pleased with the  progress we're making and I think we're well on track towards our goal of becoming a leading income-focused  REIT.

texts.speaker: David J. R. Sleath
texts.profession: Director, SEGRO Plc
texts.text: I'll come back to the strategic repositioning in a few minutes, but as it's a half-year results presentation, what I  want to start with is an operational update. So, I'm going to cover the full point first. Now, lot of data on this slide,  and I'm not going to go through all of it. But to highlight a few key points, I think we've made a solid first half or  had a solid first half in terms of leasing and lease renewals with 171 deals in aggregate signed during the period.  Our retention rate has been pretty good at 63% and nearly 70% in the core portfolio. We've held the vacancy rate  flat at 9.1%, just down from the position at the end of the first quarter. And we've managed to increase our like- for-like net rental income on the existing assets by 1%. The development program is continuing to build, and I'll  touch on that separately in a few minutes. And finally, we've achieved further cost savings and are making  operational improvements in several areas of the business such as in our management of cross-border customer  relationships, sustainability and property management systems, all of which will help to drive future efficiencies  and performance improvement going forward.

texts.speaker: David J. R. Sleath
texts.profession: Director, SEGRO Plc
texts.text: In the appendix of your packs, you'll find a slide on each of the remaining large non-strategic asset. So, I'll you a  bit more detail that I'm going show here. But briefly for those who aren't familiar with the assets, Pegasus Park is a  successful and well-established office park within close proximity of Brussels International Airport. It has a very  good customer list. It's well managed. And we're maintaining and indeed growing income with an improvement in  the vacancy rate from 23% at year-end to 16% at the end of June in a local market where there has been weak  demand and over-supply. Energy Park in Milan is a very attractive out-of-town office development site where  fully occupied. The second and third pre-let development schemes are under construction, and we believe there  will be demand to support further phases of development and refurbishment in the coming years. The  site is fully occupied and is leased to Krauss-Maffei, which produces machinery for the plastics industry, with  Siemens as an important sub-tenant for a big piece of the site. This asset offers a number of opportunities to our  value.

texts.speaker: David J. R. Sleath
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, SEGRO Plc
texts.text: So, let's now talk to the future opportunities. As we've previously explained, there are some powerful long-term  structural tailwinds behind occupier behaviors in our markets, most notably, urbanization and the technological  revolution. It's clear that more and more people are choosing to live in cities. This creates pressure to build more  homes often on land previously allocated for industrial uses, which is why we keep banging on about the loss and  the diminishing supply of such industrial land. But these growing urban population centers also push up demand  for goods and services, which require warehousing and large industrial space leading to strengthening demand  for such urban property. And this demand is being supercharged right now by e-commerce, which increasingly  needs space close into the final consumer for last-mile delivery. This can only intensify in the future as pressures  mount to use greener delivery methods in order to reduce vehicle emissions. These are some of the forces which  are driving up rents and land prices and which are leading developers and planning authorities to look at greater  intensification of use, in other words, multistory.

texts.speaker: David J. R. Sleath
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, SEGRO Plc
texts.text: What all these trends have in common is the need for more efficient buildings, much greater power requirements  and digital connectivity, and substantial capital investments being made therefore usually by the occupiers inside  many of the buildings, which of course tends to make them much stickier long-term tenants. Suitable buildings  and development sites to provide these requirements are hard to find especially in urban locations and planning  processes are slow and difficult to navigate which inevitably puts a break on new supply coming through. These  demand drivers and the supply constraints in many markets will we believe continue to provide a structural  tailwind for good quality well-located assets and landholdings for some years to come.

texts.speaker: David J. R. Sleath
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, SEGRO Plc
texts.text: So, we've identified about a dozen or 15 capital and, if you like, national regional capital cities that we think would  be ideal for building more urban space or need owning more space. And on the Continent particularly, we think  that's a great opportunity. The big challenge is always finding the assets. We look very hard across all those cities  to find existing built assets that we can acquire. We generally don't find very much. Delighted that we found a  couple in Paris. We just bought one in Warsaw and there're one or two others that we're working on, they tend to  be relatively small lot sizes, but generally as a rule, we found that the best way to grow our urban product in  Continental Europe which we think has all the same fundamentals that have benefited our UK portfolio will be to  buy sites, generally, brownfield sites, demolish buildings, and build some of this modern state-of-the-art.

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: If I go to Minerals Services, a difficult market situation; however, we are still able to win and operate some new  projects. This is now  becoming one of our most well-established lab into a network in term of coal testing, and it is now fully operational  and will process over [ph] 60,000 (37:33) samples a year for the next seven years. texts.speaker: Frankie Ng
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Oil, Gas & Chemicals, equally difficult market conditions especially in the Upstream activities as already  mentioned by Carla. However, like in Minerals, we have managed to secure new contract in this challenging  environment.

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
