file: SSEL - Q4 2018 Earnings Call 25May2018 600 AM ET CORRECTED TRANSCRIPT - 25-May-18.pdf

texts.speaker: Richard D. Gillingwater
texts.profession: Chairman, SSE Plc
texts.text: In the course of today's session, the team will set out how SSE has the strengths, strategy and assets, and the  earnings engine, cash flow capability and focus to deliver on our five-year dividend plan. It's a plan which for  2018-2019 gives clarity about the dividend in this time of transition for SSE. For 2019-2020 reflects the expected  changes to the SSE Group, arising from the planned SSE Energy Services transaction, and then for the three  years to 2023 sets the dividend on a path for sustainable growth. It is a plan to which the entire board and  management team is committed to delivering. And with that, I'll now hand over to Alistair. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Thank you, Richard, and good morning, everyone. Our dividend plan reflects our commitment to realizing the  significant opportunities we see to create value in an energy system that is changing rapidly. First, a decade on  from the Climate Change Act, the momentum behind decarbonization appears unstoppable with a focus on clean  growth, supported by public policy and falling renewables cost. This presents opportunities for SSE as a leading  generator and developer of renewable energy. We've already cut the carbon intensity, the power we generate by  50% and we have a new ambition for a further 50% reduction taking it to around 150 grams per kilowatt hour by  2030.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Second, the trend to electrification is clear and is being reinforced by the focus on air quality as well as  decarbonization, illustrated by the expansion of electricity in transport. This presents opportunities for SSE as an  electricity generator and distributor and as a utility services provider.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Third, the commitment to a major upgrade of infrastructure is at the heart of the UK's Industrial Strategy,  illustrated by the fact that public infrastructure investment is expected to have doubled in a decade by 2023. This  offers opportunities for SSE as a provider of local energy, telecoms and rail solutions. The opportunities  presented by decarbonization, electrification infrastructure development are clearly very significant but change  brings challenges as well. In particular, options to provide new infrastructure and services are a growing feature of  the energy sector with competition very strong. Meanwhile, scrutiny of the costs of energy to customers extends  to Networks and the RIIO 2 process is now well underway. Fundamental political questions are also being asked  about the privatization of energy – sorry, the private provision of energy, apologies.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Ensuring SSE's best place to meet the challenges and capitalize on the opportunities will require an even greater  focus on core strengths and competencies in regulated networks and renewables, and a range of complementary  businesses with relevant options and opportunities. This, in turn, requires the capacity to make the right decisions  at the right time. That's why we took the strategic decision to renew SSE. We're giving each of the businesses in  SSE the best platform for success in the light of the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead. We're more  convinced than ever that the strategic decision to demerge our GB household retail business and combine it with  npower is the right thing for customers and the energy market and for SSE and shareholders.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Compared with the status quo of GB household supply and services retained within SSE, the new supplier under  Katie Bickerstaffe's leadership will be able to secure a greater value from focusing entirely on strategic and  operational developments in the retail sector, combining resources and being a stronger competitor and  significant synergies that we remain confident of delivering and there will be a further update in next month's  circular on this. These synergies expected to contribute to lower costs for customers. We're confident that we'll be  able to demonstrate to the CMA that the [ph] proposed (00:05:57) merger will deliver benefits for customers and  the energy market as a whole and we remain on track to complete the creation of the new independent supplier in  the second half of this financial year.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: We believe that reshaping the SSE Group gives two clear advantages. For SSE, it gives a greater focus on the  infrastructure and related services relied on by energy customers which is more aligned to our core competencies  and for investors it gives greater visibility of assets and earnings in the future; the majority of which is expected to  come from regulated networks and renewables. Today's session marks the start of that.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: And if you look at the last three years, and exclude the SSE Energy Services business, over 80% of the SSE  Group operating profit is related to regulated networks and renewables. Going forward, Networks and renewables  will be core with flexible thermal generation such as the new plant at Keadby also having a key role.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: In the likes of Enterprise, Business Energy in Ireland, we also have businesses as a complementary that benefit  from direct and indirect synergies. In all of these remaining business areas, the needs of energy customers will  continue to be a key focus for the group. We also have growth and value options for the future across all the  businesses in a fast-changing energy and infrastructure sector where opportunities may be fleeting, this  optionality is vital. It's why we need to maintain a range of complementary businesses and so maintain the ability  to create attractive long-term growth and value options.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: It also means making the most of the strength that reshaped SSE, so we're in the best possible position to  respond to the challenges posed by the key trends in the energy sector I mentioned earlier, to seize the  opportunities arising from decarbonization, electrification and infrastructure upgrade and generate the earnings  and cash flow that will sustain dividends in the years to come.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: I work with these people every day and I can assure you that as well as being great colleagues, SSE's people are  a key competitive advantage. And when you hear later from the likes of Stewart Reid and Jerry Williamson, you  will also see why. The achievement of our dividend targets will only be possible if we execute our strategy in a  sustainable way and this is our second key strength. Our ability to create value for shareholders depends on  working constructively with stakeholders to improve the outcomes we can achieve for energy and infrastructure  users and for our society as a whole. We have good sustainability credentials, which help us to do that and we  want to do more. Our Director of Sustainability, Rachel McEwen is here with us today.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: SSE's third key strength also relates to business sustainability. It's our commitment to discipline when it comes to  financial and risk management. Gregor will say more about this later, but amongst other things it means a clear  commitment to a strong balance sheet, effective cash flow management, diverse funding sources, agility in raising  capital, maintaining optionality and a disciplined approach to capital allocation, investment and acquisitions. SSE's  capacity to generate earnings is founded on this discipline which will be maintained in the future. SSE is focused  on core markets, the energy sector complex, the interdependencies are significant and with significant ambiguity  and change. This requires a clear management focus, which in turn generates greater experience of an insight  into our chosen markets. That supports effective disciplined and timely decision making. We've demonstrated that  in the past and it will be equally important in the future. Our market focus is the UK and Ireland and it will remain  so. But although we don't have any plans in the pipeline for now, we are open to extending to other markets our  core competencies in areas such as renewables.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: The first strength I see in SSE is our relentless focus on operational efficiency, now becoming a broader culture of  continuous improvement; it's bringing clear benefits. For example later, you'll hear how our Network's team is  building a leadership position in influencing and preparing for the flexibility of evolution and transition to a smarter  electricity system. And you'll hear how our generation team is going to take steps to enhance the value derived  from some of our oldest assets, the hydroelectric schemes in Scotland.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: The quality, nature and value of our assets is a key advantage since the acquisition of Airtricity in March 2008,  we've invested £15 billion across the SSE Group. This has delivered the value, range and quality of the asset  base that we have today. We have ownership interest in five economically regulated energy networks, four  classes of renewable energy capacity including pump storage and three main types of thermal generation. This is  a prized collection of assets to which we are continuing to add. It is complemented by an extensive telecoms  network, two B2B businesses, an interesting gas production and gas storage.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: In the fast-changing sector, these assets present us with a strong pipeline of future opportunities for future value  creation. The two examples bring to mind; distribution networks are central to the fight against climate change,  connecting clean energy, supporting electrification of transport and facilitating change of system operators at  regional and local level. From the point of view of the country as a whole, the DNO is a by far better place than  any possible alternative to deliver change with the focus, speed and efficiency that electricity customers deserve.  And, in generation, we hold valuable prospects for each technology type and especially offshore wind where the  market continues to grow.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: We're taking active steps to be in a strong position to compete in the changing environment. It's now 14 years  since our venture with two Canadian financial institutions agreed to buy what is now SGN. The significant value  created in the time since reflects the enduring success of that partnership.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: So SSE is being renewed, building up on core strengths and competencies to meet the challenges and realize the  opportunities presented by the changing energy sector. Drawing on these strengths and competencies, the future  direction of SSE is clear. We will have a simple purpose to responsibly provide energy and related services  needed now and in the future.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Our vision is to be a leading provider of energy and related services in a low-carbon world and our strategy is  clear – to create value for shareholders and society from developing, owning and operating energy and related  infrastructure and services in a sustainable way.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: When it comes to the political debates about energy, we believe that our responsible approach to business, our  support for a low-carbon future, our focus on sustaining skilled jobs and our commitment to making a positive  economic and social contribution will stand us in very good stead. The financial objective of this strategy is to  remunerate shareholders' investments through paying dividends. We're pleased that today's increase in the full- year dividend to £0.947 is the 20th successive increase since SSE was formed in 1998. As we said in March, this  will be a year of transition for us to see. Nevertheless, we are keen to give shareholders as much clarity as  possible in this year of transition. Drawing on a range of forecast for RPI inflation, we intend to recommend a 3%  increase in full-year dividend for 2018, 2019, taking it to £0.975 per share. This is not subject to the timing of the  planned SSE Energy Services transaction or of the price cap bill.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: SSE is committed to remunerating shareholders' investments through paying sustainable dividends for the long  term. Our longstanding view is that dividend sustainability is based on the quality and nature of the operations and  assets from which our earnings are derived and the long-term financial outlook. We also believe the dividend  should be set at a level that allows for annual increases and that at least keeps pace with RPI inflation for the  period for which targets are set. The next period is the five years to 2023 when the current electricity distribution  price control comes to an end.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: So, through this year of transition and in anticipation of the completion of the retail transaction, the SSE team is  giving you a clear and sustainable five-year dividend plan. We are giving clarity in this time of transition, intending  to recommend a full-year dividend of £0.975 per share in 2019, planning to set the first post-transaction full-year  dividend at £0.80 per share in 2020, a level that reflects the changes in the SSE Group and is clearly sustainable,  and targeting annual full-year dividend growth that at least matches RPI inflation in each of the following three  years to 2023. This is a five-year plan that quite simply reflects the underlying quality and value of SSE's assets  and the earnings and cash flows they deliver. And in addition to it, those SSE shareholders with shares in the new  independent energy supplier will be able to benefit from the value created by that business in the years ahead.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: This morning, I've summarized the significant opportunities for SSE to create value in a changing energy system,  described how the SSE business model will evolve to seize those opportunities, set out the key strengths that I  believe will enable SSE to seize the opportunities and create value for shareholders and society and emphasize  our commitment to remunerating the shareholders' investment through paying dividends with a clear and  sustainable five-year plan out to 2023. We're fully aware of the challenges the energy sector faces but the  opportunities are there to be taken. In SSE, we have the strengths that are significant, opportunities that are  excellent and a dividend focus that is enduring.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Total exceptional charges were £213.3 million, a significant proportion relates to the gas production and retail  businesses. In Gas Production, a net impairment charge of a £104.7 million was recognized. This was driven  mainly by the latest annual independent reserves report. It takes account of all the technical and economic  variables and estimates, including current price projections for the Greater Laggan and Bacton fields. These  charges were slightly offset by reversal of previous exceptional impairments on the ECA field following an  increased estimation of hydrocarbon reserves in that field.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: The results for individual businesses are also in-line with what we set out in March. In Wholesale, operating profit  rose by 26.8% to £652.4 million, mainly through improved performance in EPM and Generation, aided by higher  electricity output from gas and renewable plant. Within this, renewable capacity has increased through sustained  investment; helping to deliver a 21.3% increase in adjusted operating profit from renewables to £374.9 million.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: In Retail, there was a relatively small fall in operating profit of 4.6% to £402.8 million. GB household energy  supply profit was similar to last year's but there was a decline in Business Energy which was offset by a recovery  in performance in Enterprise. Within Retail total £278.7 million is attributable to the SSE Energy Services  business that is subject of the planned transaction. That compares with £373.5 million a year ago.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: As you know, we increased electricity prices last year to reflect rising non-energy costs. We also secured  efficiency savings. These will offset the customer current losses and price caps for certain customer groups.  Overall, however, the financial performance of the business was robust.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: This is a year of transition for SSE and it's been clear for some time that it will present some challenges and some  uncertainties. Across the Networks segment, we expect adjusted operating profit to increase by a mid-single digit  percentage. In Wholesale, we've had to deal with the usual uncertainties associated with markets, plant and the  weather. And adjusted operating profit will also be affected by the end of – in the money power purchase  agreements. In addition, renewable energy output is forward-hedged at a price lower than in 2017-2018.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: In addition, the timing of the key SSE Energy Services developments and their impact on our financial results is  not certain. Nevertheless, we're keen to give shareholders as much clarity as possible on the dividend over the  next five years, starting with this year of transition. That's why we said we intend to deliver a full year dividend of  £0.975 for 2018-2019; that will represent a 3% increase.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Looking at 2019-2020, we've assessed the impact of the planned transaction and so we intend to deliver a full- year dividend of £0.80. This reflects the fact that SSE Energy Services business will not be contributing earnings  or cash flow to the SSE Group and is consistent with our goal of delivering from the reshaped SSE annual  increases in the dividend that at least keep pace with RPI inflation which we are targeting for the three years to  2023. This five-year plan supersedes our previous focus on dividend cover because it gives shareholders visibility  and clarity on the company's sustainable commitment to the dividend for the years to come.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: We believe this is a clear, responsible and sustainable approach to the dividend as we reshape the SSE Group  for the future. It's worth putting in context. EBITDA position from the core businesses of renewables and regulated  networks and dividends from SGN is strong. It's supplemented by the other businesses remaining within the SSE  Group.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: If from that, you take tax, interest, typical maintenance CapEx and cash payments based on an ETP dividend,  there remains significant headroom to support disciplined investment for growth. This underlines the extent to  which our dividend plan is sustainable. It was through our disciplined strategic investment in regulated networks  and renewables that we started the transformation of the SSE Group a decade ago.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: This transformation is supporting our earnings on our five-year dividend plan. Excluding SGN, we've invested £15  billion across the SSE Group since 2008; around £11 billion of this was in regulated electricity networks and  renewables.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: In 2008, including pump storage, we had 2.4 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity in operation, that's now 50%  greater at 3.7 gigawatts and delivering EBITDA of £692 million in the last financial year.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Also in 2008, we had announced electricity networks RAV of £2.7 billion that's more than doubled to over £6  billion and delivering EBITDA of £894 million in the last financial year. Supported by excellence in operations,  we've delivered a new modern asset base that creates long-term value for shareholders and society. It's an asset  base that has been expanded, particularly rapidly in recent years. It means SSE as an earnings engine and cash  flow capability that enables us to deliver our five-year dividend plan.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: In 2017-2018, we invested over £1.5 billion across the SSE Group with around 70% of this on regulated networks  and renewables, building on a decade's work since the acquisition of Airtricity. That work is continuing and in this  new financial year, we expect to invest around £1.7 billion, with around two-thirds of that in regulated networks  and renewables. By 2020, our unique and diverse portfolio of renewables will comprise over 4.2 gigawatts of  capacity, capable of generating around 12 terawatts of electricity per annum in a typical year.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Based on an electricity price of £45 per megawatt and a raw price of £50 per megawatt hour, that would earn an  EBITDA of around £800 million. A five-year CapEx plan to 2023 includes £1.3 billion investment in renewables  and assumes the joint ventures in which SSE is involved, are successful in securing some CFD contracts for  additional offshore wind capacity.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: For the purpose of our CapEx plan, we've made a prudent assumption that the SSE will add 1 gigawatt of  additional project-financed offshore wind capacity by 2023. This would increase our renewable generation output  to almost 16 terawatt hours by 2024.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Over the next five years, we expect to invest around £2.8 billion in our electricity networks. This includes the  forecast pipeline investment of around £1.2 billion in Transmission. This should help take our electricity and gas  [ph] tariff (00:30:12) from around £8.3 billion at March 2018 to around £10 billion in 2023. And over that period, we  expect our Networks business' EBIT contribution to average around £800 million a year. This is a very strong  asset base from which to deliver dividends.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: We're currently expecting capital on investment spend to total around £6 billion across the five years to March  2023, giving an annual average of £1.2 billion across the period. That compares with an average of £1.6 billion in  the last five years. Regulated networks and renewables should account for around 70% of this. And as you would  expect, the CapEx is weighted more towards the first half of the period than the second. The CapEx investment  total includes £1.7 billion planned in the current year and around £1.3 billion planned for the next, although this is  obviously subject to change. Around 80% of the £6 billion is committed as well as regulated networks and  renewables investment, it includes an additional multifuel plant and a new type of high-efficiency gas plant we  have decided to build at Keadby. We invest around £350 million in the project with a substantial proportion of the  financial exposure deferred until the plant is operational.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: The first quality is optionality. Regulated networks and renewables are core to the reshaped SSE and flexible  thermal generation is a natural complement to our renewables business. We have a significant number of options  that are not currently in our five-year plan. I've always said that optionality is key to our business model.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: But our other businesses such as Gas Production, Enterprise, Business Energy and Electricity benefit from direct  and indirect synergies, and provide us with options as the energy sector and energy provision itself evolves.  These businesses generated an EBITDA of over £310 million last year, and around 50% of that was in Gas  Production. We don't intend to acquire any more assets in Gas Production, but we are prepared to invest further  in those we already have if the prospects for returns are good enough.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: The third is discipline, as well as discipline in financial and risk management. This means be prepared to take  tough strategic decisions to make sure that the SSE Group and the businesses within it have the best platform for  success. We did it with the acquisition of Airtricity a decade ago, and we're doing it again with the planned Energy  Services transaction.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Optionality, agility and discipline are important qualities in financing SSE. Ability to raise funds at competitive rates  is fundamental to investment, and we again showed in the last financial year. In August, we issued the biggest  evergreen bond by UK company and the first of its kind issued by a UK-headquartered energy company. That  showed SSE's commitment to sustainability, responsibility and to maintaining a strong balance sheet and strong  market rating, allowing the €600 million of funding to be secured at just under 1%. This takes our total fundraising  over the last six years, including hybrid capital and term loans, to more than £7.5 billion. Excluding hybrids, our  average debt maturity now stands at 7.9 years. The reshaping of our hybrid debt means that coupons in 2018- 2019 will fall to £77 million from £128 million in the previous year.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Our proposition to shareholders is clear. In addition to creating a new independent energy supplier with significant  potential for value creation, we are targeting a full-year dividend of £0.975 for 2018-2019, regardless of the key  unknowns in the Retail business, committing to remunerating shareholders' investment through paying dividends  with new targets for up to 2023, building that dividend on a business with earnings from regulated networks and  renewables at its core. Confident of investment opportunities totaling around £6 billion over the next five years,  but disciplined in investment decision making and focused on robust financial management with robust credit  ratios.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Reshaping SSE is right for customers and right for investors. The SSE of the future will be a leading energy and  infrastructure company. It will develop on and operate energy and related infrastructure and services in a  sustainable way, and I'm confident it will create significant value for society and for shareholders in the year to  come. Thank you.

texts.speaker: Deepa Venkateswaran
texts.profession: Analyst, Sanford C. Bernstein Ltd.
texts.text: And the second question that I have is, really when you account for this project, financed projects in your CapEx  plan for offshore wind on the EBITDA side, do you include the contribution on a net income level for those or is it  kind of full your portion of the EBITDA and then you account for the project finance tax and interest separately?  Thank you.

texts.text: It's Mark Freshney from Credit Suisse. Two questions. Firstly, a large chunk of the CapEx and EBITDA growth  seems to come from renewables. What kind of competitive advantage do you have in these auctions  and why is it that you're so confident that you can find these projects?

texts.speaker: Mark Freshney
texts.profession: Analyst, Credit Suisse Securities (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: And secondly on the Gas Production, if I may. It seems that you've written down the Greater Laggan Area assets  in the three years that you've owned them. texts.text: Sure. Okay. Well, the CapEx, we obviously have significant growth in the Networks business in CapEx as well  going forward and we have significant opportunities as well, which aren't in those plans from things like other –  some of the other [ph] Ireland (00:46:20) and some other reinforcements. All of which will potentially be driven  from decarbonization and expansion of renewables in Scotland whoever build those projects. I think in relation to  the specific projects, we have, I think, particularly attractive assets in terms of their location, in terms of their size  and, therefore, their ability to essentially have those costs to generate those assets that are out there and we  have quite a widespread of those and we've obviously got Viking as well. And over in Ireland, we've got an  attractive asset there in too.

texts.speaker: Alistair Phillips-Davies
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: I think is there the write-down is a result of a technical evaluation, which people do. It can be quite prudent at  times. We've obviously got other assets in the portfolio where we found more gas. You can't always write them  up. It tends to be a one-way process, unless you've already written them down previously. So while it's  disappointing that those are there, I still think that business is performing strongly. As Greg will tell you, that's over  £160 million of EBITDA coming out of that business in the year that's gone and I think the Greater Laggan Area  continues to have significant opportunities for infill wells, which will access the rest of the gap and indeed for  putting wells nearby. And we saw in the latest round of licensing where a number of people picked up licenses in  that area, including both Shell and BP obviously expressing significant confidence in the west of Shetland Area is  having potential for the future.

texts.speaker: Gregor Alexander
texts.profession: Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Okay, [indiscernible] (00:50:03). I mean in terms of the dividend, I think we've been very consistent over the last  two or three years talking about not just about earnings but the quality of our assets. So, the growth in the RAV,  growth in the renewables, asset base as well supports our dividend. We know we'll be precise in cash flow  metrics. What we've done is we've looked at our five-year plan. We've looked at what's sustainable that's why  we've offered the £97.5 for the first year and £80 for 2019, 2020, then RPI dated 2023. We think that's more than  sustainable within our business model and we believe that having that plan and that visibility for shareholders is  important with having specific metrics.

texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley
texts.text: Thank you. It's Nick Ashworth, Morgan Stanley. Two questions from me. Firstly on the dividend and the ATP. You  set it – you set the profile through to 2023, which is through RIIO-T2, but you stop short of electricity distribution.  Assume – you've always had to make assumptions around what you expect in T2 for the dividend. If you assume  similar for electricity distribution that you're still comfortable with growing that ATP from 2020 onwards, so I guess  it's a question around why you didn't talk about 2024 given that?

texts.speaker: Nicholas J. Ashworth
texts.profession: Analyst, Morgan Stanley
texts.text: And then, secondly, just on the CapEx, you've talked about £6 billion over the next five years. In the statement,  there's a lot of options and potential CapEx and come out on top of that, I think, this heading towards £2.5 billion  in transmission potentially. What sort of flexibility – going back to the previous question, what sort of flexibility on the  balance sheet is there in the early 2020s? Could you keep CapEx in the £1.2 billion to £1.5 billion range through  to 2023 if need be for these things came through?

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Director, SSE Plc
texts.text: Give it a year or 18 months, we'll know a lot more about CfD auctions. We'll see more needs cases going in from  Colin and his team on big transmission assets and we'll probably have more feedback from Ofgem on how they  feel about those needs cases. So I think for us it was just giving a lot of visibility that hopefully gave comfort to  people about how we feel about the business now as we go through a big transition and as we go through what  may be some fairly turbulent times in terms of big changes in the energy sector. But there's no lack of confidence  beyond that, if I can put it that way.  Gregor Alexander  Executive Director & Finance Director, SSE Plc  A  Just on your CapEx and flexibility, £6 billion is not a straight read across to previous spend that we've been doing  at £1.5 billion a year. And if the returns aren't there then we wouldn't incur that CapEx.

texts.profession: you get given a mic say who you are and where you come from. Ian do you want to get a mic?

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj

texts.speaker: Jouko Karvinen
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj
texts.text: One, if you look at the track record of Renewable Packaging, but also especially when we get Montes del Plata up  and running, Biomaterials, those businesses need to grow and grow profitably. And I don't want them to be  slowed down by the reality on the other side, where we have lots of issues in the market and obviously, issues also  with the fixed cost ratios and so forth and so on.

texts.speaker: Jouko Karvinen
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj
texts.text: If we move on to slide nine. Karl, after his relatively short time as the CFO of the company, will now take over  almost 60% of the company revenue. texts.speaker: Jouko Karvinen
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj
texts.text: We've also done, not just waiting for something, but we've tried to reduce the time in the past 9 months to 12  months to get more ready, mitigate issues, risks, and so forth. One, it gives a better chance of making the right choices  and it also gives us speed when the time comes to hit the ground running, so to say.

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj
texts.text: Page 12, different presentation, but same story. The delta between the two curves, what does it say? What it's  saying that we are rebuilding the company. texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj

texts.speaker: Seppo Matti Parvi
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Stora Enso Oyj

texts.text: The bigger issue was the €40 million in temporary operational challenges and that is basically six mills. texts.speaker: Karl-Henrik Sundström
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj
texts.text: In conjunction with our fourth quarter report, we also issued a press release and it's referred to in the end the  report, and that is what we call a profit protection program to strengthen the competitiveness of Stora Enso that  has been launched. And the reason for it is that we have seen cost increases and we see cost increases in the  fourth quarter, especially continuing to the first quarter especially in the areas of wood, chemicals, and logistics.  And yes, it take one number here. The wood costs are €50 million higher we expect in Q1 2019 versus Q1 2018.  We are also reducing the CapEx by €50 million from the previously announced guidance of CapEx for the full year  of 2019. The reason is also that we are entering into a more unsecured future and we want to be proactive, first of  all, to get the competitiveness back and fighting back the cost and secondly compare – be prepared if unexpected  events are happening because right now the macro situation quite unpredictable.

texts.speaker: Karl-Henrik Sundström
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj
texts.text: This in the first phase includes that we are closing down – are planning to close down the PM6 in Imatra. texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Stora Enso Oyj

texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SA

We are more major-country exposed and at the same time, we are driving investment to  deploy this business in other geographies. So to answer your question, some of the major countries, they are not at  the best of the economic performance. So therefore, the margin on the planning was under pressure and at the  same time, we are investing in integration teams, in specialized teams in new geographies and that weighs on the  margin. But if you look at the total margin we do with our customers in the Buildings area, we are one of the  largest players in the building environment – in the active part of the building environment in the world.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SA
texts.text: The second point is that we have respect to other players also probably less exposed to the U.S. The U.S. has been  dynamic in Industry in the first half. So, what are we doing? We are working to launch to the planned structure,  which is our platform of integration for end-user automation, for manufacturing automation, including the very  big component of energy management. So, it's a fully integrated platform. It's going to take some time before it is  deployed. I'm sure in ourselves. And we are investing also in North America to make sure that we grow our market  share in that part of the world.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SA
texts.text: The second, on the IT performance, I think one of the major reasons is coming from the very good results of what  we do in the data center space, which is more and more asking for easy-to-install, quick-to-install, quick-to- commission full solutions. And we're probably the only player able to respond of the full system from the delivery  of energy from the grid till the servers in the data center. We supply everything guaranteed by Schneider, medium  voltage, low voltage, transfer switch, all the white space, all the security of the building, all the thermal control of  the building, all of this into one software repository.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SA
texts.text: On – for an industry which is dealing with very critical missions and with big responsibilities, this has a  tremendous value. Not only we ensure it during the commissioning of the system, but we guarantee the reliability.  And remember that reliability remains a key value of this market, all over the lifecycle of the data center, because  we have an unmatchable network for services helping our customers wherever they are in the world. So, this has  driven the performance in H1 and, I would say, across the past year, creating a real difference on this part of the  market. And this market is going on – through major evolutions, the move to the cloud, the collocation, needs to  review, revisit many of the data centers, many of the installations, plus the pressure on energy in many cases,  price of energy, makes people privilege our Solutions which are very energy-efficient.

texts.profession: Analyst, JPMorgan Securities Plc
texts.text: Yeah. Good morning, everybody. I have two questions, please. texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SA
texts.text: Okay. On the Buildings business, the impact of public spending, we are referring in – to the U.S. when we are  mentioning that. On one side, you've got two aspects; public spending can affect the equipment of new buildings  and probably there is less – what we mean is that there is less on this side because public spending is diminishing.  On the other side, we see the other kind of attitude of people being faced – been facing bill increases and wanting  to decrease their costs, which creates an opportunity for our technology. But also when you are speaking about  that, you speak a lot about performance contracting. And then performance contracting is made of projects that  some quarters are better than others from that point of view. I never said let's see in the world some positive  trends from energy efficiency, performance contracting point of view.  Clearly, you see, while the price of energy has really increased in a very strong manner last year, which is raising  numbers of questions for many countries. And we've seen countries like Japan, like Germany going through  energy transitions which are quite ambitious for different reasons or for reasons which are partially linked. And  on – from that point of view, the recent change of government in France is probably good news for us because the  new government has decided to go more for efficiency, for energy efficiency, for renewables, and this implies the  usage of most of the technologies that we have been developing in the past 10 years. So, we have certainly a lot to  offer into the new orientation of France, for instance. And this is happening in other countries; no need to remind  you that Europe today is not complaining – complying with its 2020 objectives of carbon emission reduction but  more so of energy efficiency across borders, and these will need to be addressed.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: President & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SA
texts.text: Yeah. On the Solutions, we say that increasing our margin by 2% is an objective over three years. So, it's not  certainly achieved in one first half. So, it's something that we are driving across the quarters. We are – I'm  optimistic because I see a lot of mastery, a lot of energy spending, understanding better what we are doing, in  pricing better, in evaluating better, in managing also the pricing over the duration of the project. So, we see  something – an objective that I feel confident we are going to be in a position to achieve. But certainly, we've not

texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SA

texts.text: Moving on to page 9 and having a look at geographies. Well, West Europe confirms its rebound, and actually Q2  is at plus 3%. So, we benefit from everything we know, low euro, low interest rates and low prices of fossil energy,  which are helping the investment of the zone. U.S. and North America are back to positive in an environment  where construction is doing well, technology is doing well. But we know that industry is impacted particularly by oil  and gas and the high level of dollar.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Second part of the work that we do in cost is on support function cost where we generate in H1 €120 million gross  SFC savings on the top of the €300 million last year. Remind you that we have a commitment to deliver €300  million on the total of 2016 and 2017. A lot of work on the simplification of our business organization and regional  organization. A lot of work on putting together some business which were separate before. A lot of work R&D  efficiency, mutualization of the back office which is something we have started a long time ago. So, all of this,  again, is carrying results in our environment.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: On the next slide, 13, some examples of some products that were launched in H1 around this architecture. There  are some very foundational products in this slide. I want to mention Masterpact MTZ, which is a world-leading  product, which is the core of the low-voltage distribution. Well, MTZ is bringing unparalleled capacity of precision  one metering which make that customers don't have to equip their systems of supplementary accessories to  measure the characteristics of power. So, that's an incredible savings for people who have to control their process  on their energy. New launch of speed drives which are saving 30% to 70% of energy on motors and preserving  the mechanical assets. And complete renewal of our range of relays of protection, plus the launch of Galaxy VX,  which is our new range of UPS for large-scale datacenter and for industrial application.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: More launches in the field of automation platforms. Our BMS, Building Management System platform. TAS, which  combines together the control of process and energy. Microgrid controls, we are doing more and more microgrids,  not only in emerging countries, but also in mature countries. And our totally new system for datacenter operation  that is [ph] plugged on (18:49) at the next level, which is a level of the analytics to our cloud base structure and  software, which helps customers to manage their assets. On that level of analytics, there again you see a number  of new applications and analytics which help our customers to manage their installations.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So, this is about innovation and launches. Now I want to go into the detail of each business, starting by the major  business of Schneider, 45% of the group H1 revenues, which is Building & Partners. That goes from home  buildings such as all of low voltage, that goes also that pervades into industry and infrastructure. Well, very good  organic growth at plus 1.3%. In this business, we have been also selective with projects of building controls. So, if  you focus on the low voltage product parts, we have been actually growing quite well, I would say around 3% for  the total of the company on a worldwide scale, which is a great performance in a place which is our area of  excellence on a global scale.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Moving on to the next slide, 18, on Industry. Well, there again progress and continuous progress. Industry has  been impacted by weaker market and especially the collaterals of the oil and gas evolution. Q1 was at minus  2.3%, Q2 minus 1.2%, resulting minus 1.9%. Work on profitability, plus 40 bps in terms of adjusted EBITA. It  would have been 1.2 points before forex there again.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We had a good dynamic in Europe boosted by OEM markets. We are impacted in the U.S. by oil and gas and  strong dollar, which impacts OEM. We had a decline in China which remains a difficult market. Process  automation, actually, which is the legacy of Invensys, was slightly up in weak markets because it's impacted by oil  and gas particularly. But we kept benefiting from the revenue synergies and the cross-synergies of the integration  of Invensys.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: A quick look at a continuous focus on sustainable development with a lot of recognition of the commitment of  Schneider in this. Lots of progress. We are above the targets of our barometer which measures us against the  main things, with practically good performance in energy savings and development of circular economy within  Schneider.

texts.speaker: Emmanuel Babeau
texts.profession: Deputy Chief Executive Officer-Finance & Legal
texts.text: We keep managing to curve our SFC and decrease our SFC and create a leverage between the revenue  evolution and the SFC. Jean-Pascal has already largely detailed all the action that we are implementing on our  SFC to deliver this performance and, of course, we will continue to do so in the coming quarters.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Yeah. On software, Andreas, we have contrasted dynamics. We keep growing in software in H1, actually sales by  2%. But it's really contrasted between the part of the portfolio which is on oil and gas, which is under pressure for  what is upstream, and very good dynamics, actually, double digit, on things which are linked to discrete  automation. So, there's a repositioning on end markets which is happening.

texts.speaker: Emmanuel Babeau
texts.profession: Deputy Chief Executive Officer-Finance & Legal
texts.text: And regarding the SFC evolution, yeah, it's true that we are not exactly at the run rate of last year. Remember that  we have the €600 million target for a three-year SFC saving. We have done something like €300 million last year.  We have done €120 million this first half. So, you are at more than €400 million. We still have 18 months to go.  So, we believe that we are clearly going to deliver on this €600 million. And, of course, we make sure that we  continue to work on saving and efficiency together. But I think we are in line with our plans.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So, we are expecting that continuous recovery coming from a market which is kind of stabilizing through the  transition to the new normal of China. People are reevaluating their priorities but we see more direction now,  especially with the publication of the new plan. But a large part of what we do here is due to ourselves. There are  places where we have diminished our location resources. There are places where we have increased our  application of resources. So, when you look at what China does today, things like the push to a more green  society is all in our direction. And it's not about new construction. Very often, it's going back into previous  construction or previous industry or previous infrastructure and instrumenting or putting together the equipment in  those infrastructures to make them more energy-efficient and more sustainable.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: We have four business, and those business have two roles. They have to develop technologies that are serving  all the markets of Schneider. And what we report on this names of the business are technologies. So IT is Secure  Power on what we report in this name of IT are Secure Power technologies. Building, Low Voltage, and what we  report on the Building is Low-Voltage technologies. Infrastructure, Medium Voltage. On Industry, Industrial  Automation.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So you're going to hear me speaking more and more about Secure Power, about Low-Voltage, Medium Voltage  and Industrial Automation, we're going to [indiscernible] (09:58) that together over the next reporting, always  associating the two names, but be prepared that we're going to report in function of the thing that we count and  that we report.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: The thing that's really important to understand with Schneider is that our – we've built our company from the end  markets, but with design the growth model to be based on cross-selling. So we have four technologies, again,  Secure Power, Low-Voltage, Medium Voltage, that's combined together into a power energy management chain.  And then we've got one business, which is Industrial Automation that combine with energy management into  complete efficiency solutions.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So, the business, the technology leading the charge in building is a business of Philippe, here in the room, so it's  Low-Voltage. But when we sell one of low-voltage, we sell 25% to – 20% to 30% of other products into the same  package. And we do it normally with integrators and distributors that buy the whole package. So cross-selling in  this field is most of the time done by our distributors and our integrators.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: In data centers and networks, the key activity or the centerpoint activity is IT, but it brings 25% of other business  of Schneider, namely Low-Voltage and Medium Voltage. And those business today – and I'll come back on that  because data center is a great, great market of Schneider is growing double-digit, which means all application is  growing mid-single-digit, okay. And when you focus – in this business, you've got two parts. You've got the  products for distributed IT and you've got the data center part of the business. When you focus on data center, it's  almost 50-50. 50% IT technology, central power technology, and 50% Low-Voltage or Medium Voltage.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: In Industry and Infrastructure, you've got a double synergy, which is we sell Medium Voltage and Low-Voltage  together into integrated packages, right. And those combining into solution of efficiency. When you do a machine,  you don't do just the automation, you do the automation and powering the machine. When you do plant, that's a  key differentiator of Schneider, but by the way, most of our competitors are doing that, too. We sell, on one side,  automation, and we combine it with powering the plant. So that it's a combined efficiency solution. So 50-50  between Low-Voltage and Medium Voltage, and then 50-50 between Medium Voltage, Low-Voltage on  automation.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So projects represent roughly 40% of Schneider turnover and that the first place for cross-selling and the first form  of cross-selling. But 60% of the turnover at Schneider is happenings with network of integrators, and those  integrators need the full offer to supply their customers, mixing power, energy management and automation. And  you see here new products that we are launching in H1 that are going to directly to distributors and integrators of  all sort, supported by integrated digital tools that don't know any border between our technologies. We support all  of our technologies for same customer. And that generate the 4% organic growth that we've had in H1.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Plenty of new bricks of our EcoStruxure architecture, which says that today this represents – EcoStruxure sales  represent 45% of the sales of Schneider. Every product that we develop today has a place on the connection into  EcoStruxure. And EcoStruxure is made of six vertical architectures that combined together to serve the  customer's needs. So you've got a few examples here.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: And I would like to mention that customers are not really interested by technologies. They are interested by the  value that the convergence of energy automation on software provide, and you've got here, four examples where  this technology really mix in connectivity, edge controls, analytics, computing capability on the cloud, brings  significant value of efficiency and reliability to the customer. And what you see also is that every time, this  combines different technologies of Schneider.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Energy and Sustainability Services whereby we help customers to manage their demand and source the right  supply of energy. It's purely digital, it's all about connectivity, analytics and specialist bureau. EcoStruxure  machine, which is machine automation. Really a great success of

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Schneider, very significant part of our Industrial Automation business. EcoStruxure Grid, which is a smart grid,  where we are scoring number of wins. And Cloud and service providers segments, which is the most  sophisticated part of the data segments where we grow double-digit.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Provisions grow, again an exceptional for the [ph] fourth of this year (20:07) mid single-digit growth for Final  Distribution on the Wiring Devices. We are really accelerating in EcoStruxure power on Building, double-digit  growth of Low-Voltage in data centers, so our data center presence is a strong accelerator of this one, I'll detail on  that one. And we should – but it's a news of the night, we should have this year acquisition of ASCO that confirm  our position of world leader in power sources management.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Priorities, more partners, more products, more connectivity, and of course, this is a place of the highest or most  acute intensity in terms of pricing to cover the cost on the ForEx. Secure Power, that's one of the flagship  technologies of Schneider. We are here growing by 2% and I'm going to be a bit more detailed about that.  Decrease of margin on this first half are the reasons I was mentioning. Launch of our EcoStruxureIT base of  comparison on projects on destocking in Japan with the road map, yeah – as a road map.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: The second part of the business are data centers, which are mixing Secure Power and Low-Voltage and Medium  Voltage technologies, while our sales in data center are growing mid-single-digit in H1. So IT, low single-digit,  MV/LV sales in DC up double-digit.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: I want to make a quick zoom about data center. Data center has been for the past 10 years a very attractive  market for Schneider, and it keeps being so. So we grew mid-single-digit. What is important to understand is that  in data centers we sell €1.4 billion of IT, which drove to the permanent increase on development of our presence  in Low-Voltage and Medium Voltage. So we sell €800 million in that space. And our market share due to that in  Low-Voltage and Medium Voltage in datacenter is much higher than on the rest of the market. So it is a strategic  objective for us to keep developing on that segment, knowing that the technology evolution makes it more intense  in Low-Voltage and Medium Voltage as we go forward than in IT, but you absolutely need the IT infrastructure to  be relevant in that segment.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So we are growing in all four regions with a strong growth in China. We are performing extremely well with  machine manufactures with EcoStruxure machines growing double digit. Process automation is now back into  positive after this year was impacted by oil and gas. On software, we spoke about it, are up.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Point one, the product that we sell in bundle with low-voltage products to low-voltage partners and we have by far  the largest network of partners around the world. Second, services that we always deliver with the common theme  between Medium Voltage and Low-Voltage around the world, and that's one of the fastest growing business, and  the most profitable business we have at Schneider over the past years. And finally, EcoStruxure Grid, which is a  smart grid, which has been developing very satisfactorily, and it's typically another automation business.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: I'll finish the presentation by a very short review of our Planet & Society barometer; I won't speak very much  because we are ahead of our objective. Schneider is very committed to corporate social responsibility, actually at  the core of our strategy. We are beating all of our objectives here. This being said, and that was a pretty extensive  presentation, I hand over to Emmanuel for the financials.

texts.speaker: Emmanuel Babeau
texts.profession: Deputy Chief Executive Officer & Chief Financial Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: And at the same time, of course, we are taking all the conclusion of this improving environment and top line and  the effort that we need to make on utilization. So that means that we've been absolutely relentlessly working on  our program for SFC saving, almost €100 million of gross saving generated in H1. I can tell you we work 360  degree on the global function like finance, and – or we work on the real estate, for instance, we work on  optimizing the structure at the level of our operation. But I can tell you everybody is working on generating  simplification, efficiency, mutualization and that has been delivering in the first half, when we then intend to  continue.

texts.speaker: Emmanuel Babeau
texts.profession: Deputy Chief Executive Officer & Chief Financial Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: All right. So, that drives the gross profit of a bit more than €4.7 billion, up more than 4%. The SFC are, despite  ForEx still a bit below the €3 billion. And we have an adjusted EBITDA of €1.718 billion, it's up plus 8.3%  organically. Same ForEx, same scope. We are up plus 7%. Remember we have this three-year objective growing  4% to 7% organically on the adjusted EBITDA, where we are actually in the high-end of this range for the first half  and that is translating into a margin of 14.1% versus 13.5%, it's up plus 60 bps. The last year number have been  restated of the de-consolidation of the Solar business. So that's why versus a 13.3% that we published last year,  we have 20 bps more.

texts.speaker: Emmanuel Babeau
texts.profession: Deputy Chief Executive Officer & Chief Financial Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Income tax, the €361 million negative. This is a 26% average tax rate for the group. We are in the low-end of the  bracket that we initially gave for the year, which was 26% to 28%. So we are hopeful to be able to finish the year  in this lower-end of the bracket. Discontinued operation, that's the Solar business that we've been  deconsolidating, and it's for the vast majority of this amount, an impairment of the goodwill of the acquisition that  we have made, I think, in 2008 of the [indiscernible] (42:48) business on Solar.

texts.speaker: Amit Bhalla
texts.profession: Senior Vice President, Head of Investor Relations, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Thank you, Jean-Pascal. I think we'll spend maybe 15 minutes or so to discuss, of course, the acquisitions this  morning of Asco Power Technologies. So, like to invite up Philippe Delorme, the Head of our buildings Low- Voltage business.

texts.speaker: Philippe Delorme
texts.profession: EVP-Building & Information Technology, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So ASCO, maybe to tell you a bit, so ASCO is a leader in North America by transfer switch. And transfer switch is  something pretty simple. In many critical application, take data center or take hospital, you need to make sure that  you always have power on. So, you will have your connection to the grid, of course, that you will have some  backup power, could be in most of the case, gensets and you need the piece of technology to connect or to  switch sources from the grid when the grid has a problem, to that sources of energy which are mostly gensets,  and coordinate the different gensets together.

texts.speaker: Philippe Delorme
texts.profession: EVP-Building & Information Technology, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So alongside with transfer switch, a collection of other products, because when you switch sources, then you  need to coordinate the different gensets, that's what we call power control system. You need to test those  installation, especially in the case of hospital and the load banks, monitoring surge. Associated with that and that's  very good, they need a lot of services. So that our service team is attached to it, which by the way needs an  additional of a few products, higher pump controllers typically, actually to monitor the gensets, so it's a full, let's  say, set of capabilities, again, very strongly positioned in North America.

texts.speaker: Philippe Delorme
texts.profession: EVP-Building & Information Technology, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So what does it bring to Schneider? A few things and these are very simple. I'll elaborate a little bit with our  position worldwide, but it position Schneider as a global market leader in power source management, which again  is really critical in critical application. It enhance our capability in North America in the field of energy management  or really the core business of Schneider. Very strong complementarity with what we have in Low Voltage. Again,  in segments like healthcare, financial services, data centers, so places where today we see market growth. So,  it's really a key piece of technology that will complement our EcoStruxure power set of technology, which is the  backbone of Schneider Electric.

texts.speaker: Philippe Delorme
texts.profession: EVP-Building & Information Technology, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So, market positioning. Again, I told you, ASCO is today the leader in North America. You know that our business,  our Low Voltage business is very strongly associated with standards. So in North America, the market is ruled by  NEMA standards, where we have China rule by CCC standards, and then Europe, and let's say international rule  by IEC.

texts.speaker: Philippe Delorme
texts.profession: EVP-Building & Information Technology, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So, to give you an example – and maybe, before giving example, so last time we met in London, we've been  pretty detailed about EcoStruxure. Jean-Pascal was talking about different field of expertise within the different  domain of expertise in EcoStruxure. The biggest EcoStruxure we have is around power, which is again the  backbone, Medium Voltage, Low Voltage application. And really we see the transfer suites of the power source  management has been a very strong complement to our capability in EcoStruxure power, really in the field of  power availability.

texts.speaker: Philippe Delorme
texts.profession: EVP-Building & Information Technology, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So it allows our customer to have better power availability and then connect to the old suite of technology of  Schneider Electric with two components, Automatic Transfer Switch, again, something that will switch a source  from the grid to a genset, if you make it really simple; and by the way, doing this is really complicated. So, this is  why these guys have been doing that for 100 years. And associated to that, you need Power Control System,  which actually will coordinate the different gensets together. So these are the two central piece of technology, with  again, would happen in places where power is critical, healthcare, financial institution and data centers.

texts.speaker: Philippe Delorme
texts.profession: EVP-Building & Information Technology, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So in data centers, so Schneider has very strong capabilities, I mean, Jean-Pascal was talking about it. It's  creating very strong growth especially in Low- and Medium Voltage and associated with Secure Power. So you  see ATS and PCS, so we like acronym, Automatic Transfer Switch, Power Control System that is – let's say, or  that was probably the last line that we wanted to complement the full, full lineup of, let's say, perfect technology  for data center application. So this should reinforce us further in the field of data center, where we see a very  strong market traction.

texts.speaker: Philippe Delorme
texts.profession: EVP-Building & Information Technology, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: These offers are actually also very interesting in the context of the new energy landscape. We know renewable  developing pretty fast. That mean that transferring sources from different sources, whether renewable, genset and  the grid will happen more and more. And the Automatic Transfer Switch will be the key component to drive those  application, and for many of these customers, power is so critical that you want the switch application to be really  reliable and done by specialist. This is what ASCO bringing us alongside with the other capabilities we used to  have in Schneider Electric. So, good market trend, a great technology and a great combination to make it a great  business going forward.

texts.speaker: Emmanuel Babeau
texts.profession: Deputy Chief Executive Officer & Chief Financial Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: So, I'll start on the first one. So first of all ASCO is not purely electromechanical play, meaning there is electronic  and software associated to it, both in the Automatic Transfer Switch and in Power Control System. So that's a first  piece of answer. And the ASCO team has been actually working pretty hard on that. Now, this is where the  EcoStruxure power story kicks in, because a lot of the technology brought by Schneider at the edge in term of on- premise power monitoring and control application and cloud application to drive power quality and these kind of  things, are things on which ASCO was probably not fully prepared and where we see a very strong fit with what  we're brining with Schneider Electric.

texts.speaker: Emmanuel Babeau
texts.profession: Deputy Chief Executive Officer & Chief Financial Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Just to add on what Philippe is saying. First, we see a future where the management of source will become  critical. I mean, the old distribution was one source of power, maybe a security to it and then the consumption.  The future clearly will be done by multiplicity of sources to manage. So you're going to have solar batteries for  storage, line of distribution, especially when you're going to emerging countries, that line can be sometimes very  unreliable. You're going to have potentially a generator of things. So that part of the installation, especially, as  people go to micro grids, decentralized generation is becoming very, very central.

texts.speaker: Jean-Pascal Tricoire
texts.profession: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Schneider Electric SE
texts.text: Can I add to that, while you drive also double-digit growth of low-voltage, it's also very accretive for Schneider.
