texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Thank you, Karen, and good afternoon to everybody. I would like to make few observations on the market before  Simon runs through our financials and finally, a few words on our expectations for 2012 before we turn to your  questions. I'm pleased with these results. We show a higher than typical level of activity in the North Sea,  reflecting the improving market environment we are seeing as well as execution of work that was originally  scheduled for late 2011 and which due to poor weather condition has pushed into early 2012. In addition, we have  seen good levels of activity in West Africa and other business. So overall, a good set of results for this first quarter  in line with our expectation.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: So let's talk about the different markets. In the North Sea, which include the UK and Norwegian Seas, we have  started the year with a strong level of activity, higher than is typical for the first quarter. As I mentioned earlier, a  significant portion of which is work which was delayed in late 2011 due to adverse weather conditions, but these  results also reflect the improving market environment.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: The summer season, weather permitting, looks also very busy, but it's too early to know exactly what activity levels  will be for the first quarter. In 2012, we expect to complete most of the activity awarded with low margin in 2010  as well as executing newer vintage work which has been awarded with improved margin. So overall, we expect to  see an improvement in both top line and margin in the North Sea in 2012.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Moving to the Gulf of Mexico, we also start to see signs of an increased activity following the recommencement of  the award of drilling permits. We should see contracts award to the market in late 2012 and execution in late 2013  and 2014 in the markets which remain competitive.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Turning to Asia Pacific, we have a number of smaller projects in this region that are progressing. And we are in the  early stage of engineering and project management on the Gorgon project. Overall, 2012 will be a relatively quiet  year. Furthermore, we expect our joint venture, SapuraAcergy, to deliver a lower contribution in 2012, following  the rescheduling of the final offshore campaign of the Gumusut project into 2013.  Looking at this market in this region, the past 12 months have seen a number of large gas-driven projects in  Australia come to award. Although further awards are expected to come to market, especially in Australia and  Malaysia over the next 12 months, our approach is to remain selective on the project we tender to ensure that we  achieve the right return.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: We continue to see more opportunities ahead in traditional deep water in the Campos Basin as well as pre-salt  developments. In 2012, we expect to see further PLSV contract awards to the market, both for existing contracts  renewal and new vessels to be built in Brazil. More larger and big projects for pre-salt developments are likely to  come to contract award in 2012 and beyond with operation in 2014 and 2015. After which, a further run at tenders  for the next pre-salt development is expected to be issued by Petrobas in early 2013.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: So in summary, we have seen a continuation of the positive momentum that we talked about in March despite in  the past few days oil price remains robust. And a robust oil price and a rising tendering activity around the world  underpin order book momentum, all of which reinforces our view that the outlook for our industry remains very  positive. We continue to see growth opportunities in all our markets albeit at different pace, and we remain  focused on building quality backlog, ensuring that we maintain a disciplined approach for both risk and pricing  perspective.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: In the Northern Hemisphere and Life of Field Business Unit, first quarter revenue of $562 million decreased 16%,  reflecting lower levels of offshore project activity compared to the prior year. This was the main driver for  the fall in worldwide vessel utilization to 68% from an unseasonably high 79% in the prior year period.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you, Ricardo. Let us turn now to slide 15. I would like to offer some comments on the market condition we  are experiencing today and Subsea 7's position. The business environment remains challenging with reduced  client spending driven by the lower oil price. The timing of new contract awards to market remains highly  uncertain and tendering is increasingly competitive.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We're also well-placed to help our clients lower the overall cost of deepwater development, which is key to helping  them reach final investment decisions. For example, on several large projects, which are being presently tendered,  we have been working with our clients and our suppliers to identify cost-effective solution. Only a few companies  in our sector can take this approach, as it requires large engineering resources, access to state -of-the-art  technologies, as well as flexibility in resources and fleet management. This is a clear differentiator for Subsea 7.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Cost reduction measures are important to protect our business in the downturn and we are making good progress  in aligning our organization to the lower activity levels. We have already seen a reduction in our head count level  and personnel costs as a result of the actions taken so far and our fleet running costs are also decreasing. As the  year progresses, we expect to implement additional cost reduction measures. We will provide an update on this at  our second quarter earnings call.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Slide 17 summarizes our view on the near-term outlook. In the Northern Hemisphere and Life of Field Business  Units, mature field development in the North Sea has been particularly impacted by the low oil price, and as a  result, there have been a limited number of market awards expected in 2015. We are tendering for the Maria  project offshore Norway and there is a tendering activity on smaller awards in both the North Sea and the Gulf of  Mexico, but the environment remains highly competitive.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Life of Field activity is expected to increase in the second quarter, helped by the seasonal uptick as the weather  improves in the North Sea, while i-Tech activity is expected to remain steady. In the Southern Hemisphere and  Global Projects Business Unit, there are still several large project awards under negotiation, although progress has   been slow and the timing of awards remains highly uncertain.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: To give you some example, I mean, some of the larger awards we have tendered for include the West Nile Delta  offshore Egypt. texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: To sum up, on slide 18, Subsea 7  has made a solid start to the year with growth in adjusted EBITDA, despite the  difficult market environment, reflecting operational performance. texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: The long-term fundamentals for deepwater oil remain intact and we would be ready to react when market activity  picks up. Additional measures will also have to be implemented and will be implemented while maintaining our core  strengths and competitive differentiation.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: To conclude, Subsea 7 is a leading oil service provider with top tier capability. Our expertise and experience e nable  us to help our clients find and execute the right solution at all points in the cycle.

texts.profession: Morgan Stanley & Co. International Plc

texts.profession: Joh. Berenberg, Gossler & Co. KG (United Kingdom)

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Y eah. We are not in a position to comment on a project-by-project basis. texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: The challenging industry conditions have not changed since we spoke to you in March. The timing of new awards  to market is still uncertain as clients continue to limit investments in major new self-developments, due to the oil  price environment.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In the North Sea, offshore activity levels and vessel utilization were low, reflecting the decline in activity resulting  from the low oil price, as well as seasonal weather conditions. texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Offshore Brazil, we completed the BC-10 project; and our newest PLSV, Seven Rio, started her long-term day-rate  contract, as planned. We achieved high levels of vessel utilization for all our PLSVs working o ffshore Brazil.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: We do not expect to sustain the hemisphere's margin at this level, because the mix of early stage to near - completed projects will change overtime. texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you, Ricardo. Let's turn now to slide 14. We are delivering solutions for our clients, but are lowering the  cost of development and enabling projects to progress at the lower oil price.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Moving to slide 15, I would like to share with you some details on three projects that illustrates the changes we are  driving to reduce costs.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Firstly, West Nile Delta Phase I, a fast-track domestic gas project offshore Egypt. Our longstanding relationship  with the client supported better ways to work together; it eliminated unnecessary administration and reduced  man hours. In addition, numerous innovative engineering ideas were implemented. One example: one cost saving  we identified was a change to the PLT protection cover design to reduce its weight and enable hourly access. I  could list a number of other examples.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In 2015, we launched a cost reduction program and resizing program to reduce the capacity and cost of our fleet  and workforce. This program was successfully completed in the first quarter of 2016, and, as I mentioned earlier,  we are already seeing the financial benefits in our reported results.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: The market outlook has not changed, with many projects pushed to the right, despite the progress we are making  to lower the cost of the projects. As a result, we will be implementing additional cost reduction measures in 2016.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We remain focused on our long-term strategic objective, and our cost reduction measures reflect this.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In the northern hemisphere and life-of-field business units, the market-wide cost challenge in the North Sea  remains. Improving weather conditions are expected to result in better utilization and activity levels over the  second and third quarter.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Our joint venture, SHL, remains well positioned to capture additional work in the renewables sector.

texts.speaker: Mukhtar Garadaghi
texts.profession: Citigroup Global Markets Ltd.
texts.text: My second question is on SHL. Could you just quantify the opportunity there as well, I mean, in terms of these  offshore renewables projects? How – basically, any color on the outlook for that business.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Regarding SHL, I mean, SHL is a joint venture that we have with some financial partners. We've been quite  successful over the last couple of years, both in renewables, but also oil and gas activities. We see some activity,  middle size or larger projects, as a possible opportunity for SHL, so we will continue to pursue these opportunities  and support SHL, as required.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer
texts.text: On the West Nile Delta, we're a shade under 20% complete, and we've done engineering procurement and we have  a lot of heavy duty fabrication ongoing in the country at the moment; and the main offshor e slopes will kick off in  quarter 3 and quarter 4 for that project.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Regarding your question on North Sea and, moderate speaking, on revenue, I mean, what we are seeing in the  North Sea, the seasonal effect that we see every year due to weather of – on the activity. But there is also an impact  from a lower level of activity, due to the oil price. So one cannot say it's only the seasonal effect. We see more  activity in Q2, Q3, but there is still impact on the lower market condition.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer
texts.text: Well, I certainly think with the relationship between procurement and our project total value on EPIC hasn't  changed. The relevant cost components of each has, but the relative split between them is about the same.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer
texts.text: In Subsea 7  world today, we have less large EPIC projects going through than we did a year or two ago, but that's  how the procurement number comes down.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Mick, we've touched on that a fair amount in previous calls. I think we've talked about the target savings that we  were hoping to get as a result of our recycling exercise in 2015.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: So I would say that we have achieved and potentially exceeded our targets in terms of our internal cost base. But,  this being said, activity still continues to be precarious and we are certainly not resting on our laurels. We're  targeting everything we can to continue achieving further reductions.

texts.speaker: Daniel Butcher
texts.profession: JPMorgan Securities Plc
texts.text: Thanks, gents. Actually, one of my questions was just asked then. texts.profession: ABG Sundal Collier Norge ASA
texts.text: Good afternoon, guys. Two questions from me, please. You mentioned that the market outlook hasn't changed. texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: One of the important things about the tie-backs in to the environment is the differentiator of Subsea 7, and I  would just name two. The differentiator is to be able to propose lower cost solution, and John elaborated on that.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And the last point on tie-back, when we talk about priority on technology we see future – the market going to have  longer tie-back, long distance tie-back, and that's why we are focusing on technology which relates to this type of  challenges. texts.speaker: Morten Nystrøm
texts.profession: Nordea Bank Norge ASA (Broker)
texts.text: And a final question from me, if I may. Let's assume that the oil moves another $2 and $2.50, will this be a level  where oil companies eventually will start sanctioning projects? texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: I'm very encouraged with the discussions we have with our clients on what we can achieve together to reduce the  costs to make projects viable. But one of the drivers you mentioned is the cash flow management of the oil  operators, and I would let them answer on when they will be ready to actually change their approach; it relates to  dividend, it relates to a lot of things. So I can't really answer your questions, it's very difficult now.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: I mean, things are going in the right direction with projects are viable at the lower oil price. What is the strategy of  the oil company in terms of the timing of release of their cash and dividend versus investments is, I would say, up  to them to answer.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And just to conclude, the fundamental long-term outlook for deepwater and oil and gas remain intact. We are,  meanwhile, adapting to industry conditions. At the same time, we are staying focused on our strategic priorities.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Our industry has functioned well at low oil price in the past, and we can do so again in the future, I have no doubt  about that. And our ability to deliver projects at lower costs is the key differentiator for Subsea 7, and I think will  be an even higher key differentiator with the progress we are making in [indiscernible] (55:45) working and  technology.

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA

texts.profession: Analyst, Bank of America Merrill Lynch

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Looking ahead, we continue to expect a valuable recovery in market activity, with around 70% of non-sanctioned  offshore resources breaking even at the $50 to $60 oil price. texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA

texts.text: Our strategy to expand our presence in targeted geographies has continued successfully. Offshore UK, the Beatrice wind farm project is nearing  completion. 82 of the 84 foundation have been installed by the quarter-end, and the remaining two were installed  in July.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: The second cable-lay campaign is underway, using Seaway Aimery, and we should – and should be completed  before year-end. We have started offshore installation on the Borkum II wind farm project, offshore Germany.

texts.speaker: Ricardo Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Thank you, Jean, and good afternoon, everyone. Let's first look at the income statement highlights on slide 7.  Second quarter revenue of $1.2 billion was up 13% from the prior-year period. This reflected increased activity in  SURF and Conventional, mostly due to the execution of projects taken on with the ECS acquisition made at the  end of the second quarter last year. Revenue from i-Tech Services and Renewables and Heavy Lifting was lower  year-on-year with reduced activity levels in both business units.

texts.speaker: Ricardo Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Net operating income was $62 million, down from $163 million in the prior-year period. We have fewer SURF  projects in the final stages of completion and those projects we are currently executing were awarded with lower  margins. In addition, this is a reflection of our change in mix of activity as conventional projects in the Middle East  typically achieve lower margins than deepwater oil and gas projects in the other geographies.

texts.speaker: Ricardo Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Renewables and Heavy Lifting revenue was $257 million, a significant proportion of it's related to the Beatrice  project which neared completion with almost all the foundations installed by the end of the quarter. Renewables  net operating income was $5 million. Activity levels were lower than in the prior-year period as the Beatrice project  [ph] wind (00:13:49) down and there was insufficient transport and installation activity to fill the gaps between  scheduled offshore campaigns on the Beatrice and Borkum II projects.

texts.speaker: Ricardo Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Turning to slide 10. On the April 10, we completed the acquisition of Seaway Offshore Cables in a related party  transaction. The addition of cable-lay capability has increased our offering in renewables and help to de-risk our  EPCI services. We can now provide our clients with a full balance of plant service, meaning that we can do  everything in a single contract, except for installation of the wind turbine generators. The initial consideration of  $164 million was paid in the second quarter. This included $117 million related to the two vessels and associated  equipment. Excluding contracts awarded to SOC by Subsea 7's subsidiaries, we added $95 million to our order  backlog as a result of the transaction.

texts.speaker: Ricardo Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Turning to slide 12, I will conclude with our guidance, and how our expectations have evolved over the course of  the quarter. Our guidance for 2018 revenue and adjusted EBITDA percentage margin is unchanged from the first  quarter, and our view of the outcome for the year has not deteriorated in the period. Based on our firm backlog  and results year-to-date, we are confident that we will achieve 2018 revenue broadly in line with the level reported  in 2017. This includes a full year's contribution from the ECS acquisition, offset by lower expected revenues in  Renewables and Heavy Lifting, as the Beatrice wind farm project reaches completion.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Thank you, Ricardo. Turning now to slide 13. We aim to create sustainable value by supporting our clients across  the whole lifecycle of the field. We have delivered on this in the second quarter by investing in cable-lay capability  to extend our renewables offering for comprehensive balance of plant services. We are developing our  relationship with Schlumberger to evolve our Subsea integration alliance into a joint venture agreement offering  fully-integrated projects and Life of Field services. Our differentiated technology continue to drive better and more  efficient solutions and our pipeline bundles are set for another busy year.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Our investment in composite pipeline technology is expected to deliver significant cost and design advantage for  our clients in the years to come. I will take each of this in turn and start with our strategy for renewables on slide  14. Subsea 7 and SHL have been involved in the provision of transport and installation services for offshore wind  farms since 2009. Our capability and experience enable us to deliver safe and reliable project execution. Over the  last 10 years, we have installed hundreds of turbine foundation and lifted many jackets topside, substation and  Subsea structures.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Our recent investment in cable-lay capability position us in a leading balanced a plant for service provider able to  offer holistic EPCI solution as well as transport and installation services. We have a team of over 1,000  experienced people and four specialist vessels for the Renewables and Heavy Lifting market. By growing our  presence in renewables, we are enlarging our addressable market and adding structural growth. We are engaging  in the energy transition and positioning ourselves for future in with renewable energy resources are increasingly  important for society. Our experience in Renewables and Heavy Lifting as well as EPCI project delivery is helping  to lower the cost and risk associated with offshore wind farms developments worldwide.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Moving to slide 17, our technology initiatives are delivering good results targeted on areas that bring most value to  our clients. Our bundle technology has advanced a long way since the first bundle was installed in 1980. Our  bundles are enabling development of higher pressure and higher temperature for fields which were previously too  costly to [ph] proceed (00:25:46). We are continuously pushing the boundaries of this proprietary technology [ph]  just now our bundle (00:25:51) will be the longest and heaviest we have installed to-date.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Our bids are submitted with the right terms and condition and adequate contingency on a cash-positive basis. We  are seeing good levels of tendering activity and visibility of FID for the larger greenfield projects is improving, the  visibility of the FID and the larger greenfield project is improving. Offshore India, the Integrated 98/2 project for  ONGC is expected to be awarded to market in the second half of this year. Offshore Brazil, the Mero 1 project is  anticipated either in Q4 or Q1 and offshore Mozambique, the Golfinho project is likely to be awarded to market in  2019. Conventional project in the Middle East under the LTA with Saudi Aramco remain in focus and we continue  to tender for new awards.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: The long-term outlook for EPCI project in Renewables and Heavy Lifting is positive with tenders ongoing in  Taiwan, Europe and the U.S. So the first of EPCI wind farm project in Taiwan has been awarded to a competitor,  but there are other opportunities in the region that we continue to tender for. In Europe, some of the larger  renewable projects are taking longer than expected to be awarded due to changes in project ownership and  governmental approval schedule, but we are still confident this will come to market in due course.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: To give you some examples, three large EPCI wind farm projects in France and the UK which were initially  planned for execution in late 2019 and are now likely to be developed in 2020, early 2021. We are targeting  transport and installation work to utilize capacity in the near-term, but this will not be sufficient to compensate for  the delayed project. In i-Tech Services, the level of tendering has increased for spot work and the outlook for  utilization is improving. However, there are no large awards expected into market near-term and activity and  pricing remains relatively low.

texts.speaker: James Evans
texts.profession: Analyst, Exane Ltd.
texts.text: Yes. Good afternoon. Thank you for taking my questions. Just a couple from me. Firstly, I wondered if you could  talk a little bit about any areas you see for incremental investment into the business. You've always, [indiscernible]  (00:30:12) this has been your first priority for usage of cash. So post the SOC transaction, do you see any other  sort of attractive areas for investment over the next year, be in renewables or elsewhere?

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Thank you. Thank you, James. Regarding incremental investment, I mean we are always looking at opportunities  and we will address them, if they come and when they come. I would say, there are two kinds. It's the type of  investments that we've done in the past, like ECS. But it's also investment on new technology. And we intend to  look at potential investment on the new technology, which are complimentary with what we do. Our balance sheet  allow us to consider opportunities when they come.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: With the decrease of activity of PLSV, I mean we talked about the Phoenix stopping operation in August, we will  continue to downsize the operation there to match the level of activity, cost control obviously remain a priority.  And I would say that the integration of the ECS and SHL is well-advanced and we'll continue to come to continue  to be executed in the months to come in an efficient way that go also in the right direction to control costs.

texts.profession: Analyst, Macquarie Capital (Europe) Ltd.
texts.text: Hi. Two questions from me. texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Yeah I think, David, new market in Taiwan we're taking what we've done in Europe and moving it over to a  different part of the world. So, for us, also Taiwan takes assets halfway around the world  from where the main areas of play are in renewables. So, again we will just tune our offering in Taiwan in due  course, but we are still bidding the large cable packages that are available on the first package in Taiwan as well  as some other second phase opportunities that are coming.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: The other question I think was Sea Lion, maybe Ricardo, your question was really around what was happening  with the project finance-related opportunities. As part of that there have been some discussions about financing scenarios as well, maybe  Ricardo, you can cover what we've seen in the market about some of those type of questions.

texts.speaker: Kevin Roger
texts.profession: Analyst, Kepler Cheuvreux SA
texts.text: Yes. Hi. Good afternoon. Maybe if we can focus ourselves on the renewables segment for two questions, please,  because if I look at the margin on the renewable segment, it has been quite low for the past three quarters, so I  was wondering how should we think about it over the long-term, especially as this quarter your top line is  comparable to the Q3 2017, when you generate quite huge margin at [ph] close (00:42:31) 20%, but you are still  very [ph] low (00:42:34) this quarter. texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Yeah. I am going to let John answer specifically to your question, but I would say that we haven't changed our  view on renewable, I'm personally quite optimistic about renewable. It obviously has this, I mean, kind of timing of  projects, but nothing has changed in our view. We see more and more, I would say more and more momentum in  Europe, but also we mentioned Taiwan before. So it's [ph] growing (00:43:19) in the right direction. The question  is what happened in very short-term it doesn't change our long-term view on reviewable which is core to our  strategy. John, you want to...?

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Yeah. So Kevin, I think you know if we take the questions as you raise them. We've always said the renewables  has an element of political decision making involved in the process of sanctioning projects. We saw in France that  the subsidy regime was reviewed again by the government, but very quickly an agreement was reached with the  operators to do that. So again, we would expect the next phase of the French wind projects to come into the  market and be available for bidding.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: I don't think we need to go into the specifics of the margins, but we need to remember in oil and gas as well that  EPCI margins are lower than T&I margins because the EPCI type work brings in a lot of other procurement and  engineering related items. Also as well we need to remember that our Seaway business has a lot of T&I work  installing substations and [ph] such (00:46:17) like which fill in gaps between some of the larger projects. So for  us, it's a mixture of T&I work, which is short-term generally slightly better margins and then longer term EPCIs. So  for us, I think probably best to reflect at the end of this year, how are the renewables' business would look like and  I'll give you an ability then to take a view of how we see it.

texts.speaker: Anne Gjøen
texts.profession: Analyst, Svenska Handelsbanken AB (Norway)
texts.text: Yeah. Thank you for taking my question. I have also a question related to renewables on this T&I work. Is it  possible for you to comment on where we typically could see kind of margins when it's dominated by T&I work,  because I would assume that 2019 also could most likely be called a transition year in that business area, or is it  opportunities coming in that could suddenly turn also 2019 already?

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: I think you know as we said in the prepared words of Jean there, 2019 will be predominately a T&I year in our  renewables business. And that's how we will focus on 2019. We see that the larger EPCI contracts in France and  the UK because the change in ownership on one of the large fields in the UK should come into play in 2020 and  2021. So, we should think of 2019 and renewables as a T&I year predominantly.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Yes. I would also add something that one of the strengths of [ph] this thing (00:48:12) is the fact that in addition to  renewable the company is also in renewable in heavy lift and that can be combined with some other business of  Subsea 7 for some of the projects. And when you talk about T&I, I mean, the visibility is not as high as when you  talk about EPCI in terms of timing. So, we see what happened in 2019, things can pop up not at the last minute,  but basically can improve the situation.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: So, again I mean, if I want to summarize where we are overall, no change in our view of renewable, although  some of the projects of 2019 are postponed. But I mean I'm personally quite optimistic and bullish about this  business in the medium term. And then regarding the market of the oil and gas, the order intake that we've seen  in the industry is what we need to be able to see improvement of the margin in, in the middle term, so that's also  going in the, in the right direction. And as far as the Subsea 7 is concerned, I mean our focus on, on the cost and  our cost control, and our [ph] personnel controlling risk (00:49:24) which means that we are still tendering the jobs  in a very prudent way is the right thing to do and that's what we'll continue to do up to the end of the year. As we  mentioned before in terms of the guidance for 2018, no reason to change what we said before in the previous  quarter, so that's where we are.

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: I also mentioned earlier the possibility of a temporary slowdown in shallow-water conventional market in Nigeria.  This could mean somewhat less variation orders on existing commercial work, but it's too early to conclude.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Regarding West Africa, what is interesting about West Afric a is we're talking not only about the traditional area  where we've seen a lot of activity in the past, but new frontiers. So we're talking about now about East Africa with  new projects coming for the gas development of Anadarko and Eni in the years to come .

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Regarding the status of the project, the first buoy has been submerged to 235 meters, which is its final position,  and it's connected to the bottom. We are presently installing the permanent tethers.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: And then SHL, it's a seasonal operation, installation for renewable and for oil and gas. The results in Q4 will be  lower than Q3, because one of the two vessel will be in dry -dock and also, because of the seasonal effect of being in  – the winter period is a period where traditionally we have less operation than during the summer. So I'm  confident that the joint venture will continue, in the years to come, to deliver good results, but I would not  extrapolate the Q3 result to the year of 2014.

texts.speaker: Henry M. Tarr
texts.profession: Analyst, Goldman Sachs International
texts.text: Okay. Just another question then on the North Sea; why do you think the EPIC model is gaining tract ion there? Is  it likely to have an impact on, so the margins conceptually, I guess, we have a high procurement element in there?  And then with the market looking quite good, I guess you are actually reducing capacity next year in the region  when the opportunities look quite good. So if you could comment on that as well, please, that would be great?

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Y es. I mean regarding the EPIC project, first, there are more and more EPIC projec ts in the North Sea. It doesn't  mean that all the projects are done in EPIC, and in fact, the majority of the projects are still done with a [ph] land  firm or very (35:45) contract with our frame agreement. So EPIC represents a growing part, but it's not t he whole  market.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: But why are EPIC project very good for Subsea 7? It's because we have, for instance, a differentiator. There are not  many companies which can actually can provide this type of services and the number of the new competitors  definitely are not in the same position as we are to provide these EPIC projects.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Regarding the fact that we are moving assets outside of the North Sea, when the market is still good. First, the  Ocean on Guará-Lula is not something that I would do if I could avoid to do it; we have to complete the Guará - Lula project and the Seven Oceans is key, so it's one of the consequence of the Guará-Lula project, and it's  something we've been talking about for a while. The Skandi Acergy is going to Australia to execute the Gorgon  project with Chevron, which is a good project.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Thank you. I'm going to answer to your three last questions and then I will let Jo hn comment on the fleet.  Regarding Guará-Lula, the buoy and the riser installation are, in fact, embedded operation. You have to do both to  be able to look at the rest of the works. So the sequence of all this operation is very complex, but they go togethe r.  And the risers are installed by the Seven Oceans, that's why the Seven Oceans is staying a bit longer in Brazil. The  installation of a flexible riser from the buoy to the FPSO, et cetera, is a full responsibility of Petrobras. So it's  something which is not part of our scope of work and we have no accountability for that.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: In terms of the main Subsea 7  fleet, we will see the Rockwater 2 go into dock towards the back end of this quarter,  and we will also expect the Rockwater 1 to go into dock either at the back end of this quarter or the start of the  next quarter, depending on the workscope in the North Sea, and how that plays out towards the end of this  quarter.

texts.speaker: Fiona M. Maclean
texts.profession: Analyst, Merrill Lynch International (United Kingdom)
texts.text: Y es, thanks. I have two questions. Firstly, following on from the previous one, could you give us an idea of how  much dry-docking you expect to be coming out in 2014 versus this year? So I guess that's for John?.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: What we started to talk about in the first part of 2013 that we are seeing a number of projects being postponed by  the IOCs for all the reasons which could be the constraints of the supply chain, which could be some concerns that  they had on the cost escalation of the project with the price of oil between $90 and $110, which actually led them  to review the technical solution that they were considering for the project to work with the industry and with  Subsea 7  in some cases to try to identify the most cost-effective solutions through technology and other means.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Y es. The only things which has changed, but we have not seen concrete evidence of wha t was said, is some  operator in the North Sea, Statoil in particular as you know have been mentioning that they could reduce the scale  of some of their project as the project cost is escalating. But too early to say, but it's something that we need to  watch because we have now similar comments in the North Sea.

texts.speaker: Eirik Ronold Mathisen
texts.profession: Analyst, DNB Bank ASA (Broker)
texts.text: Okay. But we should expect most of the delta to come in the Africa region though?

texts.speaker: Eirik Ronold Mathisen
texts.profession: Analyst, DNB Bank ASA (Broker)
texts.text: So we should expect most of the delta in Q4 to come from the Africa and Gulf of Mexico region?

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Net operating income in the North Sea and Canada was adversely impacted by an $11 million provision relating to  lease costs on the building we recently vacated in Norway with the objective of reducing future administration  expenses. Lastly, the Corporate segment had net operating income of $10 million compared to $24 million in the  previous year period. The decline was primarily due to a reduced contribution from the Seaway Heavy Lifting joint  venture, caused mainly by lower renewables activity in the period.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you, Ricardo. Let's turn now to slide 13. The uncertainty of further timing of market awards on SURF  project that we have been speaking about all year continued in the third quarter. The oil price weakness that we  experienced throughout the third quarter adds to the uncertainty.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: While we are cautious on the near-term outlook for this territory, we should bear in mind that the longer-term  prospects remain good, particularly for development in the harsher climates of Norway and Eastern Canada.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Turning to slide 18, I would like to provide you with some tangible examples of leading technology we are  employing on major projects. It's clearly a differentiator for us. We are proud of track record in utilizing advanced  technology solution developed by us to help our clients achieve more competitive projects. As mentioned, we are  currently completing the Guará-Lula project where we're installing the last Steel Catenary Risers. This riser  includes the first reeled installation of Bubi mechanically lined pipe. But that doesn't stop there. We are also going  to be installing this pipe on the complex Aasta Hansteen development in North Norway in 2015. In both of these  examples the installation of the pipelines and risers, utilizing this technology, has been a key driver in the  commercial viability of the developments. We continue to work in collaboration with BUTTING to further develop  this pipe for reeled installation including high-strength steel options for ultra-deep water and higher pressure  application.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In addition to the increasing demand for corrosion resistant pipeline, the more significant technology requirement  for the development of the complex reservoirs encountered today is the requirement for high performance Pipe- in-Pipe solution. This includes the requirement to heat the product, and our efficient electrically heated-traced  flow line technology offers one of the most thermally efficient pipeline systems. We are offering this technology on  the last project we are tendering in West Africa and really believe that this technology is key for the commercial  viability of the project.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: And our Seaway Heavy Lifting Joint Venture installed the largest float-over wind-farm topside substation in 2014,  which is an example of technology developed in the oil and gas industry being successfully applied to the  renewable energy sector by our associate – Subsea 7, our partners with SHL.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Now regarding 2015, we are in discussion with our clients to understand their views on the impact of the recent  drop of the oil price. We feel that some of them are still assessing this new situation. Uncertainties on timing of  project awards to market we continue during the first quarter of the year in 2015 and in 2016. We note that the  market has projected a revenue decline for $0.57 in 2015. We have similar view.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer
texts.text: Yeah. So Mick, on the bigger assets such as the Borealis, she has a very busy season next year. She is presently in  the States at the moment. She then moves back to work in Africa and she will be finishing the year on Ghana work  for Tullow TEN towards the end of the year. So we have a reasonable workload for her, similarly with the Oceans.  Oceans will complete Guará-Lula going into Lianzi and then go up to do Aasta Hansteen. So again we have a  reasonable backlog on the big assets there. So, and as you can see things like the Skandi Acergy are coming back in  to do some work that we have in the contract in the North Sea with Martin Linge's next phase, Aasta Hansteen's  phases as well as some of the bundle instillation projects that we have coming ahead of us next year.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: What I would – I'm going to take the question on North Sea and then pass the micro to Ricardo, I can say it that  way. Regarding North Sea, I mean, one thing you have to remember that to some extent the portfolio of projects  that we have in the North Sea has changed, and we have some EPIC last projects, EPIC, which are successfully  being executed, like Martin Linge. But depending upon the [ph] POC (39:53) and depending upon the progress in  any given quarter, it can have an impact on when are the profits recognized at the bottom line, et cetera. So the  results of the North Sea are in line with expectation with a bit of a different portfolio of projects.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: When we talk about very large projects because the number of company, which can execute a large project is more  limited, there is a bit more room than there is on the small project into the environment. So we are seeing and we  will see in the months to come more pressure on margins on small, medium size projects in some geographical  area such as North Sea or Gulf of Mexico, for instance, where there is an active competition and more competition  than in some other places.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: The reason why we are cautious on comments on margin for 2015 is what I said in my introduction. What has  changed over the last two months or so is this evolution of the price of oil going down, and it's difficult today to  have a good grasp on the volume of activities that would be in addition to already signed scope of work on existing  projects as well as on small projects which will be awarded to the industry. That's why we remain a bit cautious,  but that doesn't change my comment about 2015 that we are starting 2015 on a very sound ground and that has to  be taken into account when we try to forecast when it happens.

texts.speaker: Frederik Lunde
texts.profession: Carnegie ASA
texts.text: And secondly, are you comfortable with your goodwill on the balance sheet in light of lower oil price and the drop  in revenue you expect next year?

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: I think we have indicated in the past that with our existing fleet, which could be downsized if we release more  vessels, our operating CapEx is on a yearly basis around $200 million, $250 million. That includes dry-docks and  expenses during dry-docks that we amortize. So that's the type of level we can probably go slightly below these  values, but that gives you a range.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: As far as goodwill is concerned going back to the second question you had, Frederik, we carry out our annual  goodwill impairment test every year in the fourth quarter. It's timing that's doing it at the moment because, as you  point out, there are a number of potential indicators of impairment, both in terms of the price of oil and in terms  of client CapEx decisions. We're in the process of running the numbers, which we do based on updated forecasts  and reassessments of the market. And we will be addressing that topic in our earnings call relating to the fourth  quarter. Obviously if there's any material adjustment that may arise, and I'm not saying that there will be. If there  is, we will notify our investors promptly.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Well, if you had asked me the question two months ago, I thought we would be more specific on 2015. What has  changed is this price of oil going from $100 to $80, which is raising questions, and we are in active discussion  with our clients. There are some unknown on that, on what's going to happen in terms of increase of work on  existing job as well as some small jobs awarded in the North Sea. So as soon as we know more, we'll talk a bit more  about it, but I think it's a bit premature. But as I said before, I mean, we have some base for 2015, and I'm  confident that we will continue to operate and perform on the project very well. So, that's all I can say on 2015.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: And also, yes, certain projects that will extend into those years. And that's as far as we can guide.  David J. Thomas  Credit Suisse Securities (Europe) Ltd.  Q  Okay, I accept that, thank you. Just to return to the first question then, can you just comment on whether you've  seen any change in behavior of your clients in the last three months as oil prices have come down by 25%,  particularly in this Gulf of Mexico question and the fact that you're saying you've had a number of conversations  with people. Have they actually continued those conversations or any indication of pushback?

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: No, I think it's very fair to say that the approach of the clients varies a lot depending upon who the client is, in  some cases take a more aggressive position on the risk sharing. Our position there hasn't changed. I mean, we  have our reference and we don't move our reference and we accept projects only with the right risk profile. And I  think what we are seeing is, we can be successful with our approach. We haven't seen specific problem in the Gulf  of Mexico. I think overall the relationship with the clients in Gulf of Mexico is very good, and there is no change of  attitude even now with the price of oil going down. And John?

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer
texts.text: Yeah. As Jean said in his commentary earlier where we have seen discussions with our clients is in Asia. We saw  Gendalo-Gehem where we were the lowest bidder, publicly declared lowest bidder, that project did not proceed.  We know that publicly there are discussions about gas prices in India, which have an impact on some of the Indian  projects. And it's been very clear in Norway that Statoil are slowing down any form of investments, and that's had  a knock-on to not just Statoil pure projects, but some other people as well. So, the Gulf of Mexico conversations  are continuing and we haven't seen any material change in those conversations.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: I mean, regarding Petrobras, what I was referring to is the number of FPSO which are going to be installed on the  pre-salt field. And the fact that you may remember that we said a number of months ago that we wouldn't actually  proceed with that project with the risk profile which was in place at the time. There's a clear message from  Petrobras that they want a company like Subsea 7 to participate in this growth of activity in Brazil, both for flexible  pipe and rigid pipe and also an acknowledgement that a more balanced risk-profile contract needs to be put in  place. And that's what I was referring to and I think we're making progress and I think we understand each other  and I see opportunities for Subsea 7 in Brazil in deepwater. We're talking about post-2015. I mean these projects  are not going to materialize in 2015. So, it's post-2015 and 2016.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Looking at the Northern Hemisphere and Life of Field business in more detail, several projects made significant  progress in the quarter. In the UK, the Montrose and Catcher projects completed offshore activities for 2015, and  the Mariner project made good progress with high levels of offshore activity supported from our offices in both  Stavanger and Aberdeen. In Norway, the Aasta Hansteen project completed all major fabrication, and on the  Gullfaks project, we completed trenching. In the Gulf of Mexico, the Heidelberg project was successfully  completed, and work commenced on the Stones project for Shell. Life of Field activity remained low particularly in  the North Sea.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In the Southern Hemisphere and Global Projects Business Unit, Seven Borealis commenced pipe lay activity on  the TEN project in Ghana, and the Exxon's Erha North project in Nigeria was substantially completed with first  order achieved in September. The Lianzi SURF and Topside projects in Angola are almost complete with  umbilicals installed and flow lines prepared on schedule.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: I would also like to give you an update on our 550-ton class new-build PLSV, Seven Rio. In April this year, we  signed a two-year contract for Seven Seas with Petrobras. However, this vessel had already been allocated to work  on the Stones project in the Gulf of Mexico.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We agreed with Petrobras earlier this year, but in order to make Seven Seas available, the new-build Seven Rio  would work on the Stones project before mobilizing to Brazil to start her five-year PLSV contract. Towards the end  of the quarter, Seven Rio joined our fleet, and she will transit to Brazil once the work in the Gulf of Mexico has  been completed.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Looking ahead to next year, we expect the environment to remain challenging with lower levels of offshore activity  and fewer projects progressing to their offshore phase. With few and large projects reaching completion in 2016, it  is unlikely that the financial benefits of good execution, risk mitigation and commercial closeouts will be as  significant as we have seen so far in 2015.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Our cost reduction program is on track to deliver approximately $550 million of annual cost savings, but we do  not expect this fully to compensate for the decline in activity. As the result, our guidance for 2016 is for both  revenue and adjusted EBITDA percentage margin to decrease significantly compared to 2015.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: I will now pass you back to Jean to comment further on our continuing cost reduction measures, our initiatives in  response to the current market and our outlook.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Thank you, Ricardo. Moving to slide 16, we have taken a number of steps to ensure Subsea 7 can develop and  strengthen through the downturn and be ready to take the opportunity to grow when market activity recovers. We  were only to recognize the pressure on project returns for our clients and started to reorganize and downsize our  capacity in 2014 with the result that when the oil price halved last year, we had already embarked on the changes  necessary to lower our cost.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Turning now to slide 18. Our line objectives to lower the project cost are changing the way we are working with  our clients. We are engaging earlier, collaborating more, and being increasingly open with each other. This will  drive solution that facilitate project function at lower oil prices.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: We have signed a similar arrangement with Premier last week. It covers early-stage engineering and CapEx, OpEx  and decommissioning activities in the UK, Southern Atlantic and Norway. With MOL, we also have an agreement  to work together on their North Sea requirements.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: To sum up on slide 19, I would like to offer some comments on the outlook. The market remained depressed as a  result of sustained low oil price. The tendering activity is competitive and the timing of new awards to market  continues to be uncertain. In the Northern Hemisphere, there are few short-term new opportunities in the North  Sea and it has been particularly impacted by the downturn due to the structurally high development cost. This has  also impacted our Life of Field business as clients hold back on non-urgent maintenance expenditure.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: In the Southern Hemisphere, the timing of last project award is still very difficult to predict, but the number of  project are expected to progress in 2016. These are mostly gas projects, particularly for domestic markets as these  are less affected by the oil price.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Altogether, we have listed some of the active market opportunities which include Bonga South West, Coral FLNG,  Rotan, Golfinho, Vashishta and West Nile Delta phase 2.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: So to conclude, times are challenging, but we are acting on what we can control. I strongly believe that the  initiatives that we started to take as early as 2014, combined with our proactive cost reduction measures, would  allow us to navigate through the downturn while building a stronger company for when the business environment  improves. We are concentrating on finding cost-effective solutions which enable our clients to progress with  deepwater field development. We have already identified significant savings and with collaboration with our  clients and suppliers, we can deliver more.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer
texts.text: Thank you, Ricardo. I'll cover off with Seaway Heavy Lifting, Fiona. We have a mixture of renewable work and oil  and gas work in the Seaway Heavy Lifting portfolio. In quarter three, we worked down in Venezuela for ENI on  the Perla project, and we completed a project in former Soviet Union for a client there, which again took assets  over the North Sea. We also completed some work for Gaz de France in Cygnus field.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer
texts.text: Moving into next year, the portfolio swings back more towards the renewable-based portfolio due to the lack of oil  and gas work coming into the North Sea that time.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: But what is important in this business environment is to remain disciplined in terms of risk management. We  haven't changed our approach in terms of contingency evaluation and we accept the internal conditions which can  be accepted and we won't go beyond. So, we are not changing the way we operate our risk profile into the – we  manage our risk profile into the environment and I think it's absolutely key to continue to execute in the way  you've seen us executing in Q3.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: Regarding the new-build, they are 550 tonnes new-build vessels. The tension of the tower, say, is 550 tonnes. The  locally-built PLSV are 300 tonnes, 350 tonnes, and therefore, cannot replace the 550 tonnes for their activity.

texts.speaker: Frederik Lunde
texts.profession: Carnegie ASA
texts.text: Thanks. Very good operations this quarter. Just wondering what happens to the test drill in the Arctic. It seems to  be delayed by about a quarter. Is there something that you have initiated or is it the yard? And do you look at  further delays?

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director
texts.text: I mean it's a bit early for 2016. We've seen reduction of activity in 2015. Future will tell what happen in the North  Sea in 2016. What is sure is that the field needs to be maintained. So, although their activity had been going down,  I mean, there is a limit in the reduction which can be done while continuing to maintain production and the safety  of the operations.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Turning first to the highlights on slide 4. We have delivered another quarter of strong operational and financial  performance in a business environment, which remains challenging due to this difficult downturn in oil and gas  investments.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: During the quarter, we took delivery of our new-build PLSV, Seven Sun, which has since commenced its long- term contract for Petrobras. Normand Seven was returned to its owner at the end of its contract and we sold  Seven Petrel to a buyer outside the oil and gas industry. Including vessels that are stacked or under construction,  we have a total fleet of 36 vessels, 8 lower than at the peak of 2014.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Looking ahead over the next 18 months, we believe that the better oil price and continued progress on  sustainable cost reductions could drive more project awards to the market.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: On the Aasta Hansteen project, we have concluded our third offshore campaign with all flowlines and control  cables connected, readies for the final hook-up with the topside when it arrives in 2018. Aasta Hansteen is the  deepest development in the Norwegian Sea to-date and involves the world's largest SPAR platform.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Offshore UK, we have been installing the riser system on the Catcher project and bundled installation for Premier.  This riser system was challenging and required an innovative buoy system. The riser system comprised 10  flexibles and 3 umbilicals, supported by three mid-water arches, one of which you can see on here on the slide. It  was installed by our crews on the Normand Seven over two campaigns lasting 80 days. Our work on this project  is due to complete in 2017 with hook-up and commissioning, which involves an extended diving company.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: The phasing of our backlog was altered somewhat compared to the last quarter due to the scheduling of work on  the Beatrice Wind Farm project. Approximately two-thirds of the revenue related to this project is now expected to  be recognized in 2017.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Our Corporate business unit includes renewables and our share of Seaway Heavy Lifting's net income. It also  includes the operating and depreciation charges pertaining to our stacked vessels. This business unit contributed  revenue of $30 million in the quarter. This increase in revenue compared to the prior year was due to the  commencement of the $1.3 billion Beatrice Wind Farm project, which was awarded earlier this year.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Firstly, our margin has been boosted by our prompt action on costs. We began to reduce the size of our workforce  in 2014 as our clients were already highlighting the need for savings even before the oil price started to fall. We  have implemented two major cost reduction and resizing programs; one in 2015, promising $550 million of  annualized savings; and one in 2016, with another $350 million in expected annualized savings.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: In August, we announced the acquisition of Swagelining. We have worked with Swagelining for a number of  years. In the last few years, we have installed over 150 kilometers of water injection pipes in the North Sea with  Swagelining's polymer lining, the most recent case being the Maria project for Wintershall. It's our belief that we  can introduce this technology to projects worldwide. In addition to its existing commercial application to lower the  cost and improve corrosion resistance of water injection pipes, we have the opportunity to develop this technology  for future application in production pipelines.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: The reaction of our clients have been positive, with high levels of interest leading to [ph] Subsea's (22:35)  opportunities to investigate the potential application of an integrated solution. From this subsea engagement, we  have already carried out eight paid early engineering studies, delivering detailed analysis of the subsea  architecture and installation, and we expect project awards in the near future.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Moving on to partnership on slide 18. As a specialized contractor concentrated on offshore oil and gas, we can  get closer to our clients and be more flexible in our approach than larger conglomerate service providers. Our  growing collection of client-partnership agreement is evidence of this. We have formed collaborative long-term  arrangement with several clients to engage early and help them to find the right solution for their field  development needs.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Turning to slide 19. The near term outlook remains challenging and the timing of new awards to market is  uncertain. However, the rise in the price of oil and lower project costs have encouraged our clients to review their  future projects. Assuming that these factors can be sustained, there is cause to believe in an increase of awards  to market within the next 18 months. We do not expect a V-shaped recovery and are prepared for a slow climb  back to more normal levels of activity.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: As illustrated by this list, some offshore areas are more favorable for near term development than others. We  continue to see momentum on projects to develop gas for domestic consumption, we have already captured  significant work offshore Egypt, and we are now looking towards India for the next wave of large development  projects including block 98/2 and KG-D6.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: We have not yet included in our list any new EPIC projects offshore Brazil; expanding remains uncertain. Brazil  has potentially low project breakevens due to the high production of the pre-salt fields. And we have a long track  record of working offshore Brazil and look forward to engaging with our clients when the opportunities arise.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: We remain active in renewables and heavy lift services mostly through our joint venture company, Seaway Heavy  Lifting. There are a number of substantial renewable energy awards to market expected in 2017 and beyond.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: To conclude, we are doing what is needed to remain strong and competitive in this challenging market. The  industry-wide challenges in development costs and rebalancing of oil supply and demand are enabling some  projects to move forward towards final investment decision.

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: We are seeing reduction of cost including reduction of cost of supply chain for our projects. I think it's fair to say  that this reduction of costs is passed to the clients and, therefore, does not affect our – doesn't impact our bottom  line in a meaningful way.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: I would emphasize what I've already pointed out earlier, which is that we are doing well, in fact, I would say that  we have achieved the cost – annualized cost savings that we targeted in 2015 when we announced our first  resizing program, and that was $550 million a year. And I have a high level of confidence that in 2017, we will see  the full benefits of the $350 million annualized reductions that we've been working on this year. Now, some of  those benefits have already flowed through to us in 2016 but, I mean, there are some – a balance, if you will, that  comes through in 2017.

texts.speaker: Phillip Lindsay
texts.profession: Analyst, Credit Suisse
texts.text: Second question, are there any specific regions that have triggered the change in tone within your outlook  statement? It looks like there's incremental projects in Norway since your last update, perhaps West Africa, too,  with Zinia. But are there any – is there anything else sort of behind the scenes? I know you mentioned Brazil but  that's more of a medium term potential. Is there anything else? Wind farm sector, for example, you could talk to?

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: The two Korean-built vessels, the Kestrel is due to come out on time and she will go to work on our DSVi contract  in the North Sea next year. And equally, the Arctic, the big heavy construction vessel is being completed in the  yard and we're comfortable with her delivery and she has work allocated to her in the North Sea, again, next  season.

texts.speaker: Ricardo H. Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: The main cost elements that we've been targeting are obviously the onshore resources and offshore resources,  the cost of running our fleet, and we've taken a long hard look at our facilities worldwide and, to the extent  possible, have shaped a way at the cost structures there and have an appreciable measure of success. So, when  you evaluate our cost structure going forward, you should assume, therefore, that the reduction is associated with  our internal cost structure.

texts.speaker: John Evans
texts.profession: Chief Operating Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Feedback from BP is they're reasonably sure that our project should meet their criteria to go through sanction. We  have offered a stand-alone Subsea 7 price, and we've also offered an alliance combination with OneSubsea into  the mix.

texts.speaker: Kevin Roger
texts.profession: Analyst, Kepler Cheuvreux SA
texts.text: Hey, good morning. Just maybe one follow-up on the EBITDA guidance margin. Just you are expecting a number  of tieback project to be sanctioned in the coming months. Those tieback project are very fast track. Should we  assume that those kind of project that the competition needs [ph] much less field (55:32) that the EBITDA margin  on this kind of project is stronger than on greenfield project?

texts.speaker: Kevin Roger
texts.profession: Analyst, Kepler Cheuvreux SA
texts.text: So, can we assume that the margin will be lower than on greenfield?

texts.speaker: Jean P. Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Well, it depends. Greenfield, I mean, they are not so many large projects, when you talk about the very large  projects, and it depends on the projects where they are. But I mean, definitely on smaller jobs, there is more  competition and, therefore, more pressure on margin. Yes.

texts.speaker: Ricardo Rosa
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Thirdly, we have acquired [ph] phenomenal (16:54) consideration, the remaining shares in our Normand Oceanic  joint venture. This transaction was completed on October 31 and brings the heavy construction and flex-lay  vessel, the Normand Oceanic, into our fleet as a fully-owned asset.

texts.text: Thank you, Ricardo. Turning now to slide 14. We are differentiated by our skilled and experienced people, our innovation and  technology, and our well-developed fleet of vessels. These trends are complemented by our alliance and  partnership and our local presence in all the major offshore markets. We are helping to transform our industry with  integrated solutions and new technology that deliver the step-change in cost and productivity. We have invested  in our capability and the line capacity to meet our client's need and executed well. This has helped us to win work,  as well as make better returns on the projects that we were awarded before the oil price decline.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: Subsea 7 had installed over 80 pipeline bundles. The same patented, controlled two installation method that we  use for bundles can be used to install large subsea structures. Cost-effective provision is not just about the capital investment  of a development. Increasingly, our clients are looking at the total field cost of projects. Our i-Tech services  business is developing better data management system to announce our Life of Field solutions.

texts.speaker: Jean Cahuzac
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
texts.text: We did see some of the active SURF project tenders that we expect to see awarded to the market in the near to  medium term. texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director, Subsea 7 SA
