texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: As presented at our last Capital Market Day in October, Sulzer contributes to a lower greenhouse  gas future in various areas.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Before I hand over to Ton, allow us to show you a 5-minute movie about some of our energy  efficient solutions that our division colleagues offer to their customers. Enjoy.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Health and safety has and will always be a very important topic for any supplier into the oil and gas  industry. And in 2010, we were able to reduce the accident frequency rate with 20%. If you look at it  since 2006-07, we’ve actually reduced the accident frequency rate with 60% and it clearly shows  that we’ve made Sulzer a significantly safer place to work.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Sustainability is one of the topics and I’ll step through a few of these topics during the course of this  presentation. We look at it in three aspects. On the one side, we want to know our own footprint,  how much energy do we use, how much water do we use, how much waste do we generate, how  much CO2 do we exhaust as an organization. We measure it. We manage it and we do it so well  that when external auditors come by we get a score of A+, which is the highest score that you can  actually get for such measurements and management focus on theme of sustainability.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: What we’ve now subsequently added is the fact that we’re actually measuring the footprint of the  products that we supply to our customers. That means, if we supply thermal spray guns to our  customer through Sulzer Metco, if we supply pumps into our customer base we can actually over  the lifetime of the product, all the way from sourcing the material, the operational phase in a refinery  or a power plant or in the dismantling of the product, actually show what the footprint is and I’ll  show you an example later in the presentation.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: As a third block, we spent quite a bit of money on innovations that also contribute to looking for  alternatives that help us to become a little less dependent on the oil and gas and coal resources  that we as a world have and that we as Sulzer of course are also quite dependent on. All of these  products I’ll show later as initial customers that are quite excited using these applications of Sulzer.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Coming to the product declarations, we have basically taken a number of our products, we have  calculated the footprint, we’ve done it according to ISO norms. It’s an international EPD Corporation  on how this should work. We’re one of the first companies that is actually doing that for our type of  equipment. In the laundry machine business, you have your A, B, C and D’s in nice colors as you  have with cars, but in our industry it’s still unique that a customer can come to us and ask us what  the footprint of the equipment is when he installs it in his location.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Our EPDs, or environmental product declarations, as they are called, are externally certified by an  independent party and you can look them up on the internet and see what the footprint of those  products are, an additional sales argument out in the market with our increasingly sensitive  customer base regarding this topic.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: On the innovation side, I’ve already showed a few of innovations in the sustainable area, they are  all innovations that are in relatively early stages, but they are already providing us with double digit  million businesses in many of its aspects. In biofuels, in the first generation Sulzer was number one  in the area of pumps and extraordinarily strong in the areas of structured packings, and is today       corrected transcript

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: 5 involved in all of the development for second and third generation biofuels. Biofuels that are not  going to be competing with the food chain anymore, but will be based on things like grass, wood  and cellulose type products.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Bioplastics, you’ve seen it in the video, customers are extraordinarily excited about our technology.  The bioplastics of the historical bioplastics were never able to withstand high temperatures, and  Sulzer together with its partner has been able to develop bioplastic with a temperature resistance  up to 200 degrees Celsius and with that it opens a completely new world of applications that the old  bioplastics could never fulfill.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: The first customers are there, as you saw in the video, they are excited, they are producing. We  have a producing pilot plant here in Oberwinterthur as well and we have a very high interest from  people to see if they want to initially mix bioplastics with the existing plastic base and later on  maybe fully replace their normal oil-based plastics with a bioplastic derivative.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: CO2 capture and storage can be argued with a lot because you’re fighting the symptoms of  CO2and not the source of generating CO2, but people believe that it will be part of our mix of  dealing with greenhouse gases and Sulzer has already delivered significant size structured  packings to actually capture CO2, and a large number of pumps that allow to bring it together, to  transport it through a pipeline and later on inject it into an old gas field for another area where it can  actually safely be stored.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Last but not least, thermal solar power. Many people when you hear solar power they think about  the photovoltaic kind of cells on top of your roofs. Here we’re talking about solar thermal power,  basically heating up a boiler with concentrating sunlight on a specific point, heating up oil, heating  up molten salt that can actually even work as a thermal battery. The large advantage of these solar  power plants that are thermal based is that they cannot only create a large capacity, they can  actually also continue to produce energy when it’s extraordinarily cloudy and many of these plants  are able because of the thermal storage to generate electricity through the night. So they don’t go  silent on the production during the night because they can store some of that thermal heat during  the course of the night and continue producing.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: We’re playing in all of these applications, they are not yet the significant part of Sulzer. We are still  a very traditional oil and gas and coal based company when it comes to our core market segments,  but with the alternatives being developed, we certainly want to be part of it and these are just a  small number of examples that have already given us initial market successes with highly excited  customers.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Looking at our key market segments, as I indicated to you earlier the three market segments you  see on the screen at this moment in time, the oil and gas upstream, the hydrocarbon processing  and the power generation segments, they are our late segments and they comprise of close to 60%  of the Sulzer exposure in the market. Whereas they were very late in coming down in the cycle,  they are at this point in time at a relatively low level compared to the peak of 2008.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: The only one of the three that shows clear light at this point in time is the upstream oil and gas  segment where people are doing a significant number of FEED studies, Front End Engineering  Studies, at the contractor base, which generally over time with quite a time delay, then result in  access projects, which then potentially order at Sulzer.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: The hydrocarbon processing industry is stable, but at a relatively low level and does not show the  same level of life that the oil and gas industry seems to have shown recently, and the power  generation in 2010 actually still contracted quite significantly. We do expect it to stabilize in the next  months to come.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: You’ve seen new innovations – innovative solutions. Chemtech very much participating in the  bioplastics, the CO2 and the biofuel applications that we’ve shown as part of the video and  previous slides during this presentation. Sulzer Chemtech naturally believes that their sales will  benefit from the increased order intake of 2010. So therefore they do believe that both sales and  operating income will grow during the course of 2011.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: If you look at order intake, you can see that the order intake in total increased by 9% compared to  2009 or adjusted by currency differences and by acquisitions by 7.5%. The positive impacts here  mainly came out of the two divisions: Sulzer Chemtech and Sulzer Metco, who were both benefiting  from the good development in the early cycle markets. In Turbo Services, of course, we could see  the positive impact through the acquisition of Dowding & Mills. Sulzer Pumps on the other side was  still decreasing mainly due to the still lagging behind of the late cycle markets like oil and gas,  power and hydrocarbon processing.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Coming to the outlook and the conclusions, we – you can see very well on the slide addressing the  individual market segments of Sulzer how the individual cycles have travelled through and how  different they have been for the individual six key market segments of the Sulzer Corporation. You  see here that the late cycle segments have been rather weak during the course of 2010. The oil  and gas segment is trickling up for growth again whereas the other two late cycle segments are not  expected to significantly return to growth, certainly not the power generation industry who after a  clear contraction in 2010 is still trying to find the bottom as we speak.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: We’ve seen drastically less large projects and large projects were the ones where the amount of  competition was generally less because customers like oil companies don’t generally give large  orders to smaller players. At this point in time the number of large projects has seriously and very  significantly reduced and as a result on the remaining projects there is a high number of  participants that could actually take these much smaller projects on as part of their business.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: The result of that is price pressure in some of our segments, clearly different payment conditions,  and as we saw in 2008 with very high commodity prices that we could in many cases pass on to the  customer. We’ve seen those prices of nickel, of stainless steel reduce significantly and as a result  also there we see a completely different raw material leverage than we had during the peak of the  cycle.

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: Thank you very much. I suggest with these pictures on the screen that not only show nice things  that are truly renewable or part of the innovative solutions that we’ve driven, we suggest it’s a great       corrected transcript

Obviously that was attached to also mentioned by you abnormally high levels in the oil and gas       corrected transcript

texts.speaker: Operator
texts.profession: Operator
texts.text: As long as the major oil producers find a way to solve, collaboratively, the social issues that they  have in their countries, this may subside relatively quickly, but if they don’t, then I think the globe  has a different set of issues at hand. texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: Okay. Thank you, Klaus, for the introduction. Now what was the major challenge for Sulzer in 2011? What has  Sulzer stand for in 2011? You will see from the figures that we stand for strong growth in the business year 2011  and also substantial acquisition, which has given us now access to the attractive water market. This acquisition,  however, also imposes a strong challenge to our organization with regard to integration into the existing business  and it also has an impact on the financial figures, and I will highlight those when we go through the presentation.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: How did our markets do in 2011? What is the share of our markets compared to the total turnover of the  company? You see that the water segment, which is now also listed on this slide, contributed to us about 8%, or if  you go on a full year pro forma basis about 13% of total sales to our portfolio. The hydrocarbon processing market  still being the highest in volume with about 25%, but followed by power with 18%, and oil and gas upstream with  about 14%. Automotive wit 6%, and aviation with about 4% are a bit weaker in sales contribution but, of course,  nevertheless, very attractive market segments for Sulzer.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: How did the markets perform in 2011? The oil and gas segment had a very strong 2011. Here the main growth  drivers were some bigger projects for pipelines and FPSOs, which we booked in the first half of the year. Region- wise, the U.S., South America, Middle East but also West Africa were contributing to this development.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: The hydrocarbon processing industry, the demand for our product was also strong but this segment had different  dynamics for our two divisions, Sulzer Chemtech and Sulzer Pumps. [ph] There is also (10:45) Sulzer Chemtech,  the services in this segment mainly related to the chemical processing industry was higher and showed a year-on- year growth. In Sulzer Pumps, the level was reduced a bit and did not show any growth.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: The refinery business is still suffering from overcapacities and we could only see newbuilds in that business in  some selected countries. The power generation market showed, as expected, a decline to previous year and, of  course, this decline is also driven by the fact that this segment is, first of all, late cycle and also because of the  negative impacts from the nuclear accident in Japan which, of course, did not give a push to the market.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: Overall, however, we see a stabilization in the course of the second half of last year. Then let us talk about the  water segment a little bit more. The main contributor to this segment today, Sulzer Pumps, with the newly  acquired Cardo Flow Solutions business, which is mainly active in the waste water business, but the division also  offers solutions for transportation and water production, later developed positively also in 2011, also supported by  new products launched to the market.  Waste water activity, and that's why you have the arrow going down, was a bit slower in 2011 compared to 2010,  and this is mainly driven by two circumstances. First of all, there was a certain weakness in the Spanish market, a  very strong market for Cardo Flow Solutions, due to the economic situation in Spain. And the other impact came  from China where we also had a sort of weakening in the waste water market due to the new five-year plan, which  was under development, and which now includes quite substantial investments into the waste water market in  that country.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: External growth, as you know, was always a key driver and a key strategic goal for Sulzer. And in the year 2011, we  could demonstrate that we are delivering and we are also able to close big acquisitions. The acquisition of Cardo  Flow Solutions at the end of 2011 – July 2011, made us a strong player in the attractive water market and also very  competitive position and good prospects for us.  We had two other add-ons in the service business in Sulzer Chemtech, which now allow us to use their local base  for other services from Sulzer Chemtech in those areas. And at the beginning of 2012, we closed another  acquisition in Spain for a pump factory, which now gives us access to the North African market and strengthens  our position in the Middle East.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: Let's have a look at Sulzer Pumps. Sulzer Pumps is a market leader in pump technology. They have a clear leading  position in oil and gas upstream and they have a top three position in water and in energy or power. The 2011  performance of Sulzer Pumps was very strong. We have a year-over-year growth in sales of 15%. We have a return  on sales of 11.9%, and we have a return on capital employed of 42.2% on adjusted basis. The number of  employees, of course, through the acquisition has also increased by quite substantially, by 1,800 and Sulzer  Pumps now employs more than 8,200 people worldwide.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: The share of the water market, of course, increased through the acquisition from 10% to 16%. But the sales volume  in the other regions remained more or less unchanged and well balanced. The operating income, of course, was  impacted by the acquisition effect. Operating income was impacted by CHF30 million of non-recurring effect and  by CHF9 million, as you can see here, by [ph] I mean (21:21) five month of amortization.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: The Pumps business, ex those special impact, generated 12% return on sales – sorry, 11.9% return on sales, which  is comparable to the previous year, 21% was the normal operational performance, Cardo. Just a quick reminder of  what Cardo actually stands for. Cardo, as you know, is a leading player in the water market. It supplies pumps and  other equipment for the water and the waste water treatment. And its customers are mainly municipalities,  private and public operators of plants, and also other customers in the water industry.  The integration process was carefully designed and is well on track. The group generated, in those five months,  sales of CHF180 million and it secured a strong operating result of 14% of EBITDA to sales. A new factory in  Shanghai is currently under construction, and will be up and running in third quarter of this year.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: Now, what are the achievements and the next steps for Sulzer Pumps? Sulzer Pumps wants to develop its market  position, of course, in the attractive water market by also benefiting from the synergies with the newly acquired  business, the existing business, and it also wants to develop its presence in the beyond BRIC countries. It has also  put a strong focus on improving its operational excellence further. The outlook for 2012 expects a further increase  in volume, as well as in operating income.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: Let's have a look at Sulzer Metco. Sulzer Metco is a market leader in surface solutions. It covers a wide range of  technologies and materials, and it holds a leading position in the thermal spray market. Also, Sulzer Metco's  performance in 2011 was strong, both orders and sales increased by a double digit figure on adjusted basis. Return  on capital employed also went up and is now – amounts now to over 18%, clearly value-generating level.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: The highlights in 2011 are clearly the strong synergies, which could be realized now from the combination of the  electromechanical business. The key focus for 2012, the strengthening of the new business area of long-term  service agreements for the power industry. Sulzer Turbo Services expects another increase in business volume and  profitability in 2012 on a moderate basis.

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: We enjoy in very specific areas, good customer contacts and we have the right products specifically on the oil and  gas side. Oil and gas for us has grown last year, year-over-year. And so that gives me the confidence on, let's say, in  specifically that area. I have grown my order intake. I've grown my order backlog, and I still see the projects going  forward where we have the potential to go ahead.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: Water has also grown for us specifically in the last quarter. So that's something which we also feel confident that  we can get the right growth in that regard and that's something where we are keeping a lot of focus in terms of  executing our water strategy.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: The area which concerns me is still the power segment. That is maybe why we are also very careful in our  guidance, [indiscernible] (01:05:32) that's something which we need to watch, but this will happen on the power  side. The other two I feel quite confident with.  Bernd Pomrehn  Analyst, MainFirst Schweiz AG  Q  Okay. Thank you. And if I may, one add-on question. How core is Chemtech for you? Is the entire Chemtech  business core for you? Are parts of the Chemtech business core for you? Can you elaborate on this? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Fabian Häcki
texts.profession: Analyst, Bank Vontobel AG (Research Firm)
texts.text: And the second one as well on cost savings, can you also elaborate on how much of your cost savings initiatives  have already materialized last year and how much is still due to come?

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: The second question on the cost saving on restructuring, we have seen already some of the savings in 2013. It was  also the reason why we had a better second half – or one of the reasons – in water and turbo services. We will see  most of the savings from the group functions, of course, now coming in 2014. But it's also fair to say that 100% of  the expected savings will then materialize only in 2015. But a big chunk of that, we will see in 2014.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: We have, for instance, closed three factories in the water business, one in Finland, one in Sweden, one in the U.S.  And there you get the savings in those legal entities immediately. However, you will, in some cases,  have to  transfer the work to another factory which would, of course, then generate cost margins there.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: So it's not so simple to say. But of course, if you spend CHF 17  million, you expect to have CHF 18 million, CHF 17   million as savings. Otherwise, you wouldn't do it. All we are saying is now we will not probably get all of those  CHF 7 0 million already in 2014. But in 2015, we will have the full impact.

texts.speaker: Torsten Wyss
texts.profession: Analyst, UBS AG (Broker)
texts.text: Okay. Thanks. And just two other questions, easier questions. Basically on the end markets on pumps, in Q4, you  stated to see the environment was difficult in Q4, perhaps could you explain us which end markets spe cifically,  which I mean, upstream, downstream and that way?

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: I think we guided specifically that on the oil and gas side, we expect a certain growth. But we have also other  market segments where we are a little bit more cautious. So that is why the total guidance for IFRS is clearly  different if you would be just a pure-play in playing on those markets. We agree that specifically in the U.S. on the  downstream side, and Chemtech is well-positioned on our side, to participate in exactly those increases. So we will  also see increases in the areas you mentioned.

texts.speaker: Brian Konigsberg
texts.profession: Analyst, Vertical Research Partners LLC
texts.text: Okay. But still, I mean, if you aggregate the entire portfolio, I would still believe – I would expect there to be a  pretty meaningful order improvement given the stabilization in water. Power is probably not doing a whole lot.  But oil and gas, being such a significant contributor, it probably should be a little bit better than modest growth. Is  that an unfair statement?

texts.speaker: Alexander S. Virgo
texts.profession: Analyst, Joh. Berenberg, Gossler & Co. KG (United Kingdom)
texts.text: The second question is just a sort of a broader question on cost savings. 1% or so of the cost, I guess, is CHF 25  million, if I add up your COGS and selling expenses for this year. That doesn't sound an awful lot in terms of either  an ambition or a target, particularly given the various things that you talked about at the Capital Markets Day and  have talked about before.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: Regarding the cost savings, as mentioned also by Jürgen, I mean, we took out the people. Some of the people are  still with us and obviously will go out. We achieved already some savings in H2 last year, specifically on turbo  services as well as on the wastewater side. That was one of the reasons – or that supported the better performance  in H2. And we look at it very carefully what will happen time-wise also in 2014. And that was exactly why we gave  our guidance and to be quite honest, at this moment, we believe that this is the right number that we will get on  savings.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: The other area is COGS, of course. There, we have also started several initiatives. We do not have an overall, an  overarching sourcing initiative which is aimed to take 5% of sourcing cost out, but we're looking at different types  of materials, for instance, different type of services in the COGS area where we also try to pool and get savings out  of that. We have not quantified that and, as soon as we do have more clarity here and are more safe or more secure  that we can actually achieve those savings, of course, we will provide more information.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: All of the CHF 200 million we're guiding this 5% to 10% and this is, as I said, not related to the COGS, not to the  project costs. It's related to these other costs where I was talking about the pooling on the local level. We should  see some of that, of course, more of that coming in 2014.

texts.speaker: Jürgen Brandt
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer, Sulzer AG
texts.text: We have taken more than 300 people out together with the or which goes in line with the CHF 17 million which we  have spent. Of course, you can calculate what kind of savings that would bring but just to remind you, not all of  them are OpEx. Some of them are COGS which need to be replaced by other cost. But it's fair to say that the CHF  25 million, which we have guided, is still an assumption we would get as a saving and so what I'm saying is that  not the full effect we will see in the current year of 2014.

texts.speaker: Q
texts.profession: Thank you. I have several questions. My first one would be if you could comment on the turbo services business,
texts.text: And then within the pumps business it looks like you're going to have three sort of sub -sectors in business areas:  the water, oil and power. But those will not be reported separately and you expect that that configuration will be in  effect fully from 2015. I'm just wondering, so will we first then get the new configuration in the first half like you'll  change reporting for first half? So just if you could clarify that.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: In a challenging market environment, especially after significant oil price drop, we achieved our financial  guidance. We were able to stabilize our profitability and the effects of the restructuring changes initiated showed  adverse results. With the implemented measures, we laid the foundation to further improve the profitability in the  coming years.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: As you recall, we decided to build Sulzer's core business for equipment and services around three key markets: oil  and gas, power, water; and to maintain niche positions in selected general industry. In this market, we offer  customer-focused solutions for performance critical application. We also decided to become one focused, market- orientated, globally operating company. Let me now explain to you what we exactly mean with this.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We also want to ensure we maintain the capability to continuously adapt to changes in our environment and can  deliver value to our shareholders through optimal capital allocation. You will hear more about this program in this  afternoon, but let me briefly touch on the core elements of our Sulzer Full Potential Program.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: This year, the business unit water goodwill impaired by CHF 340 million relating to the wastewater business line.  With this, we are aligning book value with future growth rates and profitability assumptions. Thomas will talk in  his presentation in more detail about the impairment.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Our focus markets are supported by macro trends, such as population growth, urbanization, sustainability and  energy efficiency. We therefore believe all these markets remain attractive in the long term. In 2014, we have  experienced different development in our markets. In oil and gas, demand improved despite the capital discipline  of major oil companies after the significant oil price drop. With a share of 54% in the oil and gas market, our  exposure in this market has increased. The oil price volatility limits our top line visibility in 2015, but the absolute  level of investment is still expected to remain high.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: In the power market, the demand decreased driven by fewer new projects. The demand in the water market was  also lower than 2013, driven especially by the engineered water business. Here, challenging conditions in South  Africa, Spain and Brazil were the main drivers. Demand in the general industry was also lower.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Last year, as mentioned, we stabilized our margins and laid now the foundation to improve our profitability in the  future, especially the performance of our division Pumps Equipment is not satisfactory. The division achieved an  EBITR of CHF 141 million. The wastewater business has a significant influence in the margin deterioration over  time, but also the decentralized procurement approach and regional managed manufacturing network are  opportunities and levers to improve the profitability in the future.

texts.speaker: Thomas J. W. Dittrich
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Let me outline the key points I'm going to make during my presentation. As you heard already, sales and  profitability guidance was achieved. With stabilized margin, we took the impairment on the goodwill relating to  the business line, wastewater, and we're increasing shareholder return through increasing the ordinary dividend  by 9% to CHF 3.50. And we are updating the dividend payout range from one-third previously to 40% to 70% of  net income going forward. These reflect also our conviction that we will realize Sulzer's full potential going  forward.

texts.speaker: Thomas J. W. Dittrich
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: With that, let me move on to the impairment in relation to the wastewater business line. The impairment was  necessary, and it relates to the wastewater business line which, as you see on this slide here, is within the business  unit Water, and that business unit is inside Pumps Equipment.

texts.speaker: Thomas J. W. Dittrich
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: And first, let's look at the proportions, and some of them are noted on the right side of the slide. Sulzer overall  carries about CHF 1 billion of acquired goodwill on the balance sheet, of which CHF 620 million are allocated to  the business unit Water. And almost all of that CHF 620 million resulted from the acquisition of Cardo Flow  Solutions, which is the wastewater business line today.

texts.speaker: Thomas J. W. Dittrich
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: We understand the wastewater business line and our business unit management have solid plans in place going  forward. Therefore, to reflect this, the goodwill impairment of CHF 340 million resulted from the change of  estimated future growth rates and profitability assumptions in order to bring them in line with past performance  that we have seen and expected market development. And with that impairment as you also will note, we are  reducing the goodwill within the Water business unit by over 50%.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The markets, as you know, are becoming increasingly volatile because of the current developments in the oil  prices, some regional conflicts, and also some geopolitical development. The low oil price could influence Sulzer's  performance which accounts for 54% that you have seen of our business negatively. However, our business mix is  balanced through our 45% service share, as well as through our exposure to other markets, regions and customer  segment.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The outlook for the oil and gas market overall for us is negative, and we expect a slight decline in this market  driven by Pumps Equipment and Chemtech. In the Rotating Equipment division, we expect a stable order intake  in this market.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Activity in the power market overall again is forecasted to remain stable at a low level, although driven by the  demand in Pumps Equipment. Rotating Equipment Services expects in this market a slight increase.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Demand in the water market is expected to grow slightly driven here by Pumps Equipment.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: As shown, oil and gas, power and water are long-term attractive markets, and we know how to win in those  markets. With our products and services, we serve performance-critical applications where quality, reliability and  technology leadership are key. We have this truly global footprint with established manufacturing and service  centers. This helps us, as already mentioned by Thomas, with the current appreciation of the Swiss franc as we are  generally naturally hedged.

texts.speaker: Jörg-André Finke
texts.profession: HSBC Trinkaus & Burkhardt AG (Broker)
texts.text: Yes. Good morning. It's André Finke from HSBC. Two questions, the first one on the Water business. You said the  impairments reflects new assumptions on growth and profitability. Maybe you can share these assumptions with  us and maybe also comment on what cushion is left to the remaining goodwill in the Water business. And you said  also that Chemtech is an integral part of the portfolio. Is that true for Water as well?

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: In terms of water, is this part of the overall strategy? We're always looking, and I think this is something where  management has, in any case, the ownership to do so. We look at every business, their abilities to win, their  situation in the market, their relative market position, how can we make them profitable over time. And any type  of business unit which we have will always be seen with that connotation, where this can be. Clearly is [ph] today  (52:07) that we have an issue in the profitability in wastewater – you will see that also this afternoon – and that  we are committed to fix this one over time very, very quickly. The impairment was one of the steps, obviously, in  that direction.

texts.speaker: Stefan Gächter
texts.profession: Helvea SA
texts.text: Now, I'm just curious, if we would be carving out the Water business, especially the wastewater business, by how  many basis points the operational EBITA margin as of today would improve suddenly? I mean, in a perfect world,  maybe you would get a call, yeah, tomorrow by someone trying to acquire the wastewater business.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: You would see the exact figures this afternoon. But just as an outline on overall Sulzer, the impact is 1.8, if I recall  exactly or correct – 1.4, sorry, EBITA level, it's 1.4, but this is significant on Sulzer level. The impact on Pumps  Equipment is obviously a lot higher. So if you look at it over time, the margin situation which we have seen since  2010, half of that one is, in fact, related to the dilution of the wastewater business. So there's a pickup in that  range from the wastewater side.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: On things which Thomas will explain and maybe, let's say, you can say something on that one, G&A shared  services clearly applies to the whole organization what we want to do in the G&A side. Selling again is completely  different in the different avenues where the routes to market again would apply, for example, in the wastewater  site moving to distributor model away from a diagram which is very expensive. So, there's a couple of levers which  are specific to division as these are more general, but the main thrust is the  – so, Thomas, you can say something  to the G&A side if you wish.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: But if something happens drastically on the top line, like we have from the oil price hike a complete shifting of all  the projects, and the capital discipline comes to a point where really, let's say, no growth is there anymore and  there's a huge cancellation or delay of all those project, then we will have an issue. So, it is not that we need a lot of  growth. But what we cannot afford, obviously, is that this goes backfire and that we have a declining market big  time, that will have an impact.

texts.speaker: Thomas J. W. Dittrich
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: And we would obviously not stop the initiatives. We would do all that and even work even harder on them, but a  lot of it would get eaten up through, as we've said before, under-absorption effects that would go against them if  the top line really decreases substantially.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: On the other – let's say, we can talk about what is sustainable, but what you can see in the others line are already  some of the synergy savings. That is clearly something which you can see. We were also able to produce the IT cost  and get them, from that perspective, in line. But we have also some other effects, which make this one clearly not  the sustainable figure for the future. The figure for the future is different. Although I say – Thomas, if you can  quantify a little bit on those.

texts.speaker: Thomas J. W. Dittrich
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: Yeah. Sustainable figure for the future is around – I think you now see CHF 10 million in there. It's in that range, a  little bit higher maybe, sorry, but not much.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: I mean, what is clear that on the oil and gas side, the margin pressure, the price pressure from the customers is  coming through. I mean, I think there is no supplier in that field which has not received a letter from all the  majors asking for price reductions, price decreases so on and so forth.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So, on the other side, there is clearly this component. Obviously, we're trying not to pass on whatever we can to  our supplier base. So, you will see generally a reduction, I think, in prices which made certain projects again  financially more viable from that perspective. So, we expect clearly a pricing pressure specifically on the oil and  gas side and specifically in those projects which are related to the capital side.

texts.speaker: Rizk Maidi
texts.profession: Barclays Capital Securities Ltd.
texts.text: Good morning. Rizk Maidi from Barclays. Just a question on oil and gas. So, there are clearly big questions on  around how long environmental growth oil prices are going to persist. How do you think your organization is  prepared to weather a very long period of low oil prices, and have you already started any action for it?

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Definitely. Yeah. I think depending on whom you're talking with my divisional colleague on Pumps Equipment, in  fact, we've visited a couple of customers on the oil and gas side beginning of this year to just try to get exactly that  feeling. But I think if you talk to 20 people you'll get 20 different assessments on what everybody believes and  does not.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: But I think for us if you look at our footprint, if you look at our exposure in the different area, we'll find the  following. Upstream is the lowest part for us. 16% of our sales we do, in fact, on the upstream side. Then on the  upstream side, the basic capital discipline where oil companies who obviously have a longer view will cut spending  the most probably the first is going to be in the exploration side. And also, let's take a look at the [indiscernible]  (1:09:56) with fracing, those are exactly the applications where we do not have products in that regard. So, we are  less exposed on those type of projects in any case.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We then continue to the midstream side. Midstream, we see 2015, specifically in the Americas, a difficult year, but  this was already known and has nothing to do with the capital discipline. This is simply because those projects  take a long time to materialize. And we knew exactly that 2015 is going to be down, but therefore, 2016 and 2017,  we know already the projects because we are environmentally and all the legislations processes take place, so we  will know what is happening there.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The biggest exposure we have in the oil and gas market is clearly on the downstream side. This comes from  Chemtech. This comes also from Pumps Equipment. And there you see a little bit of a mixed bag. We see projects  delayed, but those sort of things which are already on the go will still remain and look forward. So what do we  obviously do is we try to get exactly a flexible organization – that's also one of the things from the manufacturing  footprint – to cater for those types of things; and to set ourselves up that we can adapt quickly to those type of  changes, and if need be, retract and get the networks, with a make-or-buy decision in such a way that we have not  all our factories set up 100% for those sort of things, but as we have enough fluctuation, so if there's a downturn,  we can react. This is basically the model which we have applied specifically on the oil and gas.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Okay. Let's start with the Cardo Flow. We did now all the restructuring on the Cardo Flow side. We also have  introduced a new product, which is coming to the market in fact 2015. So, we're seeing the improvement which we  wanted to see specifically on the wastewater side. The total water business unit this year, and I think we  mentioned that one in the presentation as well with the impacted by the engineered water side, which saw a drop  in the projects that I mentioned, the difficult situations which we had in South Africa, Brazil and also in Spain.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: So, we are seeing the improvement in the wastewater side. We know what we have to do there, and that is exactly  the reason why we're saying that this is going to be based on the measures which we have, the right path to go and  improve that profitability. So, changes have been made due to the restructuring. We are bottoming up. We are  seeing the growth, and we have new products which are showing the results out there in the market.

texts.speaker: Q
texts.profession: [indiscernible] (1:18:00) I've got two questions. What are the effects of Russia and Ukraine turmoil on Sulzer in
texts.text: 2015 and would you have to adapt somehow your footprint in Russia? And the second question, you're quite  pessimistic about the oil and gas business, but optimistic on your general industry business. But isn't there a  secondary effect of low oil and general energy prices on your industry business, namely, your trigger to save  energy costs for the industries is absent for the moment somehow?

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The other one in terms of oil and gas, maybe, let's say, don't get me wrong. I'm not optimistic in oil and gas. I'm  saying, let's say, that that is the area where we're seeing it flat to decline. So, I'm not optimistic in that regard. We  have very limited visibility and whatever happens on the oil price could have a negative influence, and that was  exactly what I said during my presentation from that perspective. So, it is not that I am very optimistic. It's exactly  the opposite around is we really don't know. Our visibility in that regard with the oil prices is very limited.

texts.speaker: Torsten Wyss
texts.profession: UBS AG (Broker)
texts.text: Excuse me. Maybe I was not clear enough. I wasn't talking about your oil and gas business. But on a possible  secondary effect of lower energy prices, not only oil and gas but also electricity on your general industry  businesses.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: General industry. Yeah. Okay. What you normally expect is exactly – sorry, then I misunderstood or did not  understand your question. The oil price is, and this is what is quoted all over the place, is that this could help in  terms of being a [indiscernible] (1:21:10) program from that perspective going forward.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: We're seeing some of those effects, and that's exactly what we expect in certain areas. But on our general industry,  we are in niches which are not necessarily directly driven by the oil price. Healthcare, and that's one of our main  areas, has very little to do with those type of things.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The other one is pulp and paper. That is more impacted about cheap energy pricing. That could have been – could  get a little bit of a profit from that perspective going forward. But the other areas in general industry has a lot to  with Europe and for us still Europe is not coming strong back again as we would all hope. And you cannot debate  if it's 1.6% or 1.2%, the general growth expectations in Europe where it's still a very, very sizable region,  geographical region for us is still limited.

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: The RES margin improvement was – yes, we saw the effects from a return of the business in Australia. And we're  also seeing some uptakes on the service integration. I'm not sure if you will see exactly the same margin  improvement obviously again year-over-year, but we have identified what we need to do specifically on certain  service centers to further improve the profitability of those.

texts.speaker: Wasi A. Rizvi
texts.profession: RBC Europe Ltd. (Broker)
texts.text: Great. Thank you. And just one more on your oil and gas prices. So, you were speaking last year about delays and  have participated in push-outs. Now, what level of push-outs have you assumed in your guidance for 2015? Have  you assumed a similar level to what you're seeing at the back end of last year or have you assumed that perhaps  things will deteriorate a bit more? Or are you saying you've assumed the same level as last year, and if things  worsened, then maybe your guidance is perhaps too optimistic?

texts.speaker: Klaus Stahlmann
texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Then if you look at the market, we still believe in, also let's say, where we are in this moment. This is the  reasonable approach in terms of the slight decline or decrease in that regard. We have seen although already on  the oil and gas side postponements of projects. This has clearly happened. And that is exactly, let's say, why we are  not – or, let's say, we are taking that one with a pinch of salt and watching that one very carefully where this will  drop. But as I said, with our business mix, this makes us a little bit more resilient to certain changes, maybe it's  another oil and gas company in that regard.

texts.speaker: Thomas J. W. Dittrich
texts.profession: Chief Financial Officer
texts.text: And just on the margin improvement on RES, just to note, as I said earlier during the presentation, they have also  benefited from being able to dispose of the building they did no longer need. So, that helped on a return on sales  before restructuring basis. On an operational EBITA basis, that would be out. So, that's the clean measure to look  at. That's what why we're doing it, right, to really make sure we know where the overall business is going. And  once we pull the levers on Sulzer Full Potential, what they really bring undistorted for footprint actions like this  one. Okay?

texts.speaker: Armin Rechberger
texts.profession: Zürcher Kantonalbank (Broker)
texts.text: Yeah. Rechberger from ZKB. Saudi Pumps, you mentioned that you closed the deal but it's not included yet. Are  there some delays? What's the problems there? Then an outlook behind 2015, I mean, 2015, two months are  already off. So, I mean, there should be some visibility behind 2015 in regards of bigger projects in energy, for  example, or Chemtech, how is the activity level there regarding bigger projects?

texts.speaker: Armin Rechberger
texts.profession: Zürcher Kantonalbank (Broker)
texts.text: And the third question, I missed a little bit a wildcard. Once you were mentioning the biodegradable plastics and  so on or food for energy and so on. Maybe if you hear more in the afternoon of that, but no wildcards around?

texts.speaker: Bernd Pomrehn
texts.profession: MainFirst Schweiz AG
texts.text: Bernd Pomrehn from MainFirst. As you already indicated, last year's EBIT included the gain from a real estate  property divestment of CHF 40 million. Should we expect similar gains in the coming years resulting from your  footprint optimization which then, for example, probably would offset some of the restructuring costs going  forward? Thank you.

texts.speaker: Grégoire Poux-Guillaume

texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
texts.text: Now, if on a CHF 3 billion company if you say 4% to 6%, that's CHF 120 million to CHF 180 million. Now we are  saying CHF 200 million. So we've raised the bar. texts.profession: Chief Executive Officer
